title: ssr-node: contain malformed HTTP targets in the request listener
description:
Contain request-target URL parsing in the HTTP request listener so one parser-accepted malformed request cannot terminate the Node SSR sidecar.

Ownership: impl_ssr_node; implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:234-241, particularly the unguarded new URL at line 236. The second parse at line 158 should consume the already-parsed value where practical. Reviewed source at baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261 and HEAD 50abcab5ce674e5107b34834ebbfd81d1af7e2cd; git diff baseline -- implementation/ssr-node was empty. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Trigger: connect to the service and send raw HTTP bytes GET // HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n. GET http://[::1 HTTP/1.1 reaches the same failure. Node accepts each request line and invokes the package request listener; new URL throws ERR_INVALID_URL synchronously outside any request-local catch. handleRender's catch cannot reach this outer listener operation.

Expected: a bounded malformed-request 400 response (or documented request-local rejection), followed by a healthy service able to answer the next request. Actual: uncaught TypeError, process exit 1, no HTTP status returned. This takes unrelated in-flight work and all capacity down with the caller's bad target. Default bind is loopback; no public Internet exposure is assumed.

Suggested repair: catch URL-construction failure in the outer request listener and send the existing CODE.MALFORMED_REQUEST Refusal. Preserve /health, /render?stream=1 and unknown-path routing. Parse once if doing so removes the duplicate URL parse. Do not replace request-local containment with a process-wide uncaughtException handler.

Acceptance criteria:
- Raw requests with // and http://[::1 yield a bounded 4xx/refusal without uncaughtException, unhandledRejection or service exit.
- Valid health and render requests to that SAME service still succeed after each malformed target.
- /missing remains 404 and /render?stream=1 retains streaming behavior.
- Include a parser-accepted malformed target, so the regression does not pass solely because Node rejected the request before this listener ran.

Fresh validation: Node v24.13.0; ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_ssr_node/probe-impl_ssr_node-1.cjs drives the actual serve() implementation via real TCP loopback on ephemeral ports in isolated children. /health returned 200 and /missing returned 404, both child exit 0; // and http://[::1 each exited 1 with ERR_INVALID_URL and http.cjs:236 in the stack. The outer witness asserted these current failures and exited 0. Log and exit receipt: probe-impl_ssr_node-1.log and probe-impl_ssr_node-1.exit in the same ignored directory. Child/socket cleanup is bounded; no persistent servers remain. This is reproduction evidence, not a repaired-test green; no package-wide suite, compilation, browser or JVM crossing run.

Deduplication and references: revalidated and split Finding 1 of aggregate rf2-fzbj.22. Current tracker searches for ssr-node, Invalid URL and related request handling found no identical dedicated open issue. rf2-fzbj.10's redirect-policy finding is a different outbound SSR URL policy. Preserve the rf2-fzbj remediation hold: this fresh review authorizes issue creation only, not remediation or fixer dispatch. Parent for this independent finding is rf2-gwye; prior statuses/notes remain untouched.
notes:
VERDICT (worker ssrnode-a, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9744 (one commit on implementation/ssr-node/**).

Re-verified at the branch base before fixing. implementation/ssr-node was byte-unchanged since the reviewed HEAD 50abcab5ce, and the rf2-gwye review probe, copied to scratch and re-rooted at the worktree, reproduced all four defects with exit 0:
- // and http://[::1 each killed the child process with ERR_INVALID_URL at http.cjs:236;
- boot-exit start() stayed pending at 1000 ms against bootTimeoutMs 500;
- the split surrogate streamed as hex 3c703eefbfbdefbfbd3c2f703e;
- non-Latin-1 requestIds came back 500 render-threw.

What landed, finding by finding:
- rf2-gwye.22 (fzbj.22 finding 1, malformed request target). src/http.cjs guards new URL() inside the request listener and answers with the existing MALFORMED_REQUEST refusal (400, x-rf-ssr-refusal). handleRender now receives the already-parsed URL, so the second, unguarded parse is gone.
- rf2-gwye.23 (fzbj.22 finding 2, worker exit before readiness). The worker exit handler in src/isolate.cjs rejects start() as MALFORMED_MODULE, with detail {modulePath, exitCode}. Once ready has resolved this is a no-op, as the error arm's reject already is. It adds no new state and no second timer. Pool.start's allSettled sibling cleanup and release()'s replacement-failure arm observe the rejection unchanged.
- rf2-gwye.24 (fzbj.22 finding 3, surrogate pair split across streamed chunks). The streaming writer holds back at most one trailing high surrogate (holdTrailingHighSurrogate) and writes it with the next chunk, or alone before res.end(). That matches the buffered join's encoding of an unmatched surrogate.
- rf2-gwye.25 (requestId that no header can carry). http.validateHeaderValue('x-rf-ssr-request', requestId) now runs before service.renderFrames. Failure is refused BAD_REQUEST_FIELD 400 with detail.field "requestId", and the JSON refusal body still echoes the token. The in-process string contract is unchanged, and the README documents the HTTP constraint.

Regression rows:
- test/bytes.test.cjs: the malformed-target row, the split-surrogate row (split pair, empty intervening chunk, several split pairs, unmatched control, compared against Buffer.from(parts.join(''),'utf8') in both modes), and the requestId row (the renderer-call spy reads zero; an ASCII control echoes in both modes).
- test/timeout.test.cjs: eval exit 7 and boot exit 0 each reject createService promptly with bootTimeoutMs at its 30 s default. A 2-isolate start where one sibling exits rejects, the healthy sibling is terminated, and both threadIds read -1. A replacement that exits before ready refuses its queued waiter with REPLACEMENT_FAILED_REFUSAL, writes the operator stderr line, and close() completes.
- test/fixtures/exits.cjs gains the env switch RF2_SSR_NODE_EXIT_AT (eval, boot, boot-even-thread). With it unset, the fixture behaves as before.

RED control: the pre-fix src/http.cjs and src/isolate.cjs were planted from the parent commit (planted blob hashes equal the parent's). All four RED runs exited 1, each on its intended assertion. After the restore, the blob hashes equal the commit's and git diff --quiet exits 0.

Gates:
- npm run test:ssr-node (CI job node-ssr-node) exits 0 on the final base, 9 suites green.
- check_readme_links.py --ci exits 0.
- The changed-surface classifier arms only ssr_node.
- The tree-wide ratchets I ran all exit 0.

Skipped on purpose, one sentence each:
- No timing witness for prompt delivery of completed chunks: the writer holds back at most one code unit, and only when a chunk ends in a high surrogate.
- x-rf-ssr-build shares the raw-header mechanism, and so does the render catch's String(err) wording a failure there would reach. The value is the module's own boot-time buildId rather than caller input, and no review claimed it, so both are left as they are.
- No global uncaughtException handler, and no extra boot timeout. Both beads ruled those out as substitutes.

spec/011-SSR.md needs no change. It names requestId as a field the JVM adapter sends but states no character set for it. The adapter sends (str (symbol frame-id)) and classifies any non-200 other than a 504 as ssr-node-refused, so a 500 that becomes a 400 lands in the same JVM error id.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9744. src/http.cjs now guards the request-target URL parse inside the listener and answers with the existing MALFORMED_REQUEST 400. handleRender reuses the parsed URL instead of parsing it a second time. The regression row in test/bytes.test.cjs sends // and http://[::1 as raw request lines. Each gets a 400 carrying this listener's own refusal header, which proves Node's parser accepted it. The SAME server then answers /health and a render, and /missing is still 404. The row was RED (the process died with ERR_INVALID_URL at http.cjs:236) before the fix.

title: schemas: preserve sensitive rejection redaction across variable-width cat sequences
description:
Preserve rejection-trace redaction when a Malli concatenation contains a regex child that consumes zero or multiple input values. Keep exact sibling precision for tuples and demonstrably fixed-width concatenations; use the existing conservative whole-node decision for ambiguous regex positions. This is a correctness repair to supported schema forms, with no new validation policy or public API.

Ownership: impl_schemas, implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc and validate.cljc; relevant schema tests under implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/. Review baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 555cd5b8c30327ac815e306ed6c4619e71881b17. No owned source changed between them. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Confirmed behavior

Under the existing schemas JVM reset fixture and the REAL with-trace-recorder! macro:

    (schemas/reg-app-schema [:items]
      [:cat [:* :int] [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :int]]])
    (schemas/validate-app-schema!
      {:items [{:token "schema-review-secret"}]} :schema-review)

The candidate correctly rejects, but its :rf.error/schema-validation-failure trace carries:

    {:sensitive? true
     :tags {:path [:items 0]
            :value {:token "schema-review-secret"}
            :explain :rf/redacted
            :explain-humanized :rf/redacted ...}}

Expected: :value is :rf/redacted. It contains the failing sensitive child even though the explanation's common input path identifies the whole map. Actual: the secret is disclosed in the diagnostic producer. This review does not allege production validation bypass or demonstrate later external transmission.

The same leak was freshly reproduced with named concatenation

    [:catn [:prefix [:* :int]]
           [:payload [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :int]]]]

and with an optional prefix [:cat [:? :int] SensitiveMap], against the same zero-prefix value. Fixed-width [:cat :int SensitiveMap] against [1 {:token "schema-review-secret"}] redacts correctly. A repeated prefix consuming two integers also redacts through the existing out-of-range fallback; this is a control, not a claim that every regex input leaks.

Cause and exact repair direction

walker.cljc:46-70 groups :tuple, :cat and :catn together as position-bearing; :239-273 extracts declarations under schema-child indices. align-in-path at :659-692 then chooses children[input-index], and sanitize-sensitive-path at :925-952 makes the same assumption. That assumption holds for one-value-per-child forms but not for Malli regex sequences. Malli 0.20.1 reports :in paths [[0] [0 :token]] in the repro. validate.cljc:994 computes their common ancestor [0], then :1051-1052 asks the walker for leaf and whole sensitivity. The walker visits [:* :int], schema child zero, although input element zero is the sensitive map from schema child one. The whole decision is true and the leaf decision false, so per-slot shaping at :1097-1124 redacts the explanations and stamps the trace while retaining the map in :value.

Distinguish fixed-width concatenations from those containing expanding/optional/nested regex children consistently in declaration extraction, alignment, and path sanitization. At an ambiguous node, retain the ancestor context and conservatively consult sensitivity/opacity for the entire unresolved node. Retain current exact non-sensitive-sibling precision for tuples and known fixed-width event :cat/:catn forms. Do not build a second Malli parser to solve this: conservative fallback within the existing pure-data walker is sufficient.

Acceptance criteria

- Regression tests use real Malli and the real trace recorder for zero-width :cat, :catn and :? prefixes; no secret substring survives a trace value-bearing slot.
- Include nonzero repetitions and nested regex expansion so the fix addresses runtime width, plus sensitive value-bearing path segments where sanitization applies.
- Existing fixed-width :cat/:catn/:tuple sibling precision, sensitive-map redaction, explanation redaction and opaque-schema behavior continue to pass.
- Share schema fixtures across CLJ/CLJS where practical and execute both hosts during remediation.

Validation and limits

Fresh process-local JVM witness: ai/surface-review-20260913/impl_schemas/probe-impl_schemas-1.clj, with corresponding .log and .exit; runner exit 0. The witness asserts the current incorrect behavior and separately checks controls, so exit 0 confirms the defect rather than claiming it fixed. Its source resource URLs resolve to this checkout. The same isolated process then ran schemas-storage-test, schemas-reg-side-effects-test, schemas-presence-test, schemas-walker-literal-operand-test, schemas-walker-opaque-warning-test and schemas.digest-parity-test: 95 tests, 456 assertions, zero failures/errors. No CLJS compilation, shared build, full spine, or production gate was executed. No source changes were made.

Provenance and duplicate check

Revalidated and split finding 1 from aggregate rf2-fzbj.25. Its current description, notes and newest three history entries were read; its existing remediation fence was not altered. Current all-status tracker searches for variable-width, print-length and print-level plus the open issue index found the aggregate and no dedicated owner of this defect. The old rf2-4q681i precision rationale remains useful and should be preserved: the requested repair targets regex width only. Parent rf2-gwye authorizes this fresh review and individual finding record, not implementation of the older aggregate.
notes:
VERDICT (schemas-a worker, 2026-09-13): PR #9750, branch worker/schemas-a, commit 5766e14472. Covers rf2-fzbj.25 (both findings), rf2-gwye.11 (finding 1) and rf2-gwye.14 (finding 2).

RE-VERIFIED AT TIP 946751a804 BEFORE FIXING. The reviewer's 20260913 probe, re-pointed at the worker worktree (its source-URL assertion pinned the worktree's walker.cljc and validator.cljc), still reproduced both findings.
- Finding 1: the secret in :value for a zero-width :* prefix in :cat and in :catn, and for an empty :? prefix.
- Finding 2: equal digests under a bounded *print-length*, a bounded *print-level*, and both, and the collision was still served from the memo after each binding ended.

FINDING 1 FIXED (walker.cljc only). Positional :tuple / :cat / :catn precision (rf2-4q681i, rf2-ss06u.4) now applies only to a :tuple, or to a :cat / :catn whose every element provably consumes one value (a keyword, symbol, fn or non-regex vector form) and which is not itself spliced into an enclosing regex op. Any other sequence:
- descends its elements index-free at the shared base-path, like :sequential, with :catn entry flags claiming the base-path;
- falls back to the whole-node sensitivity/opacity decision in align-in-path;
- takes the fail-closed tail in sanitize-sensitive-path.
There is no second regex parser and no new dependency. validate.cljc needed no change.

FINDING 2 FIXED (validator.cljc). compute-edn-print binds *print-length* and *print-level* to nil beside its existing print flags, around both canonicalisation and the final pr-str. Memo keys, the digest algorithm, the public API and the custom-printer contract are unchanged. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc reads the digest only through the :schemas/app-schemas-digest late-bind hook, so it needed no edit and ssr-a's file was not touched.

REGRESSION TESTS (all under implementation/schemas/test).
- sequence_width_fixtures.cljc, a new shared CLJ/CLJS corpus:
  - Six leak cases: zero-width :* in a :cat and in a :catn, an empty :?, a nonzero :* repetition that shifts the payload onto a later schema child, a nested :cat expansion, and a sensitive :map-of key that would ride :path / :reason.
  - Three controls that must still report their value verbatim: a variable-width :cat declaring nothing sensitive, fixed-width :cat sibling precision, and a slot outside a variable-width sequence.
  - Asserted end to end through validate-app-schema! and the real trace recorder by schemas_sensitive_test.clj (JVM) and the new schemas_sequence_width_cljs_test.cljs (CLJS).
- schemas_walker_operators_test.clj pins the index-free declaration shape.
- digest_parity_fixtures.cljc, with digest_parity_test.clj and digest_parity_cljs_test.cljs, adds a shared printer-limit observation:
  - Covers bounded length, bounded level, and both, each from an empty memo, with the tests calling the digest pipeline directly so no registry state can leak in.
  - Bytes and digests are read inside the binding and re-read after it without clearing, and each read must equal the unbounded baseline.
  - One form's collection-valued map keys and set members exercise the canonicaliser's comparator.

RED THEN GREEN. The pre-fix walker.cljc and validator.cljc (their origin/main blobs, verified by blob hash) were planted and the gates run against them:
- jvm-schemas: exit 1, 21 failures, all in the new tests (6 leak cases x 2 assertions, :value redacted and secret absent; 3 printer bindings x inside/after; 3 walker pins).
- CLJS :node-test: exit 1, 18 failures, all in the two new CLJS deftests.
The three controls passed on both trees. The restore was verified by blob hash against the committed objects, then the gates were run on the fixed tree:
- jvm-schemas: exit 0, 394 tests / 19352 assertions, against a 390 / 19312 pre-change baseline. Re-run on the final rebased base with the same result.
- CLJS :node-test: exit 0, 11993 tests / 59617 assertions.
The CLJS host reproduces both defects too; the review had executed the JVM only.

OTHER GATES, ALL EXIT 0: jvm-security (92 tests / 725 assertions), test:security (93 / 732), test:schemas-bundle (PASS, margin 39.9 KB inside 20.0-44.0 KB), and all 46 scripts/check_*.py checkers. cljs-browser-schemas-boundary-prod and the other classifier-armed browser, examples and bundle-isolation jobs are left to CI.

RECORDED, NOT BUILT.
- Keyword or symbol registry references inside a :cat are treated as single-value. The walker cannot tell a ref that resolves to a regex op from a primitive without calling into the validator, which is the same documented opaque-schema boundary that already makes keyword refs flag-invisible. Register the vector form.
- A fixed-width prefix before a regex element (element 0 of [:cat :int [:* :int] X]) could keep position precision. It was not built: the bead asks for a conservative fallback, and the whole-node decision suffices.
- No spec edit. spec/010-Schemas.md does not describe :cat / :catn position precision; the fallback is recorded in walker.cljc's docstrings.
- The printer-seam test-order isolation limit in rf2-fzbj.25's review-coverage section is an observation, not a finding, and was left alone.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9750 (commit 5766e14472); the full verdict is appended to this bead's notes.

Finding 1 (rf2-gwye.11, P1 privacy): walker.cljc keeps :tuple / :cat / :catn position precision only for a :tuple or for a fixed-width, unspliced :cat / :catn. Any other sequence descends index-free, aligns to the whole-node decision and fail-closes its :path tail.

Finding 2 (rf2-gwye.14): compute-edn-print binds *print-length* and *print-level* to nil.

Shared CLJ/CLJS regression tests went RED on the planted pre-fix code (JVM 21 failures, CLJS 18, all in the new tests) and GREEN on the fix (jvm-schemas 394/19352, CLJS 11993/59617). Non-sensitive controls pass on both trees. jvm-security, test:security, test:schemas-bundle and all 46 check_*.py checkers exit 0.

Recorded, not built: keyword registry refs inside a :cat stay single-value (documented opaque-schema boundary); no fixed-width-prefix precision; no spec edit; hydrate.cljc needed no change.

title: surface-review(ssr-node): contain malformed targets, settle boot exits, preserve streamed Unicode
description:
Recommendation: contain malformed HTTP targets at the request boundary first, then make every worker boot exit settle startup and preserve Unicode across streamed string boundaries. This review confirms three defects: one P1 process-wide availability failure and two P2 lifecycle/byte-integrity failures. Keep this single review task OPEN until the three focused repairs and their regression witnesses land. Scope and revision Owned slice: implementation/ssr-node/**, all 38 tracked paths. Runtime sources inspected: src/http.cjs, src/service.cjs, src/protocol.cjs, src/isolate.cjs, src/pool.cjs, src/worker.cjs and src/envelope.cjs; also bin/serve.cjs, package.json, README.md, the test runner and relevant protocol, isolation, concurrency, timeout, byte, egress and launcher witnesses/fixtures. Revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Coverage: request field/partition allowlists and UTF-8 input budget; read-once snapshots and worker cloning/freezing; entry/build identity; admission and one-in-flight ownership; render deadlines, terminal refusal counts, hard termination, replacement and close paths; chunk/complete frame construction; buffered versus streaming HTTP framing, body draining, malformed-request handling and response teardown; CLI options/readiness/shutdown; package exports and the existing private distribution posture. The byte and lifecycle counterexamples below used the actual checked-out runtime, not reimplementations of the relevant functions. Exclusions: no production edits, builds, installs, source gates, full package test run, live server/listening socket, browser hydration, React/CLJS bundle build, JVM crossing test or load benchmark. The HTTP probes used an unbound Node Server with a process-local override of listen/address, fed raw HTTP through an in-memory Duplex. Node's HTTP parser, IncomingMessage, ServerResponse and this package's request listener/HTTP encoder executed normally; operating-system TCP behavior was not tested. Real worker threads were used for startup and byte probes, and healthy controls were explicitly closed. Existing test coverage was inspected selectively rather than every assertion being executed. The root coordinator owns tracker checkpoint/push. Finding 1 — P1: malformed HTTP request target escapes the request listener and terminates the sidecar Source: implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:234-241, especially the unguarded new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost') at :236. The later render catch at :209-210 cannot cover this earlier synchronous request callback. Trigger/reproducer: send these bytes to the service (CRLF line endings): GET // HTTP/1.1 Host: localhost Connection: close The equally discriminating target http://[::1 also fails. Node's HTTP parser accepts both request lines and dispatches a request. The WHATWG URL constructor then throws TypeError: Invalid URL / ERR_INVALID_URL. No catch owns that request-listener exception. Executed evidence: probe-impl-ssr-node-url-1.cjs launched isolated child processes, used the actual serve() request callback and Node HTTP parser over an in-memory Duplex, and captured child exits. GET /health returned HTTP/1.1 200 OK, exit 0; GET /missing returned 404 Not Found, exit 0. GET // and GET http://[::1 each produced no status line and child exit 1, with the stack locating src/http.cjs:236:24. The parent probe asserted all four outcomes and itself exited 0. Evidence: ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-impl-ssr-node-url-1.log and .exit. Expected versus actual: malformed request syntax should receive the existing caller-fault refusal/400 (or an explicitly defined request-local rejection), leaving the service alive. Instead one request aborts the Node process, taking unrelated in-flight renders and all service capacity with it. The default bind is loopback; exploit reachability depends on deployment/network access. A public Internet listener is not assumed. Even on a trusted local interface this is an uncontained bad request rather than a renderer failure. Repair: guard URL construction in the outer HTTP request listener and use the existing MALFORMED_REQUEST refusal response for parse failure. Parse once and pass the parsed URL/stream selector into the render handler if that avoids a second unguarded parse. Keep the error handling request-local and the existing /health, /render and unknown-path behavior. A global uncaughtException handler or process restart loop is not a substitute for containing this specific operation. Acceptance: - A raw HTTP request-target corpus including // and http://[::1 receives a bounded 4xx response or the documented request-local refusal, with no uncaughtException/unhandledRejection and no process exit. - A valid health request and render sent to the SAME running service after each malformed request still succeed. - Keep valid /render?stream=1 framing and /missing 404 behavior; include at least one parser-accepted malformed target so a test does not pass solely because Node rejected the request before this listener ran. Finding 2 — P2: a worker exiting during boot cancels its only deadline without settling startup Source: implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs:132-144 arms bootTimer; :202-227 clears it in worker.on('exit') and only calls _failPendingRender. There is no pending render during boot and no rejection of the start() promise on this path. Consequences compose through src/pool.cjs:92-113 (Promise.allSettled startup) and :116-120 (_startIsolate awaiting start()). Trigger/reproducer: load a valid module whose boot hook terminates its thread, for example: module.exports = { protocol: 1, buildId: 'review-boot-exit', entries: { 'app/root': { stateAllowlist: [], runtimeAllowlist: [] } }, boot() { process.exit(0); }, render(_request, emit) { emit('

unreachable

'); } }; Then call createService({modulePath: absoluteFixturePath, isolates: 1, bootTimeoutMs: 100}). This is a concrete module startup failure that the bounded service must report; it is not a request to make process.exit successful. Actual: both Isolate.start() and public createService() remain pending after 350 ms, beyond the configured 100 ms budget. The direct isolate probe shows dead=true and worker.threadId=-1, proving the thread actually exited; even an explicit isolate.close() leaves its startup promise pending. The exit event clears bootTimer, marks the isolate dead, and has nothing to reject because pendingRender is null. No future timer or worker event can finish startup. Expected: worker exit before readiness rejects startup promptly as a boot failure. Successful siblings of a failed pool start must be closed, and replacement boot failure must reach the existing rejection/diagnostic path. Static consequence, not separately executed: Promise.allSettled prevents Pool.start from reaching its sibling cleanup while one start is forever pending; a replacement with this failure also leaves startingReplacements unresolved, which Pool.close awaits. Impact: startup/readiness can remain unresolved indefinitely despite bootTimeoutMs. A module exiting during initialization can hang an embedding host, hold healthy sibling workers, and prevent completion of replacement shutdown. A pending promise alone need not keep an otherwise empty Node process alive, so the precise claim is unresolved startup, not that every single-isolate command must visibly stay running forever. Repair: settle the startup promise from the worker exit path when readiness has not completed, using a boot refusal with service-owned context (and exit code if useful). Preserve the existing render-phase isolate-lost rejection and afterChunks behavior; let existing pool cleanup/replacement failure handling observe the rejection. Use a small explicit boot phase/settlement guard if needed rather than adding another timeout that masks the missing event transition. Acceptance: - process.exit(0) and nonzero exit during module evaluation or boot reject createService within its boot bound; healthy startup remains successful. - A multi-isolate start with one successful sibling and one early exit rejects and leaves no live worker behind. - An early-exiting replacement settles its tracked start, produces the existing operator diagnostic/caller refusal semantics, and service.close completes. - Existing render-time exit, timeout, replacement and afterChunks tests retain their behavior. Validation: Node v24.13.0, actual Isolate/start and public createService, no socket. ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-impl-ssr-node-boot-1.log and .exit, exit 0. Controls booted/rendered/closed the existing bytes.cjs fixture and confirmed the existing bad-protocol.cjs fixture rejects with :rf.ssr-node/malformed-render-module. The bounded observation confirms the pending state; the source transition explains why it cannot self-settle later. Finding 3 — P2: streaming separately encodes surrogate halves and changes successful body bytes Source: implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:164-177 writes each string chunk independently as UTF-8; :194 ends without retaining any string-encoding state. Buffered mode at :196-206 joins before encoding. The module contract accepts strings, and worker.cjs:155-165 forwards each emitted string; it does not require each chunk to end on a Unicode code-point boundary. Trigger/reproducer: use the existing test/fixtures/chunked.cjs module and send: {protocol: 1, entry: 'app/root', state: {':bytes': JSON.stringify(['

\uD834', '\uDD1E

'])}} The two chunks join to

U+1D11E MUSICAL SYMBOL G CLEF

. Splitting a JavaScript string at a fixed code-unit offset can naturally produce this shape. The public stream protocol permits arbitrary string chunks and promises that streaming and buffered responses carry identical bytes. Actual, through real workers and actual HTTP response encoding: buffered /render returns hex 3c703ef09d849e3c2f703e (the clef); /render?stream=1 returns 3c703eefbfbdefbfbd3c2f703e (two U+FFFD replacement characters). Both are successful responses. Encoding the high and low surrogate in separate res.write calls loses the pairing before the client can see it. A control with chunks ['

', '\u{1D11E}', '

'] preserves the expected bytes, so ordinary multi-chunk forwarding and non-ASCII encoding are working. Expected: chunk boundaries do not change the UTF-8 representation of the concatenated body. This is the specific byte-integrity guarantee of README.md's protocol/streaming discussion, not a new output policy. Existing bytes.cjs includes an astral character but emits the whole body once; the current buffered/streaming comparison consequently misses this boundary case. Impact: a streaming renderer or string-chunk adapter can silently corrupt astral characters and disagree with the buffered path's HTML/digest/hydration input. This probe does not claim the current production React/Hicasso bundle emits such boundaries; it establishes a supported chunking path through the existing generic service and fixture. Repair: carry at most a trailing high surrogate between streaming writes and combine it with the next string before UTF-8 encoding; flush an unmatched final surrogate consistently with buffered Node encoding at completion. Keep frames streamed and keep the state in the HTTP/string-encoding edge. Do not solve this by buffering the whole response or merely changing the test corpus to avoid the boundary. Acceptance: - Run the existing chunked fixture through buffered and streaming HTTP with a surrogate pair split across chunks; response bytes and hashes match. - Include an empty intervening chunk, multiple split pairs, and a final unmatched surrogate, comparing against Buffer.from(parts.join(''), 'utf8'). - Preserve immediate delivery of completed text chunks, no streaming Content-Length, byte-accurate buffered Content-Length, and torn-response destruction when the render fails. Validation: ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-impl-ssr-node-bytes-1.log and .exit, exit 0, Node v24.13.0. Actual Service, Isolate and existing chunked fixture; actual Node HTTP parser/ServerResponse over in-memory Duplex, with chunked transfer framing decoded in the probe. No OS network or browser was used. Known issues/history and duplicate boundaries Searched active and closed ssr-node/isolate/stream titles, plus Invalid URL, bootTimeoutMs and SSR-surrogate descriptions; searched ssr-node memories. Read current closure records and bounded recent histories for rf2-rhyi, rf2-kirm and rf2-2hmg, plus rf2-6r9j.70 and rf2-8arzr.8; read rf2-c38b's current audit closure. No existing owner was found for these three exact failures. rf2-rhyi concerns identifying fields on exits DURING RENDER; its fix is present and does not settle BOOT. rf2-kirm's afterChunks repair is present and must be preserved. rf2-2hmg/rf2-c38b close application exception egress and replacement diagnostic wording, not a replacement that never settles. rf2-6r9j.70 fixes a boot-once witness, not failed boot completion. Private:true/no registry release is the known distribution posture covered by rf2-8arzr.8, not a fresh packaging defect. Related main SSR report rf2-fzbj.10 owns safe-redirect policy and rejected hydration install claims. Finding 1 here is an inbound Node HTTP request parser exception, not that redirect URL-policy finding; this bead does not repeat either SSR finding. Validation limits and unverified risks Three focused probes passed their explicit expected-current-failure assertions; that is reproduction evidence, not a claim the package test suite is green or these defects are repaired. Every probe prints SOURCE_ROOT and has separate ignored evidence files with slice name and attempt number; git check-ignore confirmed all logs/exit files are ignored. No source was changed. title: surface-review(http): retain anonymous frame ownership and bound JVM response-body time
description:
Recommendation: fix frame ownership tracking for anonymous HTTP requests before relying on teardown/restore isolation, and enforce the JVM attempt deadline through response-body completion. Two confirmed defects remain: P1 stale response delivery into a recreated frame, and P2 an ineffective body-download timeout. Keep this bead OPEN for remediation; this review does not propose new public API or broader transport refactoring.

## Scope and baseline

Slice: impl_http. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
Revision: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Exact assigned tracked paths are enumerated at the end. Source stayed unchanged; only unique ignored probe/evidence/body files and this new bead were written. Parent: rf2-fzbj. Review began 2026-09-12 Australia/Sydney and concluded after local midnight on 2026-09-13; the campaign label remains surface-review-2026-09-12.

Coverage: followed managed-handler argument validation and reply addressing, request preparation, JVM/Fetch adapters, response status/decode/accept classification, terminal reply and error handling, captured middleware chains, retry handoffs, both cancellation indexes, frame/actor ownership and supersession. Inspected encoding and response metadata paths, optional-artifact deps.edn, machine-wrapper reply construction, and relevant existing test witnesses. Executed focused JVM probes described below against the actual checked-out namespaces, including a real router/frame-lifecycle integration; did not run a broad gate or claim whole-suite coverage.

Exclusions/limits: no CLJS compile/browser execution, production build, dependency install, external network, release packaging/deployment test, full JSON/privacy audit, full actor-concurrency census, or exhaustive execution of every assigned test. Ancillary sources and tests not needed by the focused paths were inventoried, not claimed fully executed. Process-local JVM probes used already-cached HTTP test dependencies: Clojure 1.12.4, Cheshire 5.13.0, JDK Eclipse Adoptium 21.0.10 (installed distribution 21.0.10.7). Source resource URLs printed file:/C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/http/src/... to establish the checkout actually loaded. The root explicitly authorized a bounded loopback ephemeral-port HTTP probe; its server, exchange and futures were closed in finally.

## F1 — P1: anonymous managed requests survive teardown and mutate a successor frame

Sources:
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:143-209, especially 193-202: record-in-flight! stores a handle only when request-id or actor-id is truthy. Its own docstring acknowledges that when both are nil the handle is unindexed.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:890-921, especially 909-910: abort-frame-handles! enumerates only in-flight and actor-in-flight. Both frame destroy (944 onward) and epoch restore (924 onward) delegate to this walk.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:257-271, 433-441: request-id remains optional and is passed unchanged to the attempt; ordinary event-originated requests have no owning actor.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1730-1868 and 2094-2099: the real attempt creates the handle and installs its response callback, but an unindexed handle's callback is never marked aborted by either frame boundary.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/encoding.cljc:318-325: completion dispatch targets the carried frame id. Since the orphan was never aborted, the callback reaches this normal dispatch path after that id has been recreated.

Public contract: Spec 014 request-id is optional (spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:150), while Abort on frame destroy (799-807) explicitly covers plain event-originated managed requests and requires cancellation plus no original-target delivery. The restore hook likewise promises to abort every request issued by the frame; stale host work must not write into the restored timeline.

Trigger/reproducer, including the integration controls:
1. Load re-frame.core, re-frame.http.managed, the plain-atom substrate and the normal reset-runtime fixture. Register :review/load to return an :rf.http/managed effect with {:request {:url "http://example.invalid/probe"} :decode :text :reply-to [:review/reply]}; omit request-id and do not spawn an actor. Register :review/reply to return {:db (assoc db :late-response (:value reply))}.
2. Make :review/frame. With-redefs ONLY transport-jvm/jvm-fetch to return a held java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture, dispatch-sync [:review/load] into that frame. All handlers, effect invocation, registry, frame teardown, reply dispatch and event processing remain real.
3. Call rf/destroy-frame! :review/frame, then rf/make-frame with the same id. Confirm its new app-db is {}.
4. Complete the old future with {:ok? true :status 200 :status-text "OK" :headers {} :body-text "old-incarnation"}. Wait for reply observation and a FIFO interop/next-tick barrier so the state read follows handler commit.
5. Observed anonymous case: indexed-before=0; cancelled-after-real-destroy=false; exactly one real-router :ok reply; successor app-db changes {} -> {:late-response "old-incarnation"}.
6. Identical control with :request-id :review/request: indexed-before=1; cancelled-after-real-destroy=true; zero reply delivery during the bounded observation window; successor app-db remains {}.

This is confirmed state corruption, not an inference from a dispatch stub. The final integration uses the actual router and frame incarnation behavior, and observes the committed successor state. Earlier hook-level probes separately show that BOTH abort-in-flight-on-frame-destroyed! and abort-in-flight-for-frame! leave anonymous futures live and allow late :ok dispatch; adding request-id cancels/suppresses under both hooks. The full epoch-restore UI/restore transaction was not executed, so the restore claim is limited to its actual HTTP quiesce hook.

Expected: omitting an optional public correlation id must not detach request ownership from the issuing frame. Destruction/restore cancels all requests owned by that frame, suppresses their old replies, and protects successor/restored state.
Actual: ownership discovery depends on the optional request-id/actor-id indexes. Plain anonymous work is invisible, continues host work/retries, and the real late reply may commit into a recreated frame with the same id.
Impact: ordinary one-off HTTP calls in SSR/request-scoped frames, Story variants, hot reload or multi-frame applications can outlive their frame. Recreating the id allows stale data from an old request to overwrite fresh state. The demonstrated successor mutation requires no concurrency race, invalid input or caller misuse.

Precise repair: retain every live attempt/backoff handle under frame ownership independently of the optional public correlation id (a private frame-to-handles index or an equivalent unified ownership registry). Make frame destruction/restore enumerate that complete set, and remove handles by identity on terminal completion and every retry transition. Preserve nil as the caller's public request-id and the existing actor/request lookup behavior. Do not require callers to invent ids just to obtain lifecycle safety. Ensure retry handoffs keep continuous frame registration, as they already do for identified requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- A deterministic regression using the real managed effect, destroy-frame!, same-id recreation, real router and committed app-db reproduces the case above and fails on this baseline. Anonymous old completion must produce no successor handler commit or app effects; identified and sibling-frame controls remain correct.
- Frame destruction and the epoch HTTP quiesce hook cancel anonymous plain work in both active-transport and sleeping-backoff phases, suppress late replies and leave no retained frame handles.
- Successful and failed anonymous requests clean their new ownership entries promptly; several simultaneous anonymous requests in one frame remain distinct; actor-owned/id-bearing requests are still aborted once by identity.
- Exercise equivalent shared lifecycle behavior in CLJS, especially external abort listener detachment and backoff suppression. The present review executed JVM only.

## F2 — P2: JVM timeout expires at headers, leaving body downloads unbounded

Sources:
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:167-168 only stamps HttpRequest.Builder.timeout; 283-310 uses sendAsync with BodyHandlers.ofByteArray and awaits its full-body future without any independent whole-attempt timer.
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:2032-2101 records elapsed time and classifies exceptional completion, but does not enforce a deadline around that body-reading future.
- For comparison, implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_cljs.cljc:229-283 races fetch PLUS read-body against a timer, so the browser path covers body consumption.

Public contract: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:146 and 305-316 calls timeout-ms a per-attempt wall-clock timeout (default 30000; nil/0 opt out). Line 307 specifically says the default protects against an upstream that never completes the response body and would otherwise pin CompletableFuture/Fetch work indefinitely. This finding is within one network attempt; it does not ask for an overall retry budget or for timing arbitrary user body-preparation code.

Concrete real-transport probe on JDK 21.0.10:
1. Start a loopback HttpServer on an ephemeral port. Its handler sends status 200 and Content-Length: 2, writes and flushes byte A, signals a latch, then holds byte B behind a release latch with a finite probe backstop.
2. Call the production jvm-fetch with {:method :get :url <loopback-url> :decode :text :timeout-ms 500}.
3. After server entry, get the returned future with a 1500 ms observation limit. Observed still-pending-after-ms=1504: no HttpTimeoutException and no HTTP failure despite exceeding the budget threefold.
4. Release byte B. The same future then successfully returns {:ok? true :status 200 :headers {"content-length" "2" ...} :body-text "AB"}.
5. Control: same server delayed BEFORE response headers, same 500 ms request timeout. Production jvm-fetch completes exceptionally with java.net.http.HttpTimeoutException (observed elapsed 958 ms including initial setup/scheduling).

Expected: once the positive per-attempt deadline elapses before body consumption finishes, cancel the host work and settle exactly once with :rf.http/timeout (elapsed-ms and limit-ms), allowing configured timeout retries.
Actual: the JDK request timer does not bound the stalled response-body phase in this runtime. A server can send headers promptly and then hold the request indefinitely, or deliver success after the stated deadline. The 1500 ms bound is the probe's own future.get timeout, not a framework timeout.
Impact: the advertised default cannot protect JVM/SSR callers from stalled or trickling response bodies. Futures, buffers, handles and request concurrency remain occupied; timeout-based retry never begins while the body remains stalled. This is independent of F1 and affects requests with a valid request-id too.

Precise repair: enforce an attempt-local deadline through completion of the actual sendAsync/body-consumption future, cancel that future when it expires, and classify through the existing :rf.http/timeout path. Detach/cancel the timer on success, failure and manual/lifecycle abort. Preserve explicit nil/0 opt-out and per-retry rearming. Avoid merely using a future timeout method that changes the result while leaving the host exchange running; cancellation must reach the JDK request. Preserve user/actor/frame abort precedence and exactly-one-terminal-reply behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Real JVM adapter regression sends headers and an initial body byte promptly, then stalls longer than a small positive timeout. It must return the canonical timeout at the deadline and cancel the host exchange before the body is released; baseline must fail.
- A delayed-before-headers control still times out; a complete response inside the budget succeeds; nil/0 keep the documented opt-out.
- A late body completion after timeout cannot dispatch success or a duplicate reply; configured timeout retries run once per budgeted attempt; manual/frame abort racing the timer retains its existing precedence.
- Verify both text and binary response readers are covered by the same whole-attempt timer. Do not extend the task into a total retry-sequence timeout or body-thunk interruption.

## Validation and history

- Final authoritative evidence: ai/surface-review-20260912/impl_http-probe-1.clj/.log/.exit (exit 0; hook-level anonymous controls and real adapter timeout controls); impl_http-probe-3.clj/.log/.exit (exit 0; real-router, real-destroy, recreated-frame committed-state witness with identified control). Both are focused runtime probes, not repository gate runs. Their decisive results and recipe are included above so this bead does not rely on ignored artifacts surviving.
- Harness attempt 2 is superseded: it observed real handler delivery but read app-db before commit and left the JVM's process-local router executor alive. Its exact probe process was identified and terminated, recorded exit -1. Attempt 3 adds the FIFO commit barrier and exits the disposable JVM after completion; attempt 2 is NOT cited as a green or as proof of committed state.
- Existing http_frame_destroy_abort_test.clj:163-223 exercises the real frame-destroy recipe but supplies :request-id :destroy/req, so it cannot expose F1. Other seeded frame-sweep controls similarly populate an index. Existing http_transport_security_test.clj:94-192 verifies the HttpRequest timeout attribute; http_jvm_binary_decode_test.clj:184 onward stalls before headers, so neither can distinguish F2.
- Read current all-status HTTP/cancellation/anonymous/timeout-related bead search results and rf2-o8ek history. Closed rf2-o8ek fixes frame scoping/two-index publication; rf2-wjfm fixes frame threading for actor destroy; rf2-ni74 fixes the actor-destroy midpoint. They concern requests that enter an index and do not cover F1. Closed rf2-rsv2n covers abort during body preparation/issuance; its close reason and tests were read and that repaired issue was not re-filed. Closed rf2-lddbk covers successful response metadata and rf2-v3f6 covers captured middleware chains, both distinct.
- Historical source references rf2-j538f7.8 (frame destruction) and rf2-u5kmf8 (epoch quiesce) have no current record under bd show; their shipped source/tests were inspected rather than claiming to read nonexistent tracker records. No current matching duplicate for these two findings was found by the focused searches; this was not an exhaustive reconstruction of deleted historical tracker data.
- Rejected candidate: cancelling jvm-fetch's thenApply result is NOT automatically a cancellation bug. Inspection of the installed JDK's MinimalFuture bytecode shows newIncompleteFuture retains its cancelable and cancel invokes it; a fake plain CompletableFuture would have falsely accused this path. No finding is filed for that candidate.
- No other confirmed defect is asserted from this bounded review. Unexecuted CLJS races, other JVM versions and additional MIME edge cases are validation limits, not speculative findings.

notes:
=== VERDICT (worker http-a, 2026-09-13): BOTH findings FIXED in PR #9745 (commit c0e893b339 on worker/http-a, branched at 031ff49a38). ===
Both findings were re-verified at that base before fixing, and both reproduced as described.

F1 — anonymous frame ownership (per-finding twin rf2-gwye.12): FIXED.
re-frame.http.registry now holds any managed request carrying neither :request-id nor an owning actor in a third index, anonymous-in-flight (frame-id -> handles):
- record-in-flight! writes it;
- the 2-arg clear-in-flight! removes by identity, so completion, retry handoff and every abort release it;
- clear-all-in-flight! walks it;
- abort-frame-handles! reads and clears the frame's slot in one step. That is the single walk behind both :http/on-frame-destroyed! and :http/abort-in-flight-for-frame!.
:request-id stays optional and nil. There is no public API change, and the id-keyed indexes and their lookups are untouched. Spec 014 §Abort on frame destroy now states the id-less case.

Regression tests: implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_anonymous_frame_ownership_test.clj. Every assertion is behavioural. The file was written BEFORE the fix and run red against the pre-fix source:
- Real router, destroy-frame!, then same-id make-frame. Pre-fix, the successor app-db became {:late-response "old-incarnation"}. Post-fix it stays {}, and the old host future is cancelled.
- Both frame boundaries cancel two simultaneous anonymous requests in frame A, while frame B's identical request still delivers. Pre-fix, A's futures stayed live and replies came from [:frame/a :frame/a :frame/b].
- A request asleep in backoff issues no attempt 2 after destroy. Pre-fix: 3 fetches.
- A completed success and a completed failure leave nothing for the sweep: exactly one stale-suppressed trace, for the one live request. This guards the new index against leaking.
CLJS: http_cljs_test.cljs, cljs-destroy-frame-cancels-anonymous-backoff-and-suppresses-reply. Red with the pre-fix registry planted (fetch-count 4 where 1 is required); green on the fix.

F2 — JVM whole-attempt timeout (per-finding twin rf2-gwye.13): FIXED.
jvm-fetch arms CompletableFuture.orTimeout(:timeout-ms) on the future it returns. On TimeoutException it cancels the upstream sendAsync future, which is what closes the JDK exchange. classify-jvm-error maps java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException to :rf.http/timeout.
- nil and 0 still arm nothing.
- Each retry calls jvm-fetch afresh, so it re-arms its own budget.
- The JDK withdraws the deadline on any other completion, including a lifecycle abort's cancel.
Measured before choosing this shape: an orTimeout on the result alone completed at the deadline, but the loopback server still streamed the whole 8 MB body. Adding the upstream cancel made the server's next write fail at once.

Regression test: implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_jvm_body_timeout_test.clj. A loopback HttpServer sends headers and one byte, then withholds an 8 MB body behind a latch. A managed request with :timeout-ms 200 and one timeout retry must:
- reply :rf.http/timeout at attempt 2, with :limit-ms 200, while the body is still withheld;
- have both exchanges cancelled server-side (the write fails once the latch is released);
- produce no late reply.
Pre-fix: no reply at all within 5 s. Alongside it sits an opt-out guard: :timeout-ms 0 and nil stay pending past 150 ms, then succeed on release.

Gates:
- jvm-http (clojure -M:test in implementation/http): exit 0, 505 tests, 4015 assertions.
- CLJS node-test: compile exit 0 and run exit 0, 11991 tests, 59583 assertions.
- check_doc_slugs.py: exit 0.
- api-manifest --check: exit 0.
- require-alias-dialect: exit 0.
- clj-kondo and splint: exit 0.

SKIPPED review suggestions, each deliberately (stance: fix + regression, nothing else):
- "Dual-index actor/id handles abort only once by identity": the identity dedupe in abort-frame-handles! is unchanged, and existing tests already pin it.
- "Exercise external abort listener detachment in CLJS": detachment lives in dispatch-aborted!, the single choke every abort reason goes through, :frame-destroyed included. This fix only makes the abort-fn reachable, and the rf2-3fc89f.9 tests pin the detach.
- "Execute the full epoch-restore transaction": the regression drives the actual HTTP quiesce hook, abort-in-flight-for-frame!, which is all the restore path calls in this artefact.
- "Manual/frame abort racing the timer": precedence is decided by the unchanged :aborted?/:finalised? cells. The new deadline completes through the same whenComplete -> maybe-retry! route the JDK's own HttpTimeoutException already took, so there is no new race surface to pin.
- "Verify text and binary readers separately": both read the same ofByteArray future the deadline wraps. Only :text was executed.
- "Delayed-before-headers control": the existing jvm-real-timeout-populates-elapsed-ms test covers it and is green in the gate.
No other rf2-fzbj.N or rf2-gwye.N finding was met in the files touched.
close_reason: Both findings fixed in PR #9745 (commit c0e893b339). F1 (twin rf2-gwye.12): re-frame.http.registry indexes any request that has neither a :request-id nor an owning actor under its issuing frame (anonymous-in-flight). It is removed by identity on completion, retry and abort, and read-and-cleared by the one sweep behind both frame destroy and the epoch-restore quiesce. The regressions cover the real router plus a same-id recreate (pre-fix, the successor app-db gained {:late-response "old-incarnation"}), both boundaries, the backoff phase, completion cleanup, and a CLJS backoff case. F2 (twin rf2-gwye.13): jvm-fetch arms orTimeout over the whole attempt and cancels the upstream sendAsync future on expiry; TimeoutException classifies as :rf.http/timeout. The regression is a loopback server that stalls mid-body; it proves the timeout lands at the deadline, the retry re-arms, and the exchange is cancelled server-side. Gates: jvm-http 505 tests and CLJS node-test 11991 tests, both exit 0, and both red controls were shown. Six review suggestions were deliberately skipped, with a one-line reason each, in the notes. No other fzbj/gwye finding was met.

title: bug(skill-xray): manual init!/mount bypasses the only goog.DEBUG gate despite elision guidance
description:
Surface: skills/re-frame2-xray/** (manual/programmatic launch guidance), checked independently against the current Xray facade, preload, mount path, framework initialization, elision probe, tests/config, and git history.

Problem

The skill makes a universal production-safety promise that is false for the manual path it explicitly teaches. SKILL.md:29-32 says Xray is "elided entirely from production builds." references/launch-programmatic.md:14-25 and 38-45 then tells a host app to require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, call rf/init!, call xray/init! without a guard, and invoke a mount verb. references/launch-lifecycle.md:101-128 says goog.DEBUG=false gates every dev-only branch, including Xray's, and presents npm run test:elision as proof that Xray cannot reach production.

Exact implementation evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:92-114 contains the only outer interop/debug-enabled? gate. It protects preload boot only.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:159-180 makes the documented manual init! path unconditionally register Xray handlers, trace and epoch collectors, browser globals, and the keybinding before applying options. It does not traverse preload or check goog.DEBUG.
- core.cljs:71-102 directly aliases open!, open-overlay!, toggle!, and popout! to mount operations without a production gate.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:31-36 says mount needs no elision logic because "The preload's gate means mount never reaches production builds." That premise does not hold for the public manual facade.
- mount.cljs:886-921 mounts when a substrate adapter exists. A normal production SPA has that adapter after implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc rf/init!; adapter presence is not a production discriminator.
- implementation/package.json:38 invokes the framework elision probe. implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs and implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs root/check re-frame framework trace/schema/registrar surfaces, not the Xray namespace, manual Xray sequence, browser globals, keybinding, handlers, DOM root, or Xray bundle sentinels. The cited gate therefore cannot establish the skill's Xray claim.
- Git history is consistent with this split: dbb3c35522 intentionally separated the explicit core facade from preload side effects and described production exclusion as a host/devtools-block responsibility. The later skill language generalized the preload guarantee to the manual path.

Causal reproduction

In an ordinary app namespace, follow the documented sequence: require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, run rf/init!, xray/init!, then xray/open!, and compile an advanced production build with goog.DEBUG=false. The preload gate is irrelevant because this path never enters preload. xray/init! still installs tooling surfaces; the normal production re-frame adapter lets xray/open! proceed to mount. This is a static, direct call path, not an edge-case inference.

Impact and priority

A programmer or AI following the canonical low-friction example can ship state-inspection browser globals/UI, :rf.xray/* handlers, listeners/collectors, and retained Xray code while the skill explicitly assures them production inclusion is impossible. That is a production correctness, exposure, bundle, and performance defect at the API's trust boundary, so P1 is warranted pre-alpha.

Bounded recommendation

Make the canonical manual facade safe by construction: apply one coherent debug/production gate to manual foundation initialization and externally visible mount entry points, not only to preload. Add a real optimized Xray elision probe/control rooted through the exact documented manual sequence. This preserves the elegant one-model promise and avoids making every host remember bespoke build placement.

If maintainers intentionally support production use through the manual facade, the immediate fallback is documentation-only but must be explicit: scope the elision guarantee to preload, require manual consumers to exclude or host-guard the facade, and remove the claim that the framework-only test:elision proves Xray absence.

Non-goals

Do not add a new runtime warning banner, disable setting, compatibility layer, or launch mode. Do not redesign panels, mount lifecycle, Pair, or the framework's general elision system.

Acceptance and tests

1. An optimized goog.DEBUG=false probe rooted through rf/init! + xray/init! + xray/open! cannot register :rf.xray/* handlers, install Xray browser globals or its key listener/collectors, or create #rf-xray-root. A goog.DEBUG=true control exercises those effects so the check cannot pass vacuously.
2. The optimized-bundle gate checks distinctive Xray sentinels or an equivalent reachability/size assertion, with a positive control, rather than reusing only the framework elision probe.
3. Existing preload development launch and manual development launch remain functional, including init/mount tests.
4. SKILL.md, launch-programmatic.md, and launch-lifecycle.md all state the same actual boundary and do not cite a non-Xray probe as proof.
5. Add a skill answer-quality eval asking whether manual init! from a normal app namespace is production-safe; the answer must identify the actual gate and required host responsibility, if any.

Duplicate distinction

Targeted searches of .beads/issues.jsonl and git history found no exact issue. rf2-fguoj and rf2-2oug concern an unshipped production warning banner, not the documented manual facade bypassing the only gate. Open rf2-ar67 enrolls 16 core facade exports in the API manifest/classifier; it does not address production gating or elision. rf2-11hn covers framework elision, whose probe is precisely what fails to cover this Xray path.

Uncertainty

No optimized compile or runtime was executed because this review was constrained to static/read-only analysis. The runtime side-effect path is unambiguous from the calls above; the exact number of retained production bytes is not established and is intentionally delegated to the proposed optimized probe.
close_reason:

title: bug(skill-implementor): minimum ports can skip v1-required flows and report false-green conformance
description:
## Scope

Correct the skills/re-frame2-implementor/** workflow so a minimum port cannot treat Spec 013 Flows as an optional, known-skipped capability and then call itself v1-complete. Reconcile the skill with the current pinned owners (spec/013-Flows.md, spec/Implementor-Checklist.md, and spec/conformance/README.md) and update the focused implementor-order guard that currently certifies the stale three-family model.

Keep the existing two-phase/no-interview ergonomics, host scope, conformance subset mechanism, and narrow EP loop. This is one downstream contract-drift repair, not a redesign of flows or the conformance system.

## Correctness finding

The published skill explicitly defaults flows to no, places EP 013 in the optional table, and defines required completion around only :core/*, :identity/*, and :data-classification/*. The current normative corpus says the opposite: Spec 013 is v1-required, the Implementor Checklist puts Flows in the non-gated Required table, and the conformance README says :flow/* is not optional.

That creates a clean false-green path. On a minimum-port request, the skill records flows as an intentional known skip. Its harness therefore does not trigger the unknown-capability floor; it deliberately excludes the flow fixtures, obtains claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable over the smaller claim, and the Done checklist accepts the result. The port is reported as re-frame2 v1-complete while omitting a runtime surface the contract says every port ships.

## Evidence

- spec/013-Flows.md:3-7 opens with Status: Drafting. v1-required, defines the minimum flow claim, and deliberately restrains flows to a narrow convenience rather than making them optional.
- spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:37 lists Flows under Required (not gated; every implementation ships these). Lines 122-124 say :flow/* cannot be declined; line 138 repeats that Flows is v1-required; line 562 marks :flow/* as nothing — always run.
- spec/conformance/README.md:287 says :flow/* is Not optional because Spec 013 is v1-required.
- The live corpus has 11 fixture files carrying :flow/*, including recomputation, topology, dirty-checking, lifecycle/toggle, frame scope/teardown, hot reload, and error/trace behaviour.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md:68 calls flows one of three extra optional, skill-local scope decisions and says the minimum-port default is no.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:49-61 declares only three v1-required families and maps :flow/* to that optional skill-local decision.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:74 puts EP 013 in the optional table behind flows claimed; line 81 says the checklist stops at Q7 and calls flows, managed HTTP, and resources three skill-local choices. The current checklist instead has Q1-Q9: Q8 is Managed HTTP and Q9 is Resources; Flows is Required and intentionally has no Q-number.
- The first completion gate at skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:40, skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:76, and references/cardinal-rules.md:21 runs only :core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json id 20 currently grades an answer that defaults flows to no, so the existing behavioural expectation reinforces the defect.
- scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py:50-63,184-194,335-363,422-448 hard-codes exactly three required roots, cross-checks that stale set against the skill rather than the normative spec, and reports green when every skill surface repeats the same omission.

## Failure scenario

1. Ask the skill: Build me a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript.
2. Following phase-1-decisions.md, record flows in known-skipped with the other optional capabilities and default it to no.
3. Implement the listed foundation sequence 001 -> 002 -> 006 -> views -> 009 -> 015.
4. Run the skill's gate 1 over :core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*; run gate 2 over the claimed set. The :flow/* fixtures are intentionally out of claim, not unknown, so both gates can be green.
5. Satisfy the current Done checklist and report claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable, despite having no reg-flow, lifecycle effects, flow transform in the drain, or flow conformance.

The invariant is simple: a minimum port may keep the flow API deliberately small, as Spec 013's restraint says, but it may not opt out of the Spec 013 minimum claim or omit :flow/* from its required conformance accounting.

## History / cause

Commit c261b45590 fixed the then-real phantom-Q problem by moving flows, managed HTTP, and resources to three skill-local optional choices because the checklist stopped at Q7. Commit 1b0b87a404 subsequently changed the authoritative checklist: it added Managed HTTP as Q8 and Resources as Q9, and explicitly made Flows a non-gated v1-required row because putting Spec 013 behind yes/no would let a port opt out of required behaviour. Later checklist correction 6fff78e7fc preserved that Flows ruling while sharpening cross-tagged derivation prose. No later implementor-skill commit consumed the new contract, so the formerly correct fallback became stale.

## Recommended minimal fix

1. Remove Flows from the profile's optional/default-no decisions and state it as a fixed required obligation linked to Spec 013.
2. Put EP 013 on the required implementation path after its declared dependencies and before the first completion claim. Preserve the one-EP loop; do not add a special workflow.
3. Always include :flow/* in the minimum claim and in the required gate alongside the existing required roots. Keep fixture subset semantics for genuinely cross-tagged cases.
4. Reconcile optional numbering with the current checklist: Managed HTTP is Q8, Resources is Q9, and Flows has no Q because it is Required.
5. Update the existing eval id 20 so the no-interview default still sets every genuinely optional capability to no but does not opt out of flows.
6. Update scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py and its self-tests so omitting :flow/* from any required-gate statement is red. Derive/cross-check the required roots against the authoritative checklist/conformance owner rather than merely proving that a stale skill agrees with itself.

This is a small documentation-and-guard correction. It requires no new runtime implementation, fixture, generated manifest, interview step, or compatibility path.

## Duplicate distinction

Targeted all-status title/body searches for implementor + flows/013, required/optional flows, required-family gates, and the exact three-family completion phrase found no open bead owning this false-green.

- rf2-ozocz is closed. It correctly removed phantom Q8-Q10 references when the checklist had only Q1-Q7. This issue is the later downstream drift created when the authoritative checklist changed; it reverses only the now-stale Flows part and adopts the real Q8/Q9.
- rf2-yyr6c is closed. Its landed checklist work is the source of truth this skill failed to consume; its final correction concerned cross-tagged :derivation/* fixtures, not the implementor skill's ability to skip Spec 013.
- rf2-3758j is closed and owns the distinct EP-006 live sub-cache observability witness. It does not cover flow capability selection or the omitted :flow/* gate.
- rf2-nuy8x is closed and owns the broader workflow reduction. This is a bounded correctness residual after that reduction, not a request to reopen its rejected eval-platform or ceremony work.

## Uncertainty

The required status and missing family are unambiguous. The precise presentation of EP 013 in the dependency list should be derived from its pinned owners during implementation; acceptance requires that all its prerequisites precede it and that no completion gate precede it, not a new global taxonomy or an invented ordering rule.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the existing eval-20 prompt, Build me a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript, the produced port profile cannot put Flows or any :flow/* capability in known-skipped. It defaults only genuinely optional capabilities to no and still begins work in the same run with no interview.
2. Every shipped skill surface classifies Spec 013 consistently with spec/013-Flows.md and the Implementor Checklist: Flows is a fixed v1-required obligation, not a profile scope choice. Managed HTTP is Q8 and Resources is Q9; no prose says the current checklist stops at Q7.
3. The Phase-2 path includes the minimum Spec 013 slice after its real dependencies and before any foundation/v1 completion claim. It still uses the existing six-step EP loop and does not add a flow-specific process.
4. Required conformance accounting includes :flow/* alongside :core/*, :identity/*, and :data-classification/*. A port with no flow implementation cannot achieve the skill's required passed / claimed-applicable result or satisfy Done merely by marking flows out of claim.
5. The existing eval id 20's expected output/expectations no longer asks the agent to default flows to no; its no-interview and same-run guarantees remain intact.
6. scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py is updated with focused self-tests: removing :flow/* from a required-gate statement makes the checker exit nonzero, restoring it returns green, and the owner cross-check cannot pass solely because the stale skill and checker agree with each other.
7. Implementor order/partition checker self-tests and CI modes, skill packaging checks, and skill-link checks remain green. The PR reports exact commands and exit codes.
8. No framework API semantics, Spec 013 behaviour, conformance fixture content, host scope, optional-capability policy beyond this stale mapping, generated sync layer, new eval platform, or backward-compatibility shim is introduced.
notes: Surface review performed independently at 4c44c86f206599299f8d0734de717ea33b4c5e2c. Read the full published skill, all four operational references, package/plugin metadata, evals, internal design/inputs/authoring prompt, current Spec 013, Implementor Checklist, conformance README/fixtures, focused guard source, and relevant git history. No repository files were edited.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9229 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9229). Both halves established and repaired. SKIP HALF: phase-1-decisions listed flows among three skill-local optional scope decisions defaulting to no, and phase-2-impl-order carried EP 013 in the optional table behind 'flows claimed' - both resting on the checklist numbering only Q1-Q7, which it no longer does. FALSE-REPORT HALF: conformance.md declared three v1-required families, so the flow fixtures were intentionally out-of-claim rather than unknown, which is exactly the case the harness unknown-capability floor is designed NOT to fail; gate 1 ran three families and gate 2 scored claimed-applicable/claimed-applicable over the smaller claim. Neither half fixes the other: repairing only the skip leaves the accounting certifying a flowless port; repairing only the accounting leaves the document self-contradictory. Every premise verified at source (013-Flows.md:3 v1-required; Implementor-Checklist:37 Required row, :120 always-run families naming :flow/*, :100/:108 Q8/Q9, :558 family table; conformance/README:287 Not optional; 11 fixture files, 20 distinct :flow/* tags). Fix: four v1-required families; EP 013 in the foundation after its real dependencies (001->002->006->views->009->015->013) before any completion claim, on the existing six-step loop; a sixth harness floor refusing a known-skipped entry that names a v1-required capability, which is what makes the reduced path safe by construction; Q1-Q9 reconciled with the bug's own inference named and refused (a missing Q-number is not evidence of optionality - Flows lacks one for the opposite reason); Spec 013 restraint reframed as a budget for how much flow API to build, never whether. eval 20 keeps its no-interview/same-run guarantees and no longer defaults flows to no. Guard updated per criterion 6: requires 013 with 015 in any foundation sequence and :flow/* in any gate-1 statement, and its cross-check is now two-sided - roots derived from Implementor-Checklist Part 3 always-run rows, since the one-sided check was circular (skill and guard agreed on three families throughout). Proven live, not assumed: removing :flow/* from a gate-1 statement gives exit 1; making skill and guard agree on the stale three-family set gives exit 2 citing the spec; check_doc_slugs proven with a planted anchor+target (exit 1), all restores cmp byte-identical. 12 gates run, all exit 0. Scope beyond the item: docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md (the published summary) repeated the defect verbatim and is fixed under criterion 2 'every shipped skill surface'; two residual copies in the skill's own re-authoring notes (spec/inputs.md, spec/authoring-prompt.md) also corrected - that is the mechanism by which the next authoring pass would have re-encoded the drift. NOT fixed, left for its own bead: the skill maps :derivation/* to Q6 while the checklist family table says gated-by-nothing but cross-tagged to Q1 in practice - real but separate, outside criterion 8's boundary.

title: hic: §13's two canonical tables are written over a native tier that no longer ships — reconcile or re-state the bullets
description:
Filed by the rf2-hic-064 §13 definition-of-done audit (2026-09-04, main@aa0ee76ae4). Measured at source, not inherited.

THE ARTEFACT. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc is 82 lines and defines exactly TWO public names — use-frame and use-sub. Its own ns docstring states the end state: 'The two React hooks that join a React island to the Hicasso frame it is mounted in ... and nothing else. An island is a UIx defui or a raw React function component, mounted through h/defhost or [:>].' That is rf2-6c12m.3's ruling (option A) executed. n/$, n/props, n/defcomponent, n/memo and n/lazy do not exist.

THE DOCUMENTS §13 NAMES. Two §13 bullets cite a canonical table by link, and both tables are still written over the retired grammar:
  * bullet 7 cites lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md#public-surface-ssrhydration-matrix — 4 lines still carry the retired names, including the two matrix ROWS 'Intrinsic n/$ form' and 'n/defcomponent, component-headed n/$, memo/lazy/ref helpers'.
  * bullet 11 cites lanes/hot-path-architecture.md#canonical-native-tier-acceptance-checklist and says 'Every row ... passes; no partial parity result substitutes for that checklist' — 8 lines still carry them, including the Native-form grammar row ('the provisional n/$ grammar handles omitted and literal props, explicit n/props dynamic maps/objects ...') and the Component ABI row ('One raw-JavaScript props/children ABI survives n/defcomponent, memo, lazy loading, ref forwarding').
specification.md itself carries 8 such lines, at :132-134 (the §4 facade table rows for n/$, n/props and n/defcomponent), :139, :180, :203, :209 and :353.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A TIDY-UP. §13 bullets 7 and 11 cannot be scored as written: their subjects do not exist. A reader of the definition of done is told to check a checklist whose first two rows are about a grammar the package does not have, and told that no partial result substitutes for it. Bullet 6's 'same-root native islands' is in the same position. The rf2-6c12m campaign was explicitly authorised to shrink the runtime; nothing in it was asked to restate the definition of done, and no bead carries that.

WHERE THE TEACHING CORPUS ALREADY IS. docs/core/hicasso/ carries ZERO occurrences of the retired names — the guide was swept. dispositions.md carries zero as well. So the drift is confined to the specification and its two lane tables, which is the small end of the repair and the load-bearing end of the harm.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not a request to re-adjudicate any verdict. Checkpoint 3's Phase 3 verdict stands as the record of what was measured on 2026-08-14; this is about the tables the CURRENT definition of done points a reader at.
acceptance_criteria: lanes/hot-path-architecture.md's canonical native-tier acceptance checklist and lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md's public-surface SSR/hydration matrix each state, at the top and in their affected rows, which rows describe a surface retired by rf2-6c12m.3 and what is owed of the two-hook tier that replaced it; specification.md §4's facade table no longer publishes n/$, n/props or n/defcomponent as shipped names without saying they are retired; and §13 bullets 6, 7 and 11 are either restated over the surviving surface or annotated with what they now mean. No verdict is re-scored by this bead and no threshold moves.
notes:
