title: Incomplete live-reader counts: ratom owner holdings collide across frames for the same query
description:
Audit of PR #9904 (9e2c4c1779d490496e9c7e09e492ccd1b8f82122). claim-render-owned-ref! keys the owning reaction's rfSubRefs map by k alone, while cache-key is the query vector (subs.cljc:584-588). Subscription caches are per frame, and subscribe accepts an explicit {:frame target}. One owning Reagent/reagent-slim render reaction can therefore read the same query in two frames, whose two cached reactions are different objects but whose k is identical.

Concrete supported sequence: in one render read @(rf/subscribe [:n] {:frame :a}) followed by @(rf/subscribe [:n] {:frame :b}). The second claim overwrites the first claim's map entry. On each subsequent render, A sees B's reaction and treats its existing reference as new, then B sees A's reaction and does the same. Both ref-counts grow from 1 to 2 to 3 with rerenders, and another on-dispose callback is registered for each. The audited promise that ref-count counts live readers rather than renders is therefore incomplete for multiple-frame reads. This is established from the exact source branch; no new browser/runtime reproduction is claimed. Current origin/main retains the same keying.

Smallest correction: key the per-owner holding by frame identity plus cache key (or another slot identity that distinguishes frames), while preserving reaction identity for stale-release safety. Keep the existing bump-then-release mechanism, declared-input and subscribe-once exclusions. No public API, new cache service or lifecycle redesign is needed.

Acceptance: a real owning reaction/component reads the same query from two distinct frames, is forced to rerender, and both live slots stay at one reference for that owner; final disposal releases both once. Include a one-frame control and preserve successor identity guards. Use both ratom adapters where practical through the existing shared path/tests. The existing DOM tests cover same-frame sibling owners, not this one-owner/two-frame case. Open Beads were searched for rfSubRefs and ref-count/owner overlap; no exact open record exists. rf2-ty246 status must remain unchanged.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9976 (fe72e7402b57d1891bb8e89df6473fc4dc114adc; merged 2026-09-17T19:16:00Z). Completeness: Frame-plus-cache-key holdings cover the multi-frame collision and retain reaction identity. New regressions exercise both ratom adapters, repeated renders, duplicate reads, distinct queries and disposal. Correctness: The tuple matches the actual per-frame cache slot; canonical frame-id is already passed at the claim site. Duplicate bump release and stale-reaction guard remain unchanged. Full code and regression diff reviewed; no local CLJS execution claimed. Implementation quality: Small internal key correction with no API or lifecycle expansion. Shared test scenarios cover both adapters without duplicating production mechanisms; no actionable finding. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

title: resources: the runtime-db grows unbounded — ledger rows pruned only by a later SUCCESS, and an optimistic SEED never arms a GC timer (rf2-pk4i6 item 11)
description:
Shortlist item 11 of the rf2-pk4i6 senior-review wave (from rf2-pk4i6.1#3 and rf2-pk4i6.1#4, with rf2-pk4i6.1#6 riding along). Mike ruled the whole shortlist as actioned; this is the filed follow-on. Size M.

## The defect

The runtime-db grows without bound on a production path, by two independent routes.

1. Work-ledger rows are pruned only by a LATER SUCCESS, and mutation rows never. A polled resource against a failing endpoint adds a `:failed` row per tick — 720 rows/hour at a 5s interval — into every frame-state value and every epoch snapshot. A form submitted N times keeps N `:completed` rows for the frame's life.
2. An optimistic SEED never arms a GC timer. A create-mutation's seeded detail key settles owner-free with no stale, GC or poll timer, and is collected only by luck.

`spec/016-Resources.md:554` promises "the ledger is bounded". This is the same class as PR #9857, on a production path.

## The triage's citations (claims, to be opened at tip before editing)

- `spec/016-Resources.md:554` — the bounded-ledger promise.
- `prune-terminal-for-key` — 2 call sites, against a 26-site `mark-terminal` control. That ratio is the evidence for "pruned only by a later SUCCESS"; re-measure it rather than trusting the numbers.
- `succeeded-handler` — where a `:seed` key not in `authoritative-keys` must be added to `timer-policies`.

Re-verified by the reviewer: NO. The reviewer judged the 2-vs-26 census adequate without re-running it. So the census is the first thing to reproduce, and a verified "the premise does not hold" is a complete and good deliverable.

## What the triage proposes (a proposal, verified before obeyed)

- Prune after EVERY terminal settle, not only after a success.
- Drop a key's rows and its index bucket on remove / clear-scope / gc-fired / mutation-removes — one shared helper, roughly one sentence per handler.
- Amend `spec/016` §Ledger row retention to: "next TERMINAL transition; all rows dropped when the entry is removed; mutation rows pruned per instance".
- In `succeeded-handler`, add each `:seed` key not in `authoritative-keys` to `timer-policies` (~8 lines), pinned with a `:rf.resource/gc-scheduled` assertion.
- Riding along from .1#6: the two-line `:completed-at` on mutation cancellations.

## Pins

The two mechanisms fail differently and want separate coverage: unbounded growth under repeated terminal-but-not-successful settles, and a seeded key that never arms a GC timer. A pin covering only the prune leaves the seed path unpinned, and the seed path is the one that regresses silently.

Note the class hazard recorded in this project's own tracker: a test can pass while exercising nothing. Assert a PRECONDITION inside each pin — that the ledger actually held rows before the prune, that the seeded key actually exists — so the pin reds when its own input vanishes rather than passing vacuously.

## Surface and fences

Yours, exclusively: `implementation/resources/src/**`, the resources test tree, and `spec/016-Resources.md`.

Shortlist items 9 and 14 are sequenced BEHIND this bead on exactly that surface and will not be dispatched until this PR merges. You hold it alone.

Not yours: `implementation/core/**`, `implementation/epoch/**` and `spec/002` (item 7 is live there); `implementation/schemas/**` and `spec/010` (items 12 and 13 are live there). `spec/API.md` and its manifest sidecars are hot-zone: report, do not edit.

## Implemented — PR #9895 (2026-09-16)

### The census reproduced (the item's first ask; reviewer had NOT re-verified it)

Over `implementation/resources/src/**`, comments and the `defn` separated from call sites:
`prune-terminal-for-key` = **2 code call sites**, 1 defn, 4 comments. `mark-terminal` = **24 code
sites**, 1 defn. Control: both needles counted in ONE pass over the SAME file set, so a zero would
have been an instrument fault rather than an answer — the 24 is what makes the 2 meaningful.
Flattened and comment-stripped passes agreed. The item said 26 for `mark-terminal`; that is 24 src
+ 2 test. **The ratio reproduces and the premise HOLDS.**

Mapping each site to its enclosing handler sharpens it beyond the ratio: the only two prunes are
`succeeded-handler` and `page-succeeded-handler`, BOTH on the success path. `failed-handler`,
`page-failed-handler`, `clear-scope-handler*`, `remove-handler`, `ensure-load`, mutation
`succeeded-handler`/`failed-handler`, `apply-removes`, `clear-handler`,
`dispose-resource-runtime!` and `dangle-non-terminal-work!` all settle rows terminal and prune
nothing. Mechanism 2 also verified at source: `schedule-timers` is emitted in `mutation_events`
at exactly one place, built from `(merge patch-policies populate-policies)` — the optimistic apply
path (phase 1.5) arms nothing at all.

### What landed

Two new work-ledger helpers, and the index self-heal factored into a shared `ensure-ledger-index`
so the new dropper is post-hydration correct:

- `settle-terminal` — marks a row terminal AND prunes that key's terminal tail, reading the prune
  key off the just-settled row. Now used at all 18 terminal-settle sites; the two standalone prune
  calls fold into it.
- `drop-rows-for-key` — drops every row for a key PLUS its inverse-index bucket. Called from
  remove, clear-scope, gc-fired, clear-resource, mutation `:removes`, and `:rf.mutation/clear`.

Mechanism 2: the mutation `succeeded-handler` adds each optimistic `:seed` key NOT covered by the
reply's authoritative patches/populates/removes to the timer-arming set, via the same
`timer-delays` policy a fetched entry gets. Only `:seed` qualifies — `:patch` means the entry
already existed and its read path armed it; `:remove` dissoc'd it.

Rider rf2-pk4i6.1#6: mutation cancellations now carry the causal `:completed-at`.
`:rf.mutation/clear` was registered `framework-authority-meta` (no time cofx) so the fact was
unreachable; it now declares `time-meta`, symmetric with its resource siblings.

`ssr.cljc`'s `dangle-non-terminal-work!` deliberately left alone — a one-shot restore
reconciliation over the snapshot's rows, not a repeating path, and those rows ARE the
reconciliation evidence.

### Where the implementation departs from the item's proposal, and why

The item proposed dropping a removed key's rows, which makes the terminal `:cancelled` mark at
those sites unobservable. That collided with five landed tests. Resolution taken: the rows ARE
dropped (keeping only the tail would still leak one orphaned bucket per removed key, which is the
unbounded axis), the terminal mark is KEPT ahead of the drop (a row the index self-heal somehow
missed is then left terminal rather than surviving as falsely in-flight — the one state that would
ride an epoch snapshot and be dangled on restore), and the causal `:completed-at` those tests
pinned is read from the `:rf.resource/removed` / `:rf.mutation/cleared` TRACE, where epoch and
tooling correlation actually reads it. rf2-x76af2.14's fact is relocated, not reverted.

Callers that relied on rows surviving a removal — all tests, NO production caller:
`clear-scope-cancels-in-flight-rows`, `remove-cancels-in-flight-row`,
`clear-scope-cancelled-row-carries-causal-completed-at`,
`remove-cancelled-row-carries-causal-completed-at`, `clear-resource-disposes-runtime-state`.

### Spec

`spec/016` §Ledger row retention now states the three clauses the code implements: next TERMINAL
transition; all rows plus the index bucket dropped when the entry leaves the cache; mutation rows
pruned per instance under their `[:rf.mutation <instance-id>]` key. Four in-tree docstrings
restating the old rule were corrected with it.

REPORTED, NOT EDITED (hot zone / outside surface): `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3204` carries the same
stale "next successful transition" sentence. `docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md:1881,3068` carry
it as historical design records.

### Pins and controls

Three new pins, each asserting a PRECONDITION so it reds when its own input vanishes, and each
shown RED against the unfixed behaviour by a planted fault (restored and verified by blob hash):

1. `repeated-failing-settles-keep-the-ledger-bounded` — with the prune disabled it read
   `(not (= 3 12))`: twelve rows for twelve failing attempts where three are retained. That is the
   defect, measured.
2. `removal-drops-the-keys-inverse-index-bucket` — SETTLES FIRST, deliberately. Writing the
   precondition surfaced a real property: the inverse index is built LAZILY by the first prune,
   so without a settle there is no bucket at all and the assertion would have passed having
   exercised nothing.
3. `optimistic-seed-uncovered-by-the-reply-arms-its-gc-timer` — with the seed arming neutered it
   went red on its three timer assertions ONLY, its preconditions still passing, so the seed
   genuinely happened.

### Gates

Reviewer persona: senior React view-layer engineer who has shipped a hiccup-to-React runtime (controlled inputs, portals/overlays, error boundaries, presence, a data-to-element codec)

Scope read: implementation/fresco/src/** in full (fresco.cljc 831; impl/codec.cljs 1994; impl/collector.cljs 1333; impl/mount.cljs 621; impl/intent.cljs 617; impl/overlay.cljs 572; server.cljs 546; tool.cljs 615; impl/boundary.cljs 387; impl/controlled.cljs 379; impl/presence.cljs 320; impl/state.cljc 255; impl/route_link.cljs 247; overlay.cljs 240; forms.cljs 232; impl/presence_react.cljs 202; substrate.cljs 181; impl/error.cljc 173; impl/frames.cljs 169; impl/roots.cljs 130; impl/frame_boundary.cljs 111; motion.cljs 101; evidence.cljs 100; native.cljc 82; impl/generation.cljs 81; impl/slot.cljc 74; impl/portal.cljs 62) — ~10.9K lines; test/ skimmed by deftest roster and read where a finding needed it (codec, intent, revision, view_annotation, hmr_remount, direct_return, virtualized ledger); test_kit/ skimmed by public-fn roster; implementation/fresco/spec/{README,invariants}.md; docs/core/fresco/02 (children contract) and 03 (key maps).
Owning specs consulted: docs/design/fresco/README.md (decisions.md governs); implementation/fresco/spec/invariants.md (I5, I7, I10, I11, I15); spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §The client root (244-263), §View tagging contract (749-821); spec/002-Frames.md §frame-provider (1643-1669), §frame-root (1671-1732); spec/Ownership.md line 31 (frame-provider / frame-root → 002) and line 46 (view tagging → 006). There is no Fresco row in Ownership (grep `fresco` → 0).

Overall: the slice is in good shape. The collector, the controlled-input converge, the frame-incarnation pinning and the root lifecycle are careful and pinned by tests; the four items below are the ones worth a morning, and only the first two are more than housekeeping.

## Findings, ranked

### 1. React's missing-key warning is silenced at every boundary crossing, and nothing fills the gap  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:1186-1203 (`realize-children`), :1155-1172 (`check-member-key!`), :1081-1085 (the "React warns about an unkeyed list" premise); consumers implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/boundary.cljs:386, implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/overlay.cljs:542; docs/core/fresco/02-views-and-reads.md:119-126 (the taught splice)
- What: a `(for …)` handed to a `defview`, `h/error-boundary` or `overlay/*` as children is flattened one level into `:children`, the body splices it with `into` (the guide's spelling), so every member reaches `createElement` as a separate argument — which React marks `_store.validated` and never key-checks — while the codec's dev check deliberately warns only on entity-valued keys "because an absent key is React's own warning".
- Evidence: `realize-children`'s own docstring states the mechanism ("the flatten turns a seq's members into direct arguments, which React marks validated and never warns about"); `check-member-key!` returns before any warning when `(:key p)` is nil; boundary.cljs:386 and overlay.cljs:542 both `into` the children, as does the guide's `card`. The only test on this axis, codec_cljs_test.cljs:1206 `an-unkeyed-boundary-seq-is-reacts-to-warn-about-and-the-codec-is-silent`, exercises `[:ul (for …)]` — the native-tag position, where `expand-seq` hands React an array and React does warn — never `[view {} (for …)]`. Control: case-insensitive grep for `unique "key"|Each child in a list|unkeyed` over implementation/fresco finds that test and presence's unkeyed refusal (presence_cljs_test.cljs:146-163), nothing at the crossing. Net effect: an unkeyed dynamic list of memoised boundaries reconciles by index in silence; delete row 0 and every row-local state — the controlled-input composition `useState`, an overlay's `useRef` cell, presence retention, the read-set entry — is handed the next row's data, which is the failure the entity-key warning text describes, reached from the other side.
- Action: in `check-seq-keys!`'s loop (the crossing path only; leave `expand-seq` to React) warn once per site when a boundary-headed member has no `:key`, under the same `keywarn` dedupe and `goog.DEBUG` gate; add the crossing case beside codec_cljs_test.cljs:1206 (a `[view {} (for …)]` with a spy on React's `console.error` channel must read empty and the new warning must read one). The ~150 ns/member cost argument in direct_return_cljs_test.cljs:252-255 was priced for native tags where React speaks; it does not apply here. Cheaper fallback: state the gap in 06-lists-and-collections.md.

### 2. An `h/event` inside a key map has its returned intent silently dropped  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/intent.cljs:526-544 (`key-map-handler`, the `(fn? v) v` arm at :536); :586-605 (`lower-declared-prop` routes a map there too); implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco.cljc:112-123 (`defview` docstring: a key map branch is "an intent vector or a function") and :297-305 (`event` docstring: at an on*-spelled prop "a returned VECTOR is dispatched")
- What: a branch such as `{"Enter" (h/event [e] (when (valid? e) [:form/commit]))}` takes the `(fn? v)` arm — `callback?` is `fn?` plus a marker — so it is invoked raw and the vector it returns is ignored; no error, no dispatch.
- Evidence: no `callback?` arm exists in the `reduce-kv` at intent.cljs:533-537; intent_cljs_test.cljs:384-389 pins only a plain-fn branch and 312-383 only vector branches; the guide's one key-map example (docs/core/fresco/03-events-as-data.md:196-201) is vectors only, so nothing states the contract for the marked form here. The `event` docstring promises the event contract at every on*-spelled position, and a key map sits at one; a reader of that docstring writes the branch above and gets a control that does nothing.
- Action: add `(rf.fresco.impl.intent/callback? v) (event-callback k v)` ahead of `(fn? v)` in `key-map-handler` (three lines) and one test row beside intent_cljs_test.cljs:384. If the ruling is that a key map takes data or a plain fn only, refuse the marked form there instead — either is fine; silent is the one wrong answer.

### 3. Spec 006 says the non-DOM-root skip warns once per id; Fresco's skip is silent  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/collector.cljs:984-1027 (`annotate-root`); spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:771 and :792 ("the wrapper SKIPs with a one-shot warning per id, same as the source-coord exemption"); implementation/fresco/test/re_frame/fresco/view_annotation_dom_cljs_test.cljs:218-247
- What: `annotate-root` returns a fragment-, boundary-, host- or nil-rooted body unchanged with no warning, while the owning spec's injection rules and known-limits list both require the one-shot warning.
- Evidence: the function has no warn call (control: `rg 'console|warn'` over collector.cljs → 0 hits; the Reagent path at implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs:153 calls `re-frame.views.warn-once/warn-non-dom-root!`); the two exemption tests assert only the attribute's absence. Which side is right: the code, for Fresco — every `defview` is registered in dev, and a boundary-rooted or fragment-rooted body is the routine composition, so a warn-once per id would fire across a large share of any Fresco app's views; the warning was designed around Reagent's opt-in `reg-view`.
- Action: decide: A — amend §Injection rules / §Known limits with one clause ("Fresco skips silently: every defview is registered, so the exemption is routine there"), and while in Ownership add an external-home row for implementation/fresco/spec/ (complaints, invariants, server-policy), which the matrix's preamble says it indexes and does not (control: `rg -c 'implementation/' spec/Ownership.md` → 2, neither a fresco path); or B — call `warn-non-dom-root!` from `annotate-root`. Recommend A.

### 4. `intent/lower-props` has no caller and a docstring that claims the hot path  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: simplification]
- Where: implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/intent.cljs:607-617
- What: a public whole-map lowering door nothing in src/, test_kit/ or bench/ calls; its docstring says it is "the ordinary case for the great majority of elements on a page", which misdirects a reader — the codec lowers per entry inside `convert-entry` / `host-entry` and never walks a map through it.
- Evidence: repo-wide grep for `lower-props` call sites → 3, all in intent_cljs_test.cljs (:301, :406, :409); control: `intent/lower-prop ` → 37 hits across 11 files including codec.cljs (4).
- Action: delete it with its test (intent_cljs_test.cljs:401-414), or keep it `^:no-doc` with a docstring that says test-only.

## Considered, left alone
- `h/error-boundary` given neither `:fallback` nor `:on-error` renders an empty region on failure (boundary.cljs:384-386): React 19's default `onCaughtError` still logs it, and refusing the shape is the nag the stance rejects.
- presence_react.cljs:157 `(when-not (= next state) (set-state next))` deep-compares retained hiccup and costs the tray a second pass whenever a child carries an `h/event` closure: converges in one extra render as the comment says, and no hot path is measured.
- overlay.cljs:519-523 silently replaces an author's `:on-key-down` (modal), `:on-cancel` and `:on-before-toggle` with the module's own: the public docstring's options table says exactly this.
- An `h/event` that returns `[::h/prevent …]` is dispatched literally and dies as no-such-event on `:re-frame.fresco/prevent` (intent.cljs:189-201): loud enough, and HD-026 gives a callback ownership of `preventDefault`.
- server.cljs:440-449 runs `destroy-frame!` in a `finally` even after `make-frame` threw: checked `claim-frame-destroy!` (frame.cljc:4126-4148) answers nil for an absent id, so it no-ops and cannot mask the original refusal.

## Instruments and controls
- `git -C …/review-sep16 rev-parse --short HEAD` → d89a41e057.
- Grep `:children` over docs/core/fresco and implementation/fresco/**/*.cljs → guide 02:119-126 teaches `into`; boundary.cljs:386 and overlay.cljs:542 `into`; control: the codec.cljs:14 docstring hit.
- Case-insensitive grep `unique "key"|Each child in a list|should have a unique|missing.key|unkeyed` over implementation/fresco → codec_cljs_test:1206 (native position only) plus presence refusal rows; control: `unkeyed` hits in presence_cljs_test:146-163.
- Grep `key-map|"Enter"` in intent_cljs_test → branches pinned are vectors, prevent, marker and a plain fn (:384-389), no marked callback; control: the marked-callback-in-key-map spelling exists in the tree only as a design sketch, docs/design/freehand/fable-design.md:1946.
- Grep `lower-props` callers repo-wide → 3 (all intent_cljs_test); control `intent/lower-prop ` → 37 hits / 11 files.
- Grep `console|warn` in collector.cljs → 0; control: `warn-non-dom-root!` at core/views/source_coord_annotation.cljs:153 and core/views/warn_once.cljs:31.
- Grep `fresco|Fresco` in spec/Ownership.md → 0 and `rg -c 'implementation/'` → 2; rows read by line number: 31 and 46 as the brief cites them.
- Read frame.cljc:4126-4148 (`claim-frame-destroy!`): `(when-let [candidate (frame id)] …)` — nil on an absent id.
- Read revision_dom_cljs_test's deftest roster (:271 `a-revision-change-resets-the-field-through-a-memo-wall`) before deciding that `install!` deleting the revision marker without comparing it (controlled.cljs:353-364) is NOT a finding: the revision rides `rfProps` into `boundary-props=` (codec.cljs:493-516), so its job is to defeat the memo bail-out, and the re-baseline is React's per-commit `updateInput` re-assert.
- Read hmr_remount_cljs_test's roster (:215-427): a save re-minting the head and element type (subtree remount) is the pinned contract, not a defect.
- Traced `raw-gate` / `mint-host-gate!` (codec.cljs:588-600, :1561-1589) against React's `mountSyncExternalStore` hydration path (server snapshot on the hydrating pass, `updateStoreInstance` forcing the client re-render from the passive effect): the adoption swap lands after paint by React's rules, which the docstrings state; no finding.

description:

THE FAILURE, read from the run rather than from the alert's step name.
Run https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/actions/runs/34988332272, workflow `expensive tests`, at trunk `9dbb881a95`, 2026-09-15 15:25Z. Job "Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates", step `Gate — Xray feature matrix (test:xray-feature-gate)`, `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1`.

ONE scenario of sixteen failed; the other fifteen passed and 13 matrix rows were covered:
`FAIL routes-epochs routing ladder (current route, nav-this-epoch, nested table, blocked)`

The assertion, verbatim:
`waitForValue: expected #3 route params → CURRENT ROUTE :article params {:id "intro"} + transitioned within 10000ms`
thrown at `examples/scripts/spec-helpers.cljs:110` (`waitForValue`), from `tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:2811` (`runRoutesEpochs`), via `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs:439` and `:634`.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS BEAD: the route half of that expectation MATCHED. The last observed state carried `currentId: ":routes-epochs/article"` and `currentParams: "{:id \"intro\"}"` — exactly what was expected. What was missing is the TRANSITION evidence: `navFrom`, `navTo`, `navParams` and `navOutcome` all `null`, with `noActivity: true` and `currentPath: null`. So navigation ARRIVED and the nav-this-epoch readout was EMPTY when the poll read it. Do not start from "routing is broken"; it demonstrably is not.

Corroborating, from the same diagnostics block: the trace shows `:rf.route/navigate` running to `:rf.event/run-end`, with `:rf.fx/do-fx` carrying `[:rf.route/commit-nav-counter {:counter-key :nav-token-counter, :value 3}]` and `[:rf.nav/push-url "/articles/intro"]` — the counter value 3 matches the expectation's "#3". Three browser console errors also appear in the block: `[re-frame2] :rf.error/frame-destroyed`, repeated identically. Whether those are related is UNKNOWN and is a question for the worker, not a premise.
Artefacts the run names: screenshot `implementation/out/xray-feature-gate-artifacts/routes-epochs-routing-ladder-current-route-nav-this-epoch-nested-table-blocked.png`; url under test `http://127.0.0.1:8037/articles/intro`; panels `routing`; load-check `no`.

REGRESSION OR FLAKE IS UNSETTLED, AND SETTLING IT IS THE FIRST TASK. Evidence bounding it, measured 2026-09-16:
- The eleven `expensive-tests.yml` runs before this one were all `success` (2026-09-08 through 2026-09-14). This is the FIRST red.
- `tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs` has not been touched since `8b17cc53d5` (2026-09-09), a product-name sweep. The scenario itself did not change.
- The window between the last green nightly (`3194e220d0`) and the red one (`9dbb881a95`) holds 217 commits, but most are beads checkpoints and Story work. The ones touching Xray are few, and they are CANDIDATES rather than culprits: `522695c7dc` (host focus that names a frame moves the spine — `focus.cljc`, `registry.cljs`), `124d6a3620` (coalesce the redaction-counter dispatch per task — `registry.cljs`, `config.cljc`), `c4e685d3f1` / `d240f7adbd` (drop Xray's own frameless sub reads before the privacy gate), `290015e38d` (resources panel optimistic keys). NOTHING in that window touched `implementation/routing/**` or the core route files.
- A single failure after eleven greens is equally consistent with a timing flake. The nav readout being transient — populated during the epoch and cleared once it settles — would produce exactly this signature, including `noActivity: true`.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT PER-PR: this gate runs a PR-smoke tier on pull requests and the FULL sweep only nightly (`Ran 16 Xray feature scenarios (nightly-full sweep)`). So a fix cannot be validated by an ordinary PR run — the worker must run the gate itself.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE — and the two outcomes are different deliverables, both good:
(a) A REGRESSION: name the commit, fix the cause, and the scenario passes without its expectation being weakened.
(b) A FLAKE: say so with evidence (repeat runs, and the mechanism that makes the readout transient), then repair the SCENARIO's wait so it observes the transition deterministically rather than racing it — never by deleting the `+ transitioned` conjunct, which is the only thing asserting that a navigation happened at all. Weakening it to accept the state the failure already showed would make the scenario pass on the very condition it exists to catch.

DO NOT re-run the nightly and call a green a fix: a scenario that fails one night in twelve reads green on a re-run by construction. Whichever branch holds, say how many times it was run.

THE DIAGNOSIS, transcribed from the docstring the worker wrote, because it is the deliverable and it explains the exact failure signature this bead was filed on:

The `:epoch` listener is called ONCE PER DEQUEUED EVENT, not once per epoch. So it re-delivers the same in-flight record many times, and -- for a step whose event CASCADES -- delivers a PARENT record AGAIN after the child's record has already arrived. Measured on the routes-epochs ladder's rung #3: one press produced TWELVE firings -- epoch 6 (`:routes-epochs/go`) seven times, then epoch 7 (`:rf.route/navigate`) once, then epoch 6 TWICE MORE with the ring's last already 7.

Pinning focus on that trailing stale record puts the spine into RETRO on the PARENT epoch, whose bundle carries no routing traces. So the Routing panel's NAVIGATION THIS EPOCH section reads "No route activity in this epoch" while CURRENT ROUTE still shows the arrived route.

THAT IS PRECISELY THE SIGNATURE THIS BEAD RECORDS: currentId and currentParams correct, navFrom / navTo / navParams / navOutcome all null, noActivity true. The bead's discriminator -- "the route ARRIVED; do not start from routing is broken" -- held, and pointed at the right layer.

A nil ring is treated as "no epoch artefact", in which case the listener would not have registered at all, so the some?-arm keeps the predicate honest rather than silently disabling focus-pinning. The worker's own words: this guard "is what makes the ns docstring's 'each step re-focuses head and the spine never pins into RETRO' true of the code rather than only of the intent".

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FLAKE-VERSUS-REGRESSION QUESTION, stated as the worker left it and NOT as a settled finding: the defect is in the TESTBED RUNNER's focus listener (`tools/xray/testbeds/runner/core.cljs`), not in Xray's routing panel and not in the framework's routing. It is a latent harness defect whose firing depends on dequeue ordering, which is consistent with eleven green nightlies followed by one red. NOBODY HAS YET SHOWN THE FIX RED-THEN-GREEN: the worker died at exactly the "compile, stage, re-measure" step. The measurement of twelve firings IS executed evidence; the fix is a candidate until the gate runs.

WHAT THE NEXT DISPATCH INHERITS: read the uncommitted diff first -- the diagnosis and the candidate fix are both in that one file's new docstring and predicate. Rebase (base d1cf4bf3b8 is behind trunk), then do what the dead worker was about to do: compile, stage, re-run `npm run test:xray-feature-gate`, and show the scenario red without the guard and green with it, saying how many runs each. title: WebSocket inbox overwrites the correlated result with late replies
description:
Make `:ws.app/request-reply` the sole writer of the WebSocket example's correlated result. The inbox currently overwrites that result with valid but uncorrelated late replies, undoing the connection machine's correct correlation decision. Keep unsolicited frames visible in the inbox.

Ownership: examples_patterns, primarily `examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:494-514`; related correlation producer `connection.cljs:531-556`, intended result writer `messages.cljs:562-588`, and `views.cljs:176-213` ("Last correlated reply"). Baseline: `9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261`. Revalidated at `9291090725fa3ebcad67ea81a74946fc3aac96a4`; all 25 assigned paths remain identical to baseline.

SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)

Remediation fence: split from finding 1 of `rf2-fzbj.34`, which remains open and unchanged. Preserve `[FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]`; this fresh review authorizes issue creation, not fixer dispatch or source remediation.

Trigger and observed behavior:

1. On a connected socket, register A under reusable id `[:feature/load "gamma"]`, with `:reply [:ws.app/request-reply]`, and hold its response.
2. Register B under the same id. A is correctly settled once as `:ws/superseded`.
3. Deliver B's valid wire reply with B's `:request-token`. B completes, and `[:messages :last-reply]` contains B with `:origin :ws/server`.
4. Deliver A's valid late wire reply with A's old token. The connection machine correctly leaves `:in-flight` empty and issues no callback. It intentionally dispatches `:ws/handle-message` to record the unsolicited frame.
5. The inbox handler sees `:request-id` and unconditionally replaces `[:messages :last-reply]` with raw A. The displayed result now contains A's stale body and lacks the provenance stamp.

Expected: B's complete correlated outcome remains unchanged; both vetted wire frames appear in `:received`. Actual source-derived witness: before `{request-token 1, echo tag "B", origin :ws/server}`, after `{request-token 0, echo tag "A", no origin}`, inbox count 2, callback count still 2 (A superseded and B success), and no in-flight request. This is a result-ownership defect, not a repeat callback or malformed ingress defect.

Suggested repair: remove the `cond->` result write at messages.cljs:513-514 from `:ws/handle-message`, leaving its inbox prepend and sequence counter. Keep `:ws.app/request-reply` as the only writer of a completed correlated outcome. Update the inbox handler explanation that currently equates request-id presence with correlation. Retain existing wire schemas, tokens, callback policy, local failure outcomes, and unsolicited-frame logging.

Acceptance:

- Exercise A/B id reuse through the shipped registrations, with B replying first and A last. B's exact body, token, and `:origin` stay in `:last-reply`; both frames are logged; callbacks remain exactly once per registration.
- After a timeout outcome, a late valid reply joins the inbox while the local timeout remains the correlated result. Duplicate/unsolicited replies also leave it intact.
- A matching reply still updates the result through its callback; a push only updates the inbox.
- Add the regression in the framework-owned WebSocket CLJS tests (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs`), not under examples/. Show the old inbox writer fails it.

Dedup/history: current all-status WebSocket title search and description searches for `last-reply`/`submit-invalid` found no dedicated open owner. `rf2-fzbj.34` is an aggregate and does not replace this independently actionable issue. `rf2-tb442` is closed; newest-first history and close reason explicitly preserve unsolicited-frame logging after a token mismatch. Its regression delivers A before B and checks callback log/in-flight state, so it misses B-before-A clobbering this app-db slot. `rf2-iyjae` closed the pre-correlation validation/provenance defects; this frame is valid and correlation already refuses it. `rf2-idv1m` closed fixture shadowing; retain its shipped-registration test discipline.

Validation executed: cached-dependency JVM process reading the current .cljs declaration/handler forms from the absolute source root, applying the actual Malli InboundMessage validator and public `re-frame.machines/machine-transition`, then passing the relevant dispatched inbox/outcome events through the actual source-derived handlers. Artifact `ai/surface-review-20260913/examples_patterns/probe-examples_patterns-1.clj`, matching `.log` and `.exit`; captured process exit 0 confirms the asserted defect witness, not a passing repository gate. Source-root banner checked. No CLJS compilation, full event drain, real transport, DOM run, installs, or shared build output. Process completed and source remained untouched.

title: Resource SSR example polls a frame value as an ID and always waits five seconds
description:
Pass the already-bound request frame ID fid to await-resource-loaded! in the resource SSR example. This one argument repair makes the existing bounded poll observe the resource it intends to await, avoiding a deterministic five-second delay on every successful render.

Remediation fence: split from rf2-fzbj.37 F2. Preserve [FENCE: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj]. Review/issue creation does not authorize implementation or fixer dispatch.

Ownership and revision
- Slice examples_capabilities; examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:298-323 and 354-370, exact repair at line 370.
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. Owned paths are unchanged across these revisions and in the working tree.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).

Mechanism
f at line 358 is the frame VALUE returned by make-frame. Line 370 passes it as :frame f to await-resource-loaded!, whose public rf/resource-state read at line 317 forwards that target to ID-keyed frame readers. implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:144-182 describes :frame <frame-id> and reads via frame-app-db-value/frame-runtime-db-value. implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1381-1398 looks up the supplied ID directly in the frame registry. A frame value is not a registry key, so every poll reads nil, even when fid already identifies a loaded article entry.

Fresh reproducer and actual result
Initialize the SSR adapter, require unchanged resources-ssr.core, and supply a synchronous successful article reply through the shipped canned-success managed effect. In a process-local wrapper around rf/resource-state, record both the supplied-target read and the same target normalized through frame-target->id; return the supplied-target result unchanged.

The real example handle-request took 5080.50 ms and 853 polls. First and last reads both reported keyword-target?=false, by-value-status=nil, by-id-status=:loaded. Its response eventually contained the article, so a content-only test passes despite the broken readiness condition. Control: change only the wrapper's returned read to the normalized-ID read. The same handler returned in 7.57 ms with one poll and identical article content. Both paths left no registered request frame.

Expected: the poll exits when this request's resource becomes :loaded or :error and consumes the five-second deadline only for unsettled work. Actual: it always exhausts that deadline. Impact: five seconds of unnecessary latency per successful request and a readiness check that never actually reads its target.

Suggested repair
Change the existing call to :frame fid. Keep the public introspection API and existing bounded polling shape; no API expansion or generalized waiting framework is required. Ensure the regression measures terminal-state readiness rather than merely the final response content.

Acceptance
- A synchronous loaded reply exits immediately, without exhausting preload-deadline-ms.
- A parked asynchronous request waits; success or failure release exits on the real terminal entry rather than only on the deadline.
- Assert the supplied target names the request's actual live resource entry.
- Preserve runtime payload projection, fresh-skip client acquisition, and finally teardown. Add regression coverage to implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj or an equivalent existing framework suite; no tests inside examples/.

Validation and limits
Fresh cached-dependency JVM witness: ai/surface-review-20260913/examples_capabilities/probe-examples_capabilities-resource-2-attempt-1.log/.exit, exit 0. Source ai/surface-review-20260912/review-examples-capabilities-resource-2.clj was inspected and rerun against absolute current source/classpath paths. Process exited after explicit shutdown; no source changes, dependency installation, shared build or browser execution. Existing examples_test.clj dynamic-payload checks were inspected: response-content success does not establish this poll's identity or latency.

Deduplication and references
Revalidated current rf2-fzbj.37 and its latest three history rows. Current all-status search for await-resource-loaded returns only that aggregate; SSR path/title searches found no dedicated open duplicate. rf2-h3c9 is closed and owns client acquisition plus the deliberate whole-app lifetime of the undispatched page-closed event, not this server poll; its decision remains intact. This independently implementable issue owns only F2 of rf2-fzbj.37.

title: HTTP RealWorld: admit optimistic comment IDs in durable schema
description:
Make the HTTP example's durable optimistic-comment shape accept its temporary IDs while preserving the integer-ID wire schema. In the normal development build, Post Comment currently rejects its own app-db candidate and never sends the POST.

Remediation fence: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This is an independently actionable split of confirmed finding 1 in rf2-fzbj.21, revalidated by the fresh review under rf2-gwye. Review/issue creation is authorized; implementation is not.

Ownership: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:192-195,391-428; realworld_http/schema.cljs:257-258,266-267; realworld_shared/schema.cljs:120-127. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; inspected HEAD 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879.

Trigger/reproducer: run the documented development example, sign in, open an article, enter a nonblank comment, and click Post Comment. The recordable :realworld/temp-comment-id supplier returns a temp- UUID string. :comment-form/submit inserts it as the optimistic comment's :id and emits the managed POST. The app registers [:comments :data] as [:maybe [:vector ws/Comment]], but ws/Comment requires :id :int.

Expected: commit one optimistic card, send one POST, then replace its temporary ID/card with the successful integer-ID response. Actual: development app-schema validation rejects the pending comment candidate at [0 :id]; core rejects the db transition and its effects, leaving zero cards and zero POSTs. Release validation elision masks the defect.

Suggested repair: give the application a durable optimistic comment schema admitting the explicitly temporary representation, or use an integer temporary ID scheme. Keep the shared Conduit wire Comment/CommentsResponse decode schemas strict; do not disable validation or widen unrelated server IDs.

Acceptance: extend the existing framework-owned RealWorld harness with the production app schemas attached to its test frame. Drive the real comment-form event and its normal supplier, assert one optimistic card and one POST, then replacement on success. Failure removes the temporary card and restores a usable form. If a separate durable schema is introduced, retain a wire-schema control rejecting string server IDs. Keep examples test-free.

Validation performed: reran ai/surface-review-20260913/examples_real_apps/schema-probe.clj against current source, using cached Malli 0.20.1 and a process-local plain-atom frame. It reads/evaluates the actual shared schemas, app schema registry, request builder and comment-submit reducer, then dispatches through current re-frame.core and re-frame.schemas. schema-examples_real_apps-1.log/.exit: exit 0; before-valid true, candidate-valid false at [0 :id] for temp-probe; real dispatch leaves comments [] and HTTP calls 0. Integer-ID control commits a card and records HTTP calls 1. The log prints the actual SOURCE_ROOT. This is a source-handler/core-schema witness, not a browser or CLJS compile run.

Coverage explanation: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:3601-3655 exercises the production backend on an anonymous frame without installing the app's comments schema. Its AuthSlice-specific test at :258-310 documents why default-frame schema registration does not cover such a frame.

Deduplication/references: current tracker searches for realworld, real-apps and feed found no dedicated open owner of this mismatch. rf2-fzbj.21 is an aggregate, not an independent issue. Closed rf2-2xzc/rf2-ghxt concern nullable boot slices and remain closed; this occurs after normal boot. Closed rf2-84iek concerns cross-article reply ownership and is unrelated to the candidate's ID type.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-gwye.33): fixed — the durable comment shape now admits the optimistic temp id while the wire decode schemas stay strict.

Remediated in PR #9758 (branch worker/realworld-a), which fixes all four confirmed findings of rf2-fzbj.21 together. Every finding was re-verified at tip before the fix; all four still held.

What landed, per finding:

1. rf2-gwye.33 (HTTP optimistic comment) — realworld_http/schema.cljs gains DurableComment: the wire ws/Comment with :id widened to [:or :int [:re #"^temp-"]], derived from ws/Comment rather than restated. [:comments :data] registers that instead of the wire shape. ws/Comment, ws/CommentResponse and ws/CommentsResponse are untouched and still reject a string id.

2. rf2-gwye.34 (HTTP home feed) — realworld_http/http.cljs gains current-nav-token / same-navigation?. :articles/load and :feed/load capture the committed route's :nav-token and carry it on both reply targets; :articles/loaded, :articles/load-failed, :feed/loaded and :feed/load-failed refuse a reply whose navigation the reader has left. Supersession could not cover this: the two families carry different :request-ids and settle one machine whose :empty/:some/:error states take no :fetch-succeeded.

3. rf2-gwye.35 (Resources feed invalidation) — :realworld/follow and :realworld/unfollow now invalidate {:from-db :realworld/session} #{[:feed]} beside the viewer's [:profile username], via a shared follow-invalidates helper. Re-verified against PR #9746 (rf2-fzbj.7) first: that change touched only the infinite-feed accumulated-pages tag path, and the RealWorld feed is a scalar resource, so the premise stood unchanged.

4a. rf2-gwye.37 (HTTP editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete carry the issuing nav-token; :editor/submit-success, :editor/submit-error, :editor/delete-success and :editor/delete-error are each gated on it. :editor/load-article now dispatches the machine [:reset] before [:use-edit], so a refused settle cannot leave the next editing session at :submitting with its inputs locked (that strand is reachable only once the settles are gated, and is pinned by a test).

4b. rf2-gwye.39 (Resources editor writes) — :editor/submit and :editor/delete use :reply-to [:editor/replied nav-token]; :editor/replied refuses a departed reply whole: no slice write, no navigation, and no instance clear. Clearing nothing is what scopes cleanup to the completed operation — the next editor entry clears the shared :editor/save instance anyway, and the runtime already suppresses a late result for a cleared instance.

4c. rf2-gwye.42 (Resources detail delete) — :ui/delete-article carries its slug on :reply-to [:ui/article-deleted slug]; the continuation clears its own instance on :ok and navigates home only while the committed route is :realworld.article/show for that slug, mirroring the HTTP twin's article-route-for-slug?.

Tests (examples stay test-free per rf2-8cevm): new rows in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs (realworld-comment-feed-and-editor-ownership) and realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs (delete-article-continuation-leaves-a-departed-reader-where-they-are, editor-write-continuations-stay-with-the-page-that-issued-them, follow-and-unfollow-restale-the-session-feed). The comment row registers the app's REAL app-db-schemas on its test frame, which is what no existing row did and why the defect was invisible.

Two existing rows changed as a consequence. The Resources test delete-article-continuation-navigates-home issued its delete from /register and asserted a navigate home — that is exactly the departed-page case rf2-gwye.42 says must be refused, so it now issues the delete from the article page. Two HTTP rows that dispatch [:articles/loaded ...] directly now pass the nav-token explicitly (nil on a frame that never navigated).

Gates, each exit code captured to a file and quoted from it, run on the final rebased base:
- npm run test:cljs: captured exit 0, 12026 tests / 59924 assertions, 0 failures (CI job "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)", key cljs).
- node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs: captured exit 0, all 58 swept builds compiled with zero warnings, examples/realworld and examples/realworld-resources among them (CI job cljs-examples-compile).
- RED-then-green control: with the eight example sources checked out at the merge base and the test tree left as committed, the focused run of both RealWorld namespaces gave captured exit 1 with 39 failures across the same 63 tests / 907 assertions as the green run, covering every finding; green after restore, and the restore verified by content hash against each committed blob id.
No markdown or spec page was touched, so the doc-link gates are not nominated for this change.

Skipped suggestions, each with its reason:
- rf2-gwye.34 suggested a shared request identity or cancellation may supplement ownership: NOT built. The nav-token gate alone closes the defect, and queued replies still need the gate regardless, so a cancellation scheme would add machinery this example exists to stay clear of.
- rf2-gwye.39 asked that cleanup be scoped so a stale callback cannot clear a newer :editor/save incarnation: met by refusing the reply whole rather than by introducing an incarnation id.
- rf2-gwye.33's alternative repair (generate an integer temporary id) was not taken: the durable/wire split keeps the recordable temp-id coeffect and its temp- prefix, which the app documents as a replay-safe join key.
No framework change was needed: rf2-gwye.35 and rf2-gwye.39 cite files under implementation/resources/src, but both defects were in the examples' own descriptors and continuations, and those library files are untouched.

title: surface-review(skill_reagent_migration): repair reporter pin and shadow-test instructions
description:
Fix the executable migration workflow in the skill: repin the mandatory reporter command to a revision that actually contains its Fresco path/namespace, cross the original Reagent component through React in the shadow-test sample, and teach explicit checkpoint/cleanup calls for scriptless comparison. These are two P2 findings and one P3 residual. Keep this review OPEN until the skill instructions are repaired. No runtime implementation change is proposed.

Scope and revision

Slice: skill_reagent_migration. Reviewed source baseline: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. Final evidence HEAD: 49fcc8f60bbcf5621cfba93134bfcb08752954a5. The entire owned skill directory and the cited Fresco codec/mounted implementation files have an empty diff against the baseline; concurrent tracker checkpoints have not changed this reviewed source.

SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review)

Exactly 22 owned tracked paths, all beneath skills/reagent-migration/:
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json
- LICENSE

- evals/evals.json
- package.json

- tests/fixture/package.json
- tests/fixture/shadow-cljs.edn
- tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs

Coverage

Read the skill/router, all seven migration reference leaves, authoring specifications, behavioral/trigger evals, package/plugin metadata and the cold-start fixture. Checked target shapes against Fresco's public facade, codec/head classification/prop crossing, memoization, reg-state, native hooks, root/server and mounted-test APIs. Followed the reporter entry point and pinned Git tree, adapter dependency wiring, and the cold-start fixture's classpath/build/CI intent. Reviewed the Reagent/Form-2/Form-3 ownership decisions, whole-view discipline, event timing/capture escape, callback contracts, keys/props, SSR startup and HMR ordering, adapter-retirement census caveat, and shadow verification workflow.

The assignment is the SKILL content, not an actual application migration. Legacy/source examples are intentional inputs; none is reported merely for using old names. This review does not claim every arbitrary consumer widget/lifecycle or external vendor integration was executed. Existing implementation tests and the cold-start fixture were inspected, not compiled or run. Behavioral eval JSON is an external grading specification, not an executed CI suite. JSON metadata parsed successfully. No production/source changes, dependencies installed, compilation output, services, commits or push; root owns tracker checkpoint/push.

F1 — P2: every mandatory reporter command combines a pre-rename SHA with a post-rename path and namespace

Owned source: skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:64-69; references/procedure.md:33-38 and :232-237. These three commands pin 6a5194c0aa029ac1ad34aaf3a62974fd3e5c0221 while selecting :deps/root "migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod" and -m re-frame.migration.fresco.codemod.

Trigger: a consumer follows the skill's required first step, copying the printed clojure -Srepro -Sdeps command unchanged. The same problem blocks the later --rewrite command.

Expected: the pinned Git coordinate resolves the reporter and produces the census/fixer EDN report before view edits begin.

Actual and direct reproduction: the commit exists, but that tree contains only migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod and re-frame.migration.hicasso.codemod. From SOURCE_ROOT:

    git cat-file -e 6a5194c0aa029ac1ad34aaf3a62974fd3e5c0221:migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/deps.edn
    # own exit 128: path exists on disk, but not in this commit

Positive controls, each own exit 0:

    git cat-file -e 6a5194c0aa029ac1ad34aaf3a62974fd3e5c0221

The archived evidence logs the exact commands/objects. The two material positive paths are:

    git cat-file -e 6a5194c0aa029ac1ad34aaf3a62974fd3e5c0221:migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/deps.edn
    git cat-file -e 6a5194c0aa029ac1ad34aaf3a62974fd3e5c0221:migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/codemod.clj

The old source's ns declaration is re-frame.migration.hicasso.codemod. The current HEAD does contain the Fresco path, so this is pin/path incoherence rather than a missing local installation. Even correcting only :deps/root to the old directory would leave the printed Fresco main namespace absent. The prose's optional suggestion to choose a newer SHA does not repair the command users are told to run first.

Impact: the skill blocks at its automated inventory step before producing its migration plan or report. This is an executable dependency coordinate, not an intentional historical spelling.

Repair: choose one landed post-rename SHA whose tree contains both the Fresco deps root and main namespace, and update all three owned command fences together. Keep the existing checkout-free Git delivery and the codemod's shared slot-source provenance. Check the same published recipe in docs/core/fresco/20-migration-from-reagent.md and migration/reagent-to-fresco/codemod/README.md when implementing; those copies are outside this slice but share the defect and should not retain an incompatible pin. Do not blindly change only the path back to Hicasso, since that tool targets the historical product namespace.

Acceptance: each exact printed command resolves its deps root and main at its own pinned SHA. Run the chosen command from a consumer directory against a small source fixture, assert the expected census/fixer entries and no input writes in scan/dry-run mode, and exercise the documented --rewrite spelling. Record the own CLI exit, not only Git object presence. The current review proves the missing tree entry without fetching/installing dependencies; it does not claim an actual cold-cache Clojure invocation.

F2 — P2: the shadow-test example sends an unconverted Reagent component through Fresco's ordinary head path

Owned source: skills/reagent-migration/references/procedure.md:195-208, specifically :reference [old/article-row {:article-id 7}] at :203.

Trigger: keep old/article-row as the original ordinary Reagent function, define the Fresco candidate, and run the shown hm/shadow! call in a correctly provisioned DOM test target. Minimal counterexample: old/article-row is (defn article-row [{:keys [article-id]}] [:h3 article-id]); it is not an h/defview product.

Expected: the reference renders via Reagent, the candidate via Fresco, and the shared script compares their DOM/intents.

Actual: implementation/fresco/test_kit/src/re_frame/fresco/test/mounted.cljs:2101-2102 passes BOTH forms unchanged to mount!. mount!'s contract at :768-771 confirms that it uses the Fresco runtime. The ordinary unmarked function therefore reaches implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/codec.cljs:1766-1789's invalid-head branch and raises :rf.error/fresco-bad-head. It never reaches a meaningful comparison. This is established by tracing the current executable branches, not by treating old/ as an incorrect namespace spelling.

Repair: hoist (r/reactify-component old/article-row) once at top level, cross it as [:> old-article-row {:id 7}] (or a declared defhost), and use the matching single-word prop on the candidate. Explain why both test arms are Fresco hiccup and the reference must cross a renderer boundary. Preserve the prop conversion caveat: simply wrapping the existing {:article-id 7} recipe camelCases its key to articleId on the React/Reagent side; a single-word id or a deliberate mapping avoids introducing a false difference. For interaction-bearing originals, explicitly supply frame-bound callback contracts at the crossing or preserve their valid frame capture; do not imply the wrapper alone repairs arbitrary old ambient-dispatch closures. Assert the returned :status in executable examples.

Acceptance: the skill sample mirrors the working foreign-reference form in mounted.cljs:1918-1929 and the existing a-foreign-reference-crosses-in-and-compares-green test at test_kit/test/re_frame/fresco/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs:537 onward. A faithful small Reagent original and equivalent candidate compare green; a changed candidate tag/value turns the comparison red. No unmarked Reagent function is shown as a direct Fresco reference head, and the example does not accidentally change inbound prop names.

F3 — P3: scriptless comparison is described as automatically checkpointing every commit

Owned source: skills/reagent-migration/references/procedure.md:219-220: omit :script and "each committed render becomes a checkpoint as you use the screen by hand."

Trigger: after providing valid reference/candidate forms, omit :script and interact with the two mounts, following the skill's instruction without retaining or invoking the returned handle.

Expected from the instruction: every committed change records/computes a comparison and discrepancies become available automatically.

Actual: mounted.cljs:2129-2155 returns {:status :live :reference ... :candidate ... :checkpoint! f :stop! f}. The checkpoint index and checkpoint-difference call live only inside the returned :checkpoint! closure; there is no automatic checkpoint on return or on later commits. Its public contract at :2044-2050 explicitly says per-commit checkpointing and click mirroring are not built. description:

WHY: ui/shell.cljs main-pane renders (case mode-tab :docs [docs-view] :test [test-view variant-id] [framed-canvas]), so selecting the Tests tab UNMOUNTS the canvas and returning to Canvas remounts it. The canvas's component-will-unmount clears canvas-last-run-key, so the remount re-prepares the run (in place, ensure-fresh-frame! -> frames/reset-state!) on the frame reset-variant re-allocated, and every subscription the fresh mount wires is on that live frame. The only UI caller of reset-variant is test_mode/state.cljs run-variant-pane! (the Re-run button and the pane's first-encounter auto-run), and test-view is reachable only from the :test tab. The RHS panels that stay mounted across a Re-run hold no subscribe / frame-provider on the variant frame (dispatch_console.cljc read at source).

MEASURED in headless Chromium (Playwright) against a shadow-cljs compile of :examples/counter-with-stories from the worker tree, variant :story.counter/loaded:
- Canvas before any reset: count 7, one click -> 8 (the instrument clicks and reads the live view).
- Tests tab, pane rendered: canvas sections 0, [data-rf-story-variant-root] 0, [data-test=count] 0. Nothing of the variant view is mounted.
- Auto-run "3 PASSED"; Re-run pressed three times, the ran-at stamp moving each time, still "3 PASSED".
- Back to Canvas: count 7 (fresh run), three clicks -> 8, 9, 10. The canvas re-renders. No page errors.

POSITIVE CONTROL, so the zero above is a statement about the UI path and not a blind probe: calling re_frame.story.runtime.reset_variant directly from the page while the canvas IS mounted leaves the DOM count stuck at 8 across two clicks and logs :rf.error/frame-destroyed twice. The orphaned-reaction hazard the frames/reset-state! docstring describes is real; the Test-mode Re-run simply never reaches it.

NO CHANGE MADE. runtime.cljc / reset-variant untouched (held by the vacpass-a worker at dispatch). The latent hazard stands for any FUTURE caller that runs reset-variant under a mounted canvas; if one appears, this bead's smallest change (drop the destroy! and rely on phase 0's in-place reset) is the right shape, and it is a runtime.cljc edit.

title: story: the step-debugger and the scrubber walk the raw :script, not the compiled plan's script — [:arg], :compose and :plays variants step a different program than the one auto-run
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Source read by the reviewer; re-verify at tip.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:353-356 (variant-play-steps -> (parse-spec (:script body))), play.cljc:255-265 (variant-play-events, same source), consumed at ui/test_mode/stepper_state.cljs:138 and ui/test_mode/state.cljs:86. Contrast plan.cljc:1387-1398:
    script*  (substitute-args script arg-map subs!)
    ;; ... Without this, an [:arg ...] in a play script would reach the dispatched event verbatim.
    scripts* (mapv (fn [p] (update p :script substitute-args arg-map subs!)) scripts)
and plan.cljc:1325-1330 (composed fragments' scripts are prepended to the child's).

For an [:arg k] script the stepper dispatches the placeholder verbatim, the exact case the compiler comment forbids. spec/009-Test-Mode.md:409-420 claims "The debugger and the auto-run path are therefore equivalent".

WHY IT MATTERS: the README's headline :test feature steps a different program than the one it auto-ran for any variant using [:arg], :compose or :plays, the three things spec/017 promotes.

SMALLEST CHANGE: make both readers plan-sourced: (-> (rf.story.plan/variant-plan variant-id {:run-args ...}) (get-in [:world :scripts 0 :script])), threading the shell's run-opts (the same ones prepare-variant receives). notes:
VERDICT (worker playstep-a, 2026-09-13 AUSEST) — CONFIRMED AT SOURCE AT TIP AND FIXED in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc` only. PR #9718 (branch `worker/playstep-a`, one commit on trunk `e88f4e80fb`).

DEFECT, as described: `variant-play-steps` and `variant-play-events` parsed the registered body's raw `(:script body)`, while `runtime/run-phase-4!` executes `(mapcat :script (auto-runnable-plays (get-in plan [:world :scripts])))` of the compiled plan. So an `[:arg]` script stepped its placeholder verbatim (and its scrubber events matched no epoch), a `:compose`d fragment's script was missing, and a `:plays` variant stepped nothing.

FIX: one private `stepped-program` returns that exact runtime expression, compiled through `rf.story.plan/variant-plan` with `{:run-args (rf.story.args/run-arg-layers variant-id opts)}`, exactly as `runtime/prepare-context` compiles. Both readers read it; `begin-stepper!` seeds from it. Details:
- When nothing auto-runs it yields the PRIMARY compiled play, so an `:auto-run? false` script can still be stepped by hand. `story_play_test`'s `:story.stepper/full` depends on this.
- An unregistered variant still yields `[]`, the pre-fix contract.
- `variant-play-events` degrades to `[]` on a plan-construction error (ex-data `:where 'rf.story/variant-plan`), so the scrubber's `store-result!` cannot throw away a run result when an `[:arg]` resolves only through an active mode or cell override.
- `variant-play-steps`, `variant-play-events` and `begin-stepper!` gain an `opts` arity (the `run-variant` opts map).
- play requiring plan and args adds no require cycle: none of plan's direct deps require play, and the JVM lane loads green.

WHERE THIS DIFFERED FROM THE BEAD'S SMALLEST CHANGE: the bead suggested `[:world :scripts 0 :script]`. The runtime executes ALL auto-runnable plays concatenated, so a `:plays` variant with two auto-run plays would still diverge under a scripts-0 read. The fix uses the runtime's own expression instead; the `:plays` witness has two auto-run plays and one manual play to pin exactly that.

FENCES: `execute-play!`, `dispatch-one!` and `read-assertions-after` are untouched (rf2-tb75 owns them). Not one of rf2-fzbj.3's findings: its only step-debugger mention defers to the closed rf2-k6y2.

- A plain `:script` variant is the control.
- Own namespace: exit 0, 9 tests / 31 assertions.
- Raw read planted back into `stepped-program`: exit 1, 13 failures across exactly the seven witnesses. Control and unregistered stayed green, and totals were unchanged at 9 / 31. Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object.
- Full `jvm-tools-story` on the final base: exit 0, 1923 tests / 7078 assertions, 0 failures.
- The CLJS lane and the story-xray-browser pane gate are CI-verified on the PR; the worktree carries no node_modules.

RESIDUAL, fenced and filed as rf2-ad25: the UI call sites still use the 1-arity readers. `ui/test_mode/state.cljs` `store-result!` does not thread the shell's opts to `variant-play-events`; `stepper_state.cljs` `begin!` is self-consistent (it prepares with no opts). title: Incomplete: Managed FX inspector identities do not distinguish simultaneous mounts
description:

That second half is the one a distinctness-only witness would have passed, and this item named it as
required acceptance. It was measured, not assumed.

THE REPAIR is the shipped `mount-app-db-diff!` shape the item named -- an optional `:instance-id`
threaded through the public facade, the `ManagedFxList-bridge`, the `ManagedFxList` boundary and the
four `edn/inspect-view` sites -- not a new identity framework. Record identity and disclosure
semantics are untouched, with rows asserting both directions.

TWO THINGS ESTABLISHED HERE THAT THE NEXT PANEL SHOULD REUSE RATHER THAN REDERIVE:

  1. ONE QUALIFIER DOES BOTH HALVES HERE, WHERE app-db NEEDS TWO. `edn-widget/inspect-view` builds
     the boundary's `:mount-id` AND its `:panel-id` from ONE node-key, and this panel passes no
     `:site-id`, so the widget's effective-id falls back to the mount-id. Qualifying the node-key
     therefore separates the lifecycle key, the measured-width slot and the expansion/zoom identity
     together. `app-db-diff` needs two because `value-body` composes its `:mount-id` and `:site-id`
     separately. A reader arriving from rf2-t3fz will expect to qualify a `:site-id` as well; here
     that is unnecessary.

  2. THE BRIDGE TOKENISES BEFORE THE CROSSING, carrying rf2-4bsq's landed repair rather than
     re-deriving it. Reagent converts a named prop value with `cljs.core/name`, which DROPS a
     keyword's namespace -- so `:left/list` and `:right/list` would both arrive as `"list"` and
     restore the very collision this repair removes.

SCOPE WIDENED ONCE, CORRECTLY: three spec sentences stated `:instance-id` was `mount-app-db-diff!`'s
ALONE (`tools/xray/spec/007-UX-IA.md`, `008-Embedding-Contract.md`, `API.md`), which this change
makes false. They were corrected with the `panels.cljs` ns docstring -- the same coordinated set
rf2-s2g7 updated when the opt first shipped. Shipping without them would have left the spec
contradicting the code it describes.

ONE DESIGN QUESTION WAS ROUTED BACK AND RULED, AND THE RULING STANDS: keep the duplicated
`managed-fx-template/instance-token` rather than calling `app-db-diff-state/instance-token`. The
shared function's throw names the WRONG PANEL, and sharing would couple managed-fx to a sibling
panel's state namespace for a string normaliser while both panels migrate on independent schedules.
Twelve duplicated lines is cheaper than that edge. The full reasoning is in this bead's notes; a
third copy, not a second, is the signal to promote it.

GATES, every number the runner's own: `test:browser` 1 pre-fix (the reproduction) then 0 post-fix
(940/5200); `test:cljs` 0 (11678/58534); xray JVM 0 (1278/6130); kondo, splint, alias-dialect,
api-manifest gen/xray-spec/api-md, doc-slugs, readme-links, test-lane-bijection, retired-spellings
and keyword-catalogue-drift all 0.

TWO HARNESS DISAGREEMENTS WERE MEASURED IN PASSING and are recorded in the notes: the harness
reported exit 0 for the pre-fix run whose captured exit file said 1 -- the run whose whole purpose
was to be red -- and reported completion while no exit file existed, the orphan still running and
writing exit 0 later. Both are why the captured number is the one that counts.

title: Incomplete rf2-qhoj repair: type-changing inspector diffs lack a Fresco regression test
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9606 (61d475f93382427e464f190b8e7a4dac7d3e3225). The one-token runtime repair is correct, but its explicitly deferred regression coverage has no separately trackable open owner.

rf2-qhoj is CLOSED. Its close reason says the coverage gap was deliberately withheld as separate work and remains described on that closed Bead. Its description identifies the required witness: render edn-inspector-view through Fresco with a leaf type change, such as nil -> string, or drive that shape in the existing PR-smoke tier. The #9606 body likewise says this coverage was not added. A fresh census of all 24 literal-open Beads found no exact owner; the broad Xray epic is not one.

Why this matters: the previous [mini prior 40] form returned a plain function as a hiccup head. Only Fresco's codec rejects that form (HD-016). A nil-to-string diff reached it and unmounted the entire Xray root, while the regular number-to-number smoke and hiccup inspection tests stayed green. The merged change calls (mini prior 40), but those existing tests still would not detect a recurrence.

Verified at the landing: edn_inspector_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs contains W1-W5 (paint/frame, liveness, trace isolation, teardown and mount independence), with no :before or diff/type-change input. The app_db_diff unit helpers inspect the boundary's props or shallow panel-tree hiccup instead of rendering the inspector body through the codec. The new #9606 tests exercise testid uniqueness, not the type-change branch.

Add ONE focused regression to the existing Fresco DOM coverage (or the equivalent existing smoke lane). Reuse its frame/mount helpers. No new test framework, broader widget audit or runtime redesign is needed. Preserve rf2-qhoj's closed ruling; this Bead owns only its remaining explicit test obligation.
acceptance_criteria: A normal CI lane renders the real edn-inspector-view through Fresco for a before/after pair containing a leaf type change (nil -> string is sufficient), and asserts the rendered diff/prior-value content and live mounted inspector, rather than merely inspecting returned hiccup or assuming no error from a non-vacuous mount. Show that temporarily restoring the former plain-function-head form makes this regression fail through the actual codec path; restore the call and show it passes. Keep the test scoped to this already fixed crash.
close_reason:
Delivered by PR #9616, merged to trunk at ce09d020b6 (rebase). One regression row,
`w6-a-leaf-type-change-renders-through-the-fresco-codec`, in
`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector_fresco_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.

RED-TO-GREEN PROVEN BY EXIT STATUS WITH BOTH CONTROLS, not asserted:
  call form (committed)   -> BROWSER_EXIT=0, 898 tests / 4962 assertions, 0 failures
  pre-fix bracket form    -> BROWSER_EXIT=1, 898 tests / 4962 assertions, 5 failures
Totals identical either side, so the plant caused a RUNTIME failure and not a load error, and
all 5 failures are W6's own assertions with no other namespace moving. The red's signature is
the incident's: a pageerror naming the edn-inspector component, every assertion reading
`actual: (not (some? nil))` INCLUDING the precondition on the host panel div OUTSIDE the
widget -- the whole root unmounting, exactly as rf2-qhoj described. Not a hollow gate: delete
the signal and the fault remains visible.

THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE ROW, and it corrects a natural assumption about this branch:
`nil -> "a string"` CANNOT reach the type-change branch. `engine/type-change?` is set only for
a container KIND FLIP, and the engine's own `yucxn-number-to-string-is-not-type-change` row
pins scalar->scalar as not one. The incident's nil -> 20 KiB string reached it only because
the SIZE WALK had already elided that string into `{:rf.size/large-elided ...}`, which is a
MAP. The two classifiers then disagree ON PURPOSE: the engine reads the sentinel as a
container (nil -> container is R7) while the inspector's `collection-kind` reads
`:sentinel-large`, which its `container?` excludes -- so it renders as a LEAF and reaches the
`:modified` + type-change branch. That disagreement is what keeps the branch live; a future
reader who "fixes" the classifiers into agreement would silently retire the branch this test
covers. Recorded in the test docstring and the PR body as well as here.

The worker declined the AI-attribution trailers its harness asked for, per CLAUDE.md.
