title: Xray-substrate SPIKE: build one real panel BOTH ways, on two adapters, and report
description:
CONTEXT IS ON THE PARENT EPIC rf2-k97c. Read it first — it is the durable record (the
analysis lived in an untracked ai/findings/ tree and is gone). Line numbers drift; verify.

PURPOSE: settle, by experiment, which of the epic's two candidate designs to build. Nobody
should choose from source reading alone; both were argued to a standstill that way.

BUILD ONE REAL PANEL BOTH WAYS. Not a toy. Use the App-DB inspector or the event spine —
something with real focus/expansion/filter machinery and real subscriptions. Keep the
production registry, image seating, trace collection and epoch code.

  ARM A — Xray owns a stock-Reagent root; the panel's subscription reads go through a
          tool-local binding: subscribe -> rf.interop/activate-derived-value! -> baseline
          deref -> add-watch -> rf.interop/add-on-dispose! -> re-wire on invalidation.
          (interop.cljs:85 and :121 are public; the activate call no-ops on the React-hook
          spine.)
  ARM B — the same panel re-authored in Hicasso, mounted through Hicasso's root API
          (hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:252 createRoot), reusing its collector.

RUN EACH ARM ON TWO ADAPTERS: reagent-slim FIRST (it stresses demand-driven activation
across different view machinery, and the existing foreign-root test seats stock Reagent, not
slim), then UIx or Hicasso (to prove escape from the element-shaped mount path).

THE WORKFLOW TO EXERCISE, in one sitting, with TWO application frames carrying
distinguishable values so wrong targeting is observable:
  open on seeded evidence -> dispatch an application event and observe the updated
  spine/value -> stop application activity, then expand/filter the inspector -> select an
  earlier epoch and restore it into ONE chosen frame while the other stays unchanged ->
  unmount -> reopen -> update the application again.

OBSERVE DOM CHANGES AND READER/LISTENER BASELINES, not merely the absence of exceptions.
FIRST PAINT PROVES ALMOST NOTHING — the whole point is what happens on the second update
and on teardown.

RECORD, per arm and adapter:
  * did the panel update after a real dependency change?
  * did frame targeting hold (the other frame untouched)?
  * did unmount release watches/listeners (no retained subscription, no leak)? Compare
    baselines before and after.
  * did Xray invoke the host adapter's rendering entry at any point? (It must not.)
  * did any Xray activity appear in the APPLICATION's epoch :renders? (It must not — see the
    rf2-tqlmq leak on the epic.)
  * how many call sites did the arm actually touch, and of what kind (mechanical vs
    semantic)?

FALSIFIED IF an arm requires a second adapter installation, fails to update after a real
dependency change, cannot preserve frame targeting or callback behaviour, or cannot keep
tool activity out of application evidence without substantial new ownership machinery. A
broad need for compatibility wrappers throughout an arm also counts against it.

DELIVERABLE: a written comparison on this bead (bd update --append-notes) with the six
observations above per arm, the measured touched-site counts, and a recommendation. This is
a SPIKE — throwaway branches are fine, do not open a PR against main, and do not delete the
denylist here.

RE-MEASURE FIRST, do not trust the epic's counts: over tools/xray/src/ the epic records 125
(rf/subscribe sites in 37 files and 51 rf/reg-view in 35. Take a positive control and a
negative control; grep -iF ABORTS on this box (exit 134, silent), so never use that flag
pair.
notes:
YOUR REPORT IS THE INPUT TO A MECHANICAL DECISION RULE (rf2-k97c.2), not to a discussion. The rule keys on: (a) whether Arm A's binding stayed within the four public interop calls or grew toward hicasso/impl/collector.cljs; (b) Arm A's MEASURED touched-site count and what fraction needed per-site judgement rather than substitution; (c) whether either arm leaked tool activity into the application's epoch records; (d) Arm B's measured touched-site count. REPORT THOSE FOUR NUMBERS EXPLICITLY. A report that omits them cannot be ruled on and will be sent back.
=== SPIKE REPORT (rf2-k97c.1) — part 1 of 3: the four decision numbers ===

Both arms were BUILT AND RUN in a browser, each on TWO host adapters
(reagent-slim FIRST, then Hicasso — the bead's "UIx or Hicasso" option,
chosen because Hicasso is the kind the denylist newly names and the one
`docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` teaches as the default install).
The panel is the PRODUCTION App-DB inspector. The production registry,
trace collector, epoch collector, browser-API exports, image seating and
first-mount hooks all ran exactly as `preload.cljs` runs them; the ONLY
step skipped was `mount/boot-on-runtime-ready!`, the auto-open that calls
the host adapter's `:render` — owning the root is the subject.

Worker-worktree guard ran and exited 0 before any edit.

Everything below is MEASURED in a driven browser session, not reasoned
from source. Instrument controls are stated with each number.

------------------------------------------------------------------
(a) DID ARM A's BINDING STAY WITHIN THE FOUR PUBLIC INTEROP CALLS?

NO. It needed TWO additions, each forced by a measured failure, and it
still did not reach every read site. It did NOT grow the collector's
reaping / dirty-batching machinery — but the one collector behaviour it
lacks (re-wire AND NOTIFY on invalidation) is exactly what produced its
stale-value failure.

V1 was exactly the bead's four calls — subscribe ->
`rf.interop/activate-derived-value!` -> one baseline deref -> `add-watch`
-> `rf.interop/add-on-dispose!` — mirroring each subscription into a
stock-Reagent `r/atom` so Reagent tracks it.

ADDITION 1 — a FIFTH public op, `rf/unsubscribe`, plus a keyed
[frame query-v] table so the acquire happens once instead of once per
render. MEASURED on the Hicasso host with V1: the `:rf/xray` sub-cache
ref-count total climbed 22 -> 25 -> 32 across renders and did NOT fall on
unmount. The cause is stated in `re-frame.subs/unsubscribe`'s own
docstring — "Reagent views auto-dispose via the reaction lifecycle" — and
the reaction lifecycle in question is the INSTALLED ADAPTER's, which
cannot see a stock-Reagent render. With V2 the same cycle released to 3
entries / 6 refs (the residue is the 3 injected reads the binding does
not reach; see (b)) and on the matched slim root to 0 / 0.

ADDITION 2 — a RENDERER SWITCH at the tool root, which is not a
subscription concern at all. On the reagent-slim host a stock-Reagent
root FAILS OUTRIGHT: `:adapter/current-component` routes to
`reagent2.core/current-component`, which returns nil during a
stock-Reagent render, so `re-frame.views/current-frame` resolves nil and
EVERY `reg-view` in the tool raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`. Panel
never painted; 0 DOM nodes in the tool host across the whole workflow.
Repaired by mounting Arm A on a reagent-slim root instead
(`reagent2.dom.client`), which costs no new dependency — `tools/xray/
deps.edn` already declares BOTH Reagent builds — but does mean the tool
must branch on the host's adapter kind at its own root.

This is the epic's coupling (2), and `rf/frame-provider` does not solve
it: that component is `re-frame.views`' own (a `:r>` interop head), not
adapter-routed, so it renders fine — the failure is one level down, in
the routed `:adapter/current-component` hook that `current-frame` reads
through. On an ELEMENT-SHAPED host the same hook is not consulted at all
(`function-component-current-frame` reads the shared React context slot
directly), which is why Arm A paints on Hicasso and not on slim.

------------------------------------------------------------------
(b) ARM A's MEASURED TOUCHED-SITE COUNT, AND THE JUDGEMENT FRACTION

On the panel actually built (the App-DB inspector, closure = 14 files /
8,423 lines):

  2 sites   `@(rf/subscribe q)` -> `(obs/<sub q)` in
            `panels/app_db_diff.cljs`.  PURE SUBSTITUTION.
  3 sites   `@(subscribe q)` — the INJECTED noun `reg-view` binds
            lexically — in `views/edn_inspector.cljs` (three reads: the
            expansion slot, the zoom slot, the widths slot).  NOT
            reachable by substitution: they sit inside a FORM-2 inner fn
            and carry the reg-view's render-time frame capture.
  1 site    the tool root's renderer switch.
  1 site    the release call.

  => 5 subscription-read sites, of which 3 (60%) needed per-site
     judgement, plus 2 non-read sites.

LEAVING THOSE 3 UNCONVERTED IS NOT COSMETIC. It killed Arm A's own
interactions on the Hicasso host: four successive expand/collapse toggle
clicks produced NO DOM change and NO console error — silent — because the
toggle's write landed in `:rf/xray`'s app-db but the reader
(`@(subscribe [expansion-slot])`) returns a spine derived value that
stock Reagent does not track. That is the epic's coupling (3) arriving at
precisely the sites the binding did not cover.

TREE-WIDE on the same rule: 118 mechanical `@(rf/subscribe` + 6 judgement
`@(subscribe` = 124 read sites, 4.8% judgement. TREAT THAT FRACTION AS AN
UNDERSTATEMENT OF EFFORT: the 6 concentrate in the two form-2 widgets
(`views/edn_inspector.cljs`, `views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs`) that every
panel renders, and they are the sites whose omission breaks interactions
silently.

------------------------------------------------------------------
(c) DID EITHER ARM LEAK TOOL ACTIVITY INTO APPLICATION EVIDENCE?

TWO INSTRUMENTS. Only the second is informative, and I am reporting the
first as uninformative rather than as a green.

INSTRUMENT 1 — the application frames' epoch `:renders`, read through
`rf/epoch-history`. Result: EMPTY in every configuration — INCLUDING the
deliberately mis-scoped POSITIVE CONTROL (Arm A mounted under
`[rf/frame-provider {:frame :above}]`, the exact rf2-tqlmq mistake). A
control that does not fire makes the zeros vacuous. The reason is
structural: `:renders` rows are captured inside a dispatch cascade, and a
tool paint scheduled on an animation frame lands outside every epoch.

INSTRUMENT 2 — the trace stream, via `rf/register-listener! :trace`,
counting `:rf.view/*` ops naming the arm panels. Its positive control
FIRES (2 events for the mis-scoped mount). Measured:

  Arm B, Hicasso host      0 tool render events
  Arm B, reagent-slim host 0 tool render events
  Arm A, Hicasso host      6 events for `:xspike.arm-a/Panel`, every one
                           tagged `:frame nil`
  Arm A, slim host,
    stock-Reagent root     2 such events (and the panel does not work)
  Arm A, slim host,
    reagent-slim root      0

`:frame nil` matters: `re-frame.trace/emit!`'s frame-level gate
(`tagged-frame-trace-disabled?`) suppresses an event tagged with the
trace-disabled `:rf/xray` frame, and a nil-framed event slips past it.
Xray's own `trace_collector/collect-trace!` routes frameless events to
its `:ungrouped` secondary ring — so on the element-shaped host Arm A's
own renders land in the evidence buffer Xray reports from. Not the
rf2-tqlmq epoch leak; a milder sibling, in the trace stream instead.

  ANSWER: neither arm put anything in the APPLICATION's epoch records as
  measured (uninformative instrument). On the instrument that does
  discriminate, ARM B contributed ZERO on both adapters and ARM A
  contributed 6 frameless render events on the element-shaped host.

Separately, and with a live control: `hostRenders` — a spy on
`re-frame.substrate.adapter/render`, the substrate's single public paint
door — read 0 for BOTH arms on BOTH adapters, while a deliberate direct
call moved it 0 -> 1 on both pages. NEITHER ARM INVOKED THE HOST
ADAPTER'S RENDERING ENTRY.

------------------------------------------------------------------
(d) ARM B's MEASURED TOUCHED-SITE COUNT

On the same panel:

  1 site   `rf/reg-view` -> `h/defview` for the panel root, positional
           arg vector -> the one props map `defview` takes.
  2 sites  `@(rf/subscribe q)` -> `(h/sub q)`.
  1 site   the ONE hiccup HEAD the section body emits — `value-body`'s
           `[ei/edn-inspector v opts]`. The other TEN section-renderer
           fns needed NO change: they are plain hiccup PRODUCERS called
           by application, never heads, so Hicasso's "a plain function in
           head position is a loud error" does not touch them.
  1 site   `rf/reg-view` -> `h/defview` for the edn-inspector widget
           itself — SEMANTIC and large. It is a FORM-2 component whose
           outer body allocates a per-mount id, a ResizeObserver and a
           projection cache in three closure atoms; Hicasso boundaries
           are real React function components and have no form-2. In THIS
           panel the per-mount id was replaceable by the stable
           `:site-id` the App-DB panel already passes, so the port needed
           no `h/reg-state`; a panel that passes no site-id would.
  3 sites  the injected `@(subscribe` reads -> `h/sub`.
  7 sites  `(dispatch-fn ...)` callbacks -> intent vectors at `on-*`
           props (a `defview` binds no `dispatch`).

  => 15 sites on the panel, 2 pure substitution and 13 judgement.

TREE-WIDE on the same rule: 49 `reg-view` registrations + 69 reg-view
hiccup-HEAD use sites (positional -> props at each) + 6 injected
`subscribe` + 109 injected `dispatch` + 29 `(dispatch-fn` captures
= 262 sites across roughly 40 files, essentially all judgement.

THE EPIC'S "~51 SEMANTIC VIEW REWRITES" IS AN UNDERCOUNT BY ABOUT 5x. It
counted REGISTRATIONS only and missed the surface that disappears WITH
`reg-view`: the lexically injected `dispatch` / `subscribe` nouns the
macro binds for the whole view body. Those are 115 further sites, and
they are invisible to any census keyed on `rf/`-qualified names.
=== SPIKE REPORT (rf2-k97c.1) — part 2 of 3: the six observations ===

The workflow was driven end to end in one sitting per configuration, by
a scripted browser session: open on seeded evidence -> dispatch an
application event -> bump the OTHER frame -> stop application activity
and expand/collapse inside the inspector -> restore an earlier epoch into
ONE frame -> unmount -> drive the app while the tool is down -> reopen ->
update the application again. Two frames carried distinguishable values
(`:above` counter 100, `:below` counter 900) so wrong targeting is
visible at a glance.

------------------------------------------------------------------
ARM A — stock-Reagent root + tool-local binding — HOST reagent-slim

1 update after a real dependency change:  N/A — NEVER PAINTED.
2 frame targeting held:                    N/A.

title: spec/006 + 016: write the :inputs discriminator - three registrars, THREE callback contracts (reg-sub vector / reg-flow spread / reg-resource-scope named map + 2-arity resolver); prose only, does NOT reopen vector-vs-map
description:
The one overlap wave 3 left standing: `:inputs` is a key name shared by three registrars with no
written discriminator, so an author who meets it three times meets three contracts and no rule.
That fails rf2-kuky's own bar — "a dual is legitimate only when its discriminator is written down;
unwritten discriminators are option soup wearing a uniform."

Ruled 2026-09-09 at the epic closeout: WRITE THE DISCRIMINATOR. Prose only.

THE THREE CONTRACTS (all verified at source 2026-09-09 — these are DIFFERENT OPERATIONS, not
competing doors to one result):

  reg-sub
    `:inputs` declares  : ordered subscription QUERY VECTORS (a literal vector, or produced by an
                          input-fn run once at materialization)
    callback receives   : `[values-vector query-v]` — ALWAYS a vector at every arity: `[]`, `[v]`,
                          `[a b]`
    source              : `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:694-704`

  reg-flow
    `:inputs` declares  : ordered frame-state PATHS
    callback receives   : SEPARATE POSITIONAL VALUES — flows SPREAD
    source              : `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:326`,
                          `(apply (:derive flow) new-inputs)`

  reg-resource-scope
    `:inputs` declares  : a NAMED MAP of db-source descriptors, `{input-name [:db <rf-path>]}`
    callback receives   : `[values-map ctx]` — TWO arity; `ctx` is reserved and passed literal nil
    source              : `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:495`
                          (`((:resolve spec) in-vals nil)`), with `eval-inputs` at `:431` building
                          `{input-name resolved-value}`

So `reg-sub` and `reg-flow` share a DECLARATION shape but NOT a callback contract, and
`reg-resource-scope` shares neither. The discriminator to write: `reg-sub` / `reg-flow` `:inputs` is a
POSITIONAL DEPENDENCY LIST (order is the contract); `reg-resource-scope` `:inputs` is a NAMED ARGUMENT
MAP for a resolver fn (names are the contract).

WHAT MOVES:
  - `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` — one compact note beside the existing `:inputs` vector paragraph
    at `006:1078`, tabling all three contracts.
  - `spec/016-Resources.md` — a cross-reference back to it from the named-resolver `:inputs` grammar.

CONSTRAINTS ON THE PROSE (each of these was an error in the source dossier; do not reproduce them):
  - Do NOT write that `reg-flow` delivers a vector. It spreads via `apply`.
  - Do NOT justify the split by "arity is small". That is not the reason; the reason is that the three
    declare different things (queries / paths / named db sources).
  - Do NOT imply flows consume subscription queries. They consume frame-state paths.
  - Do NOT touch, restate or pre-empt `spec/013-Flows.md:566`'s vector-vs-map deferral. Its trigger
    (N >= 3 real flows at 4-or-more `:inputs` bitten by positional-destructure fragility) is written,
    falsifiable and UNFIRED — 15 static-4+ subs exist, 14 of them Xray's, none with a measured
    positional bug. The note must read as documenting a ruled dual, never as settling that question.

NON-GOALS: NO code, NO tests, NO `spec/API.md`, NO `spec/api-manifest*.edn` sidecars, NO manifest
regeneration. No public name moves, so the API.md/manifest holding does not move.

HOT ZONE: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` is a listed hot-zone file — SINGLE TOUCHER, sequence against
any other bead holding it.

title: attribution guard: the beads-named job is what reds when the attribution step fires (rf2-uo5f option (d))
description:
CARRIED OUT OF rf2-uo5f, which closed on its option (b/c) half (the compliance-statement false positive, PR #9385). This is option (d) and it is UNCHANGED and still fenced.

THE DEFECT. The attribution CI arm runs as a STEP inside test.yml's job named 'Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)'. When the attribution step fires, THAT is the check that goes red — so a worker or mayor reading the name goes looking for a tracker file in the diff. That is exactly what happened on PR #9330, which touched no .beads path at all. Same nominate-by-path-not-by-job-name trap CLAUDE.md already records for the two link gates.

THE FENCE, from rf2-uo5f's own ruling note, re-test it rather than re-deriving it: renaming a CI job renames the CHECK. If that check is required by branch protection, the protection rule still names the OLD string, so every open PR waits for ever on a check that will never report again — and it moves the clause-5 band mid-session. So this is dispatchable ONLY at fleet-zero with no open PRs, and its brief must read the branch-protection required-checks list BEFORE the rename and update it in the same change. It is small.

PARTIAL MITIGATION ALREADY LANDED (PR #9385): CLAUDE.md > Git Conventions now says in prose that the check that reds is named for beads and says nothing about attribution, so a reader at least has the pointer. That is documentation, not the fix.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-09-08 05:0x AUSEST — HALF THIS BEAD'S FENCE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. Re-priced rather than re-asserted, as the bead itself asks ("re-test it rather than re-deriving it").

THE FENCE AS WRITTEN HAS TWO LIMBS:
  (1) renaming a CI job renames the CHECK; if branch protection REQUIRES the old string, every open PR waits for ever on a check that will never report;
  (2) it moves the clause-5 band mid-session.

LIMB (1) IS REFUTED. main is NOT PROTECTED AT ALL. Measured: gh api repos/day8/re-frame2/branches/main/protection returns exit 1, HTTP 404, message "Branch not protected", and the response body carries only {documentation_url, message, status} with required_status_checks ABSENT. That is a positive 404 rather than an empty list from an unreadable endpoint — I checked the exit code and stderr precisely because an empty list would have been the false-zero shape this project keeps recording. There is no required-checks list naming the old string, so no PR can strand on one, and the instruction that a brief must "read the branch-protection required-checks list BEFORE the rename and update it in the same change" has nothing to read and nothing to update.

LIMB (2) SURVIVES, BUT WEAKER THAN WRITTEN. A rename does not change the check COUNT, so the band (a count, currently 87) does not move. What changes is SET MEMBERSHIP: a PR whose runs predate the rename carries the old name while the trunk matrix carries the new one, and clause 5 computes the check set against the trunk's CURRENT matrix. That is a real but transient mismatch which resolves as each PR re-runs. So fleet-zero remains the tidy time to do this — it is a convenience, not a hard blocker, and it should no longer be described as "dispatchable ONLY at fleet-zero".

NET: this bead is smaller and safer than its own text says. It is a job rename in .github/workflows/test.yml (the job at :1244, name "Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)") so that a red from the ATTRIBUTION step is not reported under a beads-named check. Still worth doing at a quiet moment with few open PRs, but the catastrophic limb is gone.

title: [implementation/adapters/uix] Reacquire mounted subscription hooks after their cached reaction is evicted
description:
## Finding
A mounted UIx use-subscribe hook keeps reading its disposed committed reaction after normal subscription re-registration. The cache invalidation succeeds, but the hook never takes the next subscription needed to rebuild the live source. A same-component/same-query rerender remains bound to the old body, and later app-db writes no longer notify it.

## Source and supported causal reproduction
Reviewed snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; relevant files unchanged on mayor HEAD b1facc0dbf99871adf68604a0d5c1170b67e7809.
- implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:47-56 supplies native hooks to make-react-spine; :140-146 exports its use-subscribe.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3080-3104 stabilizes the hook key solely on frame keyword and query value. The render snapshot memo and subscribe-fn memo depend on that key (:3186-3206, :3347-3436).
- subscribe-fn stores the durable reaction in committed-ref and attaches only an ordinary value watch (:3387-3435). No disposal/cache-replacement listener reacquires it. get-snap chooses that committed handle whenever its key matches (:3301-3325), even if cache disposal has invalidated it.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc:347-388 removes all affected cache entries on reg-sub replacement and disposes their reactions. The React derived container's -dispose at spine.cljs:934-958 removes source wires and clears outward watchers; deref-derived at :809-815 still runs the old closed-over recompute.

Minimal supported browser sequence (source-causal proof, not executed): install uix/adapter, make a live frame :review/app with app-db {:n 1}, register :review/n as (fn [db _] (:n db)); mount one unchanged defui Probe calling (uix/use-subscribe [:review/n]) under ($ uix/frame-provider {:frame :review/app}). After its committed subscription is established, re-register :review/n as (fn [db _] (+ 100 (:n db))). Rerender the same Probe instance by changing an unrelated parent prop, without changing query/frame or unmounting it. Expected current value 101 and continued updates; actual getSnapshot dereferences the old disposed reaction and yields 1. Dispatch an event setting n=2: the disposed handle has no source watches or outward callback, so this component no longer updates. A newly mounted independent consumer can correctly subscribe to a rebuilt v2 cache entry; the stale mount does not.

This is the ordinary live reload path: spec/001-Registration.md:271-286 says the system stays live and caches invalidate on sub re-registration; docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:89-107 promises the hook returns current subscription value and rerenders on change. examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-114 preserves a root and frame across after-load renders. No requirement to reuse a manually disposed reaction is assumed; the hook itself retains it across framework-owned eviction.

A related ownership edge belongs to this same repair: the eventual committed cleanup uses address-only unsubscribe (:3435), so after an independent consumer rebuilt the same key, stale cleanup can decrement that successor's reference. The provisional path already uses unsubscribe-if-reaction for this precise stale-holder problem (subs.cljc:2479-2501); apply equivalent exact ownership to committed teardown.

## Impact and smallest repair
Live-editing a subscription in an otherwise mounted UIx app can leave the panel on the old computation and permanently deaf to new events until it is remounted. Keep the hook's committed source current across framework cache eviction/replacement and make its release exact-reaction-owned. Reuse the existing subscription/cache lifecycle seam; preserve commit-owned durable acquisition, provisional reaping, stable snapshots and stable same-key steady state. Do not fix this by remounting every component, disabling memoization globally, or acquiring a fresh reaction on every getSnapshot call.

## Dedupe
rf2-4lp1 owns missing cache invalidation on frame generation changes. This finding starts after successful invalidation and concerns the UIx mounted holder; it is not that fix. rf2-sqhjtu is not present in the current tracker (show reports not found); historical commit 6eca9cd056ae5fae34e2303e953a22872c045a04 and its current react_shared_suite.cljs:4998-5165 test repair first-mount provisional-vs-committed selection, not eviction of the committed reaction. Active rf2-kuky.57 renames use-subscribe to use-sub and removes unused variants; rf2-kuky.62 changes frame resolution. Neither changes this acquisition lifecycle.

## Verification limits
Exact source/control-flow trace only; no CLJS/browser compilation, runtime test, dependency mutation, or implementation edit was performed.
acceptance_criteria: Mount a real UIx hook consumer, replace its reg-sub body without unmounting/changing its frame/query, and prove both an unrelated parent rerender and subsequent app-db update use the replacement and remain reactive. Assert component identity survives, and compare with a new independent consumer. After eviction and successor acquisition, unmounting the original consumer must not decrement/dispose the successor's ref. Cover replacement plus explicit cache clear if both share the seam. Preserve ordinary same-query stable watch/ref counts, query/frame retarget, StrictMode and abandoned-render cleanup; a pre-fix control must show the old body/no notifications.

WHY NOT DONE, STATED PLAINLY. This bead was dispatched alongside rf2-oyrj (P2)
and rf2-ytyq (P3) as "three adapter bugs, three different adapters, otherwise
independent". Those two are genuinely confined to `implementation/adapters/**`
and both landed with failing-first evidence. THIS ONE IS NOT AN ADAPTER CHANGE:
the UIx adapter file is a thin re-export (`use-subscribe` is
`(:use-subscribe spine-fns)`), and every construct the bead names as defective
lives in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs` — outside the
dispatched surface, and the most safety-critical file in the repository. Landing
it half-done would be worse than not landing it, so it is reported rather than
attempted. What follows is the located seam, so a re-dispatch starts here rather
than from scratch.

PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE (the bead is accurate).

- "Relevant files unchanged on mayor HEAD b1facc0dbf" — STILL HELD at base
  90e9b0008a for all three cited files (uix adapter, spine.cljs, subs/cache.cljc);
  the diff is empty. Note the UIx adapter HAS moved recently for other reasons
  (the `client-root` / `render!` / `unmount!` trio landed in 5fde90a5b4), but not
  in a way that touches this lifecycle.
- The mechanism is real and reads exactly as filed. `subscribe-fn` is
  `use-callback`-memoized on `#js [stable-key]`, and `stable-key` is derived
  solely from frame keyword + query value — so React calls it ONCE per
  (frame, query) target and never again for the life of that target. It takes the
  durable `rf.subs/subscribe` ref, publishes `#js [stable-key committed]` into
  `committed-ref`, and adds an ordinary value `add-watch` on that one reaction.
  Nothing re-acquires. When `invalidate-sub-on-replace!` evicts and disposes that
  reaction on reg-sub replacement, the reaction's `-dispose` clears its outward
  watchers, so `on-change` can never fire again (the component goes permanently
  deaf), while `get-snap` still finds a key-MATCHING entry in `committed-ref` and
  derefs the disposed handle (the component keeps showing the old body). Both
  halves of the bead's expected/actual pair follow from the code.
- The ownership edge is real too: the committed cleanup calls
  `rf.subs/unsubscribe stable-frame-kw stable-query-v` — ADDRESS-only. After an
  eviction and a successor's rebuild, that address names the SUCCESSOR's entry,
  so a late cleanup decrements a reference it does not own.

THE SEAM TO REUSE — this is the useful part, and it is NOT the one a reader
reaches for first. `re-frame.subs.cache/emit-dispose!` looks like the disposal
notification, and it is NOT usable: it is a `rf.trace/emit!` wrapped in
`(when rf.interop/debug-enabled?)`, so it is dead-code-eliminated from production
CLJS bundles. A correctness fix hung off it would work in dev and silently not
exist in a release build.

The production-safe seam is `re-frame.interop/add-on-dispose!` — the documented
cross-substrate teardown contract (`:adapter/add-on-dispose!` in the late-bind
directory, with `re-frame.disposable/-add-on-dispose` as the CLJS protocol
method). `re-frame.disposable`'s own docstring names UIx as one of the adapters
that wire it, so it is available on exactly the substrate this bead is about.

SHAPE OF THE REPAIR (not implemented, not gate-tested — treat as a design, not a
finding). Inside `subscribe-fn`'s closure, replace the single `committed` binding
with a re-acquirable cell plus an `acquire!` that (a) takes the durable ref,
(b) publishes the key-tagged handle into `committed-ref`, (c) adds the value
watch, and (d) registers an `add-on-dispose!` callback which — guarded on the
disposed reaction still being the one this closure holds — re-runs `acquire!` and
then calls `on-change`. `subscribe-fn`'s IDENTITY stays memoized on
`[stable-key]`, so React's subscribe/unsubscribe contract is untouched and the
same-key steady state is unchanged; the hook simply tracks the rebuilt cache
entry across a framework-owned eviction. The returned cleanup then releases the
reaction it ACTUALLY holds via `rf.subs/unsubscribe-if-reaction`
(`[frame-id query-v reaction]`), which already exists for precisely this
stale-holder problem — the spine calls it today for the render-phase provisional
token. That single change also closes the ownership edge above.

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS BIGGER THAN IT LOOKS, and are why it wants its own
dispatch rather than a tail-end patch:

1. `unsubscribe-if-reaction`'s docstring currently scopes it explicitly to "the
   ONE holder whose reference can outlive its slot — the React-hook spine's
   render-phase provisional acquisition", citing Spec 006 §"Render-phase
   provisional acquisition and commit adoption". Extending it to COMMITTED
   teardown makes that docstring wrong and probably wants a row in
   `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` — a hot-zone document held by another worker
   in this same wave.
2. The bead's own acceptance criteria is broad: besides the eviction case it
   requires preserving stable same-query watch/ref counts, query/frame retarget,
   StrictMode, and abandoned-render cleanup, plus a comparison against an
   independently-mounted successor consumer. That is a UIx browser-lane suite,
   and each iteration of the browser lane on this machine is a full
   `shadow-cljs compile browser-test` plus a Chromium run.

NOTHING WAS CHANGED FOR THIS BEAD. No spine.cljs, subs.cljc, cache.cljc, spec or
UIx edit is in PR #9361 — its diff is confined to
`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**` and `implementation/adapters/test-react/**`.

--- 2026-09-07 AUSEST — IMPLEMENTED on worker/core-a, PR #9373 (open, ready). Bead left OPEN for the mayor to close after merge. ---

THE MAYOR'S TRAP NOTE WAS RIGHT AND I VERIFIED IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth keeping. rf.subs.cache/emit-dispose! is (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? (rf.trace/emit! ...)) — confirmed at source. rf.interop/add-on-dispose! is a bare late-bind consult of :adapter/add-on-dispose! with NO debug gate, routed to re-frame.disposable/-add-on-dispose, which the spine's own derived-value container reifies. A fix hung on the obvious seam would not have existed in a release build.

REPAIR, as the previous worker's design sketched it. subscribe-fn's closure now holds #js [reaction watch-key] in a volatile instead of one closed-over reaction, and a wire! fn (a) publishes the key-tagged handle into committed-ref, (b) adds the value watch on a per-ACQUISITION key, and (c) registers an add-on-dispose! callback that re-runs wire! on the rebuilt entry and then calls on-change. Three guards: released? (an unmounted hook takes nothing back), identity (fires only while the disposed reaction is still the one held), and frame liveness — destroy-frame! flips :destroyed? at step 4 BEFORE disposing the sub-cache at step 5, so a torn-down frame reads nil and the hook lets go instead of emitting a frame-destroyed recovery per mounted component. subscribe-fn's IDENTITY is untouched, so React's subscribe/unsubscribe contract and the same-key steady state are unchanged.

THE OWNERSHIP EDGE (the bead's "related edge... belongs to this same repair") is fixed in the same closure: the cleanup now calls rf.subs/unsubscribe-if-reaction with the reaction it actually holds. Its Spec-006-scoped docstring, which said it existed for "the ONE holder whose reference can outlive its slot", is corrected IN THE CODE FILE to name both holders. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md is UNTOUCHED — the code failed a contract 006 already states.

ONE THING NEITHER THE BEAD NOR THE BRIEF ANTICIPATED, and it cost a cycle. Eager reacquisition inside the disposal ran too EARLY: rf.registrar/register! fired replacement-hooks (cache invalidation) BEFORE registration-hooks (live-frame's mark-projection-dirty!), so the re-acquire resolved the frame's STALE generation and rebuilt the entry against the very body the re-registration had just replaced. Nothing had noticed because, until now, every invalidated consumer merely dropped its entry and rebuilt LATER, past the mark. Fixed by moving the registration hooks above the replacement hooks in register!, with the reasoning written at the site: recording a change completes before anything reacts to it. Both batches already ran isolated under try/catch, so the move changes no failure propagation, and no test pins their relative order (checked).

FAILING-FIRST, as a real React lifecycle regression (browser lane, UIx). Source reverted to HEAD with the new tests in place, lane run, then restored and verified by SHA-256 against a saved copy before the green run. Pre-fix: exit 1, 815 tests / 4462 assertions, 13 failures / 0 errors. Post-fix: exit 0, 815 / 4466, 0 failures / 0 errors. The pre-fix failures were the defect itself — a re-render read 1 where the replacement gives 101; an app-db write produced NO notification at all (nil); and unmounting the original consumer left the successor's cache slot nil, its reaction disposed under a live holder, with the survivor unnotified.

TWO EXISTING TEST SURFACES MOVED WITH THE MECHANISM, both narrowed rather than relaxed. Add a real mounted two-parent/shared-child regression across replacement and explicit cache clear, assert the child's two refs, continued updates of BOTH parents, and one surviving ref/reactive parent after the other unmounts. The PR's four new browser cases exercise a single layer-1 query and never clear the cache; they cannot expose this interleaving. No new public API or programmer-facing ceremony is needed. rf2-kuky.57's explicit-target leak is repaired and is not reopened; rf2-4lp1's generation trigger is present, so the eager-holder integration residual remains here rather than being duplicated there.

title: skill(re-frame2): Frames canonical machine test uses an unresolved macro and the wrong state partition
description:
## Scope

Repair the canonical per-test frame recipe in `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md` and add the smallest regression witness on the existing re-frame2 skill gate surface. The public frame/subscription APIs are correct; this is a teaching-surface defect.

## Correctness finding

The canonical mini-example has two independent faults:

1. It calls `(with-new-frame ...)` unqualified, although the snippet uses the standard `[re-frame.core :as rf]` convention for every surrounding public operation and does not establish a `:refer`. In an ordinary consumer namespace the symbol does not resolve.
2. Its assertion calls `(rf/compute-sub [:auth.login/state] (rf/app-db-value f))`. That subscription derives from `[:rf/machine :auth.login/flow]`, whose source is runtime-db, while `app-db-value` returns only app-db. `compute-sub` needs the coherent `frame-state-value` for a mixed app/runtime dependency graph. Once the macro spelling is fixed, the shown assertion still observes `nil` instead of `:authed`.

This is the leaf's canonical, copy-oriented recipe, not incidental prose. `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md` tells an author or AI that implementation is ground truth, to match the canonical declaration rather than re-derive it, and to copy the worked shape.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md:102-116` labels the block "Canonical mini-example" and shows `(with-new-frame [f ...] ...)` at line 107 plus `(rf/compute-sub [:auth.login/state] (rf/app-db-value f))` at line 113. The following sentence calls `app-db-value` the sanctioned harness shape for this example.
- The same leaf already states the partition contract at `frames.md:28-35`: app-db is application data; machine snapshots live in runtime-db and app code reads them through `[:rf/machine <id>]`; the coherent composite is `{:rf.db/app ... :rf.db/runtime ...}`. The canonical block contradicts its own model.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1352-1372` defines the public macro as `re-frame.core/with-new-frame`. The skill's API index uses `rf/with-new-frame` at `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:36`, and working sibling recipes use it at `references/cross-cutting/testing.md:80` and `testing-views.md:88`. Nothing in the Frames block establishes an unqualified refer.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljc:700-707` registers `:auth.login/state` with `:<- [:rf/machine :auth.login/flow]` and returns `(:state snapshot)`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:394-401` registers `:rf/machine` with `reg-runtime-sub` and reads the machine snapshot from runtime-db.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1866-1893` distinguishes a supplied full frame-state from a bare partition and selects `:rf.db/runtime` for a runtime sub. Its `compute-sub` contract at lines 2193-2213 explicitly says a mixed dependency graph must receive a full frame-state, normally `(rf/frame-state-value id)`.
- The implementation's matching auth-machine test uses the correct call twice: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj:849-864,868-882` computes `:auth.login/state` against `(rf/frame-state-value f)` and observes `:authed` / `:locked-out`.
- The dedicated testing leaf is also correct and explicit: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:219-246` says machine snapshots are runtime-db, warns that `app-db-value` is app-db only, and recommends `[:rf/machine ...]` / `frame-state-value`.

## Programmer / AI impact and reproduction

A programmer asks for a per-test frame around the shipped login-machine shape. The skill routes them to Frames and instructs them to match its canonical block. Copying it into the normal namespace with `[re-frame.core :as rf]` fails first at the unresolved `with-new-frame` symbol. If they repair that obvious typo, dispatch does run in the isolated frame, but the subsequent pure subscription computation receives only app-db. Its runtime-backed input sub cannot see the machine snapshot, so `:auth.login/state` produces `nil` and the asserted `:authed` result fails. An AI may instead "fix" the application sub or reach into runtime internals because the canonical recipe presents the wrong accessor as sanctioned.

Expected: the copy-oriented recipe resolves entirely through the `rf` alias and computes a runtime-backed subscription from one coherent frame-state snapshot.

Actual: it neither resolves under the stated alias convention nor supplies the partition its own subscription graph reads.

## Root cause / history

The stale accessor is historical drift, not an implementation ambiguity. `git blame` shows the assertion's `app-db-value` spelling came from `84a34b8b575` (2026-06-01, the old frame-db rename). Machines moved to runtime-db in `e868bf604e` (2026-06-09), which changed `subs.cljc` and `machines.cljc` but did not update this skill block. The later API-shrink sweep `02ec7dbc4c` edited this same leaf to teach `frame-state-value` for runtime reads, yet left the canonical assertion unchanged. The unqualified macro arrived separately in `99d0dcc23fa`.

## Recommended minimal fix

- In `frames.md`'s canonical mini-example, spell the macro `(rf/with-new-frame ...)`.
- Supply `(rf/frame-state-value f)` to `compute-sub` for `:auth.login/state`.
- Amend the adjacent explanation so `app-db-value` remains the right input for an app-db-only sub, while a runtime or mixed graph uses `frame-state-value`; do not continue calling the former the sanctioned shape for this machine assertion.
- Add one narrowly anchored regression rule/test in the existing `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` self-test/eval surface so reintroducing either exact bad shape makes the skill gate red. A tiny behavioural witness may reuse the existing auth-machine smoke setup rather than create another framework abstraction.

## Non-goals

- No change to `with-new-frame`, `app-db-value`, `frame-state-value`, `compute-sub`, machine storage, or any other runtime API.
- No implicit merging of runtime-db into app-db and no convenience overload that guesses which partition a graph needs.
- No general Markdown code-block compiler, prose parser, new test framework, or broad rewrite of frame/testing documentation.
- No requirement that every app-db-only `compute-sub` call use full frame-state; preserve the smaller bare-db form where every input is a `:db` sub.

## Duplicate distinctions

Targeted all-status searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered `frames.md` with `app-db-value` / `frame-state-value` / `with-new-frame`, `auth.login/state`, and app-db machine reads. No bead owns this canonical block or its runtime-partition error.

- Closed `rf2-jwmkq` is adjacent but distinct: it removed a bogus JVM `(rf/with-frame id (fn [] ...))` instruction that silently skipped test bodies. It did not inspect this `with-new-frame` block, macro qualification, or mixed-partition `compute-sub` input.
- Closed `rf2-kyure` was a partition-A hygiene sweep whose listed Frames items were a phantom symbol/footer and which explicitly characterized its items as not making an agent write broken code. This executable recipe failure was not among them.
- Closed `rf2-lpanl` deduplicated Frames prose for size and expressly retained distinct claims; it did not correct this block.

## Uncertainty

Confidence in the defect is high from the public definitions, partition selector, actual example registration, and matching implementation test. This review deliberately did not execute a runtime probe because its worker brief prohibited application/runtime operations. Line numbers are tip-relative. If the login fixture is reorganized during the fix, the behavioural witness can register a tiny runtime-backed machine sub locally; the invariant is the same: the old app-db-only input must not satisfy a runtime dependency, while full frame-state must.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md`'s canonical block uses `rf/with-new-frame` and computes `:auth.login/state` from `rf/frame-state-value`; no positive sentence around the block presents `app-db-value` as sufficient for that runtime-backed graph.
2. The corrected recipe is valid in a minimal consumer namespace that only aliases `[re-frame.core :as rf]` (plus the artefact/example namespaces needed to register the machine and stub): the macro resolves, dispatch reaches the isolated frame, and the state assertion observes `:authed`.
3. A focused behavioural check proves the partition discriminator: `compute-sub` over the runtime-backed state sub with the same frame's full `frame-state-value` returns the expected state, while supplying only `app-db-value` cannot observe that machine snapshot. The positive check must not pass merely because runtime data was duplicated into app-db.
4. Extend the existing re-frame2 skill drift/eval gate with a bounded check for this canonical block. Its self-test accepts `rf/with-new-frame` + `rf/frame-state-value`, rejects an unqualified `with-new-frame`, and rejects restoring `rf/app-db-value` at the machine assertion. Do not ban legitimate app-db-only `compute-sub` examples elsewhere.
5. Run the focused behavioural test and the relevant skill gates, including `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --self-test`, `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --verbose --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose --ci`, and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`. Plant and restore one exact old-shape mutation to show the new skill rule fails non-vacuously.
notes:
## Post-merge audit of PR #9233 (2026-09-05)

Rule 9a's exemption is broader than its documented contract. FENCE_REFER_RE is :refer\b, and unqualified_frame_macro_problems skips the entire fence when that token occurs anywhere. Therefore a fence such as (:require [cljs.test :refer [is]]) followed by (with-new-frame ...) is accepted even though re-frame.core/with-new-frame was never referred. The regex also matches :refer-macros (the hyphen creates a word boundary) and comments merely mentioning :refer.

This leaves the newly added generic copy-safety guard fail-open. Rule 9c still protects the one canonical block, so this is a gate-correctness defect rather than a runtime regression.

Minimal repair: either require alias-qualified frame macros unconditionally, or recognize only a re-frame.core import whose actual :refer list contains the exact macro used. Add dirty self-tests for an unrelated :refer, :refer-macros, and a comment mentioning :refer; retain a clean case only for an exact re-frame.core refer of the matching macro.

title: routing navigate: reject non-map :query-merge before it mutates or throws
description:
## Slice reviewed

`implementation/routing/**`, with the actionable center at the public `:rf.route/navigate` in-place-edit path. I inspected the implementation, Spec 012, API/guide examples, focused routing tests, representative repository consumers, all-status beads, and the introducing/refactoring history. This is the single cohesive finding selected from the review.

## Problem and user impact

A present `:query-merge` is documented and used as a map of query deltas, but the routing always-on structural gate validates only its key relationships, not its value shape. `re-frame.routing.navigate/navigate-handler` then hands the value to Clojure `merge` outside the protected `route-url` construction boundary.

That produces two materially bad outcomes from one missing boundary check:

- A two-element vector is accepted by Clojure as a map entry. `[:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge [:page 2]}]` silently performs a real navigation, changes the route query, and advances the nav token even though the edit value is not the documented map.
- Other non-map values can raise host errors from the handler. For example `:query-merge "oops"` reaches a raw `ClassCastException` with no structured ex-data instead of the promised `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` rejection.
- `:query-merge nil` also passes and becomes a silent no-op because the fold uses `if-let`, despite key presence being the grammar's discriminator.

This is an ergonomics and correctness defect at a common SPA operation (filters, pagination, tabs). A programmer or generated call site that passes one map entry, a sequence, or a conditional nil should get one immediate, local explanation; it must not sometimes navigate, sometimes disappear, and sometimes fall into generic event-handler exception containment according to incidental Clojure collection semantics.

## Independently verified behavior

At repository tip `52b2579e9b53816abddd3406f72db5a5278bed1c`:

- Direct calls to `re-frame.routing.address/classify` returned `nil` (accepted) for all three requests `{:query-merge [:page 2]}`, `{:query-merge "oops"}`, and `{:query-merge nil}` when a current route was supplied.
- Through the real public dispatch path in a fresh plain-atom frame, with the JVM launched using `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, starting from query `{:q "x"}` and token `"nav-1"`, dispatching `[:rf.route/navigate {:query-merge [:page 2]}]` produced query `{:q "x", :page 2}` and token `"nav-2"`. This proves the malformed value is not merely a diagnostic mismatch: it commits navigation in the production posture.
- Calling `navigate-handler` with `{:query-merge "oops"}` raised `java.lang.ClassCastException` (`Character cannot be cast to java.util.Map$Entry`) with `ex-data nil` at the merge fold. The outer event engine contains handler exceptions, but that is the generic failure channel, not this operation's structural rejection contract.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/address.cljc:186-251`, `classify`: validates the closed roster and cross-key exclusions, but has no present-`:query-merge` `map?` branch. Its docstring says the gate is total and rejects malformed requests before guards.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/navigate.cljc:409-412`, `navigate-handler`: `(if-let [merge-in (:query-merge request)] (merge (:query current) query-params merge-in) ...)`; the fold is before the `route-url` try/catch at lines 442-459.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:277-282`: the event registration supplies allocation coeffects but no independent request schema, so the always-on gate is the relevant boundary in both postures.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:433-470`: the canonical request grammar names `:query-merge` as an edit and promises malformed requests reject through `:rf.error/navigate-bad-request` before guards; lines 475-499 describe it as query-delta folding and every example supplies a map.
- `docs/routing/concepts.md:205-225` and `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:501`: the public recipes likewise use map deltas and advertise loud structural rejection.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_navigation_test.clj:1729-1904`: positive `:query-merge` coverage uses maps (ordinary fold, nil member deletion, falsy member values, precedence, exact no-op). Lines 2319-2336 cover only relationships with `:url`, `:query`, and destination forms. No test gives the key a non-map value.
- Repository-wide non-test/non-doc search found no intended non-map consumer; the only executable example outside the implementation is a checker fixture using `(select-keys ...)`, also a map.

## History

- `bfde6b4fb7` (2026-07-03, rf2-ue2d4t) introduced `:query-merge` as a delta fold.
- `3b9f457674` (2026-07-21, rf2-vwwvp.1) moved navigation to the flat request-map grammar and added the structural gate, but kept the unchecked fold.
- `c60cb3ebf0` (2026-07-21, rf2-oq0ld) made top-level navigate/route-url map boundaries exact and total; it did not close this nested edit-value boundary.
- `git blame` attributes the current fold at `navigate.cljc:409-412` to `1ae6555f640` (2026-07-26). No later commit adds a value-shape guard.

## Bounded recommendation and posture rationale

Extend the existing always-on `re-frame.routing.address/classify` boundary: when `:query-merge` is present, require its value to be a map and return a stable `navigate-bad-request` reason (suggested `:query-merge-not-map`, `:keys [:query-merge]`) before guard evaluation or query folding. Keep the check plain and local; do not add a schema dependency or a general request-builder abstraction.

An empty map remains a valid exact no-op. Nil values *inside* a valid delta map continue to remove keys, and falsy non-nil member values continue to round-trip. A present nil for the delta map itself should reject rather than silently vanish: omission is already the unambiguous spelling for “no merge”. This is the small pre-alpha correction that makes the minimal API trustworthy for both people and generated code.

## Non-goals

- Do not redesign the flat navigation grammar or add a builder/record type.
- Do not broaden this bead into validating every navigation policy/value slot.
- Do not change query merge precedence, nil-member deletion, canonical URL encoding, guard semantics, or no-op classification.
- Do not make Schemas/Malli mandatory for routing.
- Do not change `merge` behavior elsewhere in the library.

The exact reason keyword may follow the catalogue owner's convention; the required behavior is the always-on operation-specific rejection, not the suggested spelling.

A focused branch of the form “key present and value not map” is enough. Preserve the gate's existing precedence for unknown keys and mutually-exclusive forms; add one stable reason for the value-shape failure. Exercise both the pure classifier and the real dispatch path so a future refactor cannot leave the verdict disconnected from behavior.

title: schemas: registered nil app-schema disappears from hot-reload change detection
description:
## Scope

Fix the app-schema hot-reload change detector in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc` so registration presence is not inferred from the stored schema value. Keep the registration grammar, validator API, candidate validation, privacy policy, and public query return shapes unchanged.

## Correctness finding

`reg-app-schema` permits an opaque schema token, including `nil`, and the shipped presence work (`rf2-6eh5h`) established the law: only an absent declaration means “no schema”; a present falsey token is handed verbatim to the configured validator. App-db candidate validation already follows that law.

The hot-reload side effect does not. `reg-app-schema` reads only the previous `:schema` value, then `maybe-emit-schema-violation!` gates on `(some? prior-schema)`. A real registry entry whose schema token is `nil` is therefore indistinguishable from an absent entry. Re-registering that path with a different schema that rejects the live value silently skips the `:rf.schema/violation` diagnostic promised for schema evolution.

This is visible during ordinary authoring: a custom validator may legitimately use `nil` as one of its opaque tokens; after a save changes that declaration, the schema registry updates, but Xray/pair tooling receives no stale-slice warning even though the current `app-db` violates the new shape. The next dispatch may expose the mismatch, but the dedicated hot-reload diagnostic exists precisely to explain state that predates the edited schema.

## Concrete evidence

- `spec/010-Schemas.md:23` makes schema values opaque to re-frame; absence is a declaration-presence question, not a truthiness question. `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_presence_test.clj:1-34,62-78` pins exact `nil`/`false` delegation to custom validators.
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:805-807` requires a changed sub-path schema whose live value fails the new schema to emit `:rf.schema/violation`. `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:43` makes the same user-facing promise.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:461-474` takes `prior-schema` and uses `(some? prior-schema)` as the “was registered” gate.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:567-577` stores a full metadata map but throws away its presence information by reading `[frame-id path :schema]` before calling that helper.
- `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj:68-125` covers truthy prior schemas, unchanged schemas, first registration, and valid live values, but has no registered-`nil` case.

Fresh JVM reproduction with the public API and plain-atom substrate:

1. Create frame `:audit/nil-schema` with live app-db `{:count :bad}`.
2. Install a custom validator where schema `nil` returns true and schema `:needs-int` returns `(int? value)`.
3. Capture trace events; register `[:count]` with schema `nil`, then re-register it with `:needs-int`.
4. Observed: `app-schema-meta-at` reports the new `:needs-int` registration, but the capture contains **0** `:rf.schema/violation` events. The only operation was the unrelated one-shot opaque-walker warning caused by the root `nil` token.
5. Non-vacuity control: repeat with prior token `:anything` (validator returns true), then `:needs-int`. The same live value and new schema emit exactly **1** violation with `{:pre-reload-schema :anything, :post-reload-schema :needs-int, :mismatching-value :bad}`.

The discriminator is solely prior-token truthiness; registration, live value, new-schema verdict, and trace harness are otherwise the same.

## Recommended bounded fix

Carry prior-entry presence separately from its value. For example, capture the prior registration metadata map (or a `contains?` boolean) before replacement, and let `maybe-emit-schema-violation!` gate on that presence while comparing/publishing the exact prior `:schema` token. A full metadata map is already stored, so this needs no sentinel type, registry redesign, or new abstraction.

Add the regression beside the existing hot-reload cases in `schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj`. Keep first-registration suppression by testing entry absence, and keep unchanged `nil -> nil` silent via equality.

## Posture rationale

This is a small identity fix at an existing boundary, not a request for richer schema semantics. It preserves the library’s low-friction promise that validator tokens are truly opaque and makes the existing hot-reload feedback trustworthy for SPA authors and agent tooling. One presence bit and one focused regression are enough; no new public API or machinery is warranted.

## Non-goals

- Giving `nil` special validation meaning in the default Malli adapter.
- Changing `app-schema-at` (callers needing registration metadata already have `app-schema-meta-at`).
- Validating schema forms at registration time.
- Changing hot-reload recovery, redaction, trace shape, source-coordinate collision warnings, or registry concurrency.
- Generalizing this into another framework-wide presence census; `rf2-6eh5h` already handled the validation seams.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses (title, descriptions, and notes) for `nil schema`, `app schema nil`, `schema presence`, `key-presence`, `hot reload schema`, `hot-reload`, `prior schema`, `pre-reload-schema`, `schema violation`, `re-registering a path`, and `schemas-by-frame`. No bead owns this storage-side presence loss.

Closest item is closed `rf2-6eh5h`, which fixed falsey `:schema` delegation across validation consumers. Its scope and close record explicitly left app-db path validation unchanged because that path already delegated falsey values; it did not inspect or change `storage.cljc`'s hot-reload prior-entry gate. Closed `rf2-ee38b.6` introduced the hot-reload warning for ordinary truthy schemas. Git history searches (`-S"(some? prior-schema)"`, `-G"prior-schema|pre-reload-schema"`) show that gate originated there and no later commit addresses falsey prior registrations.

## Uncertainty

A `nil` schema token is uncommon with default Malli, which will reject it as malformed. It is nevertheless an expressly supported opaque token for a custom validator, and the framework now has dedicated tests guaranteeing exact falsey-token delegation. The impact is diagnostic rather than state corruption, so P2 is appropriate rather than P1.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With a custom validator that accepts prior schema token `nil`, registering `[:count]` as `nil` and then re-registering it with a different schema that rejects the live value emits exactly one `:rf.schema/violation`; its tags preserve `:pre-reload-schema nil`, the exact new token, path, frame, and mismatching value.
2. A first registration whose schema is `nil` remains silent: absence is still distinguished from a present-nil entry.
3. Re-registering `nil -> nil` remains silent because the schema did not change.
4. The existing truthy-token, valid-live-value, per-frame, and sensitive/opaque redaction hot-reload tests remain green.
5. A negative control that restores `(some? prior-schema)` makes the new registered-nil regression fail, proving the test reaches this branch.
6. `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/schemas` passes.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9196 (branch worker/schemas-a). PREMISE HELD, verified at source: reg-app-schema read only [frame-id path :schema] and maybe-emit-schema-violation! gated on (some? prior-schema), so a registry entry carrying a nil token was indistinguishable from an absent entry. Failure direction established empirically before fixing: SUPPRESSION — the reproduction emitted 0 violations where the truthy-token control emits 1. CONTRACT settled against Spec 010: its opening statement makes schema values opaque to re-frame's validation, rf2-6eh5h's declaration-presence law is already followed by the validation seams, and 010 Schema migration on hot-reload says the trace fires when a schema CHANGES with no truthiness carve-out — so outcome 1, the spec was right and the code was wrong. FIX is the presence bit the bead recommended, not a truthiness change: one deref of the frame's path map yields contains? presence and the exact prior token together, so they cannot disagree; the helper gates on presence and still publishes the exact prior token as :pre-reload-schema. No sentinel type, no registry redesign. validate.cljc untouched, so the ruled rf2-xpd8/rf2-vkn8 sequence is not pre-empted. AC1-6 all met. Gates (exit codes captured from the runner, implementation/schemas clojure -M:test): before 0 (373 tests/19223 assertions/0 failures); witness in place with fix absent 1 (376/19234, 8 failures, headline wrong value 'expected (= 1 (count violations)) actual (not (= 1 0))'); after 0 (376/19234/0 failures); AC5 negative control restoring (some? prior-schema) 1 with 8 failures ALL AND ONLY in the registered-nil regression while both suppression controls stayed green. Doc gates proven non-vacuous rather than trusted: python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0 with the added paragraph present in the built site/spec/010-Schemas/index.html, and check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 whose empty log was validated by planting a broken anchor (exit 1 naming 010-Schemas.md:809) then restoring and verifying the restore by blob hash. npm run test:cljs NOT run: no node_modules in this worktree and the shared tree was deliberately not linked; storage.cljc is .cljc and does reach the shared CLJS path, so CI owns that gate.

title: resources: reject non-function request handlers at registration
description:
## Finding

The public reg-resource and reg-mutation authoring boundary accepts any value in the required third request-fn slot. Both validators check only that the reconstructed spec contains :request, so 42 registers successfully. The runtime later invokes that value and the first ensure/execute fails with a raw host ClassCastException and nil ex-data.

This is a material correctness and ergonomics defect: a deterministic definition error survives application registration/boot and is displaced to the first user interaction, outside the library's structured registration-error contract.

## Governing contract

- spec/016-Resources.md:576-585 defines the strict three-slot forms and calls the third value a handler fn / request-fn.
- spec/016-Resources.md:752 and 1105 describe :request as the resource handler with signature (fn [params ctx] -> managed-http-args).
- docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:33-37 and 133-137 document request-fn as the third slot for resources and mutations.
- docs/resources/concepts.md:61-62 describes the same strict grammar.
- The sibling resource-scope registrar already enforces this shape with fn? in implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:311-321.

## Implementation evidence

- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:260-384, especially 328-337: validate-resource-spec! checks only contains? for :request. reg-resource at 435-535 reconstructs metadata plus the unchecked third value before validation.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc:59-183, especially 78-86: validate-mutation-spec! has the same presence-only check. reg-mutation at 187-296 stores the unchecked third value.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:753-754 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during ensure.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1280-1283 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during execute.
- Existing boundary tests cover missing/mislocated request and malformed metadata but not a non-function third slot: implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs:109-151 and implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:207-247.

## Verified behavior

Reproduced from implementation/resources at HEAD ac778f089a by registering a resource and mutation with valid metadata and integer request values:

    (r/reg-resource :review/nonfn-resource
      {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map]} 42)
    (r/reg-mutation :review/nonfn-mutation
      {:params-schema [:map]} 42)

Both calls returned their IDs and both introspection APIs reported :request 42. Directly exercising ensure-handler and execute-handler then produced:

    :ensure  java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil
    :execute java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil

The reproduction process exited 0 because it caught and printed the exceptions; registration itself did not throw.

## Bounded recommendation

At the shared registration-validation boundary, require the reconstructed :request value to satisfy the library's documented function predicate, matching the existing reg-resource-scope convention. Reject a bad resource with :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and a bad mutation with :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec, include the definition ID and offending value/type in ex-data, use :recovery :fix-registration, and do so before registry mutation. Add focused resource and mutation registration regressions in the existing boundary suites.

Non-goals: do not introspect callback arity; do not invoke request functions during registration; do not validate the managed-HTTP result until normal invocation; do not broaden this bead into auditing every optional callback or redesigning metadata validation.

## Posture rationale

This is a small fail-fast guard on a core public API, not defensive gold-plating. It removes a low-information delayed crash and makes both human and AI-authored SPA definitions faster to diagnose while preserving the minimal three-slot API and trusting valid programmer-supplied functions.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched all bead statuses for request-fn, request function, non-fn, resource-bad-spec, mutation-bad-spec, ClassCastException, request handler, callable, and third slot; repeated description/notes searches for request-fn, request function, non-fn/non-function, and third slot. There was no matching resources issue. The only callable hit was closed rf2-6r9j.30 in reagent-slim; the only third-slot hit was closed rf2-td8oe about reg-resource-scope documentation.

Searched all Git refs by commit message and diff for the same terms plus fn?/request combinations. Commits 06303b9ade, 3d22a1d776, and 04c585b6aa introduced/migrated the strict request-fn grammar; 06261ac1a9 added metadata-slot guards; 56fe742fac introduced mutation registration. None validates request function-ness, and current-tree search finds no such guard or regression.

## Uncertainty

The contract and sibling registrar point to fn? rather than the broader ifn?. If deliberately supporting custom IFn objects is desired, that should be stated and tested explicitly; keywords/maps/sets should not become accidental request handlers merely because they are invokable on one host. Portable two-argument arity validation is intentionally outside scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- reg-resource synchronously rejects a non-function third request slot before registration, using :rf.error/resource-bad-spec with the resource ID, offending value/type, and :recovery :fix-registration in structured ex-data.
- reg-mutation does the same using :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec and the mutation ID.
- Focused tests in resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs and resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc prove the invalid entries are not introspectable after rejection and valid request functions still register unchanged.
- The regressions run in every supported host exercised by those existing CLJS/CLJC suites and assert canonical structured errors rather than only matching host exception text.
- No callback arity probing, eager request invocation, managed-HTTP return validation, or optional-callback audit is added.
notes:
REOPENED BY MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #9218. The registration validators and host-specific coverage are correct, and Spec 016 now states the callable request contract. The consolidated error catalogue in spec/009-Instrumentation.md was not updated, however. Its :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec rows still say the errors cover only an omitted required key or a non-map spec; their recovery text says merely to declare :request plus :params-schema; and their payload text says :value is present only when the spec itself is not a map. The landed validators also raise these ids for a PRESENT but non-callable :request and put that offending request in :value, so both catalogue rows now understate the raised condition, prescribe an insufficient repair, and misdescribe the payload.

Minimal repair: update those two Spec 009 rows to include non-callable :request, say the handler must be a fn (or accepted Var), and state that :value carries either the bad spec or bad request as applicable. Preserve the existing ids and links and hand-check the Markdown table column counts. No implementation or test expansion is needed.

---
AUDIT-NOTE VERIFIED AT TIP, AND THE REMAINING WORK IS FENCE-BLOCKED (2026-09-05, worker coreguard-a).

The 2026-09-04T17:30:38Z reopening note is correct in every particular; re-verified at
source rather than taken on trust:

IMPLEMENTATION HAS LANDED. Both registrars now gate the third slot before any registry
mutation, with `(when-not (or (fn? (:request spec)) (var? (:request spec))) …)`:
  - re_frame/resources/registry.cljc — raises :rf.error/resource-bad-spec, ex-data
    {:resource-id … :value (:request spec)}, :where 'rf/reg-resource.
  - re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc — raises :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec,
    ex-data {:mutation-id … :value (:request spec)}, :where 'rf/reg-mutation.
The predicate is `fn? OR var?`, NOT the bare `fn?` this bead's description proposed —
a deliberate, documented improvement: on the JVM `clojure.lang.Var` implements `IFn`
but not `Fn`, so `(fn? #'my-fetch)` is FALSE there and TRUE in CLJS, and `#'my-fetch`
is the idiomatic hot-reload indirection. A bare `fn?` gate would have rejected working
code on one host only. `ifn?` is deliberately still refused, for the silent-nil reason
the bead itself gives. This resolves the bead's stated Uncertainty.

TESTS HAVE LANDED: resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs (:test/nonfn-request) and
resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc (:m/nonfn-request), both asserting the canonical id,
the definition id, and that the entry is NOT introspectable after rejection.

SPEC 016 HAS LANDED: :576-585's successor now states the callable contract explicitly
("`:request` is gated on being CALLABLE, not merely present"), and 016's own local
error table row says "or its `:request` is not callable".

GATE: `clojure -M:test` in implementation/resources — 829 tests / 7537 assertions,
0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0.

WHAT REMAINS IS EXACTLY WHAT THE NOTE SAYS AND NOTHING ELSE: the two
spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is a HOT-ZONE,
single-toucher file under this repo's dispatch convention, so this worker did NOT edit
it — stop-and-report per the fence. The rows still understate the raised condition in
all three ways the note names; the payload clause is the sharpest, since both landed
guards put the offending request in `:value` while the rows say `:value` is present
only when the spec itself was not a map.

Ready-to-apply substance for whoever holds spec/009 (preserve the existing ids, links,
Channel and tags; hand-check the Markdown column counts):
  - Condition: add "or its `:request` was present but NOT CALLABLE" alongside the
    omitted-required-key and non-map-spec cases.
  - Recovery: "declare :params-schema + :request, and make :request a fn (a Var
    holding one is also accepted)".
  - Payload: ":value carries the offending spec when the spec was not a map, or the
    offending :request when it was not callable".

NOT a new bead: this is the same bead's remaining leg, held only by the hot-zone fence.

---
CATALOGUE ROWS NOW AUTHORED (2026-09-05, worker coreguard-a). Supersedes the
"stop-and-report" paragraph above.

The coordinator widened the fence to make this worker the single toucher of
spec/009-Instrumentation.md for exactly three rows. Both rows this bead owed —
:rf.error/resource-bad-spec and :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec — are updated in commit
965f290508 on PR #9259, alongside rf2-xn13's new row, because the catalogue ratchet pins
source against the table and the halves cannot be split across PRs.

Each row now (i) names the PRESENT-but-NOT-CALLABLE :request condition beside the
omitted-key and non-map-spec cases, (ii) says the handler must be a fn, with a Var
holding one also accepted, and (iii) states that :value carries the offending spec when
the spec was not a map OR the offending :request when it was not callable. Existing ids,
links, Channel cells and tags preserved; column counts hand-checked (7 pipes each).

Gates: catalogue ratchet 30 tests / 179 assertions exit 0; full core artefact 2183 tests
/ 11283 assertions exit 0; full resources artefact 829 tests / 7537 assertions exit 0;
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. No implementation or test change was needed, as the audit note
said. This bead has no remaining work; the coordinator closes it when #9259 merges.
close_reason:

The dispatched worker's bd history walk found that audit note as the newest text-bearing mutation (notes 0->1143 chars), and the walk was CONTROLLED — it detected real changes on this item, so 'no newer change' is a finding rather than an empty-walk artefact.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE at tip: both registrars already gate the third request-fn slot BEFORE registry mutation. And the landed predicate is BETTER than the one my dispatch brief specified: (or (fn? ...) (var? ...)) rather than bare fn?, because a JVM Var implements IFn but not Fn — so (fn? #'my-fetch) is FALSE on the JVM and TRUE in CLJS, and a bare fn? guard would have rejected a var-held handler on one host while accepting it on the other. That difference resolves the bead's own recorded Uncertainty. Tests and Spec 016 prose also landed with #9218.

The worker verified the diff touched exactly three hunks by grepping the diff rather than by eye, and left rf2-6g6e's stale frame-destroyed row in the same file untouched.
