title: bug(hicasso-ssr): server/render leaves its Node request frame on the client effect platform
description:
## Correctness finding

`re-frame.hicasso.server/render` is the whole-page Node renderer, but the private request frame it creates is not tagged `:platform :server`. In a ClojureScript process the host-wide default is `:client`, so the frame runs the wrong platform contract unless an application supplies an undocumented workaround.

The mismatch is visible inside one file:

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:345-363` destructures `:frame-opts` and calls `rf/make-frame` with the private `:id` and setup `:initial-events`, but no `:platform`.
- The sibling `render-body` at `server.cljs:478-495` explicitly associates `:platform :server`, with the contract at lines 466-467: the tag gates client-only effects out of a render with no client.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:195-214` initializes CLJS's host marker to `:client`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:208-222` resolves platform as frame `:config :platform` first, then that host marker.
- Installing the documented `re-frame.ssr/adapter` does not change the marker: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/substrate.cljc:68-89` is only the adapter map, and `rf/init!` installs it without inferring a platform. `rf/init-platform :server` is a separate operation.

This contradicts the public recipe and promise. `docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md:48-78` tells a Node host to call only `(rf/init! ssr/adapter)` before `server/render`; lines 111-118 say that render does not run client effects and specifically tells authors to put browser work behind `:platforms #{:client}`. The MIG-23 consumer recipe and executable cold-start fixture use the same boot shape (`skills/reagent-migration/references/ssr-hydrate.md:33-67`, `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:81-95`). No in-repo `server/render` caller supplies `:frame-opts {:platform :server}` or pairs the call with `rf/init-platform :server`.

## Verified behavior

A read-only core probe was run from outside the checkout, using this worktree's `implementation/core` as a local dependency. It installed the plain-atom adapter, set the host marker to `:client` (the CLJS default), registered one `#{:client}` effect and one `#{:server}` effect, then created two otherwise identical frames whose initial event returned both effects:

- untagged frame: `rf/frame-meta` contained no `:platform`; observed effects were exactly `[:client]`;
- `:platform :server` frame: metadata contained the tag; observed effects were exactly `[:server]`.

That is the exact branch `server/render` and `render-body` respectively select. Source inspection additionally confirms the former is untagged and the latter tagged. The worktree stayed clean.

Consequences are not cosmetic. A correctly declared browser-only effect or coeffect reached from `:initial-events` can execute in Node (DOM/storage access, host calls, or duplicate external work), while a server-only one is skipped. The request can fail, mutate an unintended host resource, or render/build a payload from the wrong settled state without a platform error. Passing `:frame-opts {:platform :server}` masks the defect, but neither public recipe teaches that and a renderer's server identity should not depend on every caller remembering it.

## Recommended bounded change

Make `server/render` own `:platform :server` in the same final `assoc` that already owns `:id` and `:initial-events`, mirroring `render-body`. This also means a contradictory `:frame-opts {:platform :client}` cannot hijack the server request frame. Amend the local docstring/public recipe only as needed to state that `:platform` is renderer-owned.

Add a focused row to `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs` beside `frame-opts-ride-under-the-modules-id...`:

1. deliberately leave/set the host-wide marker to `:client`;
2. register one server-only and one client-only spy effect, dispatch both from a `server/render` initial event, and prove exactly the server effect runs;
3. pass `:frame-opts {:platform :client}` in the adversarial arm and prove it cannot reverse the result;
4. keep a non-vacuity/control assertion showing the same untagged frame shape selects the client effect (or perform the standard source mutation control by temporarily removing the new `:platform` assoc).

The existing `render-body` platform behavior remains unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Do not mutate the host-global platform inside each render; request-local frame configuration is already the right seam.
- Do not make `rf/init!` infer platform from adapter kind, change core platform fallback rules, or redesign the SSR adapter.
- Do not add an option, diagnostic, platform abstraction, or broader effect policy.
- Do not change host-component `:server` policies, hydration, payload projection, recovered-error handling, or the body-only renderer.

## Posture rationale

This is one owned map entry plus a focused regression test. It removes a silent cross-platform semantic inversion on a public SSR door and makes the older renderer match its already-correct sibling. It is high correctness and ergonomics leverage without adding machinery or asking trusted programmers to repeat hidden boot knowledge.

## Duplicate and history search

All-status bead title/description/notes/design/acceptance/close-reason searches covered: `hicasso platform`, `render platform`, `server render client`, `server/render effect`, `server/render fx`, `server-only effect`, `client-only effect`, `whole-page renderer`, `untagged frame`, `active-platform`, `init-platform`, `skipped-on-platform`, and `frame-opts`. No bead owns this runtime defect.

Related but distinct:
- closed `rf2-ypom` / `rf2-ct24`: recovered render errors, not platform routing;
- closed `rf2-8arzr.5`: added the correctly tagged `render-body` and explicitly fenced the existing `render` from change;
- closed `rf2-umi1w` / `rf2-33lfn`: fixed test fixtures whose missing client tag was masked by CLJS's client fallback; they provide direct precedent for why an untagged frame is not equivalent to a tagged one;
- closed `rf2-vpdrf` / `rf2-byig6`: adapter installation preconditions, not active-platform selection.

History confirms commit `30317bfe0e` introduced `server/render` untagged on 2026-08-14; `bbc97a5678` introduced `render-body` with `:platform :server` on 2026-09-02. No later commit adds the tag to `render`, and the current `origin/main` has no diff on the source/test paths.

## Uncertainty

A fresh Hicasso Node compile was not run because this worker checkout intentionally has no `node_modules` and the review brief forbids creating the shared junction or mutating files. The core probe exercised the exact platform resolver and effect dispatcher without repository writes; the remaining link is direct source inspection of the two `rf/make-frame` option maps. No in-repo caller demonstrates an intentional need to force `:client` through `server/render`; if such an external caller exists, it conflicts with the renderer's documented server-only semantics and should migrate rather than preserve the inversion.
design: Prefer the existing per-frame override seam: add `:platform :server` to `server/render`'s final `assoc`, beside its private id and setup vector. This is request-local, deterministic, and already proven by `render-body`; avoid a process-global `rf/init-platform` mutation or adapter-kind inference.
acceptance_criteria:
- `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` creates every private request frame with an explicit renderer-owned `:platform :server`, including when `:frame-opts` contains a contradictory `:platform :client`.
- In a CLJS test whose host marker is `:client`, a render initial event returning paired `#{:client}` and `#{:server}` spy effects executes only the server effect; the test is shown to fail when the request-frame tag is removed.
- Existing snapshot/initial-event ordering, frame-id ownership, payload/document output, cleanup-on-throw, recovered-error verdicts, and `render-body` behavior remain green.
- The Hicasso Node test lane and focused server-render suite pass, and any touched public prose consistently states that the renderer owns the server platform.

title: hic: chapter 06's documented entity-:key collision warning is never raised at any tier - Hicasso pr-strs the key, so the hazard does not arise and neither does the promised warning
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F18 · outcome 5 · `unresolved` · `api`

**The fault I induced**

The mistake chapter 06 spends a warning box on: keying a sequence child by an
entity instead of a primitive. In the feed's sidebar, `:key {:tag tag}` instead
of `:key tag`. Chapter 06: "A complete entity changes when the entity is
edited; React also coerces non-primitive keys, which can remount or collide.
Hicasso reports `:rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key` and identifies the child."
Chapter 16 lists the same id in its complaint table.

**Whether the documented route reached it**

**No. Nothing fired at all**, at any tier I could reach.

- **L2 (`ht/tree`)**: tree built, 2 children, `console.warn` captured and empty,
  and my own view tests stayed green. A real fault, a fully green suite.
- **The dev browser build**: every console message captured from boot through
  the render. Four messages, all of them React's DevTools notice, shadow's
  ready line, and two 404s for a missing stylesheet. No `:rf.warning/…`
  anything. No React key warning either.

I tried it in both child spellings — spliced with `into`, and with the sequence
directly in child position, which is the form chapter 06's own paragraph about
where the check runs describes. Neither produced a complaint.

**What actually happens**

I read the key React received, off the fibers:

```
{"text": "intro",    "key": "{:tag \"intro\"}"}
{"text": "demo",     "key": "{:tag \"demo\"}"}
{"text": "clojure",  "key": "{:tag \"clojure\"}"}
{"text": "re-frame", "key": "{:tag \"re-frame\"}"}
```

The map is `pr-str`'d into a stable, distinct string. So the two hazards
chapter 06 names do not occur: the keys do not collide, and they are stable
across renders for an unedited entity. The behaviour is *better* than the
chapter describes — which is the most likely explanation for the silence, and
would make the missing warning correct rather than broken.

But that reading and "the warning is not raised on this surface" are
indistinguishable from outside, and I cannot tell which without reading source
I am not allowed to read. Either way the chapter is wrong about something: it
either overstates the danger ("React also coerces non-primitive keys, which can
remount or collide" — not here; Hicasso converts first) or it promises a
warning that does not arrive.

**The one that would still bite**: an entity key changes when the entity is
edited, so a favourited article's card would still get a new key and remount,
silently, with no warning. That hazard survives the `pr-str`; the collision one
does not.

**Bead**

Either raise the warning where the chapter says it is raised, or correct the
chapter to describe the `pr-str` behaviour and narrow the hazard to
edit-induced remounting.
close_reason: PREMISE DID NOT HOLD; fixed as prose in PR #9140. The warning is NOT dead: impl/codec.cljs defines warn-entity-key! emitting :rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key, with direct coverage in codec_cljs_test.cljs. Hicasso does not pr-str the key either - every emission path does (unchecked-set js-props "key" k), handing it to React verbatim; React's own '' + config.key reaches CLJS's toString, which is the printed form the pilot read off the fibers. So the collision hazard IS real for a foreign JS object (all coerce to [object Object]; pinned by test a-foreign-object-key-collapses-distinct-children-onto-one-key) and is not real for a CLJS collection, which stays distinct per value. Nothing fired for the pilot because check-member-key! gates on (boundary-head? h) and the induced fault keyed [:a.tag-pill ...], a native tag, not a marked defview boundary; uuid and symbol are also deliberately classified safe. The guide, not the code, was wrong: it promised the warning for any sequence child. Chapter 06's warning box now separates remount-on-edit (every non-primitive key) from collision (the foreign-object case), and a following paragraph states the real scope and names the native-tag case the check does not cover. Chapter 16's complaint-table row now reads 'A boundary-headed sequence child's :key'; chapter 02's one-clause overstatement narrowed to a view-boundary child. implementation/hicasso/** untouched - implementing a warning that already exists would have been the gold-plated remedy.

title: Enroll published Hicasso in the implementation root coordinator
description:
## Finding

The root Clojure coordinator did not follow Hicasso's transition to a published artefact. `implementation/deps.edn` says its top-level `:deps` pulls every artefact onto one classpath, but the map has no `day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "hicasso"}`. Its `:test` alias nevertheless adds `hicasso/test`, leaving the tests on a classpath that lacks `hicasso/src` (and the supported kit root `hicasso/test_kit/src`). `implementation/README.md:46` repeats the every-artefact claim, while lines 165-166 still call Hicasso pre-publication with no `:clein` deploy alias. The same inventory also still says core depends on Reagent at line 52, although commit d44c4f7d20 moved that dependency to the Reagent adapter.

## Evidence

`clojure -Spath -M:test` from `implementation/` exits 0 and lists `hicasso/test`, but contains no `implementation/hicasso/src` or `hicasso/test_kit/src`; it does list every other published artefact's source root. `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` has declared `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` under `:clein/build` since commit f35ba5d13e (2026-08-15), and `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh` plus `.github/workflows/release.yml` both enumerate and deploy it. `hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/slot_cljs_test.cljc` directly requires `re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot`, demonstrating that a test-only path is not a self-contained substitute for the missing source root. The shadow coordinator is not affected: its explicit source-path list already includes `hicasso/src`, `hicasso/test`, and both test-kit roots.

## Impact

The advertised aggregate classpath is incomplete specifically for a shipped artefact; ad-hoc root REPL/test selection cannot load the Hicasso implementation through this coordinator even though its test path is present. The root inventory also tells maintainers obsolete publication and core-dependency facts, making future classpath/release reviews unreliable.

## Recommendation

Add the Hicasso local-root dependency to the root coordinator and make the aggregate test alias match the Hicasso artefact's intentional test roots (including the supported test kit where the aggregate promises the full CLJS test classpath). Refresh the adjacent `implementation/README.md` inventory: Hicasso is published, and core's production deps are Clojure + ClojureScript, not Reagent.

## Risks and contracts

Do not add Hicasso to core or to an adapter artefact, change its published dependency DAG, publish the test kit as a second coordinate, or alter shadow's already-correct explicit source paths. Preserve Hicasso's optional-by-reachability bundle contract and post-matrix release ordering.

title: hic: rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b)'s 'PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE' log header vs rf2-dc0c's blinding rationale — the blank log a BLINDED pilot receives cannot both name the run's kind and stay silent about it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 07:1x AUSEST by the operator assembly for rf2-t4jpz, at the
point of actually writing the two FRICTION-LOG.md copies. UNRESOLVED — the
operator did NOT write the header, and says so, because writing it is the
irreversible half.

THE CONFLICT. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) says: "Each friction log's header reads
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE and records the pinned commit."

workspace.md's rehearsal section (added under rf2-dc0c, PR #9049) says of the
two operator-applied replacements: "Both replacements are written to be read
alone. Neither names a rehearsal, a counted run, or this page, so the pilot
meets one instruction rather than a choice between two."

These pull opposite ways on the SAME artefact. The friction log is handed to a
BLINDED pilot. A header reading "PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE" tells that pilot
(a) that a section 13 exists, (b) that it is inside an experiment whose
evidence status is contested, and (c) that its own run does not count — which
is precisely the kind of framing rf2-dc0c removed from outcome 7 on the
reasoning that a blinded pilot must not be asked to reason about which kind of
run it is in. The read fence separately bars reading the tracker, and "§13" is
an in-tree design reference.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNDECIDED, and why the operator stopped rather than choosing:
METHOD (b) does not say WHO writes that header or WHEN. Part 4 of the log is
explicitly the operator's section, written after the pilot ends, so the label
can be applied at disposition time without ever reaching the pilot — which
would satisfy both texts. But that is a reading, not a ruling, and the previous
rehearsal's logs did carry the header.

TIMING NOTE. rf2-t4jpz's METHOD was written 2026-09-02, BEFORE the rf2-dc0c
operator-applied variant landed with its blinding rationale, so the newer
package text may simply refine the older method rather than contradict it.

WHAT THE OPERATOR DID on the pilotasm-a run, pending a ruling: applied
workspace.md's two mandated rehearsal edits verbatim, filled the pin and the
baseline exit code that step 1 and step 5b make the operator's, and left the
PRE-PILOT header OFF the blank logs. Rationale: adding the line later is
trivial; un-leaking a blinded pilot is impossible. Both FRICTION-LOG.md copies
therefore currently carry 0 bead-id lines, 0 workspace.md links and 0 stray
fence lines, verified against source-page controls that bite.

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE DISPATCH: does the blank log a pilot receives carry the
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE header, or is that label applied by the operator
in Part 4 after the pilot ends? Either answer is cheap to apply to the two
assembled workspaces.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:4x AUSEST. LEAVE THE HEADER OFF THE PILOT TEMPLATE. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT ON COLLECTION.

THE CONFLICT IS REAL AND BOTH SIDES ARE RIGHT, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDED A RULING RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) wants a "PRE-PILOT - NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE" header on the friction log, so the archived artefact cannot later be mistaken for adoption proof. workspace.md says the operator replacements deliberately "name no rehearsal... so the pilot meets one instruction rather than a choice between two", which is the blinding rationale rf2-dc0c established.

THEY BELONG TO DIFFERENT READERS, AND THAT DISSOLVES IT. The header exists for whoever reads the log LATER - an auditor, or rf2-hic-064 section 13 checkpoint. It does nothing for the pilot except tell it it is inside an experiment, which is the one thing the blinding forbids: a pilot that knows it is rehearsing reports differently, and every outcome it records is then evidence about a pilot who knew.

THE RULING: the pilot TEMPLATE carries no such header. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT WHEN THE LOG IS COLLECTED, before it is filed under ai/findings/. METHOD (b) purpose is fully served - the archived artefact is marked - and the blinding is untouched. That is one line of operator work at collection time and zero risk.

THE WORKER INSTINCT WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND I AM CONFIRMING RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT: it left the header off and said "adding a line later is trivial, un-blinding a pilot is not." That is the correct asymmetry and it is the reason this ruling goes the way it does. An error in the reversible direction beats an error in the irreversible one, and only one of these two errors can be undone after the pilots run.

RECORD THE MECHANISM IN THE PACKAGE, not just here: workspace.md operator section should say the header is stamped at collection, so the next operator does not re-derive this and does not leave the artefact unmarked. That edit is NOT urgent and must NOT delay the pilot dispatch - file it or fold it into the next pilots-package pass.

title: tools/xray(local_render): exposed singleton keeps dead-frame sentinel registrable
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-g1vu worker (cluster code-a) while censusing the sentinel defect class. OUT OF THAT WORKER FENCE (tools/xray/**), so filed rather than fixed.

THE DEFECT, third instance of the class. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106 defines

  (def ^:private dead-frame-sentinel "..." ::no-egress-frame)

which expands to the ORDINARY PUBLIC KEYWORD :day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.local-render/no-egress-frame, and local-render-opts (:175) stamps it as the :frame opt whenever the named frame is nil / unreachable:

  :frame (if reachable? frame-id dead-frame-sentinel)

Its docstring carries the SAME false claim the other two carriers did: "The keyword is namespaced into this panel so it can never collide with a real frame id." make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever id it is handed, so an app CAN register a live frame under that literal. The stamp then RESOLVES, rf/elide-wire-value takes its live-frame branch, and the value egresses under that frame empty declaration registry — the fail-CLOSED stamp becomes a fail-OPEN one. Note local-render also passes :rf.size/include-large? true and, under the :rf.egress/local-raw profile, include-sensitive?, so the blast radius differs from the off-box carriers; the leak arm is the local-redacted default.

THE CLASS, now three carriers, each found only after the previous fix scope was drawn too tight:
1. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs — ::no-frame. FIXED by rf2-7htk7 third pass, PR #8987 commit 449bfd21c7 (private identity value (js/Object.)), with a collision regression at tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:559.
2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — ::no-egress-frame. FIXED under rf2-g1vu on branch worker/code-a: #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) plus the collision regression g-graph-egress-nil-frame-fails-closed-under-sentinel-id-collision in implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The premise was REPRODUCED first: with a live frame under the literal id, project-graph with a nil frame-id egressed {:cart {:items "tenant-jwt-9f3a-SECRET"}} raw instead of :rf/redacted (captured exit 1, two failing assertions).
3. THIS BEAD — tools/xray/.../panels/local_render.cljc:106/123/175. NOT fixed.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT, so the next pass does not have to re-derive it: git grep -n "dead-frame-sentinel" over *.clj/*.cljc/*.cljs finds every carrier by its shared var name (control-checked: it returns 2 hits in the already-known egress.cljc). The class is "a keyword literal used as an unregisterable-frame substitute stamped into a :frame opt". One NEAR-MISS was inspected and CLEARED: implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1145 passes ::no-frame to elide-against-frame, but only on the branch where the caller has explicitly waived sensitive redaction, and a colliding registry there supplies :large declarations that cause MORE elision, not less — it fails closed, so it is not this defect.

FIX SHAPE, settled by precedent, no design needed: make dead-frame-sentinel a fresh host object (the file is .cljc, so #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) as in the core fix), correct the docstring sentence that claims a namespaced keyword cannot collide, and ADD A COLLISION REGRESSION — register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted. The regression is the point: this class has now been found three times precisely because the first two fixes shipped without one covering the sibling.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9044 — REOPENED. The object replacement does not satisfy the claimed "NO frame can be registered under it" invariant because the public `local-render-opts` function returns the singleton itself in `:frame` for every nil or unreachable target. A caller need not manufacture an equal object; it receives the identical value.

Reproduced at merged commit 7369668070 on the JVM lane without editing source: take `(:frame (local-render-opts nil))`, pass that exact value to `rf/make-frame` as `:id`, then call `local-render-value` with a nil observed frame. Result: `{:same-sentinel? true, :registered? true, :rendered {:auth {:token "secret-session-jwt-abc123"}}}`. The value ships raw, so the fail-CLOSED branch is still fail-OPEN.

The added regression misses this because it registers only the retired keyword and structurally asserts merely that the replacement is not a keyword. Minimal repair: generate a fresh opaque identity for each unreachable projection (or otherwise keep the identity from being reusable across calls), then add the discriminating control: extract and register one call's `:frame`, make a subsequent `local-render-value` call, and prove it uses a distinct unreachable identity and redacts the whole value. Preserve the existing explicit `local-raw` opt-out; no profile redesign is needed.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — I CHECKED WHETHER THE SIBLING CARRIERS HAVE THE SAME ESCAPE, AND THE ANSWER IS THE USEFUL PART OF THIS NOTE.

The audit finding is that a PRIVATE identity value is not enough when a PUBLIC function HANDS IT TO THE CALLER. local-render-opts returns the singleton itself in :frame for every nil or unreachable target, so nobody has to manufacture an equal object — they receive the identical one, register a frame under it, and the fail-CLOSED branch is fail-OPEN. Reproduced at the merged commit with a raw secret shipping. That is a real P2 and it stands.

CARRIER 2 DOES NOT HAVE IT, and I verified at source rather than assuming the class was uniform. In implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc the sentinel is bound into walk-opts INSIDE project-graph (a let, at :421) and consumed by the local redact-node fn; project-graph returns the TRANSFORMED GRAPH, never the opts map. So the value has no public exit. The fix under rf2-g1vu stands as made.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THEREFORE NOT "private def" BUT "does any public fn RETURN a structure containing it". That is the rule to carry, and it is sharper than the one all three carriers were fixed against. A private identity value is necessary and not sufficient; what makes it sufficient is that it never leaves the namespace as a value.

WHAT THE NEXT WORKER SHOULD CHECK, and I did not: CARRIER 1 — tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs, fixed under rf2-7htk7 in PR #8987 with a bare (js/Object.). Does anything public there return a structure carrying it? If it does, this class has a fourth instance and the same repair applies. If it does not, the class is closed after this bead.

AND THE REGRESSION NEEDS THE SAME UPGRADE THE FIX DOES. The audit notes the added test misses this because it registers only the RETIRED KEYWORD and then asserts structurally that the replacement is not a keyword. That is a test about the SHAPE of the sentinel. The test that would have caught this takes (:frame (local-render-opts nil)) — the value a real caller actually receives — passes THAT to make-frame as :id, and asserts the value still redacts. Write the regression against the caller-visible value, not against the definition.
FIXED (second pass) by PR #9056, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9056, branch worker/xrayleak-a.

LEAK REPRODUCED FIRST, at base 146ee34b85 (which contains #9044's 8258cb5d70), JVM lane, source untouched: registering a frame under (:frame (local-render-opts nil)) and projecting a nil observed frame yielded {:same-sentinel? true, :registered? true, :rendered {:auth {:token "secret-session-jwt-abc123", :user-id 42}}} with captured exit 1. The audit's premise holds exactly as stated.

THE FIX. dead-frame-sentinel (a shared ^:private def) becomes fresh-dead-frame-sentinel (a defn-), minting a new identity PER CALL. The identity governing any one projection is created inside that call and is not observable before the walk consumes it, so there is no durable identity left to poison; what a direct caller of the public local-render-opts receives is single-use and governs nothing else. Zero cost on the hot path (the call sits on the unreachable branch of an if), and frame/frame is a plain registry get with no interning or per-id caching, so fresh identities are immediately garbage. local-render-opts stayed public: it has no production callers outside its own namespace, and the alternative (returning :frame nil for an unreachable target) is the ambient-borrow shape the seam exists to abolish.

THE REGRESSION, written against the CALLER-VISIBLE value as instructed. Two new arms in local_render_cljs_test.cljc: local-render-fails-closed-when-a-frame-is-registered-under-the-handed-out-sentinel (takes (:frame (local-render-opts nil)), registers a live frame under THAT EXACT VALUE, asserts nil / unreachable / path-aware local-render-value-at all still redact whole) and dead-frame-sentinel-is-single-use-per-projection (two calls must not share an identity; a live frame is still carried verbatim). PROVED THEY BITE: restoring the pre-fix source from base (plant verified by blob-hash equality with the base blob 3d540bcd82) turned the namespace RED with captured exit 1 and 7 failures, both new tests failing — while the #9044 collision test stayed GREEN under the same plant, which is precisely the blindness being repaired. Restore verified by blob-hash equality (93810892d5).

CARRIER 1 ANSWER — THE CLASS IS CLOSED. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs has NO fourth instance. Its one public fn, egress-value, builds its opts map INLINE as the argument to rf/elide-wire-value and returns that walker's result — the projected value, never the opts map. no-frame is ^:private, never returned, consumed only inside the cond-> immediately passed to the walker. Census: only egress-value is required elsewhere (7 files); nothing reaches no-frame. Same structural shape as carrier 2, re-verified at the rebased tip where rf2-g1vu's identity fix has now landed (4944195bff): walk-opts is bound inside project-graph's let and project-graph returns the transformed graph. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: at my original base carrier 2 was STILL the ::no-egress-frame keyword — the rf2-g1vu fix merged mid-flight — but the escape-route verdict is the same either way, because the discriminator is the return shape, not the spelling.

THE RULE, now written into the fresh-dead-frame-sentinel docstring so the next pass need not re-derive it: not 'is the definition private' but 'does any PUBLIC fn RETURN a structure containing it'. Carriers 1 and 2 answer no (no public exit); carrier 3 answered yes by design, and is repaired by making what escapes single-use.

GATES (all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, re-run on the final rebased base origin/main=3009c45058): tools/xray JVM clojure -M:test exit 0, 1315 tests / 6227 assertions (#9044 measured 1313 / 6217 — exactly +2 tests / +10 assertions, my two new deftests); npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11203 tests / 55820 assertions; clj-kondo exit 0 with zero findings on any changed file; nine documentation gates exit 0; mkdocs build --strict exit 0. test:xray-feature-gate NOT run — #9044's caveat still holds, no scenario mounts an unreachable frame, so it does not exercise the changed branch.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9056 — REOPENED. The per-call identity does not make the public local-render-opts result safe: the caller can register a frame under (:frame opts) and then pass that SAME opts map to rf/project-egress. Reproduced at current tip in tools/xray with the real JVM runtime: {:registered? true, :projected {:auth {:token audit-secret}}}; exit 0. The new regression misses this path because it obtains a sentinel from one local-render-opts call, then invokes local-render-value/local-render-value-at, which each call local-render-opts again and mint a different identity. The source itself says there are no production callers of local-render-opts outside this namespace, so the minimal repair is to withdraw that builder from the public surface and keep sentinel creation plus consumption inside the public projection functions, matching the two sibling carriers whose identity has no public exit. Pin the actual public-surface invariant; do not add a larger sentinel framework. The opener pagehide announcement is independently sound.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): stories.md teaches the run-variant loop with no adapter prerequisite — run-variant refuses with :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on a bare launch, and the pair skill OWNS the run side
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md teaches the run-variant / read-failures self-healing loop and states no host prerequisite for it. Grepping that file at tip: no occurrence of 'no-adapter-installed', 'plain-atom/adapter', or any adapter/substrate prerequisite at all (the only 'substrate' hit is a snapshot-identity hash tuple).

This matters more here than in the authoring skill, because the pair skill is the OWNER of the run side. skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md explicitly hands off to it: 'switch to the re-frame2-pair skill (it owns run-variant / read-failures against a running app behind shadow-cljs watch) and run the self-healing loop there'.

TRUTH AT TIP

title: test(websocket): integration fixture shadows the example registrations it claims to cover
description:
Audit finding from PR #8959 across completeness, correctness, and implementation quality.

The focused WebSocket integration fixture does not consistently exercise the runnable example registrations it claims to protect. `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs` calls `register-all!` for every test, and that function re-declares registrations from `examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs` inline. Because `reg-*` is last-write-wins, the fixture copies replace the example's own handlers before assertions run.

This is measured, not hypothetical: PR #8959 records that a fault planted in the example's `:ws.app/request-reply` handler body left the whole focused suite green. The same ownership split also weakens the boundary checks by construction: `inbound-boundary-structural-test` reads `handler-meta` only after `register-all!` has installed the fixture's copied `:schema` and `:rf.schema/at-boundary` metadata, so the suite can certify the copy while the runnable example drifts.

Completeness: machine/schema/mock vars are genuinely reused, but the source registration bodies and metadata are not. Correctness: a regression in the shipped example can remain green while its test-local twin behaves correctly. Implementation quality: the docstring now tells maintainers to mirror changes into both copies, preserving the drift mechanism instead of removing it.

Minimal outcome: make the example registrations re-invocable from one source of truth and have test setup call that source (or reuse named handler/metadata values directly). Add one focused mutation/control proving that changing the example's ingress handler or boundary metadata makes the suite red. Keep this local to the WebSocket example; do not build a generic registrar reload framework or broaden the public API.

Duplicate search covered all-status terms for `websocket register-all handler bodies`, `websocket test fixture mirrors example`, `request-reply body left suite green`, `websocket handler drift`, `websocket inbound boundary test`, `websocket at-boundary fixture`, and `websocket example registration test`; no existing owner was found.
acceptance_criteria: The WebSocket focused suite registers the example's handler bodies and boundary metadata from the same definitions the runnable example uses, with no independent test-local copy that can drift. A controlled fault in the example's `:ws.app/request-reply` body or removal of its `:rf.schema/at-boundary` metadata makes the focused suite red; the restored focused and adapter suites pass. The repair stays local and adds no generic reload framework.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8969, worker/wsfixture-idv1m) — finding CONFIRMED at source and repaired; premise held in full.

REPRODUCED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, both directions, on the pre-fix tree:
- gutting the example's :ws.app/request-reply body ({:db db}) -> focused suite exit 0, 29 tests / 240 assertions / 0 failures. Matches what PR #8959 recorded.
- deleting the example's :rf.schema/at-boundary from :ws.app/request-reply -> focused suite exit 0, 29 tests / 240 assertions / 0 failures. This second direction was NOT previously measured; it confirms the 'weakened by construction' half — inbound-boundary-structural-test was reading handler-meta back for metadata register-all! had installed moments earlier.

REPAIR (minimal outcome, first option): each example ns (websocket.schema / .connection / .messages / .core) now installs its registrations through a named re-invocable (defn register! ...), still called once at ns-load, so the production-app ns-load idiom and core/run are unchanged. Ignoring whitespace the diff to the four example files is exactly the wrapper — defn + docstring + one closing paren + (register!) — no registration content changed. The fixture's register-all! calls the four entry points and keeps no copy. Registered ids in the fixture: 30 -> 5 (four :ws.test/* reply-log targets it genuinely owns, plus the two framework :rf.machine/* runtime subs no example ns owns). Verified line-oriented AND over whitespace-collapsed text, with origin/main as the positive control. No generic registrar-reload framework, no public API change, nothing outside the WebSocket example.

The docstring instructing maintainers to mirror body changes into both copies is deleted with the mechanism it described.

CONTROL ADDED: websocket-example-registrations-are-live — three assertions, one per way the coupling can be lost: registered :doc (identity: which definition won the last write), registered :schema + :rf.schema/at-boundary read off the live registry, and the handler body driven through a real dispatch.

BOTH PLANTS REPLAYED ON THE REPAIRED TREE:
- body fault -> exit 1, 18 failures across 8 tests (new control among them)
- at-boundary removal -> exit 1, 2 failures (websocket-inbound-boundary-structural + new control)

GATES (implementation/, test:cljs split into its two phases; captured runner exit codes, all re-run after rebase onto the current base):
- compile-node-test.cjs node-test: exit 0, 1876 files, 0 warnings
- node out/node-test.js (full CLJS contract suite): exit 0, 11121 tests / 55163 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
- node out/node-test.js --test=re-frame.websocket-cljs-test: exit 0, 30 tests / 245 assertions / 0 failures (was 29/240; +1 test, +5 assertions = the control)

Concurrency check: 4 open PRs at dispatch time, none touching implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs or examples/patterns/websocket/ (pattern control positive). No live change beside this one.

Acceptance criteria met in full. Left open for the mayor to close on merge.

The premise was REPRODUCED before anything changed, in BOTH directions: on the pre-fix tree, gutting the example's :ws.app/request-reply body left the focused suite at exit 0 (29 tests / 240 assertions, 0 failures), and deleting its :rf.schema/at-boundary did the same. The second direction had never been measured - the item asserted it 'by construction' - and it holds, because inbound-boundary-structural-test was reading back metadata register-all! had installed moments earlier. After the repair the same two plants give exit 1: 18 failures across 8 tests for the body, 2 for the metadata, the new control among them both. TWO FURTHER DRIFTS the finding did not name, both gone with the copy: the fixture registered a :messages sub the example does not have (the example uses :messages/slice) and a hand-rolled :ws/snapshot runtime sub instead of the example's chained one; no test referenced either. QUALIFICATION from the rf2-tb442 worker, confirmed independently: the shadowing was confined to the handler bodies register-all! re-declared inline - where the fixture points at example VARS (ws.connection/connection-machine, messages/socket-actor-machine, ws.schema/InboundMessage and RequestOutcome, and the mock transport the actor reaches through) the example's own code genuinely was under test, and a planted fault in connection.cljs reds on the first try. title: [method] the mayor briefs from the bead's oldest layer — make the newest-mutation read and hold-banner sweep a STEP, not a thing to remember
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the acting mayor, against my own practice. This is at least the THIRD recorded instance of one failure class and the memories have not stopped it, which is the argument for a mechanical step.

THE PRIOR RECORD, found while filing this: bd memories 'mayor-brief' returns three keys, two of them predating today - mayor-brief-accuracy-stop-asserting-file-paths-i (2026-07-18, 'three times in one session') and mayor-brief-premises-must-be-verified-at-head (2026-08-17, whose own text says 'fifth instance'). Today added a third. A note that has been written three times and re-learned each time is not working as a control.

TODAY'S THREE, all the same shape - briefed from the bead's Scope/description rather than its newest text-bearing mutation, all three caught by the WORKER rather than by me:
- rf2-y8jjk: dispatched onto an unstruck '*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. ***' banner that WAS the newest text-bearing field. Worker refused, wrote nothing, opened no PR. A sweep then found ELEVEN of 27 open beads carrying a hold banner - I had been reporting two of them as dispatchable.
- rf2-9n43e: the newest note split the work into A (dispatchable) and B (sequenced behind two open beads sharing a test file). The brief asked for both; the worker did A only.
- rf2-i3og0: ruled from a skill page's prose without checking the owning spec or the history. Ruling was backwards. Worker refused and filed rf2-lspr9.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH A STEP: the dispatch preamble ALREADY orders the worker to read by tracker timestamps, at length, with the reasoning. The mayor writes that preamble and then does not do it. So the knowledge is present, written down, and pasted verbatim into every dispatch - what is missing is that nothing makes the mayor execute it before the brief exists. That is the same property the stash ban, the beads-boundary hook and the draft interlock all have and the reason they hold: enforced where it cannot be forgotten.

PROPOSED (small, and it belongs in the existing 'Write the brief in this order' section rather than as a new section): make step one of writing a brief a READ of the item's newest text-bearing mutation plus a fixed-string hold sweep - probes short enough to survive the ~76-column wrap ('NOT DISPATCHABLE', 'AWAITING MIKE', 'OPERATOR CALL'), exercised once against a bead known to carry one, because a zero from a wrong pattern reads exactly like a clean bead. State that a hold banner is the newest field often enough that the Scope section cannot be trusted to mention it.

SEQUENCING - MANDATORY. docs/the-mayor-method/ is SOLE-TOUCHER hot-zone per rf2-ttu8i, never parallel with another method-file bead. PR #8949 (mayor/one-rule-draft-interlock) is open against BOTH method pages right now. Do not dispatch until #8949 merges.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict (exclude_docs does NOT hide the-mayor-method/, verified by a planted-link red on #8949). Run mkdocs as 'python -m mkdocs' - bare mkdocs returns 127 here, which is NO VERDICT rather than a pass.
FIFTH INSTANCE, 2026-09-02, and a DIFFERENT SHAPE worth naming separately — a blanket fence in the brief that the bead had already lifted.

rf2-fmns2 (PR #8954). My brief said: 'Do not touch implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. If a new example build-id is genuinely required, that lives in the hot-zone top-level shadow-cljs.edn, so STOP and report rather than editing it.' The worker edited it anyway and was RIGHT to:

- the item's AC4 requires :examples/login-hicasso to exist and enrol automatically, which is only possible in that file;
- the bead's own TRIAGE NOTE had already anticipated the hot-zone touch and SEQUENCED this task behind rf2-3xq1v (shadow-cljs.edn) and rf2-39rc5 (package.json) - both closed and merged before dispatch;
- it checked every open PR first and found none touching either file.

I verified all three claims after the fact: rf2-3xq1v and rf2-39rc5 both read CLOSED, and a sweep of every open PR's file list found #8954 is the only one touching implementation/shadow-cljs.edn or top-level deps.edn.

WHY THIS SHAPE IS DISTINCT from the four already recorded. Those were the brief carrying STALE instructions - a hold banner not read, a work split not read, a ruling made without checking the owning spec. This one is the brief carrying a fence the mayor invented generically and correctly by default, which the ITEM had already discharged by naming the predecessors that had to land first. A blanket 'do not touch X, STOP and report' is the right default and is WRONG whenever the bead has already sequenced X - and the bead is where that sequencing lives, so the mayor cannot know it without reading the newest layer.

IMPLICATION FOR THE PROPOSED STEP: the newest-mutation read must look for SEQUENCING as well as for holds. A triage note that names predecessors is an authorisation with a precondition, and re-stating a fence over it converts a satisfied precondition back into a blocker - which either strands the work or, as here, costs the worker a justification round it should not have had to write.

Cost this time: nothing, because the worker read the item and overrode the brief. That is five for five on workers catching it, which is the safeguard working and not a reason to keep relying on it.
CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED REMEDY, 2026-09-02 — the marker sweep I proposed has a FALSE-POSITIVE mode, and I hit it within hours of proposing it. Do not build the step as written.

WHAT HAPPENED. I ran the fixed-string sweep over dispatch candidates and it flagged THIS BEAD as held, carrying both 'AWAITING MIKE' and 'OPERATOR CALL'. I wrote this bead and put no banner on it. The probe was matching (a) my own note QUOTING rf2-y8jjk's banner, and (b) the proposed remedy's own list of probe strings. It also flagged rf2-6c12m, whose text says outright 'its AWAITING MIKE banner is struck, so it is DISPATCHABLE' - the opposite of held.

I then tried to discriminate automatically - active marker vs 'struck' nearby vs a banner attributed to another bead id - and THAT failed too, because the standing banner text itself ends 'WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT', so the word 'struck' appears in every ACTIVE banner as an instruction. rf2-y8jjk, which is definitely held, scored active=2 struck=2. A second instrument, same shape of failure.

THIS IS THE HAZARD THE METHOD ALREADY NAMES, and I walked into it while building a check meant to prevent a different error. loops.md Tracker mechanics: 'An instrument can be RIGHT and still answer a different question from the one you asked... a marker scan finding a banner read as this item is held.' It lists that exact instance. The scan answers 'does this text contain these characters'; the question is 'is this item currently held', and the gap is invisible in the answer.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MY EARLIER REPORT: I told the operator '11 of 27 open beads carry a hold banner'. That number is UNRELIABLE and at least two of the eleven (this bead, rf2-6c12m) are false. Do not carry it forward. The two I can stand behind are reads rather than scans: rf2-y8jjk (a worker read it, refused the dispatch, and quoted the unstruck banner) and rf2-zq34m (I read its banner and its diverged-blockers note directly).

WHAT THE STEP MUST BE INSTEAD. A marker scan is a CANDIDATE FILTER, never a verdict. It narrows 27 items to a handful; the hold is then established by READING each candidate - which is cheap at that size and is the only thing that distinguishes an active banner from one quoted, discussed, or struck. Write the step that way, and write beside it the question the scan actually answers, so the gap is on the page rather than in the reader's head. If a machine-checkable hold is wanted, the durable fix is a STRUCTURED FIELD on the item rather than a marker in prose - but that is a tracker change and a separate decision, not this bead's.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8962, verified on main at commit 2a018d54fd (docs(method): make the newest-mutation read a dispatch step...). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. Built with the bead's own CORRECTION note governing, not its original proposal: the step reads the item's newest text-bearing mutation for a hold AND for sequencing, and a hold-marker sweep is written as a CANDIDATE FILTER with the hold established by reading each candidate - the question the scan answers stated beside the question being asked. The structured-field idea stayed out of scope. Worker pointed at loops.md Tracker mechanics rather than restating it, and correctly reported that #8958 had landed MORE there than my brief credited.

title: realworld-http: late article delete success overrides the reader's newer route
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-84iek (PR #8898), named in source by that worker as a suspected same-class defect it deliberately did not fix.

THE SUSPICION (verify at source before acting; this is a CLAIM, not a finding). rf2-84iek corrected three optimistic comment WRITE paths in examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ that mutated shared state without checking the reply belonged to the current route. While doing so its worker observed that :article/author-follow-rollback looks like the same shape: a failed follow on article alpha, settling after navigation to beta, would flip the on-screen author flag for BETA.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED THERE. rf2-84iek non-goals it, and the worker had no reproduced defect for it. It named the suspicion in the source rather than acting on an unverified premise, which is the right call and is why this is a separate bead rather than scope creep on that PR.

WHAT MAKES THIS NON-OBVIOUS, and the reason it should not be fixed by pattern-matching the sibling: rf2-84iek established that gating alone was NOT sufficient for the comment paths. The comments slice is route-owned and resets on slug change, but the comment FORM was not -- so refusing a stale settle left the next articles form permanently locked with its textarea and Post button disabled. The fix needed a gate AND a reset, as two halves of one change. Whoever takes this must ask the same question of the author/follow state: is it route-owned and reset on navigation, or does it ride across? If it rides, a gate alone reproduces that same lock-out bug in a new place.

FIRST STEP IS TO REPRODUCE OR REFUTE. If the author-follow state turns out to be route-owned and already reset by :article/load, there is no defect and saying so with the evidence closes this. Do not fix it on the strength of the resemblance.

SCOPE: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ plus the existing production-source CLJS suite at implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs. No framework work, no new mutation abstraction, no Playwright spec.
acceptance_criteria: `:article/delete-success` carries the issuing slug and navigates home only while that slug still owns `[:article]`. A held alpha delete settled after navigation to beta leaves beta current; the same success settled while alpha is current still navigates home. Reuse the existing slug gate and request target shape; no new framework machinery.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8911 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

The three db-write gates are correct, route-owned, and well tested. Completeness stops one settle too early: `:article/delete-success` is excluded because it writes no db, yet it dispatches navigation and the source itself acknowledges that a late alpha success sends a reader who has moved to beta home. Navigation is the active route's stateful effect; a stale reply changing the screen is the same ownership violation even though it does not use `:db`.

Correctness scenario: delete alpha, navigate to beta before the server settles, then deliver alpha success. Current code unconditionally navigates home and discards the reader's newer route choice. Nothing needs to be stranded: the server deletion succeeded, beta remains valid, and returning to alpha later will naturally fail/reload. Implementation quality: carry the issuing slug on the success target and gate the navigation with the existing `reply-for-current-slug?`; add the late-success refusal plus current-slug navigation control. No request epoch, cancellation scheme, or new abstraction.

VERDICT (PR #8938, 2026-09-01). DEFECT REPRODUCED, then fixed. The audit note governs and was followed; the description's author-follow framing is the older layer, already discharged by PR #8911.

REPRODUCTION, against unmodified source. Read /article/alpha, press Delete, hold the DELETE open, walk to /article/beta before the server answers, then let alpha's DELETE succeed. Observed: route id :realworld/home, route params {}. The reader is taken off the article they chose and out to the home page. Three assertions red in the new test; the other 55,169 assertions in the node-test lane green — which is exactly why the existing suite passed with this bug.

FIX. `:article/delete`'s `:on-success` now carries the issuing slug, as its `:on-failure` already did, and `:article/delete-success` asks the existing `reply-for-current-slug?` before dispatching the navigation. No request epoch, no cancellation scheme, no new abstraction — the acceptance criteria's shape exactly.

DOES REFUSING STRAND ANYTHING? Checked at source rather than taken from either text. No. `:article/delete` writes no `:db` at all — it fires the request and nothing else, so there is no `:deleting` flag; the Delete button in `article-meta` has no `:disabled` binding and no pending state; `[:article]` is rebuilt wholesale by `:article/load`'s request hat on a slug change. The server deletion succeeded regardless, so there is no retry to lose, and returning to alpha later fails and reloads like any other missing article. This is the difference from rf2-84iek, where `[:comment-form]` was a boot-time singleton riding across the navigation still `:submitting` — that one needed a gate AND a reset; this one needs the gate alone. A gate alone is what landed.

TESTS (2, both in realworld_cljs_test.cljs, in the existing realworld-article-social-cross-slug deftest, reusing the existing held-request harness): the late-success refusal, carrying the same `beta-slice-is-rebuilt` strand control the three sibling refusals use; and the current-slug navigation control, proving a delete settled on its own slug still goes home.

PROSE. The correlation-gate roster in comments.cljs goes from nine members to ten; `:article/delete-success` moves out of the NON-members note, which now states the real test — "produces no outcome the route owns", not "writes no db", since `:article/delete-success` satisfies the latter while very much needing the gate.

OUT OF SCOPE, untouched: `:editor/delete-success` in article_editor.cljs is a different slice with its own `still-editing?` law; the acceptance criteria names `:article/delete-success` only. Noted here rather than acted on.

GATES, exit codes captured with `echo $?` on the redirect's own command line and quoted from the file. Pre-fix control: compile exit 0; run exit 1, 11152 tests / 55172 assertions, 3 failures, 0 errors. Post-fix: compile exit 0 (5 files recompiled — positive evidence the runtime observed the edit); run exit 0, 11152 tests / 55172 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. check-examples-compile.cjs exit 0, all 56 swept builds compiled with zero warnings, `:examples/realworld` among them. Both gates print their config path, and both named the worker worktree's shadow-cljs.edn. The control here is the pre-fix run rather than a plant, which is stronger: the tests were written and run against unmodified source before the gate existed.

RED UNDER THE CONTROL, all three in the new test: "the DELETE's SUCCESS target carries the slug it was issued on" (actual `[:article/delete-success]`); "a LATE alpha DELETE SUCCESS does not yank beta's reader home" (actual `:realworld/home`); "…the reader's own newer route choice is the one that stands" (actual `{}`). GREEN UNDER THE CONTROL: everything else, including the three db-write gates the audit calls correct, their non-vacuity control, and article-detail-delete-test's existing "a successful detail-page delete navigates home".
AUDIT PR #8938: REOPENED. The alpha→beta case is fixed, but the gate does not actually establish that the issuing slug still owns the ACTIVE ROUTE. `reply-for-current-slug?` compares only the reply slug with cached `[:article :slug]`. Navigating from `/article/alpha` to a non-article route (home, profile, login, editor, etc.) runs that route's own `:on-match` and does not clear the article slice, so its slug remains `alpha`. When the held alpha DELETE succeeds, the new gate still returns true and `:article/delete-success` navigates home, overriding the reader's newer non-article route. The added refusal test covers only `/article/beta`, whose `:article/load` happens to replace the cached slug and therefore cannot expose this gap.

This contradicts the new prose's route-ownership claim and the Bead's “newer route” outcome. Keep the repair small: require that the active route is `:realworld.article/show` with the same slug (or an equivalent explicit release on article exit), and add the non-article-route refusal plus the existing current-slug control. Reuse the existing gate shape where practical; no request epoch, cancellation machinery, or new abstraction.
MAYOR SEQUENCING NOTE, 2026-09-01: NOT dispatched this tick, deliberately - it collides with a live worker.

rf2-9n43e (surface-review(examples-real-apps), worker/conduit-9n43e, dispatched 2026-09-01) is working examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs, BOTH apps' thin app-local managed-HTTP override seams, the external RealWorld test wrappers and the two READMEs. This bead's repair lives in the realworld-http app's :article/delete-success handler and its adapter regression - the same app-local seam territory. Two workers there conflict.
