title: check-examples-assets: missing main.js bootstrap passes the host-page gate
description:
## Scope

The monorepo example host-page contract in examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and its focused executable coverage in implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Cover every index.html and *.index.html already enumerated by listExampleIndexHtml, including ordinary apps, auxiliary Story hosts, and baked SSR/hydration hosts. Do not change application source, the staging runner, or the test-free examples policy.

## Correctness finding

The gate proves that every example host references the shared favicon, OG raster, and stylesheet, but it does not prove that the host loads the compiled application entrypoint. BUILD_OUTPUTS contains main.js only so reference resolution can skip a generated file; absence is never an error. A host with the only <script src="main.js"></script> line deleted therefore passes the live asset scan even though the canonical runner stages and serves a page that cannot boot, render, or hydrate.

This is a cross-example false green rather than a cosmetic metadata gap. The same miss applies to all host shapes the scanner advertises as covered. The independent compile gate compiles shadow-cljs build definitions and never consumes their HTML, while headless example wrappers require namespaces directly and likewise do not prove that a browser host loads main.js.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a disposable checkout, remove the <script src="main.js"></script> line from examples/core/counter/index.html while leaving its favicon, stylesheet, and og:image references intact.
2. Run node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs. It still reports all example host pages plus the shared tree as valid and exits 0.
3. Run node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Its live scan also remains green because it asserts only the errors produced by the same production scanner.
4. Launch the counter through the canonical dev:example runner. The staged index has no bundle entrypoint, so the browser shows no counter and executes none of counter.core/run.

The failure is reproducible without editing the checkout by wrapping fs.readFileSync for one real page, returning its contents with the main.js script removed, and passing that io to scanPage. That exact read-only probe returned errors=[] for examples/core/counter/index.html, examples/core/login/stories.index.html, and examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/index.html.

## Evidence

- examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs:201-209 defines REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS as favicon.svg, og.png, and style.css only.
- Lines 298-300 define BUILD_OUTPUTS = new Set(['main.js']) solely to avoid resolving generated output as a repository source file.
- Lines 558-663 already classify <script src> references distinctly in the shared HTML inventory, so the scanner has the information needed for a precise boot check.
- Lines 1517-1524 skip main.js during local resolution; lines 1539-1563 enforce only REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS. No later scanPage branch requires a script entrypoint.
- Lines 1904-1911 run that same scanPage logic over every enumerated host. The live regression at implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs:308-316 therefore inherits the omission.
- All 32 currently enumerated hosts contain a main.js script reference, which establishes a uniform current invariant rather than an exception-driven policy.
- Removing the script in memory from one ordinary host, one *.index.html Story host, and one SSR host produced only the three remaining shared refs and zero scanner errors in each case.
- examples/TESTING.md:17-20 separates compile, headless CLJS, browser-DOM, and static asset gates. None of those other lanes visits every example host page.

## Failure scenario / invariant

Every monorepo-staged example host must contain a load-bearing script reference to the generated main.js entrypoint. If that reference is deleted, commented out, or changed into a non-loading href, the host is not runnable and the always-run host-page gate must fail. Merely mentioning main.js in an anchor, canonical link, preload, comment, or other generic href must not satisfy the invariant; the proof must come from the existing tagged <script src> inventory.

Without this invariant, an index-only change can merge with a green compile, green headless tests, and green asset scan while the documented one-command runner deterministically serves a blank or non-hydrating page.

## Recommended minimal fix

Reuse extractHtmlReferenceInventory's existing assets rows and add one explicit scanPage check for a tagged <script src> whose normalized ref is main.js. Report the host path and missing entrypoint. Keep BUILD_OUTPUTS' current resolution exemption: generated main.js should be required as a host reference, not looked up in the source tree.

Add one focused synthetic mutation test plus a tag-specific negative control. No parser replacement, build-to-page registry, browser matrix, or new gate is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. scanPage reports a clear violation naming the page and main.js when an otherwise valid host carries every shared asset but has no <script src="main.js">.
2. The check consumes the existing tagged asset inventory: <a href="main.js">, <link href="main.js">, text, and commented-out script markup do not satisfy it.
3. A canonical quoted or unquoted <script src="main.js"> remains green, including the scanner's existing query/hash normalization behavior; main.js remains exempt from source-file existence resolution.
4. A focused test mutates a real currently enumerated host in memory by removing only its live main.js script, asserts the mutation actually removed one script, and proves the production scan turns red. This is the non-vacuity control and must fail against the pre-fix implementation.
5. The live test enumerates a non-empty host set and proves every current index.html and *.index.html passes the new invariant; ordinary, auxiliary Story, and SSR hosts are represented without hard-coding a second build roster.
6. node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs, node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs, and npm run test:script-policy from implementation pass after the fix.

## Non-goals

- Running every example in Playwright or asserting application-specific DOM behavior.
- Resolving generated main.js as a repository source file or inspecting its bytes.
- Supporting alternate legacy bundle names, optional entrypoints, or a generalized HTML/build manifest when every current host uses main.js.
- Changing example apps, shared CSS/images, launch documentation, shadow-cljs builds, or staging behavior.
- Replacing the focused HTML inventory with a general-purpose parser.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for main.js example host, script src main.js, missing main.js, example host page, blank example page, check-examples-assets build output, entrypoint host page, runnable example HTML, and examples asset gate. A full all-status scan of 1,127 issue titles, descriptions, and acceptance fields for main.js, script src, blank page, host page/HTML, example asset, runnable example, and entrypoint found no issue enforcing this invariant.

Open rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 address stale core/capability README commands and prove the existing dev runner can stage a complete page; they do not make the host scanner reject a missing boot script. Open rf2-fmns2 adds a distinct Hicasso example and bundle-isolation coverage. None is a duplicate or owns this scanner/test slice.

## Priority rationale

P2. The repository is pre-alpha and every current host is intact, so this is not an active production outage. However, one ordinary HTML-line deletion breaks the primary runnable-example contract across every example family while all mandatory gates that claim compile/host coverage remain green. The fix is small, central, and directly restores trust in an existing always-run gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- scanPage rejects an otherwise valid host that lacks a live tagged <script src="main.js"> and names both the page and entrypoint.
- Generic hrefs, preload links, text, and commented script markup containing main.js do not satisfy the requirement.
- Quoted and unquoted live main.js script references remain accepted, and generated main.js is still not resolved as a source file.
- A focused in-memory mutation of a real enumerated host removes exactly one main.js script and turns the production scanner red; the control fails on the pre-fix implementation.
- The non-empty live host inventory, including ordinary, Story auxiliary, and SSR hosts, remains green.
- The focused scanner test, scanner CLI, and implementation test:script-policy gate pass.
notes:
--- 2026-09-01 AUSEST — implemented, PR #8855 ---

FINDING CONFIRMED at tip before implementing. A read-only in-memory probe over
the real tree (wrapping readFileSync for one page, returning it with the live
main.js script removed) returned errors=[] from the pre-fix scanPage, and the
CLI still printed "all 32 pages resolve their assets and carry the required
_shared contract". The gate proved every host was DRESSED (favicon + OG raster +
stylesheet) but never that it could RUN.

FIX. scanPage gains one check reading the EXISTING tagged asset inventory for a
live <script src> whose normalised ref is main.js (new exported predicate
loadsBuildEntrypoint, a pure function over the `assets` view). No new parser, no
build-to-page manifest. Because the proof comes from the tagged view rather than
raw HTML, a mere mention does not satisfy it: preload/modulepreload links are
tagged as links not scripts, <a href> and rel=canonical never reach `assets` at
all, prose is not a tag, and commented markup is stripped before extraction.
BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption is UNCHANGED — main.js is required as a page
REFERENCE and still never resolved as a source file. Quoted/single-quoted/
unquoted forms and the existing ?query/#hash normalisation all stay green.
The CLI failure epilogue now names the boot-script cause too.

CONTROL (AC4). The non-vacuity control mutates a REAL enumerated host in memory,
one per host shape, with the shape classified from the ENUMERATED PATH rather
than a second hard-coded build roster (which could drift from
listExampleIndexHtml). It asserts exactly one script element was removed — by
byte length AND against the scanner's own inventory in both directions — then
proves the production scanner turns red for that reason alone (errors.length===1).

RED-BEFORE EVIDENCE. The check was neutralised at its scanPage call site to
reproduce the pre-fix implementation: captured exit 1, 9 failures, all of them
the new boot-contract tests; the control reported "(no errors — the pre-fix
false green)" and the CLI under the same plant still printed "all 32 pages …
valid". The other 157 assertions passed under the plant, so the fault was scoped
and stopped no other namespace. Restored and verified by git blob hash against
the committed object, not by reading a diff. An earlier plant that neutralised
the shared helper instead was discarded: it tripped the control at its inventory
assertion rather than at the production scan — weaker evidence.

GATES (foreground, exit codes captured to file, final rebased base 4e27fbbe49):
  node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs  -> exit 0, 166 PASS / 0 FAIL (18 new)
  node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs             -> exit 0, all 32 hosts green
  npm run test:scripts (from implementation/)                 -> exit 0, 122 tests / 122 pass / 0 fail

AC6 PREMISE FAILURE — worth carrying forward. AC6 names `npm run
test:script-policy` from implementation. THAT SCRIPT DOES NOT EXIST, neither on
this branch's base nor on origin/main (no key matching /polic/ in
implementation/package.json in either). The covering gate for
implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs is `npm run test:scripts`, which is what ran;
it executes the focused suite as one of its files (18 new assertions confirmed
present in its log). Future beads citing this gate should name test:scripts.

LIVE SET. 32 enumerated hosts, every one carrying exactly one
`<script src="main.js">` — 30 ordinary index.html (three of them the baked
SSR/hydration hosts under examples/capabilities/ssr/) plus the two Story
auxiliary *.index.html showcase hosts. Uniform invariant, not an
exception-driven policy.

NON-GOALS HONOURED: no application source changed, no staging-runner change, no
example index.html edited (the mutation is in-memory only), examples stay
test-free, no alternate/legacy bundle names or generalised HTML/build manifest,
main.js bytes never inspected.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8855 (commit 23be46c684) — scanPage now requires a live <script src=main.js> read off the existing tagged asset inventory; BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption unchanged. Control mutates a real enumerated host in memory per host shape and proves the production scan turns red; verified red against the pre-fix implementation (9 failures, control reporting '(no errors — the pre-fix false green)'). Gates: focused suite exit 0 (166 PASS), live scan exit 0 (32 hosts), npm run test:scripts exit 0 (122/122). NB AC6's 'npm run test:script-policy' does not exist on origin/main; the covering gate is 'npm run test:scripts' — see notes.

title: testbed-support: auto-detect skips the position probe for column-only coordinates
description:
## Scope

Correct the repository dev-server open-in-editor behavior for the already-supported `:windsurf` editor preference in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj`, with focused server/client contract coverage. Preserve the existing endpoint-preferred, editor-URI-fallback architecture and all other editor behavior.

## Correctness finding

The endpoint advertises Windsurf as a supported editor hint but the installed `launch-editor@2.14.1` does not know how to encode a Windsurf source position. It strips `:line` and `:column`, invokes `windsurf` with only the bare file, and can exit successfully. The server then returns HTTP 200, so the browser logs endpoint success and suppresses the existing `windsurf://` fallback that would have retained the coordinate.

This breaks the core jump-to-source invariant: a successful open for a supported configured editor must land at the requested line/column, or the endpoint must decline so the coordinate-preserving fallback gets its turn.

## Evidence

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj:23-30` explicitly maps query value `windsurf` to command `windsurf`.
- The same file's `build-file-spec` and `launch!` pass `path:line:column` to `launch-editor`, and lines 177-183 interpret child exit 0 as `{:ok true}`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs` serialises keyword `:windsurf` as `editor=windsurf`; its fetch path treats every 2xx as final success and calls the URI fallback only on a non-2xx/network failure.
- Xray's documented/configured editor vocabulary includes `:windsurf`; `implementation/core` also has a coordinate-preserving `windsurf://file/<path>:<line>:<column>` URI implementation and tests.
- `implementation/package-lock.json` installs `launch-editor` 2.14.1. Its `get-args.js` has explicit position cases for `code`, `cursor`, `zed`, and JetBrains binaries, but none for `windsurf`.
- Executable probe from `implementation/`:
  `node -e "const g=require('./node_modules/launch-editor/get-args'); for (const e of ['windsurf','code']) console.log(e, JSON.stringify(g(e,'C:/repo/src/app.cljs','27','9')));"`
  produces `windsurf ["C:/repo/src/app.cljs"]` versus `code ["-r","-g","C:/repo/src/app.cljs:27:9"]`.
- The current JVM tests assert only that `editor-hint "windsurf"` equals `"windsurf"`; they never exercise the dependency's resulting argv or prove line/column survival.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a repository Story/Xray dev testbed through its wired `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` handler.
2. Configure the tool editor preference as `:windsurf`.
3. Click a source coordinate such as `{:file "src/app.cljs" :line 27 :column 9}`.
4. Observe the endpoint request includes `line=27&column=9&editor=windsurf`.
5. Inspect the installed launcher's computed arguments: Windsurf receives only the bare file, whereas VS Code receives a goto-position argument.
6. When the Windsurf command exits 0, observe the endpoint returns 200 and the client does not navigate to its coordinate-preserving `windsurf://...:27:9` fallback.

## Expected Behavior

A successful Windsurf click opens the requested file at line 27, column 9. If the installed endpoint launcher cannot guarantee that coordinate, the endpoint returns a non-2xx result so the existing Windsurf URI fallback runs exactly once.

## Actual Behavior

The endpoint can report success after launching Windsurf with only the file path. The requested line and column are lost, and the success response prevents fallback.

## Failure scenario / invariant

For any supported editor preference, endpoint success means the complete source coordinate was handed to an editor in that editor's accepted position syntax. A bare-file launch is not success for a coordinate-bearing request. This matters on every Windsurf source chip in Xray/Story: the visible action appears to work, but lands at an arbitrary prior cursor position or file start rather than the diagnostic site the programmer selected.

## Recommended minimal fix

Until `launch-editor` itself supports a Windsurf goto-position mapping, deliberately decline the Windsurf endpoint hint with a non-2xx response and let the already-implemented `windsurf://file/...:line:column` client fallback handle it. Keep this as a small explicit capability decision near the editor-hint/handler boundary; do not silently auto-detect another editor and do not build a second per-editor process launcher. If a later pinned `launch-editor` release demonstrably preserves Windsurf positions, the explicit decline can be removed with the same contract test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused executable test drives a coordinate-bearing `editor=windsurf` request through the real server/client decision seam and proves one of two valid outcomes: the editor invocation demonstrably retains line 27 and column 9, or the endpoint returns non-2xx and the existing Windsurf URI fallback runs exactly once with `:27:9`. A 2xx response paired with bare-file-only Windsurf argv must fail the test.
2. The preferred minimal implementation for the currently pinned `launch-editor@2.14.1` returns a bounded launch-declined response for Windsurf before a misleading bare-file success; the browser then uses the existing `windsurf://` fallback without a second endpoint attempt.
3. Non-vacuity: a negative-control stub/path that reports successful bare-file Windsurf launch makes the focused test red. A positive control using the same coordinate with `editor=vscode` still reaches the endpoint, retains `27:9`, returns 2xx, and does not call fallback; the repair must not make every editor fall back.
4. The existing testbed-support JVM suite and the shared open-endpoint client tests pass. The supported editor vocabulary remains `:vscode`, `:cursor`, `:windsurf`, `:zed`, and `:idea`; only the transport selected for Windsurf changes while the dependency lacks coordinate support.
5. Tracker/docs comments that claim the endpoint handles every configured editor are made truthful if touched; no new configuration knob or compatibility layer is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the endpoint path/query grammar, loopback security boundary, classpath resolution, timeout/drain logic, or checkout-root plumbing.
- Vendoring or forking `launch-editor`, teaching it a general editor capability registry, or implementing a second direct Windsurf CLI launcher.
- Changing URI syntax, editor preference vocabulary, Xray/Story source-chip UI, or behavior for VS Code, Cursor, Zed, IDEA, custom editors, and auto-detection.
- Speculative support for editors not already in the repository vocabulary.

## Related / duplicate search

- `rf2-3xq1v` (open, owned) retires checkout-root plumbing. It explicitly lists editor vocabulary and `launch-editor` behavior as non-goals, so this runtime coordinate-loss repair is distinct.
- All-status tracker title, description, and notes searches for `windsurf` found no issue. All-status `launch-editor` searches found only `rf2-3xq1v`, whose scope excludes this finding. Searches for editor hints and line/column loss found no matching testbed/open-endpoint owner.
- Historical endpoint work introduced the preferred endpoint/fallback seam, but no current or closed outcome bead owns Windsurf position preservation.
acceptance_criteria: A column-only no-hint/custom launch (`line=nil`, `column=7`) runs the same dependency capability probe as a line-bearing launch, using normalized line 1. A real-node test proves a position-blind resolved editor is declined and a position-capable editor still reaches a launch attempt; the endpoint maps the decline to 422 and fallback retains `:1:7`. Existing no-coordinate behavior stays unchanged.

title: [views] adapter switch makes the lookup cache fall back to the stale registered head
description:
## Scope

The registry-keyed UIx view path spanning `implementation/adapters/uix/**`, the adapter seam consumed by `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs`, its React-hook shared tests, and the public UIx registry-addressing contract. This is specifically the value registered by `rf/reg-view*` and returned by `rf/view` when the UIx adapter is active.

## Correctness finding

The documented UIx registry-keyed path does not return a component head that UIx/React can mount. `build-frame-aware-view` unconditionally attaches `{:contextType frame-context}` with CLJS metadata, so `(rf/view id)` is a `MetaFn` object rather than a JavaScript function component. Passing that advertised value directly to UIx `$` / React `createElement` fails React's element-type validation before the registered view renders.

The obvious partial repair—only removing the metadata—is also incorrect for UIx. UIx sends lossless CLJS props through its `argv` channel only for a native/marked UIx component head; a generic React function goes through JS-prop conversion. The registered outer wrapper therefore needs to be both genuinely mountable and on UIx's native prop-marshalling path. It must also preserve a real React component boundary for hooks rather than requiring callers to invoke the registered function inside an ad-hoc host component.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:16` tells users to use `rf/reg-view*` for registry-keyed view addressing; `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:109` and `:253-262` repeat that UIx contract.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:496-612` (`build-frame-aware-view`) creates the registered head with `(with-meta (fn frame-aware-view ...) {:contextType frame-context})`. `reg-view*` stores and returns that value at `:614-650`.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:6610-6625` explicitly records the current defect: `(rf/view id)` is a CLJS `MetaFn`, React cannot use it as a component type directly, so the test mounts a plain JS `host` that manually invokes `render-fn`. The void-root test repeats this bypass at `:6670-6678`. Those tests therefore prove teardown below the workaround, not the advertised registry-head mount.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:93-106` and `:131-138` require native `defui` shells specifically because UIx reconstructs lossless CLJS props there. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1627-1650` documents the prior failure when a plain function sat below `$`: namespaced keyword values were mangled and frame selection silently changed.
- Reading the pinned `com.pitch/uix.core` 1.4.4 sources (`uix/core.clj`, `uix/compiler/alpha.cljs`) confirms `defui` stamps a JS function as a UIx component and UIx's compiler uses that marker to carry original CLJS props in `argv`; the generic React-component branch converts props instead.
- Repository search found no UIx test that mounts `(rf/view id)` directly as the `$` component head. Existing UIx DOM coverage either mounts `wrap-view` itself or uses the manual-invocation host above.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `uix-adapter/adapter`, define a UIx `defui` component that receives a CLJS prop and calls `uix-adapter/use-subscribe`, then register it with `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)`.
2. Under the normal UIx frame boundary, render `($ (rf/view ::row) {:payload {:tenant/id :tenant/admin}})` without an intermediate function that invokes the returned value.
3. Observe that React rejects the `MetaFn` as an invalid element type before the registered view renders. The existing shared browser test avoids this result only by mounting a plain JS host component that manually invokes `(rf/view id)`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A registry-keyed UIx component cannot be used through the component syntax the public docs advertise. If a caller copies the test workaround, hooks and instance lifetime belong to that host and the UIx component's `argv` prop contract is bypassed.

Invariant: every public value advertised as a UIx component head must be directly mountable through `$`, receive the original CLJS props/children losslessly, own a real React hook boundary, and retain the registration wrapper's frame, tracing, source-coordinate, display-name, and unmount behavior.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the UIx adapter's registered-view result an outer, stable, native/marked UIx component shell after the shared frame-aware/instrumentation wrapper has been composed. That shell should receive props through UIx's `argv` path and delegate them without JS round-tripping while retaining a genuine React component boundary. Adjust the shared registration seam only as much as needed to let a React-hook adapter own that outer componentization; do not merely strip `with-meta`, and do not document the manual-invocation host as the solution.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a focused browser test under `implementation/adapters/uix/test/` that installs the UIx adapter, registers a hook-using `defui` via `rf/reg-view*`, and mounts `($ (rf/view id) props)` directly under the normal UIx frame boundary. The test must contain no host function that calls the registered value manually.
2. Pass a nested CLJS prop containing a namespaced keyword/value through that direct mount and assert exact equality inside the registered component; include children if the chosen public form supports them.
3. Have the registered component call `uix-adapter/use-subscribe` (and/or `use-frame`), assert its initial DOM, dispatch an update, and assert the DOM rerenders. Capture browser page errors plus `console.error` and assert there is no invalid-element-type or hook-boundary failure.
4. Retain executable coverage for registered-view render traces/source coordinates, stable instance identity, and exactly-once unmount emission; remove the shared suite's manual-host rationale/bypass where the direct UIx mount now covers it.
5. Non-vacuity/control: in the same harness, directly mount an unregistered native `defui` with the same prop/hook probe and show the harness passes independently of the registry path. During implementation, temporarily restore the current metadata-wrapped returned head (or remove the new UIx componentization seam) and record that the new registry row fails while the native control remains green.
6. `npm run test:browser` from `implementation/` passes with the new direct-mount witness and the existing UIx adapter browser coverage.

## Non-goals

- No new registry API or mandatory host/wrapper ceremony for callers.
- No Reagent registration rewrite.
- No broad React interop compatibility layer or support for arbitrary non-UIx prop conventions.
- No unrelated refactor of the shared spine, tracing schema, or UIx hooks.
- No docs-only workaround.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched the full bead corpus by title and description with `bd search "UIx" --status all`, `bd search` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `registry-keyed view`, `rf/view UIx`, and `invalid element type`, plus `bd list --all --desc-contains` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `(rf/view`, and `uix-component?`. Repeated the material terms against `--status open,in_progress`; there were no matches. Closed `rf2-9hcyf` concerns a copy-pasteable UIx component test recipe, and closed `rf2-3afns` concerns Story selecting the wrong substrate; neither owns direct mountability of a registered UIx view.
acceptance_criteria: A focused CLJS test registers while a componentizing adapter is active (so the registrar stores H1), switches to a differently componentizing or non-componentizing adapter, and proves at least two consecutive `rf/view` lookups both return the new correct stable head and never H1. The cache continues to recognize its original registrar face across re-derivations, while genuine foreign re-registrations pass through untouched. Do not rewrite the registrar or add public API.

## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8874)

CONFIRMED and FIXED. Both premise checks the bead asked for hold.

**Premise (a) — line numbers.** Essentially zero drift. `build-frame-aware-view` is at views.cljs:496 exactly as cited (its body ends 612; `with-meta` closes at 578). `reg-view*` is at :614 as cited. The shared-suite citations are within ~2 lines: the manual-host rationale sits at 6610-6621 (cited 6610-6625) and the void-root repeat at 6667-6672 (cited 6670-6678).

**Premise (b) — the bypass.** Still present and still read exactly as described: both rows mounted `(fn host-cmp [_props] (render-fn))` and the comment named the MetaFn as the reason. Removed in this PR; both rows now mount `(rf/view id)` directly.

**Mechanism, verified at source rather than from the bead's summary.** `uix.compiler.alpha/component-element` (uix.core 1.4.4, read from the pinned jar) branches on `(.-uix-component? component-type)`: marked heads take `uix-component-element`, which stashes the ORIGINAL CLJS props map on `argv`; everything else takes `react-component-element` -> `interpret-attrs`, which converts props and drops keyword namespaces. A MetaFn has no marker, so it fell to the React branch and `createElement` rejected the object.

**Repair.** New OPTIONAL `:adapter/componentize-view` late-bind hook, consulted last in `reg-view*` (after the substrate wrap and the frame-aware wrapper compose, so the shell is outermost and every existing wrapper keeps its frame/tracing/source-coord/unmount behaviour). Seam split follows rf2-z7hfp's frame-provider precedent: `spine/make-componentize-view` builds the substrate-agnostic forwarding shell; the UIx adapter stamps `uix-component?` on it. The marker -- not the meta-stripping -- is what makes the mount correct. The shell is a marked FORWARDER, not a `defui`: `defui` glues `argv` for its own body, so the shell must pass the props object down untouched for the registered component (typically itself a `defui`) to read in its own idiom -- which is what keeps `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)` ceremony-free, per the bead's Non-goals. Reagent publishes no hook and is unaffected.

The head remains the callable render fn Spec 001 describes. The shell separates React's `Component(props, secondArg)` call from direct positional invocation; react-dom 19.2.0's `updateFunctionComponent` passes `void 0` as `secondArg` (read from source), so without that split a stray undefined would reach the user fn and the rf2-rpgq8 render-args capture.

**No spec change was needed, and this was checked rather than assumed.** Spec 001 s`(re-frame.core/view id)` says "the registered render fn (whatever shape)" -- the change is a strict superset. `spec/Conventions.md:1762` is a generic `:adapter/<surface>` pattern row with examples, not an enumeration, so the HOT-ZONE file stayed untouched. No new public adapter Var, so `spec/API.md` needs no row either.

**Acceptance criteria.** AC1-AC3 met by the new browser row `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` in `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (no manual host anywhere in the file; nested namespaced-keyword prop asserted for exact equality inside the component; trailing `$` child; `use-subscribe` + `use-frame`; console.error AND window-error capture asserted clean of invalid-element-type and hook-boundary diagnostics). AC4 met: both shared-suite rows now mount the head directly, plus a third row pinning stable instance identity and continued headless callability. AC5 met (control below). AC6 met.

**Gates (captured exit codes, all on the final rebased base fd0113d5bf).** browser compile 0; browser run 0 (755 tests / 4130 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors); node lane `test:cljs` 0 (11133 / 54718, 0 failures); late-bind drift JVM 0; `:advanced` prod-elision release build 0 and its browser run 0 (91 / 289) -- run deliberately because the shell exists in production builds and `uix-component?` is a property name under a release compile.

**Control (AC5) -- the gate bites.** Restoring the metadata-wrapped head (hook key pointed at a non-existent key; source change proved by blob hash, 313 files recompiled so the runtime saw it) turned the browser run RED, exit 1: `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` failed 9 assertions, the first reading verbatim "Element type is invalid: expected a string ... but got: object", while `native-defui-control-mounts-independently-of-the-registry` -- the same probe body and the same assertion block, mounted as an unregistered native defui -- stayed GREEN. The two de-bypassed shared-suite rows also errored, which shows the bypass removal was load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object (35f57741a4467ede665e33b162a1523e5779f426, both sides). A second control confirmed the late-bind drift gate is non-vacuous: removing the directory row reds it in both directions.

**Found beyond the brief.** `make-react-adapter` initially routed the new hook unconditionally, so every React-shaped caller supplying no factory published a NIL impl -- and `route-hook!` stores what it is handed and calls it once its adapter is installed, so the first `reg-view*` under that adapter THREW instead of declining. The browser lane could not see this; the node lane caught it as 16 errors, all on `re-frame.hicasso.substrate`, which owns its own view path (the spine's bench/test adapters are in the same position). Fixed by guarding the routing on the factory being present. Worth remembering as a general hazard of `route-hook!`: an optional routed hook must not be published at all when its impl is absent, because a routed nil is indistinguishable from a published handler until it is called.
AUDIT PR #8874 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The new componentization is decided at registration time through a routed hook, so it still misses the repository's canonical boot order. `boot-and-mount-an-app.md` requires registration namespaces (including views) at namespace load, before `run` calls `rf/init!`. In that sequence `:adapter/componentize-view` sees no installed adapter, `route-hook!` returns nil, `apply-adapter-componentize-view` keeps the MetaFn, and `init!` only seats the adapter—it never revisits existing `:view` entries. `(rf/view id)` therefore remains a non-JS-function and the advertised direct UIx `$` mount still fails. The new browser fixture installs UIx before every `reg-view*`, so it cannot see this normal path. Minimal repair: add a register-before-init → init-UIx → direct-mount witness and make existing view registrations acquire the UIx head without requiring application authors to move top-level registrations into `run`; retain post-init registration, inactive-adapter routing, and stable lookup identity. No broad adapter redesign.

## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8909) — the AUDIT reopen

CONFIRMED and FIXED. The audit's claim holds exactly as written, and was verified at source rather than taken from the note.

**Mechanism.** substrate-adapter/route-hook! (adapter.cljc:788) wraps every published impl in a closure that dispatches to it ONLY while same-adapter? says its adapter is the installed one, and otherwise chains to the previous handler or calls fallback-fn — (constantly nil) for this hook. reg-view* consulted it at REGISTRATION. Under boot-and-mount-an-app.md's order the registration namespaces load first, at ns-load, and run calls rf/init! afterwards, so the consultation happened with no adapter installed, returned nil, apply-adapter-componentize-view kept the MetaFn, and install-adapter! (which only seats a generation and re-arms the SSR emitter) never revisits existing :view slots. Every row that installed the adapter before registering sailed past it.

**Repair — a SEAM fix, not an adapter one.** The head is not a property of the registration; it is a property of (registration x installed substrate), and the substrate is not knowable at registration under the canonical order. So derive it at LOOKUP and memoize. views/view-head is what re-frame.core/view calls on CLJS. Validity is keyed on BOTH halves: the composed wrapper's object identity (a re-registration or hot-reload forces re-derivation, and a :view slot views.cljs did not build is handed back untouched) and the adapter spec via same-adapter? (a dispose then install of a different substrate re-derives rather than serving a UIx-marked shell to Reagent). Identity is stable within an adapter generation, so React reconciles (rf/view id) as one component type. Post-init registration is unaffected — the reg-time derivation seeds the cache and the first lookup is a hit.

**Why the registrar slot is NOT rewritten on the lazy upgrade.** registrar/register! fires every replacement hook and emits :rf.registry/handler-replaced on EVERY call (Spec 001 Hot-reload trace surface). Re-registering at lookup would publish a phantom hot-reload to devtools on the first render after boot — a worse bug than the one being fixed. The slot keeps what registration stored; the cache owns the substrate projection.

**Reagent shares the seam but not the defect, and the reason decides the fix's home.** Reagent's create-class / fn-to-class machinery reads the :contextType meta off the MetaFn and converts it into a React component type; React has no such conversion and rejects the object. So Reagent tolerates a MetaFn where React does not, publishes no componentize-view (grep for componentize across adapters/reagent/src, adapters/reagent-slim/src and hicasso/src returns zero, control search for frame-provider returns matches), and its head is the wrapper unchanged. Reagent's returned value is bit-identical in every ordering after this change, because apply-adapter-componentize-view returns the wrapper both at registration and at any re-derivation when no hook is published.

**Public contract.** docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md told users to reach for rf/reg-view* for registry-keyed view addressing and never showed what to do with the result — there was no working continuation to document. It now carries a Registry-keyed views section stating the route end to end and three properties: the head is a component rather than a function to invoke, props and children arrive losslessly through UIx's argv channel, and REGISTRATION ORDER DOES NOT MATTER. That last clause is the contract change worth naming: previously neither stated nor true.

**Witness.** New browser row boot-order-registration-yields-a-mountable-head-after-init registers at ns-load before any adapter exists and asserts that premise before mounting (no adapter at registration; the reg-time head really was the MetaFn), so it cannot decay into a copy of the post-init row. use-fixtures moved below that registration because make-reset-runtime-fixture snapshots the registrar at call time as its ns-load baseline (rf2-7hwnu).

The post-init row direct-mount-of-registered-view-head and the unregistered-native-defui control both stayed GREEN, so the red is attributable to the boot-order path and not to the harness. That degrades only dev-only source-coord annotation (the walk mis-classifies a React element root and skips it) rather than the mount, so it is a separate, lower-severity bead rather than a widening of this one.
AUDIT PR #8909 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

The boot-before-init repair and its witness are sound. The cache's adapter-change claim is not. Let a post-init UIx registration compose wrapper W into head H1; the registrar slot stores H1 and the cache stores {wrapper W, head H1, adapter A1}. title: surface-review(story-mcp): make project stories reachable on first launch
description:
## Scope

Make the published headless Story-MCP server expose a consumer project's JVM-loadable Story registry on its first MCP connection. Add one explicit launch-time namespace-loading seam, document one copyable consumer-project/MCP-host configuration, and prove the path end to end against a project-owned story. Preserve the settled boundary that live browser/CLJS stories are reached through re-frame2-pair.

## Findings

Story-MCP is a same-JVM adapter: every catalogue read, run, and write operates on the process-local Story registry. That makes loading the consumer's registration namespaces a prerequisite, not optional setup polish.

The only canonical launch is `clojure -M -m re-frame.story-mcp.server` from the tool directory. The README adds one sentence saying the launch “must preload” registry-populating JVM namespaces, but supplies no argument, alias, wrapper, MCP-host config, ordering rule, or executable example that does so. The server CLI accepts only the two gate flags and ignores every other flag; `boot!` installs canonical vocabulary and immediately enters the stdio loop. A normal launch therefore has tags/assertions but no project stories.

The integration corpus proves protocol and synthetic in-memory behavior, not the consumer workflow. `stdio-roundtrip.js` uses the bare canonical command and deliberately probes missing stories/variants. The SDK conformance harness starts the same command with `--allow-writes`, creates a synthetic variant only after connecting, and explicitly notes that a successful story read would need a registered story. No test starts the published server from a consuming project, preloads a project namespace, then discovers and runs that already-authored story.

This is the first-use bottleneck for the whole 20-tool catalogue: until a project registry is present, the documented `list-stories -> get-story/get-variant -> run/refine` workflow cannot begin. More protocol hardening or another tool would not fix it.

## Recommended Action

Add one repeatable explicit startup option, for example `--require app.stories.login`, whose values are trusted namespace names from the invoking project's classpath. In `boot!`, install Story's canonical vocabulary first, then `require` the supplied namespaces, then start the MCP loop. Let an ordinary require failure abort startup loudly; do not add namespace scanning, a custom discovery protocol, allowlists, or redundant name validation.

Document a single golden consumer path: a `deps.edn` alias that depends on `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp`, a project-root MCP-host command using that alias plus the explicit namespace option, and the write-gate flag only when the author/refine loop is wanted. State plainly that the namespace must be CLJ/CLJC-loadable in this headless JVM; a running browser's CLJS registry remains the pair's one live door.

Back the path with one consumer-shaped fixture driven through the official MCP SDK: launch from the fixture project, load its story namespace at boot, and immediately discover/read/run its pre-authored story without first calling `register-variant`.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:37-51` shows the bare tool-directory command and only the unimplemented “must preload” sentence.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:337-365` parses only `--allow-writes` and `--allow-sensitive-reads`; unknown flags are logged and ignored.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:368-384` applies gates and installs canonical vocabulary but has no consumer-namespace load step.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:17,74-80` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:35-55` make registrations/runs process-local and define Story-MCP as the headless same-JVM host.
- `tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js:45-51,247-281` calls the bare launch and verifies only missing-variant plus gated-write behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consuming project's documented `deps.edn` alias and MCP-host configuration start the published Story-MCP main from the project root without repository-local source paths or a user-written wrapper namespace.
- One repeatable explicit namespace option loads named CLJ/CLJC registration namespaces after canonical vocabulary installation and before the server accepts MCP requests; multiple supplied namespaces preserve command order.
- An official-SDK end-to-end fixture launches through that consumer path and, before any MCP write, proves `list-stories` finds the fixture story, `get-story` or `get-variant` reads it, and `run-variant` executes its fixture variant.
- A missing or throwing supplied namespace terminates startup with a useful stderr diagnostic/non-zero exit rather than continuing with a misleading empty project registry. The implementation relies on ordinary `require` failure; it does not invent a second validation layer.
- README/spec guidance clearly distinguishes JVM-loadable project namespaces from the running browser's CLJS registry and routes the latter to re-frame2-pair.
- Existing no-namespace launches, gate semantics, the MCP method set, tool names, tool input/output schemas, and Story's public registration API remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Adding nREPL, a JVM-to-browser bridge, or a second live-app transport.
- Auto-discovering namespaces by scanning source roots, classpaths, files, manifests, or naming conventions.
- Hot reload, namespace watching, runtime load/unload tools, or persistence of registrations to source files.
- Adding a new MCP tool, a new Story registration primitive, or extra env/sysprop aliases/config DSLs for the same bootstrap.
- Redesigning the 20-tool catalogue, token budgeting, privacy egress, cursor protocol, or JSON-RPC lifecycle.
- Making CLJS-only story namespaces JVM-loadable.

- `rf2-s99lw4` (closed) documented the pair-side browser recipe through `eval-cljs`; it is the complementary path, not a duplicate.

title: Incomplete Graph preview fidelity: shortened record extension keys erase the type tag
description:
Merged-PR audit #10096, d672b7f4ce07744d350a78a3c1468a72a3fadd36. The collision/order fix works for plain maps and sets, but the new rendered map window in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_helpers.cljc:269-288 always opens with "{". Records also satisfy map?, so a record with an extension key that needs bounding loses its printed record type tag. That changes the operator-visible first 80 characters, even though the PR claims preview fidelity and record preservation.

Concrete reproduction from the exact merged helper: (defrecord Probe [body]); (assoc (->Probe "short") (apply str (repeat 200000 "x")) 1). The original and pre-PR bounded print start #graph_record.Probe{:body "short", ...; the merged print starts {:body "short", ... . Independent assertions establish that the pre-PR helper preserves the prefix and the merged helper does not. The ordinary long record VALUE still preserves its tag, so that existing positive control does not cover this branch. Plain-map collision and prefix corrections remain good.

Keep this a small preview-production correction: preserve the record's original printed type prefix when rendering a bounded key window, without reinserting shortened keys or materializing unbounded strings. Add a discriminating record-extension-key regression that checks the visible prefix as well as bounded work; retain the plain-map/set collision regressions. No new public policy or general collection framework is needed.

Evidence: ignored ai/audit-graph-record-audit-sep20-monitor-1.clj and ai/gate-graph-record-audit-sep20-monitor-1.log/.exit, exit 0, correct worktree banner. Exact merged-source Babashka/CLJC reproduction, not a claimed CLJS/browser run. title: False breadth in the beads-durability claim: 'bd rewrites it in every checkout' reads as 'a bd READ dirties your worktree'
description:
Found by the mayor's §5 method reread, 2026-09-17, by re-running a test rather than re-reading a report.

## The claim, and what is wrong with it

CLAUDE.md § Beads durability opens: "`.beads/issues.jsonl` is a full-database export, not an ordinary
source file. `bd` rewrites it in **every** checkout, so each worker worktree carries a snapshot of the
tracker as it stood when that worktree was created."

The paragraph's PURPOSE is correct and must survive: committing that snapshot time-travels the tracker,
and PR #6677 landed exactly that (135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Nothing here
weakens the rule that worker branches never carry `.beads/issues.jsonl`.

What is too broad is the sentence "`bd` rewrites it in EVERY checkout", read — as it naturally is —
to mean that ANY `bd` invocation rewrites the export in the checkout it runs from. A reader who takes
it that way concludes that even a READ dirties a worker worktree, and therefore that a worker must not
run `bd` at all.

## The measurement, both ways

On a FRESHLY CREATED worktree at `origin/main` (`git worktree add --detach`), confirmed clean at zero
porcelain lines before anything ran:

    bd show rf2-y8doi.13 --json    -> exit 0, porcelain 0, blob 168055bf02aa (unchanged)
    bd ready --limit 0 --json      -> exit 0, porcelain 0, blob 168055bf02aa (unchanged)
    bd list  --limit 0 --json      -> exit 0, porcelain 0, blob 168055bf02aa (unchanged)

Blob hash identical before and after all three. Repeated independently on an OLD worker worktree
(`restoregc-9nlg1`), where `bd` may already have initialised, with the same result: exit 0, porcelain
0, blob `b457814e4b` unchanged. Both the fresh-checkout case and the already-used case were tested,
because "fresh checkout" is the confound the sentence's own wording suggests.

So: a `bd` READ does not dirty a worker worktree. The export is rewritten by WRITES.

## Why this cost something, and the shape it belongs to

This is a SIBLING OF rf2-d3l8g, which is currently in flight as PR #9940: a claim that is TRUE in the
narrow case it was measured from, stated as a universal, where the over-broad half sends a worker to
the wrong action. There it was "late-bind changes are graded by the node lane ALONE"; here it is "`bd`
rewrites it in every checkout".

The cost was real rather than theoretical. A worker reported the over-broad reading back to the mayor
in good faith, and the mayor propagated it into THREE live dispatch briefs as "do not run `bd` at all"
within the hour — without testing it. Two of those three beads (rf2-y8doi.18 and rf2-y8doi.30) carry
their RULING and their IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF in the bead description and nowhere else, so the
instruction told those workers not to read the one artefact they most needed. All three were corrected
mid-flight by message; none had acted on it.

It also creates a CONTRADICTION INSIDE ONE DISPATCH, which is the mechanical tell: every brief opens by
telling the worker to read the bead FIELD with `bd show <id> --json` (item (k)), so "do not run `bd` at
all" cannot be obeyed alongside it. A worker flagged exactly that conflict and resolved it by following
the more recent instruction — correctly, but it should never have had to choose.

## Required correction

Narrow the sentence to what was measured, WITHOUT weakening the boundary rule. Something of the shape:
`bd` regenerates the export when it WRITES, so a worker worktree accumulates tracker state through `bd`
writes rather than through reads; reads (`bd show`, `bd ready`, `bd list`, `bd recall`) leave the
working file untouched. Keep every existing statement that worker branches must never carry
`.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json`, keep the PR #6677 evidence, and keep the pre-commit
hook and CI arm exactly as they are.

Acceptance: a reader is told why a worker must not COMMIT tracker state and must not run `bd` WRITES
from a worktree, without being told that reading its own bead is unsafe. Verify the wording against a
re-run of the measurement above rather than against this bead's report of it.

## Scope and sequencing

- Fence: `CLAUDE.md`, and within it the § Beads durability opening paragraph only.
- SEQUENCE THIS BEHIND PR #9940 (rf2-d3l8g), which is open against `CLAUDE.md` right now. Two workers
  must never edit one file concurrently; this is a blocks dependency in substance even where the
  paragraphs differ.
- No new gate, no CI lane, no script. This is a wording fix.
- `CLAUDE.md` is `i/lf w/crlf`: never `sed -i` (item (u)), build replacement text with the Write tool
  rather than a heredoc (item (o)), and take the three line-ending numbers with Python on bytes, since
  a bare `grep -c $'\r'` reads 0 on this exact file (item (s)).
- The gate for repo-root markdown is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`, NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`,
  whose roots exclude repo-root markdown and which exits 0 on a broken link there.

PR #9943, merged at 8354b88e53. ONE LINE, one file, CLAUDE.md § Beads durability opening paragraph.
Band 88 on all five clauses, matrix unmoved by ancestry.

DELIVERED. The paragraph now says `bd` regenerates the export when the tracker is WRITTEN, that a
checkout otherwise receives it the way it receives any other tracked file, and — in terms — that a `bd`
READ is not how a worktree acquires tracker state and reading your own bead is safe. The measurement is
inline, scoped to `bd` 1.2.2 and dated.

THE WORKER BUILT A BETTER INSTRUMENT THAN THE ONE IT WAS GIVEN, AND THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING
HERE. The mayor's original test was porcelain plus a blob hash. The worker added two observables that
test cannot produce:

  * A CONTENT HASH CANNOT SEPARATE "did not write" FROM "rewrote the identical bytes". An idempotent
    rewrite is still the tool touching the checkout and is invisible to the hash. It recorded MTIME
    alongside; unchanged mtime is what actually rules out a rewrite.
  * `git status --porcelain` IS BLIND TO GITIGNORED SIBLINGS, and the write you are hunting may not be
    to the tracked file at all. `.beads/.gitignore` provides for a per-worktree `redirect` file plus
    locks, daemon files and export state — all gitignored, therefore invisible to porcelain, and all
    genuinely tracker state accumulating in a checkout. It listed `.beads/` before and after. This was
    the falsifier it EXPECTED to fire, and neither of the mayor's two instruments could have seen it.

MEASURED BOTH CASES, because "fresh checkout" is the confound the old wording's own phrasing suggests:
a freshly created worktree (confirmed at 0 porcelain before anything ran) and an already-in-use one,
five reads each — `bd show --json`, `bd ready --limit 0 --json`, `bd list --limit 0 --json`,
`bd recall <key>` and a plain `bd show` — all ten exit 0. Fresh: porcelain 0->0, blob 856ceaf132
unchanged, size 27746918 unchanged, mtime 1789646991 unchanged, `.beads/` listing identical at 7

AND IT TOOK A POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE INSTRUMENT, which is what makes the zeros evidence rather than a
probe that cannot see: an 18-byte append moved EVERY reading at once — porcelain 0->1, blob ->cd7da2c287,
size +18, mtime advanced — and `git checkout --` returned all three.

IT FOUND A NON-SEQUITUR THE BEAD DID NOT NAME, and the repair makes the paragraph's purpose STRONGER
rather than weaker. The old sentence's "so" claimed the base-commit snapshot FOLLOWED FROM `bd`

title: tracker: 36% of cited bead ids do not resolve - a branch-retention ruling cited by two sweeps (rf2-lafmr) is gone from the database but recoverable whole from a checkpoint
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by the §4 HYGIENE LOOP doing exactly what §4 prescribes: before disposing of a
retained branch, "ask the tracker who owns it — include CLOSED items, because such rulings are
written in close reasons." The tracker named an owner. The owner does not exist.

## THE INSTANCE

`worker/receipts-hic081` is kept under a standing ruling. Two separate beads cite that ruling by id:

    rf2-pi2p   "worker/receipts-hic081 is NOT in scope: KEEP under rf2-lafmr
                (release condition: counts-only capability receipts implemented on main
                 with both owed witnesses discharged, or the design explicitly abandoned)"
    rf2-7ngc   "ALREADY RULED KEEP by rf2-lafmr (2026-08-21) with a release condition"

**`rf2-lafmr` does not exist.** Two instruments, controls both ways: `bd show rf2-lafmr --json`
exits 1 against `bd show rf2-pi2p` exit 0 returning a list; an identity-field select over the
1,676 issue records finds no id beginning `rf2-laf` at all, while `rf2-pi2p` reads EXISTS and a
nonsense id reads ABSENT. Ten records cite it.

## THE CLASS, MEASURED — AND THE FIRST INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG

Over all 1,676 issue records, distinct `rf2-` ids appearing in title, description, notes or
close reason, excluding each record's own id:

    distinct ids cited       2199
    resolve                  1407
    DANGLING                  792   (36%)

Ranked by distinct citers: rf2-wad2fl 17, rf2-w01c 11, rf2-csbbwu 9, rf2-s52w 8, then a tail of
sevens including rf2-lafmr.

**THE FIRST PASS READ 35% FOR PARTLY WRONG REASONS AND THE TOP TWO ENTRIES WERE PHANTOMS.** A
character class admitting only letters and digits truncated `rf2-hic-063` at its hyphen, so a
non-existent `rf2-hic` collected 74 citations; and a bare word boundary let the HTML attribute
`data-rf2-source-coord` answer as `rf2-source` with 12 — the same shape as instrument item (g),
where `host-transient` answers for `transient`. Corrected (admit hyphenated ids, refuse a
hyphen-prefixed match) the two artefacts collapse to 1 and 0, real hyphenated ids are seen and
resolve (`rf2-hic-063` cited 32, EXISTS), and the nonsense control stays 0. **The rate barely
moved — 36% — because 74 phantom citations of one phantom id do not shift a population of 792.**
Re-measure before quoting; the corpus grows every tick.

## THEY EXISTED. THEY WERE NOT TYPOS.

Sampling historical exports from git (issue-record counts, control rf2-hic-063):

    2026-06-01  n=5111     2026-08-05  n=2046
    2026-07-01  n=9528     2026-08-22  n=981    rf2-lafmr PRESENT, rf2-w01c and rf2-s52w PRESENT
    2026-07-20  n=2298     2026-09-01  n=1145   rf2-lafmr PRESENT
                           2026-09-08  n=1087   rf2-lafmr GONE

rf2-wad2fl is present on 2026-07-01 and gone by 2026-07-20; rf2-csbbwu is present only on
2026-07-20. The population is wildly non-monotonic, and the last four days are monotonic growth
(1482 to 1676), so nothing is being lost NOW.

## THE RULINGS ARE NOT LOST — THEY ARE UNINDEXED, AND RECOVERY IS CHEAP

`rf2-lafmr` recovered whole from checkpoint `1246e4e42271e7faef74535e9c2891122638a06c`
(2026-08-31): status closed, description 2,586 chars, notes 10,070, close_reason 3,496. Its
close reason carries the KEEP ruling in full, names the release condition, and cites
rf2-hic-081's own close reason recording the retention verbatim.

**So the remedy is the recovery walk CLAUDE.md already documents for an erased close_reason,
applied to a whole bead instead of one field** — git log the export, then
`git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl`, selecting on the identity field. The two traps that bullet
names both bite here and are already written down: select on the id FIELD, never grep the id (it
cross-references, item (f)); and walk a RANGE, never conclude from the newest, because the window
is narrow.

## WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG

It fails in the REASSURING direction for the §4 loop specifically. A sweep that asks the tracker
who owns a branch and gets a bead id back has been ANSWERED — the id is well-formed, two
independent beads agree on it, and the ruling it names is real. Nothing on screen says the
pointer is dead. This tick survived only because rf2-pi2p and rf2-7ngc had each RESTATED the
ruling and its release condition inline, and rf2-lbs9 had independently re-measured the patch
evidence. **That is precisely the practice rf2-im2i1 landed one tick earlier** — carry the
decisive measurement inline, cite a pointer only as supporting detail — and this is a measured
second instance of it paying, on a pointer class that bead did not cover. rf2-im2i1 measured
33% of 67 FILE citations dangling; this is 36% of 2,199 BEAD-ID citations, and unlike the `/ai/`
tree the tracker is not disposable by design.

And the irony is load-bearing rather than decorative: rf2-lafmr's own close reason exists to
answer the complaint that "what is missing is a recorded reason for keeping them, so every
future sweep re-derives it." A month later the recorded reason was unreachable and this sweep
re-derived it.

## NOT ESTABLISHED — AND THIS IS MOST OF WHAT IS LEFT

  * **WHY they vanished. Not investigated, and there are at least three plausible causes already
    named in CLAUDE.md, with different dispositions.** (1) The two empty-export events that
    reached main by plain `git add` — `7aea52459` (2026-06-10, 7172 rows) and `4d8042d80d`
    (2026-07-26, 2573 rows) — sit inside this exact window; CLAUDE.md rules those REGENERATION
    events rather than data loss, because Dolt is the source of truth. (2) Pre-ban `bd gc` decay,
    which deletes closed beads and is the reason the ban exists (rf2-nj0c). (3) A migration.
    **The regeneration reading does not obviously cover these ids, because they are absent from
    the DATABASE now and not merely from an export** — `bd show rf2-lafmr` exits 1 — but that
    was checked for one id, not for the 792.
  * **Whether the mechanism is already closed.** The pre-commit hook now refuses a staged
    `.beads/issues.jsonl` below 90% of HEAD, and decay is off. Both guards postdate the drops.
    If so this is a fixed-size historical residue, not a growing one — the monotonic last four
    days are consistent with that and are nowhere near enough to establish it.
  * Whether any of the other 791 carries a live ruling the way rf2-lafmr does. Only the one
    was recovered.
  * Whether any CURRENT decision is blocked by a dangling id. None found this tick; not searched.

## WHAT THIS SHOULD AND SHOULD NOT BECOME

**P3 deliberately.** Recovery is complete, cheap and already documented; no live decision is
known to be blocked; and the likely mechanism is likely already guarded. What earns it a filing
is the rate and the silence.

  * **Do NOT bulk-restore the 792.** That is the expensive half of a cheap problem, and most are
    probably closed beads nobody will cite again.
  * **Do NOT add a gate.** A citation cannot be distinguished mechanically from prose mentioning
    an id, and a gate would flag every legitimate historical reference.
  * **Do NOT rewrite existing beads' citations.**
  * The plausible whole fix is ONE SENTENCE in the §4 tracker-query step: when a cited ruling id
    does not resolve, walk the checkpoints before re-deriving the ruling — and say so in the
    report. Whoever takes it should first establish whether the mechanism is closed, because if
    it is not, that is the larger finding and this sentence is the wrong deliverable.

## VERDICT ON THE MECHANISM QUESTION — ANSWERED 2026-09-17 BY THE rf2-uxh3e WORKER

Recorded here by the MAYOR, from the worker's report, because the worker correctly declined to
write to the tracker from a worker worktree (a `bd` write dirties the export there, and the
"never checkout `.beads` after a mutation" trap makes it unsafe from that side). Until this note
the verdict existed ONLY in PR #9916's body — which is the fragile-location failure this very
bead is about, so it is recorded on the item rather than cited from it.

**This discharges TWO of the three NOT ESTABLISHED items above: *why they vanished*, and
*whether the mechanism is closed*. Both are now settled. The description above is superseded on
those two points and should be read through this note.**

### WHY THEY VANISHED: cause (2), `bd gc` decay. Operator-run. Not an export accident.

Nine decay commits between 2026-07-17 and 2026-09-08 removed roughly **13,478 issue records**,
the largest single run being **9,524 at `d7d7b61dcc`**. Each commit is self-described as a
14-day retention run.

**It attributes the CLASS rather than the one instance**, because the four most-cited
unresolvable ids were each removed at a DIFFERENT commit:

    rf2-wad2fl  ->  d7d7b61dcc
    rf2-csbbwu  ->  668f819037
    rf2-lafmr   ->  8372d15e06   "full GC, 14-day closed-bead retention",
                                 `bd gc --older-than 14 --force`, 127 deleted
    rf2-w01c    ->  5e22f68194

**Cause (1) is EXCLUDED by that same history**, and excluded in the way CLAUDE.md predicts rather
than merely ruled out: the empty-export events do appear there, and each is followed by a restore
commit — exactly the "an empty export is a REGENERATION event, not a data-loss one" reading.
Cause (3), a migration, did not arise.

### WHETHER THE MECHANISM IS CLOSED: YES, in both halves — and verified by EFFECT, not only on paper

rf2-nj0c ruled routine decay OFF permanently on 2026-09-09 and closed 09-10, recording both the
in-repo backstop (`.beads/PRIME.md:68`, re-verified live at tip) and the out-of-repo operator
prompt change.

**The worker did not rest on that documentary evidence, and this is the part worth keeping.** The
ruling made a falsifiable prediction: under the old regime, deletions were due on 2026-09-12/13,
with `rf2-9wmqd` named as the first casualty. **`rf2-9wmqd` is still present on 2026-09-17, four
days past that threshold**, with no decay commit since 09-08 and the record count grown
monotonically throughout. Controls both ways: a resolving id resolves, `rf2-01zvu` is absent, a
nonsense id reads 0.

### THE CONSEQUENCE THAT DECIDED THE DELIVERABLE

Because the mechanism is closed, the residue is **fixed-size and permanent**. It does not grow,
and it will never shrink by waiting — so the §4 tracker-query step meets it forever and cannot
resolve it by patience. That is precisely why the one sentence was judged worth writing rather

title: method: the dispatch fence's two release conditions have no tracked home — 24 beads restate the protocol by hand, and CLAUDE.md already names this drift while documenting a different one
description:
FOUND BY THE §5 METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-09-17, on the axis that loop says drift lives on: checking a rule the mayor has been ENFORCING against what the tree actually does. It is the SAME FINDING as the browser-exclusive one already recorded in CLAUDE.md, one level up — and CLAUDE.md already says so, in passing, while documenting the other one.

## THE PROTOCOL

Every dispatch fence this project writes carries TWO release conditions, and they are NOT the same event:

  1. THE RE-DISPATCH FENCE — "do not dispatch a second worker onto this bead or that branch".
     RELEASES ON: a completion report, or a recorded death. This is the condition the §4 reaping
     rule uses, and a report really does discharge it.

  2. THE SURFACE FENCE — "the worker holds <surfaces>".
     RELEASES ON: THE PR MERGING. Not on the report.

The reason the second is not the first is CLAUDE.md's own hot-file rule: "two beads touching the same hot file = sequence them, second waits for the first's PR to merge." A worker that has REPORTED still has an OPEN change editing those files; a second worker branched off trunk today would not carry it, so the two diffs collide at merge — which is precisely what the fence existed to prevent, reached by way of the fence's own release line.

## THE MEASUREMENT — IT HAS NO TRACKED HOME AT ALL

Counted over the four files that could plausibly carry it:

    TERM                      CLAUDE.md   loops.md   template   bootstrap.md
    surface fence                 0           0          0          0
    re-dispatch fence             0           0          0          0
    until its PR merges           0           0          0          0
    releases on the PR            0           0          0          0
    two release conditions        0           0          0          0
    recorded death                0           0          0          0
    completion report             0           1          0          0

Controls both ways over the same four files, so a zero means absence rather than a broken reader: `hot-zone` reads 3/2/5/1, `worktree` reads 46/24/50/8, a nonsense token reads 0/0/0/0.

MEANWHILE, IN THE TRACKER: **24 beads carry the fence release line**, and **7 carry a "FENCE WORDING AMENDMENT"** block that was replicated BY HAND across them in identical words precisely because there was nowhere else to put it.

## WHY THIS IS THE BROWSER-EXCLUSIVE FINDING AGAIN, AND WHY THAT MATTERS

CLAUDE.md's machine-exclusive bullet records that the shadow-cljs take-and-release protocol "existed only in per-dispatch brief text, retyped every tick — **which is exactly how the fence wording drifted, one level up**."

**So this project has ALREADY OBSERVED this exact drift, named it in writing, used it as the evidence for writing DOWN a different protocol, and then left this one where it was.** The sentence diagnosing the disease is in the file; the patient is untreated. That is worth more than the fix, because it is the mechanism by which a catalogue of hazards can grow while a hazard it names stays open: a finding mentioned as SUPPORT for another finding never gets its own item.

AND THE COST IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The amendment block records that at the moment it was written, THREE workers had reported while their PRs remained open on surfaces they held — #9900 (implementation/resources/**, spec/016), #9902 (epoch tool_pair.cljc), #9903 (tools/xray/**). Under the unamended wording each of those surfaces read as released, and a dispatch onto any of them would have been a collision the fence was written to stop.

## WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN, SO THE FIX IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS

Both halves exist separately and neither states the distinction:

  * CLAUDE.md § Workflow carries the underlying rule — hot files are sequential, the second waits for the first's PR to MERGE.
  * loops.md §4 Reaping carries the other half for worktrees — "Deferring the reap until the change merges is free insurance ... Do not make that a second condition on a rule whose strength is having one."

What is missing is the sentence joining them: **a fence has two release conditions; a report frees the BEAD and the BRANCH, only the merge frees the SURFACE.** Plus the operational test that has been retyped into 24 beads: ask "can you quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?" AND "has the PR that edits this surface merged?" — a yes to the first and a no to the second means reap the worktree if you like, but do NOT dispatch onto that surface.

## SCOPE, AND ONE GENUINE DESIGN QUESTION

The clause is a few sentences. The question is WHERE, and it is not obvious:

  * **loops.md** — the distinction is METHOD, not project-specific: any project whose workers open changes has it. §2 (Dispatch) owns the fence filter and §4 (Reaping) already owns the worktree half, so the two halves would finally sit in one document. Argues for loops.md.
  * **CLAUDE.md** — the hot-file sequencing rule it depends on lives there, and the browser-exclusive precedent put a coordination protocol there for exactly this reason. Argues for CLAUDE.md.

**Do NOT put it in both.** Pick one and cross-reference. Whoever takes this should read the browser-exclusive bullet first, because its reasoning about announce-versus-ask is the closest existing model for how to write a coordination rule down.

**Do NOT rewrite the 24 beads.** They are correct as written; the point is that the NEXT fence should be able to cite a home rather than restate the protocol. **Do NOT add a gate** — there is nothing mechanically checkable here.

## NOT ESTABLISHED

Whether the wording has actually drifted ACROSS those 24 beads, or merely been retyped identically. The amendment block asserts drift as its motivation; a diff across the 24 was not taken. If someone takes it, that is a supporting measurement and not a precondition for the fix.

title: Machine completion carriers (spawn-done / spawn-error) drop run propagation: the handler body cannot reach the envelope
description:
SPLIT FROM rf2-gbzv9 by the spawnprop-a worker, 2026-09-13, verified at source at trunk 92b220e32c.

THE GAP. rf2-gbzv9 made the machine SPAWN edge a "queueing children" edge per `spec/002-Frames.md` §Run propagation: the `:rf.machine/spawn` fx's bootstrap dispatch into the newborn actor (its `:start`, or the synthetic `[:rf.machine.spawn/spawned]`) now queues through `rf.fx/child-dispatch!`, so the spawning envelope's `:fx-overrides`, `:interceptor-overrides`, `:trace-id` and `:origin` ride into everything the child does. The two COMPLETION carriers were NOT carried, and could not be from `implementation/machines/**` alone:

- `dispatch-spawn-done!` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc` (the reserved `[:rf.machine.spawn/done <invoke-id> <completion>]` carrier, both spawn forms);
- `dispatch-spawn-error!` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn_error.cljc`, reached from `finalize-machine` (error leaf under an `:on-error` parent) and from `registration.cljc`'s action-exception route.

Both still dispatch with only `{:frame frame-id :source :machine-spawn}`.

WHY IT NEEDS CORE. Both sites run inside the finishing child's machine HANDLER body, not inside an fx, so there is no `(:envelope m)`. The router's `prepare-handler-ctx` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`) surfaces only `:source`, `:trace-id` and the resolved `:rf.cofx/mint-policy` off the envelope as coeffects; `:fx-overrides`, `:interceptor-overrides` and `:origin` are unreachable from a handler, and core binds no dynamic var carrying the in-flight envelope.

THE EXACT CORE CHANGE. Expose the in-flight (dequeued, machine-tagged) envelope to framework internals for the duration of the handler call — e.g. a `^:no-doc` dynamic var bound by the router around the handler pipeline, beside the existing `*event-owner*` binding (`call-with-event-owner-token`), read through a `^:no-doc` accessor. Then each carrier becomes `(rf.fx/child-dispatch! frame-id (dissoc env :rf.machine/internal?) event {:source :machine-spawn})` — the same shape rf2-gbzv9 used at the spawn site, where dropping `:rf.machine/internal?` keeps the carrier's FIFO queue position.

DECISIONS TO MAKE FIRST.
1. Mint policy. `rf.fx/child-dispatch!` carries the per-call `:rf.cofx/mint-policy` alongside the five spec keys (EP-0017 §6). `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/join_strict_mint_cljs_test.cljc` records, at its deleted test (5), a deliberate choice that the completion carrier does NOT inherit mint policy ("new machinery no bead has asked for; if it is ever wanted, it belongs to the cofx/replay area"). Reusing the helper overturns that; redeclaring a key list without it duplicates the helper.
2. Which envelope. The envelope inherited is the one of the event that FINISHED the child (e.g. an HTTP reply into it), so whether a completion carries a per-call override at all depends on how that event was dispatched. Decide whether that is the wanted lineage, or whether completions should stay fresh like `:after` timer wake-ups.

CONSEQUENCE TODAY. A per-call `:fx-overrides` reaches every fx a spawned child fires, but NOT the spawning parent's continuation after a child completes (a parent `:on-done` / `:on-all-complete` / `:on-error` step that fires an fx runs under the carrier's envelope, which has no per-call overrides). Per-frame overrides are unaffected. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `spec/002-Frames.md` say nothing either way about the completion carriers.

Both carriers dispatched with only `{:frame frame-id :source :machine-spawn}`. `dispatch-spawn-error!` is reached from `finalize.cljc` and from `registration.cljc`'s action-exception route. `prepare-handler-ctx` reads the owner token via `rf.frame/current-event-owner-token`. `child-dispatch!` / `inheritable-envelope-keys` are in `fx.cljc`. No sibling had already landed the change. The item's history was walked to creation: 38 snapshots, all byte-identical (the control was the whole record, not one field), so the item has no mutation of any field since filing.

1. MINT POLICY: the carriers INHERIT the per-call `:rf.cofx/mint-policy`, by reusing `rf.fx/child-dispatch!` (one key list, not two). The reasoning recorded at `join_strict_mint_cljs_test.cljc`'s deleted test (5) was "new machinery no bead has asked for; if it is ever wanted, it belongs to the cofx/replay area". It does not survive this bead. rf2-ix8fd asks for exactly that machinery, the in-flight envelope in a handler body, and once the envelope is reachable the policy rides with it at no additional cost. EP-0017 §6, quoted in `child-dispatch-opts`, forbids a strict cascade silently falling back to `:live`. And rf2-gbzv9 already carries the policy INTO the child on the spawn edge, so dropping it on the way back out was the inconsistent half. Test (5) is reinstated as a positive test, `completion-carrier-inherits-strict-into-the-join-resolution`, and its comment records the overturn.

2. WHICH ENVELOPE: the envelope of the event whose handling FINISHED the child. Spec 002 §Run propagation defines inheritance as "envelope-field-copying when queueing children". A carrier is queued by the runtime while that event's handler runs, so it is that event's child. `:after` wake-ups are fresh because a host timer fires them with no event in flight, not because they are machine-owned. A carrier is also the declarative twin of the `[:fx [[:dispatch [parent-id …]]]]` escape hatch that `spawn_error.cljc` names, and that hatch already inherits. Consequence, pinned by tests in both directions: a child finished by an event carrying an override hands the override to the parent; a child finished by a plain event hands over nothing, even when its spawn carried one. The carrier still drops `:rf.machine/internal?` and keeps its FIFO place.

CORE SHAPE: no new dynamic var. The router's EXISTING `*event-owner*` binding around the handler pipeline (`run-handler-pipeline`, via a new 5-arity of `call-with-event-owner-token`) now carries `:envelope`. The new `^:no-doc` accessor `rf.frame/current-event-envelope` reads it, scoped to the owner frame. The override-free path pays one more entry in a map literal already built per event, and no extra binding frame. No nested owner scope sits between that binding and the handler body; verified: the only 4-arity rebinds are in the outer drain. Both carriers share one seam, `spawn-error/dispatch-carrier!`.

- Accessor. The new `^:no-doc` `rf.frame/current-event-envelope` takes a frame id and reads it. It answers nil outside a handler pipeline or for another frame.
- Machines.
