title: surface-review(template): honor browser-proof mount and click timeouts
description:
Recommendation: fix the two Playwright waitForFunction argument lists in the template browser proof so RF2_TEMPLATE_BROWSER_PROOF_TIMEOUT_MS actually governs mount and click waits. This is one confirmed P3 test-harness defect. Preserve the current twelve-file generated SPA contract: this review found no confirmed defect in the emitted application source, substitutions, or dependency/build wiring.

Scope and revision
- Slice: tools_template; all 38 assigned tracked paths under tools/template/** (exact roster below).
- Source snapshot: 1c9ff9697b0fa3a018c7a4371e02983ad2e79b2f. At review completion HEAD was 1b285ba9a841a336dd6f54f81f77aaee3150253b; git diff --exit-code from the snapshot through the working tree for tools/template returned 0. Tracker checkpoints did not change this source.
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2.
- WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). No tracked source/build edits, installs, commits, checkout, or push. The isolated probes and their evidence live on an ignored path; no shared node_modules link was created.

Confirmed finding F1 — P3: configured browser-proof timeout is passed as browser data and ignored
Source: tools/template/test-support/page-boot-proof.cjs:243-257 and :295-298. TIMEOUT_MS is read at :135. Current callers deliberately set the override to 8000 ms in tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:495 and :888.

Trigger and reproducer
1. Run the actual checked-in page-boot-proof.cjs with the already-installed Playwright 1.59.1, RF2_TEMPLATE_BROWSER_PROOF_TIMEOUT_MS=500, RF2_TEMPLATE_BUNDLE_MODE=dev, and a synthetic local index.html that defines goog/cljs objects for the driver's dev-bundle check.
2. Mount case: leave #app empty for 2000 ms, then paint an h1, a +1 button, and a span initially containing 0; clicking immediately sets the span to 1.
3. Click case: paint that same initial counter immediately, but delay its 0 -> 1 click update by 2000 ms.
4. Supply RF2_TEMPLATE_EXPECT_H1=review-timeout-witness to pin the synthetic fixture identity.

Expected: the mount case and click case both exit 1 with Timeout 500ms exceeded because their awaited condition misses the selected deadline.
Actual: the UNMODIFIED checked-in driver exits 0 for both. Measured total child-process elapsed times were 2544 ms (late mount) and 2530 ms (late click), and both printed the normal page boot proof PASS. The synthetic condition's own 2000 ms delay, rather than process startup, establishes that the 500 ms deadline was exceeded.

Mechanism: Playwright's signature is waitForFunction(pageFunction, arg, options). Both calls supply only pageFunction and {timeout: TIMEOUT_MS}, so the object is serialized into the page as arg and options remains empty. Neither callback consumes this arg. The driver sets no page/context default timeout. The installed Playwright implementation therefore uses its 30000 ms default. page.goto uses the options correctly, which makes the env var appear partially effective while leaving the two central proof waits unbounded by its selected value.

Independent control: a scratch-only copy of the driver, with exactly two edits inserting undefined as the second argument and moving the existing timeout object to the third argument, rejected both identical pages. Late mount exited 1 in 994 ms; late click exited 1 in 1079 ms. Both explicitly reported Timeout 500ms exceeded. No framework bundle was compiled for this witness, and these synthetic pages are not evidence about generated-app runtime behavior.

Impact: custom time budgets can produce a false pass for late mount/click behavior. More routinely, the existing deliberately broken boot/click witnesses request 8 seconds but wait for Playwright's 30-second default, adding roughly 22 seconds per failing condition. This is a low-priority harness contract/performance defect, not evidence that either generated application fails to boot.

Precise repair: call page.waitForFunction(predicate, undefined, {timeout: TIMEOUT_MS}) at both sites. The two call-site changes are sufficient; no timeout framework, generator changes, or new public option is needed.

Acceptance criteria
- Both existing waitForFunction sites pass the timeout in Playwright's options position.
- With a short configured timeout, an intentionally late mount and an intentionally late click each return exit 1 with the configured timeout named; an immediately responsive control page still returns exit 0.
- Existing broken-mount and broken-click witnesses keep their exit-1 verdicts and honor their requested 8000 ms waits.

title: xray: 34 metadata React keys across 13 files die silently under Fresco — sweep them into attrs maps
description:
A React key carried as Clojure METADATA reaches React under Reagent and reaches it NOWHERE under
Fresco. Every one of these sites is correct today and loses its key silently the moment its file
renders under Fresco — no error, no warning, just React reconciling by position and the DOM
churning. This class has now been cleared three times in the migration (rf2-twil, rf2-hxfy, and
rf2-fcy5 slice 1). Sweep the remainder while the whole surface is free.

=== THE CENSUS, MEASURED 2026-09-11 AT TRUNK 9bf7961349 ===

34 sites across 13 files, ALL of them `^{:key ...}` on a VECTOR LITERAL:

    10  panels/fresco.cljs
     6  panels/epoch/view.cljs
     4  settings/view.cljs
     4  shell.cljs
     2  filters/pills.cljs
     1  chart/timing_waterfall.cljc
     1  frame_switcher.cljs
     1  panels/managed_fx_template.cljs
     1  spine_filters.cljs
     1  static/machines/sim.cljs
     1  static/mode_pill.cljs
     1  static/routes/browse_list.cljs
     1  static/routes/simulate_url.cljs

(all paths relative to `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/`)

ZERO SITES ARE ON A CALL FORM. That matters, because `^{:key ...}` on a CALL form reaches React on
NO substrate — broken today, everywhere — while on a VECTOR LITERAL it works under Reagent and dies
only under Fresco. The worse class is already clear; what remains is entirely the latent one. Do
not go looking for call-form sites; there are none.

Separately: 5 `(with-meta ...)` sites across 4 files. Same hazard, different spelling. Include them.

=== THE INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS PROBE MISSES 85% ===

29 OF THE 34 SITES PUT THE VECTOR ON THE NEXT LINE, not the same one — the metadata sits alone
above the form it decorates. A same-line probe finds 5 of 34 and returns a reassuringly small
number with nothing on screen to say so. Measured both ways in one session: the same-line-only
version read 5 across 3 files, the version that falls through to the following line read 34 across
13.

AND DO NOT REGEX-STRIP STRING LITERALS FIRST. The obvious pattern mispairs quotes across Clojure
docstrings — measured on `shell.cljs`, it claimed 39% of the file and ate two real `(rf/reg-view`
registrations. Exclude COMMENT LINES by position (first non-space char is `;`) and accept that
docstring prose will produce a handful of unclassifiable hits to eye: there were 6, and all 6 were
prose in this tree.

=== THE FIX ===

Move the key into the form's ATTRS MAP. `:key` in a hiccup attrs map is honoured by Reagent AND by
Fresco, so this is a no-op today and a fix tomorrow — which is exactly why it can be done ahead of
the migration rather than during it.

Where the decorated vector has no attrs map, insert one. Where the thing being keyed is a value
handed in by a caller rather than a literal, a helper is needed that injects `:key` into a hiccup
vector's attrs map and leaves a non-vector alone — `views/resizable_table.cljs` already carries
exactly such a helper from rf2-fcy5 slice 1; reuse its shape rather than inventing a second one.

=== HOW TO VERIFY — NOT AT `(meta ...)`, AND NOT WITH REAGENT ===

`(:key (meta node))` is hollow in BOTH directions: it passes on metadata React never sees and fails
on an attrs-map key that works perfectly.

AND `(.-key (r/as-element node))` IS ALSO HOLLOW FOR THIS EXACT QUESTION — Reagent reads metadata
AND props and returns the same key either way, so it passes before and after the fix. Measured on
rf2-fcy5 slice 1: with the fix reverted, the Reagent assertion PASSED while the Fresco assertion on
the next line failed with `[nil nil nil]`.

GRADE WITH `(.-key (codec/as-element node))`. `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/
resizable_table_key_cljs_test.cljs` reads both doors and is the pattern to follow.

Hollow-gate check on any new test row: delete the signal, keep the fault, and confirm the test
TOTALS are IDENTICAL either side — an identical total is what separates a real runtime failure from
a suite that merely got smaller.

=== SCOPE NOTES ===

`panels/epoch/view.cljs` and `panels/managed_fx_template.cljs` are rf2-fcy5's slices 2 and 3
surface, and `shell.cljs` is the next rf2-k97c.3 slice. None of the three is in flight right now,
which is precisely why this sweep should happen NOW — it removes the hazard from those files before
anyone migrates them, and a migration worker that inherits clean keys cannot lose them.

This is a whitespace-adjacent behavioural no-op under the current substrate. It should not change a
single rendered key today; if it does, that is a finding, not a success.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9647 (2026-09-11): the sweep is incomplete across its original surface; the exact eight remaining metadata-key defects and correction are already explicitly tracked by open rf2-h100. Forward pointer reaffirmed; audit evidence appended there. No new distinct defect in the 32 repaired sites. Existing status and closure record preserved.
close_reason:
DONE for 27 of the 35 sites, in PR #9647 (merged, trunk 606ba24a19). The remaining EIGHT are
rf2-h100, filed rather than left implicit. Closing on that split.

## THE BEAD'S OWN TITLE WAS WRONG IN THREE WAYS, AND THE WORKER CORRECTED IT

Quoting its report, because these are the durable parts:

  "It is 35 sites, not 34. `shell.cljs` carries 5, not 4. The missed one is the tab bar at
   `shell.cljs:2332`: its `^{:key id}` is separated from the vector by a COMMENT LINE."

That is a census-instrument lesson, not a bookkeeping one: a metadata key and its vector are
adjacent in the AUTHOR's mind and need not be adjacent in the FILE, so any pattern requiring them
on one line, or on consecutive lines, under-counts by however many carry an intervening comment.
Mine required adjacency and read 34.

## THE SHAPE TRAP, WHICH IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE BUILD

  "10 of the 35 sites are component vectors — inserting a map at index 1 of
   `[mute-row dispatch id]` shifts the callee's arguments."

The naive repair — move the key into an attrs map at index 1 — is CORRECT for a hiccup vector with
a keyword head and WRONG for a component vector, where index 1 is the callee's first argument. The
worker used the keyed-fragment pattern for those ten: `[:<> {:key ...} [mute-row dispatch id]]`,
which carries the key on a wrapper React can read while leaving the call untouched. Nearly a third
of the sites were this shape, so a brief that prescribed only the attrs-map move would have been
wrong about a third of its own work.

## ITS NO-OP PROOF IS THE INSTRUMENT WORTH KEEPING

  "every React-key expression extracted from each touched file before and after and compared as a
   multiset — 0 of 13 files changed a key expression"

This grades the actual invariant: the sweep moves a key's CARRIER (metadata to props) and must not
disturb its VALUE. A multiset comparison catches a reordering, a duplication and a silent
substitution alike, and it does not care that the surrounding lines all moved. Compare against the
instrument this session had to throw away on rf2-tdlg, which measured a symptom (a list-count drop)
that a correct repair also produces. Reuse this one on rf2-h100.

## WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND WHY THE STATED REASON DOES NOT HOLD

The eight remaining sites are in `panels/epoch/view.cljs` (6), `panels/managed_fx_template.cljs` (1)
and `panels/trace.cljs` (1). The worker skipped them because it read `epochkey-a`, `keymeta-a` and
`tracefx-a` as holding those files on committed, unmerged branches. Measured at trunk, all three
read `-` under `git cherry` — patch-id proof of containment; the worker had used
`git rev-list origin/main..<branch>`, which reports every REBASE-merged branch as unmerged. The full
sweep and its refutation are on rf2-lbs9. So the fence was not real, and rf2-h100 inherits a free
surface.

MY OWN WORDING IN THAT BRIEF WAS ALSO LOOSE AND DESERVED THE CHALLENGE: I wrote "No other worker
holds any of your files" when I meant no LIVE worker, having checked live agents rather than
branches. Right in substance, imprecise in words — and a worker that checks a fence claim instead
of trusting it is the behaviour to keep, even on the occasion it reached the wrong answer.

title: xray: two latent Fresco-migration hazards in managed_fx_template.cljs and trace.cljs (4 HD-016 heads, 1 meta-only key)
description:
TWO SITES THAT ARE CORRECT TODAY AND BREAK THE DAY THEIR PANEL MIGRATES. Both were found
by the rf2-hxfy worker while repairing the two dead-key sites, reported rather than fixed,
and both are outside that bead. Neither is a defect on trunk right now.

=== 1. FOUR HD-016 SITES: A PLAIN `defn` IN HICCUP HEAD POSITION ===

`views/edn_widget.cljs:102` defines `inspect` as a plain `defn`. `panels/managed_fx_template.cljs`
uses it in HEAD position at FOUR sites.

MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk 2b7e026254, before filing:

    grep -c -F '[edn/inspect'  managed_fx_template.cljs   ->  4     (head form)
    grep -c -F '(edn/inspect'  managed_fx_template.cljs   ->  0     (call form)
    edn_widget.cljs:102                                   ->  (defn inspect

**THIS IS THE EXACT CLASS THAT COST A P1 TODAY.** rf2-qhoj was one token --
`[mini prior 40]` where Fresco's codec demands `(mini prior 40)` -- and its consequence was
not a broken widget: a plain function in head position is a loud error by design (HD-016), the
throw escaped the boundary with no error boundary above it, and REACT UNMOUNTED THE ENTIRE
XRAY ROOT. It presented as a panel that never appears rather than as an error, and no unit
suite could see it because the panel's rows walk hiccup and never render through Fresco's
codec.

`managed_fx_template.cljs` is still REAGENT, where a plain fn head is form-1 and legitimate,
so nothing is wrong today. The four sites become four HD-016 throws the moment that panel
becomes a Fresco boundary.

**NOT EVERY HEAD IN THAT FILE IS AFFECTED, and the distinction is the useful half**:
`ei/edn-inspector` and `rt/resizable-table` are proper `reg-view` heads and are FINE. Only
`edn/inspect` is a plain `defn`. Do not sweep the file indiscriminately.

=== 2. A `^{:key ...}` THAT SURVIVES ONLY BECAUSE ITS META RIDES A VECTOR LITERAL ===

`panels/trace.cljs` carries `^{:key "ops-header"}` on a VECTOR LITERAL. Reader metadata rides
onto the vector the reader produces, and Reagent reads metadata THEN props, so React receives
the key today and the site is correct.

**Fresco's codec reads `:key` from the ATTRIBUTE MAP and reads Clojure metadata NOWHERE.** So a
migration that faithfully preserves this `^{:key ...}` preserves a NO-OP -- the key silently
stops reaching React, with nothing on screen to say so. Same destination as rf2-hxfy's two
call-form sites, reached from the opposite direction: those never delivered a key at all, this
one delivers today and stops later.

The repair is the same and is already the standing direction: move the key into the returned
hiccup's attribute map, which satisfies BOTH substrates because Reagent reads meta then props.

=== WHY ONE BEAD ===

Same two files, same character -- correct on Reagent, broken on Fresco -- and both are cheapest
to fix inside whichever dispatch migrates those panels, exactly as RULING 2 on rf2-k97c.3
prescribes for the key class. **This bead exists so that dispatch has something to read, not so
a separate worker sweeps the tree.** If a panel dispatch reaches `managed_fx_template.cljs` or
`trace.cljs`, fold these in and close this; do not dispatch it standalone ahead of that.

=== AN INSTRUMENT TRAP MEASURED ON THE WAY, WORTH MORE THAN EITHER FINDING ===

`rf.test-helpers/expand-tree` REBUILDS NESTED VECTORS WITH `mapv`, WHICH STRIPS READER
METADATA. So a test that navigates through `expand-tree` and then asks for `(meta ...)` reads a
FALSE `nil` -- the metadata was on the source vector and did not survive the rebuild. It
reported a false `nil` for a meta-keyed sibling via `find-by-testid` during the rf2-hxfy work.

It fails in the REASSURING direction for the only question such a probe asks -- *did the key
survive?* answers *no* -- and it would make a metadata-based regression row look like a real
finding. **The guard: navigate the RAW tree structurally when the property under test is
metadata, and say in the test why.** Both rf2-hxfy rows do exactly that.

**AND THE DEEPER POINT, which is why the rf2-hxfy repair asserts at the renderer:** `(meta ...)`
reads `nil` at both repaired sites even AFTER the fix, because the key now lives in the
attribute map rather than in metadata. A metadata row would have been hollow in both directions
-- green on the broken code and red on the fixed code.
notes: DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-hxfy by its worker (keymeta-a), which reported both findings and correctly did NOT touch either -- they are outside that bead's two sites. The mayor verified finding 1 at source at trunk 2b7e026254 before filing: 4 head-form uses against 0 call-form, and `inspect` a plain defn at edn_widget.cljs:102. Finding 2 and the expand-tree instrument trap are taken from the worker's report and are marked as such rather than re-measured.
close_reason:
Delivered by PR #9624, merged to trunk at 58399caf58 (rebase). Four files, +187/-7 — the two
named files plus their two tests. Scope was NOT widened, despite the worker finding three things
that would have justified widening.

=== BOTH HAZARDS REPAIRED ===

1. The four `[edn/inspect ...]` head-position sites in `managed_fx_template.cljs` converted to
   CALL form.
2. `trace.cljs`'s `^{:key "ops-header"}` moved out of reader metadata and into the props map.

=== A DELIBERATE CHOICE THE MAYOR'S BRIEF GOT WRONG, AND THE WORKER GOT RIGHT ===

I told it `edn/inspect-view` already existed and to consider it. It chose `edn/inspect` instead,
and the reasoning is worth keeping: `inspect-view` emits `[ei/edn-inspector-view ...]`, which IS a
Fresco boundary — and a Fresco boundary in a REAGENT head position is the MIRROR failure. This
panel's mount is still an `rf/reg-view`, so `inspect` is correct TODAY and `inspect-view` becomes
correct the day that mount migrates. The source comment says this at the site, so the next reader
does not re-derive it.

=== THE RED-TO-GREEN PAIR, MEASURED BOTH WAYS ===

Pre-fix meta form planted -> exit 1, 2 failures, both in the new
`trace-feed-children-keys-live-in-the-attribute-map`. Fixed form -> exit 0, 0 failures. Totals
IDENTICAL either side at 11584 tests / 58099 assertions, so a runtime failure and not a load
error. **The existing rf2-hxfy row stayed GREEN through the red run** — direct evidence that the
older row cannot see this move, which is worth more than the new row itself.

=== THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE WHOLE HAZARD ===

The four HD-016 sites are UNREACHABLE AT RUNTIME. They sit inside sections built with
`:expanded? false` literals, and `theme/section/section-row` renders its body under
`(when expanded? ...)` — so those vectors have never reached a rendered tree. That is the complete
explanation for the three-tier coverage blind spot: no walker, no codec and no DOM row could grade
them.

**The hollow-gate guard caught itself.** The worker's first draft asserted the returned inspector
was present in the tree, and it READ ZERO. Rather than keep a row that quietly could not fail, it
rewrote the row to state plainly that it cannot go red on a revert, and WIDENED it from `inspect`
by name to ANY PLAIN FN IN HEAD POSITION — which catches the `ei/mini` sibling mistake rf2-qhoj
actually made. That is better than what my brief asked for.

=== THIS BEAD'S OWN DESCRIPTION CONTAINED A FALSE CLAIM ===

It said "`ei/edn-inspector` and `rt/resizable-table` are proper `reg-view` heads and are FINE".
They are not. `codec/boundary-head?` reads one own property — `(true? (unchecked-get f
"frescoBoundary"))` — and ONLY `rf.fresco/defview` sets it; `rf/reg-view` expands to the installed
substrate's component head, a plain fn under Reagent, so `head-kind` grades it `:invalid` down the
SAME arm as a plain `defn`. The worker derived this independently before writing any code, which is
why it never flipped either Panel to a `defview`, and filed rf2-fcy5. I had relayed the false claim
into its brief as fact; that error is mine and is recorded on rf2-fcy5.

=== THREE FOLLOW-ONS, ALL FILED RATHER THAN SWEPT ===

  rf2-fcy5  reg-view heads block the migration; `resizable-table` needs a boundary — and its rows
            are keyed with `(with-meta ... {:key ...})`, a THIRD instance of the metadata-only-key
            class, in a SHARED widget. Now unblocked by this merge.
  rf2-s6m6  three managed-fx sections permanently collapsed. Its sequencing constraint — must land
            after or with this head-form repair — is DISCHARGED by this merge.
  rf2-xhy9  unrelated, from a sibling slice.

Green at band: 87/87, 0 pending, 0 failed; 4 runs at the full head oid
75ca54fb55cddbc52c2b50d56f299a85b8ea5420 all completed/success; merge-tree clean; 0 job keys; no
overlap with any of the three other open PRs. Merged on the worker's own ready flag plus its
explicit "Work is DONE" report.

Two process notes the worker reported against itself, both worth keeping: it briefly piped
`check-commit-attribution.sh` through `tail` and got a FALSE 0 on a failing-closed message — the
exact pipeline-status hazard CLAUDE.md catalogues — and re-ran it bare. And it accidentally

title: False roster-authority statement: attr-string puts Spec 011 downstream of code
description:
Merged-PR audit of #9602, landing c123aa288918ca40729183281f57ff6d1a1132c2. The roster completion itself is correct and executable code is unchanged. One new sentence in the attr-string docstring reverses the normative relationship it is meant to explain.

implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc now says: "It is downstream of strip-prop? the way Spec 011's enumeration is downstream of both". At this same landing, spec/011-SSR.md, XSS at output boundaries, explicitly says the enumeration is the contract for other-language ports and "That fn is downstream of this list". The two statements give opposite answers when the implementation and specification disagree. The source rf2-twyh also expressly retains #9598's decision rather than reopening it.

Correct the docstring's directional comparison, or omit that comparison while keeping its useful distinction between a local gloss and the single implementation point. This is a narrow documentation correction, not a request to change the filter, its name sets, the accepted spec authority, or the decision about adding a drift gate.

No exact open owner records this contradiction. rf2-7ntc owns only the optional roster drift-gate decision; rf2-ounh owns JSX test coverage. Neither records this false authority statement or its correction. Source rf2-twyh is closed; preserve its ruling and append only a forward pointer.

Evidence: both contradictory passages were read from the exact landed Git object. All executable prefix/body text around attr-string is unchanged. Relevant CI tested fb0361484754c9db9ab5d7949305be78e962b9a7, byte-identical for both changed files; docs/link checks and JVM/CLJS SSR coverage are green but do not establish prose authority consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Make the attr-string docstring consistent with Spec 011: the spec roster is the normative contract, strip-prop? implements it, and the attr-string list is a gloss of that implementation. Removing the mistaken directional comparison is sufficient. Preserve the completed roster and runtime behavior; no new gate or runtime test is needed for this prose correction.
close_reason:
Landed in PR #9612 as its own commit, merged 5d577c73b6. The attr-string docstring's directional comparison is corrected; spec/011-SSR.md is untouched.

THE WORKER CHOSE TO CORRECT THE COMPARISON RATHER THAN OMIT IT, and its reason is better than either option the brief offered. The sentence carried two things worth keeping beyond its direction -- the three-way chain, and the clause saying that standing apart is a defect in whichever moved without the others, which the gloss then demonstrates against itself. Only the DIRECTION was wrong, so only the direction moved. It now reads that the gloss is downstream of strip-prop?, which is itself downstream of Spec 011's enumeration -- that list being the contract and what an other-language port implements.

WHICH WAY ROUND IT GOES WAS NOT THE WORKER'S CALL TO MAKE AND WAS NOT TREATED AS ONE: this project's stated posture is that the spec is the artefact and the code is downstream, and spec/011-SSR.md already said so in terms at the same landing. The docstring had reversed it. Correcting the code's prose to match the spec is the only direction consistent with the posture.

SCOPE HELD EXACTLY WHERE THE BEAD DREW IT: no change to the filter, its name sets, the accepted spec authority, or the drift-gate decision -- that last is rf2-7ntc's and remains deliberately unmade.

Gates, captured unpiped: SSR JVM 0 (673 tests / 4465 assertions after, from a 672 / 4454 baseline), clj-kondo 0 errors 0 warnings on both files, Splint 0 with three pre-existing style warnings in executable code the change does not touch. Restore verified by blob hash with the per-file form from git ls-files --eol.

This was filed by the merged-PR audit of #9602 and it was right: the roster completion itself was correct and executable code was unchanged, but one new sentence reversed the normative relationship it existed to explain. The audit caught prose that no gate grades -- nothing in this repository validates prose authority consistency, which the audit note said itself.

title: A drift gate for the SSR prop-drop roster — feasibility measured, decision not made
description:
A DRIFT GATE FOR THE SSR PROP-DROP ROSTER: FEASIBILITY MEASURED, DECISION NOT MADE.

Filed from rf2-twyh, which brought the last two stale enumerations of the roster into
step (spec/Security.md and the `attr-string` docstring). rf2-2fes / PR #9598 did the
same for spec/011-SSR.md. The repairs are done; this bead is only about whether to stop
the RECURRENCE with a gate. A gate is a new permanent obligation, so it gets its own
decision rather than riding on a prose bead.

=== THE RECURRENCE, AS MEASURED ===

`strip-prop?` in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc drops six classes
of prop at SSR attribute-emit time. Four documents enumerate that roster; three went
stale, and the failure is silent in both directions — nothing errors, and a short roster
reads as a complete one.

  * spec/011-SSR.md            — went short 2026-05-15 -> 2026-05-27, ~3.5 months (rf2-2fes)
  * spec/Security.md           — same three classes missing (rf2-twyh)
  * the `attr-string` docstring — written 2026-05-21, went short SIX DAYS later when the
                                 JSX class landed 400 lines above it IN THE SAME FILE,
                                 and was three classes behind by 2026-09-10 (rf2-twyh)
  * `strip-prop?`'s own docstring — the only one that stayed correct

The in-file one is the sharpest: the whole argument for duplicating the roster into the
spec is that `strip-prop?` is the single realisation point, and a second, shorter
enumeration in the same file undercuts it. Six days is the shortest half-life here, and
that site had the least excuse.

=== THE CASE FOR: THE INVARIANT IS MECHANICAL, AND IT WAS MEASURED WORKING ===

Four of the six classes are backed by a literal `^:private` name set. A ~50-line probe
that regex-reads the four `def ^:private <name> #{...}` forms and requires every literal
member to appear in each enumerating spec page was written and run at two revisions.
Extraction succeeded at both, yielding all ten names:

  reserved-prop-keys      __proto__ constructor prototype
  jsx-source-prop-names   _jsxFileName _jsxLineNumber _jsxColumnNumber
  structural-slot-names   key ref
  content-channel-names   children dangerouslySetInnerHTML

Result at trunk BEFORE either repair (a0e48243321d0c37d132a672beaf519405dbe92f):

  spec/011-SSR.md    RED, missing _jsxFileName _jsxLineNumber _jsxColumnNumber :dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  spec/Security.md   RED, missing _jsxFileName _jsxLineNumber _jsxColumnNumber :ref :children :dangerouslySetInnerHTML

Result at rf2-twyh's branch head, both repairs applied: GREEN on both, 0 missing.

So the gate would have caught both drifts before they landed, is green today, and needs
no configuration beyond a two-entry list of pages. That is the same shape as the
api-manifest job and as `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py`, whose own docstring
describes itself as the api-manifest pattern applied to keywords. The idiom exists.

=== THE CASE AGAINST, AND IT IS NOT WEAK — FOUR MEASURED CONSTRAINTS ===

(1) WHOLE-FILE MATCHING IS CONTAMINATED, so the naive gate is weaker than it looks.
    011 pre-repair went red on only FOUR of the six names it was genuinely missing,
    because `:key`, `:ref` and `:children` already occur elsewhere in that file for
    unrelated reasons — `:children` is a key into a structured-children map in the
    path-segment addressing section, same token, different meaning. (rf2-2fes recorded
    that same trap pointing the other way.) A gate that means it must scope to the
    roster's own section, which means parsing a heading range and tracking where the
    roster lives on each page. That is the difference between a 50-line script and a
    real one, and it is a second thing that can go stale.

(2) A GATE CAN ONLY EVER GRADE FOUR OF THE SIX CLASSES. `strip-prop?`'s body is a
    six-arm `or`: four `contains?` calls against name sets, plus `(event-handler-name? nm)`
    — itself a regex plus an allowlist, not an enumerable roster — and `(fn? v)`, a type
    predicate with no name at all. The two classes with no name set are exactly the two
    that were never stale, so the gate covers the part that drifts; but a green from it
    is not "the enumeration is complete", and anyone reading it as that will be wrong.

(3) A COUNT INVARIANT IS ALREADY VIOLATED BY TWO CORRECT DOCUMENTS. The obvious cheap
    gate — "every site lists as many classes as `strip-prop?` has `or` arms" — fails on
    day one: merged 011's nested roster has FIVE list items for SIX classes, because it
    groups `on*` and function-valued props into one entry, while spec/Security.md says
    "six classes". Both are right. Legitimate grouping differences mean only the
    literal-NAME test is sound, not any structural count.

(4) THE FOURTH SITE CANNOT BE INCLUDED WITHOUT PER-SITE CONFIGURATION. The `attr-string`
    gloss names `:key`, `:ref`, `:children` and `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` but deliberately
    does NOT spell out `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` or the three JSX names — it
    says "reserved prototype-pollution keys" and "JSX source-coord props" in prose,
    which is the right register for a downstream gloss. Grading it needs a per-site
    allowance, and that allowance is itself a roster that can go stale.

=== WHAT rf2-twyh DID INSTEAD, WHICH MAY BE ENOUGH ===

Both repairs used the two mitigations rf2-2fes established, which cost nothing and
cannot themselves go stale:

  * the enumerating LEDE was retired. spec/Security.md's bullet title was
    "Event-handler-prop filter + reserved-prop-keys gate at static-markup emission" —
    short in exactly the way the roster was — and is now the non-enumerating
    "Prop-drop roster at static-markup emission", matching 011's.
  * the `attr-string` gloss is now explicitly labelled a gloss rather than a second
    roster, names `strip-prop?` as the single realisation point, and carries its own
    six-day drift as the worked example of what going out of step costs.

If the recurrence is judged tolerable, the honest disposition is to close this bead with
that reasoning recorded, not to leave it open indefinitely.

=== SUGGESTED DISPOSITION (a recommendation, not a ruling) ===

Build the section-scoped literal-name gate over the TWO SPEC PAGES only (011 + Security),
skip the docstring gloss, and document in the script that it grades four of six classes.
That is the version whose green means something. If that is more machinery than the
problem deserves, close as won't-do — the measurements above are the record either way.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE and needs its own bead if wanted: the same four name sets have no
CLJS-side or conformance-fixture cross-check either; this bead is only about the prose
enumerations.
notes:
== MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-11: BUILD IT, BUT THE SIMPLE FORM — NOT THE SECTION-SCOPED ONE.

The bead asked for a decision and recommended a section-scoped literal-name gate over the two spec
pages. DECISION: build the gate, over those two pages, but WITHOUT section scoping. Whole-file
literal-name matching, ~50 lines, no heading-range parsing.

=== WHY I AM DEPARTING FROM THE BEAD'S OWN RECOMMENDATION

Constraint (1) is the reason the bead reaches for section scoping, and read carefully it cuts the
other way.

The contamination it measured — `:key`, `:ref` and `:children` occurring elsewhere in 011 for
unrelated reasons — makes a whole-file gate UNDER-REPORT. A name present elsewhere on the page reads
as present, so the gate misses that name's absence from the roster. It does NOT invent failures.

So the whole-file form is sound in exactly one direction: it never cries wolf, and it catches most
drift. At the pre-repair revision it went RED on both pages — which is the whole question, because
those are the two drifts that actually happened. A gate that would have caught both real incidents,
never false-alarms, and has no second stale-able component in it is the right trade here.

Section scoping buys the remaining names at the cost of a heading-range parser that must track where
the roster lives on each page — and the bead says so itself: "a second thing that can go stale". We
would be adding a stale-able mechanism to a gate whose entire purpose is to catch staleness. That is
the gold-plating the stance names.

RECORD THE FLOOR HONESTLY: a green from this gate means "no literal name is wholly absent from the
page", not "the roster is complete". Combined with constraint (2) — four of six classes are
name-backed at all — the script's own docstring must say both limits in terms. A gate whose green is
over-read is worse than no gate; a gate whose green is correctly labelled a FLOOR is useful.

IF a false green on a contaminated name is ever met in practice, THAT is the trigger to add scoping.
Not before. One incident, not a theory.

=== WHY A GATE AT ALL, GIVEN rf2-twyh'S MITIGATIONS

The bead fairly asks whether retiring the enumerating lede is enough, and the honest answer is: it
addresses the root cause and it may well be, but it is untested prose and the recurrence has a
measured six-day half-life at its sharpest site.

The tiebreaker is WHAT the roster is. This is not an ordinary doc-drift item: the names are
`__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and one of the two pages is
`spec/Security.md`. A short roster there is a security document understating a security control. That
is not minutiae, and it is why this clears the bar that an ordinary prose-drift gate would not.

=== SCOPE, AND IT IS SMALL

Two pages: `spec/011-SSR.md` and `spec/Security.md`. Read the four `def ^:private <name> #{...}` forms
out of `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`; require every literal member to appear
on each page. No section parsing, no per-site allowance.

EXPLICITLY OUT: the `attr-string` docstring gloss (constraint 4 — grading it needs a per-site
allowance which is itself a stale-able roster, and rf2-twyh has already relabelled it as a gloss
naming `strip-prop?` as the single realisation point); any count or structural invariant (constraint 3
— two CORRECT documents already disagree on the count); and the CLJS-side / conformance-fixture
cross-check the bead names as out of scope. If any of those looks worth doing, say so in the report
and do not do it.

== MAYOR, 2026-09-11: THE WORKER WENT BEYOND MY RULING ON ONE POINT AND I ENDORSE IT. PR #9662.

My ruling said "read the four `def ^:private <name> #{...}` forms". The worker instead made the
script DERIVE which four sets to read from `strip-prop?`'s own `(contains? …)` arms, and flagged the
departure rather than making it silently. ENDORSED, and it is better than what I ruled.

The reason is the item's own logic turned on the script: a hardcoded list of four set names inside
the gate would go stale in exactly the way the `attr-string` gloss did — a fifth class lands, the
copy does not follow, and nothing says so. That is the failure this gate exists to stop, and my
ruling would have reintroduced it one level up. Deriving the roster REMOVES the script's only
stale-able list instead of adding one, and it fails CLOSED (exit 2) on five measured ways the source
shape can move. Keep it.

=== A SECOND MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE BEAD'S OWN PROBE, AND IT MATTERS

The bead's throwaway probe evidently searched the `:`-prefixed spelling for at least some names (it
reported `:ref` missing from Security). Measured at tip WITH BOTH PAGES ALREADY CORRECT, that form
reports `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` missing from BOTH pages — they are JS property
names and are spelled bare in the prose.

So the `:`-prefixed form would have CRIED WOLF on two conformant documents on day one. That is the
one thing the ruling forbids, since the whole case for the simple form rests on it never
false-alarming. The shipped form matches the bare literal name, word-bounded on `[A-Za-z0-9_]`.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, ACCEPTED AND PINNED: that form finds `ref` present on `spec/Security.md` via the
unrelated `:rf.mcp/ref`, so it reports one fewer name than the bead's probe did. That is precisely
the UNDER-REPORT direction the ruling accepted as the price of never crying wolf — and it is pinned
by a self-test case rather than left as a prose claim, which is the right place for it.

=== WHAT LANDED

`scripts/check_ssr_prop_drop_roster_drift.py`, wired as TWO STEPS inside the existing
`verify-skill-mcp-drift` job (no new job key — the check band is unmoved, confirmed) plus two lines
in `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`. 689 insertions, 0 deletions, three files.

Gate numbers, all captured by the runner: self-test 35 cases 0 fail, exit 0; live scan at tip exit 0;
**at the pre-repair revision `a0e482433` exit 1 on BOTH pages**, reproducing the bead's measurement;
a planted fault exit 1 naming that page and that name alone; after restore exit 0. The invariant
job's 49 checkers 49/0, the docs-lane gates 15/0.

The pre-repair control is the number that matters: this gate WOULD have caught both drifts that
actually happened.

=== NEITHER SPEC PAGE WAS TOUCHED, CORRECTLY

Both were already repaired at tip by rf2-2fes and rf2-twyh, so there was nothing to edit and
`mkdocs build --strict` was declared skipped with that reason rather than run for form. Right call.

=== STILL OUT OF SCOPE, AND STILL CORRECTLY SO

The `attr-string` gloss, any count/structural invariant, and the CLJS-side / conformance-fixture
cross-check all stayed out. The worker's read is that only the third is genuinely still on the table
and wants its own bead, which is what the bead itself says. Not filed now — it is a second sighting
of a want, not a defect, and nothing is drifting while it waits.
close_reason:
ALREADY DONE — merged as 62099083a9, "feat(gate): SSR prop-drop roster drift gate (rf2-7ntc)".
The item was left at in_progress; its newest notes already read as a completed worker report with
captured gate numbers, which is the tell I nearly misread as a stranded dispatch.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE: `scripts/check_ssr_prop_drop_roster_drift.py` exists at tip (30,505 bytes) and is
wired into `.github/workflows/test.yml` as two steps — a `--self-test --verbose` step and a live scan —
inside the existing always-on `verify-skill-mcp-drift` job, plus two lines in the fast-PR spine,
following `check_keyword_catalogue_drift` exactly.

THE RULING THIS ITEM WAS WAITING ON WAS MADE AND IS IN THE LANDING: whole-file matching, not
section-scoped (2026-09-11). The argument is that contamination — `:children` as a key into 011's
structured-children map, `:rf.mcp/ref` in Security.md — makes the check UNDER-report, so it can never
cry wolf; section scoping would buy the remaining names at the price of a heading-range parser that
tracks where the roster lives on each page, which is a second thing that can go stale added to a gate
whose whole purpose is catching staleness.

The gate derives its name sets from `strip-prop?`'s own `(contains? ...)` arms rather than carrying a
list, so a fifth class is graded on arrival rather than silently ignored — which is exactly how the
gloss went short. Both limits are pinned by self-tests rather than claimed in prose: RED on both pages
at the pre-repair revision a0e482433, GREEN at trunk. A green is a FLOOR — "no literal name is wholly
absent from the page" — over four of the six classes; the other two arms (`event-handler-name?`,
`fn?`) carry no enumerable roster, and are exactly the two that never went stale.

BAND CORROBORATION, recorded because it matters to every merge tick: this landed as STEPS inside an

title: RULED 2026-09-13 TRACK 19.3.0: bump the re-frame2-pair fixture's react/react-dom pin to the project's React and guard it in lockstep (was: operator decision on React 18 coverage)
description:
AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT A TASK. Nobody should implement this without an answer from Mike, and the answer is
cheap to give and cannot be derived from the tree — which is why it is recorded rather than left in chat.

THE QUESTION: does the re-frame2-pair fixture's LIVE BROWSER LANE deliberately exercise React 18, or should
it track the project's React (19.3.0)?

WHY IT IS A REAL QUESTION AND NOT A STALE PIN. `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/package.json` pins
`react`/`react-dom` at 18.3.1 while the rest of the project is on 19.3.0. That pin is EXERCISED, which is the
fact that makes this a coverage decision rather than a version sweep:
`tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs` npm-installs the fixture, runs
`shadow-cljs watch app`, serves it and drives headless Chromium over the rendered Reagent view;
`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` arms `mcp_live=true` from `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/*`
specifically, so `test.yml`'s `mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair` job runs it per PR and `expensive-tests.yml`
runs it again nightly on Linux and Windows.

SO BUMPING IT CHANGES WHAT THAT LANE COVERS. Both readings are defensible and NOTHING IN THE TREE STATES
WHICH IS INTENDED:
  * KEEP 18.3.1 — the lane is deliberate React-18 coverage, the only place this project still exercises 18
    against a real renderer. Then say so, and the existing comment key becomes the durable record.
  * TRACK 19.3.0 — the fixture is meant to mirror what a user of the pair skill would install today, and an
    18-pinned fixture silently validates against a React nobody ships. Then bump it and expect the lane's
    behaviour to move.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so this bead is not re-doing it: rf2-2z4c landed a top-level `//` comment key in that
`package.json` recording WHY the pin is what it is. The intent is now readable from the file. What is not
recorded is whether the intent is still WANTED.

UNTIL ANSWERED THE PIN STAYS AT 18.3.1. Do not bump it as part of a version sweep; a sweep is exactly the act
this bead exists to stop.

OUT OF SCOPE: `skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md`'s `^19.0.0`, which is migration advice
where the caret is the point, and the two 19.3.0 pins moved by PR #9576. Both settled.
notes:
=== MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION, 2026-09-12. THE DECISION IS STILL THE OPERATOR'S, BUT THE TWO READINGS ARE NOT EQUALLY SUPPORTED BY THE RECORD. Recommendation: TRACK 19.3.0. Measured at trunk b844c1b611. ===

The bead states two defensible readings and asks which is wanted. **One of them rests on a premise
the git history refutes.** I did not bump anything; the pin stands at 18.3.1 as this bead requires.

FINDING 1 — THE PIN WAS NEVER CHOSEN. IT IS A FOUR-DAY RESIDUE.

Value of `react` in the two files, across their whole histories, change-points only:

    implementation/package.json       2026-05-08  18.3.1
                                      2026-05-17  19.2.0     <- the tree crossed here
                                      2026-09-10  19.3.0
    pair fixture package.json         2026-05-13  18.3.1     <- born here, four days BEFORE the cross
                                      (never changed since; 5 commits touch the file, none the value)

So the fixture was created while 18.3.1 WAS the tree-wide value, copied it, and was simply not
revisited when the implementation tree moved four days later. **No commit in this repo ever chose 18
for this fixture in preference to 19.** The only commit that ever touched the pin's MEANING is
8947675398 (2026-09-10, rf2-2z4c), which added the `//` key — and read it again closely: it records
that the pin is EXERCISED and that moving it changes what the lane covers. It does NOT record that 18
was wanted. That gap is exactly what this bead was opened to close, and the history closes it.

**This bead's KEEP reading is stated as "the lane is deliberate React-18 coverage." There is no
deliberation to find.** I looked for it and it is not there.

FINDING 2 — AND THE COMBINATION THE LANE ACTUALLY RUNS IS ONE THE OWNING ARTEFACT REFUSES.

The fixture's `deps.edn` pins `reagent/reagent 2.0.1`. `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md`
is the owner of that coordinate and says, under its own heading "Floor: Reagent 2.x + React 19":

    "The bridge supports exactly one combination: Reagent 2.x ... running against React 19.
     There is no Reagent 1.x compat path and no React 17/18 fallback."

and, in its posture bullet: "no React-18 fallback". Reagent 2.0.1's own devDependencies pin
react/react-dom to 19.2.0, so 19 is what Reagent itself is tested against.

**So the lane is not React-18 coverage of a supported configuration — it is the project's only
exercise of a combination the project states it does not support.** A green there is evidence about a
configuration this repo refuses, and a red there would be a bug nobody owns. That inverts the KEEP
reading's value proposition: the bead calls this lane "the only place this project still exercises 18
against a real renderer", which is factually true (I censused every react pin in the tree: this is the
sole 18, against 19.3.0 in implementation, the playground and the reagent-migration fixture, and a

title: RULED: :where names a place a reader can land on (public var | reserved event id | full namespace) - widen 3 instruction sites, respell the 23 SSR module sites to re-frame.ssr.emit (NOT 57)
notes:
A SECOND where-sym convention exists and nobody has ruled on it. Found 2026-09-08 by the rf2-z5lv worker
while baselining the first one, and it is filed separately because the answer is a RULING rather than a fix.

THE TWO CONVENTIONS, from the same measured sweep over implementation/**/src (193 where-syms total, 82
non-resolving):
  * THE `rf/` FAMILY — 25 non-resolving sites. These name a VAR that should be callable and is not, which
    is the defect rf2-z67m, rf2-0v23 and rf2-z5lv address: an author reads the message, types the name and
    gets "no such var".
  * THE MODULE FAMILY — the other 57. These name an internal MODULE rather than a callable var:
    'rf.ssr/*, 'rf.http/*, 'rf-machines/*, 'rf.resource/*. I verified the shape myself on trunk —
    'rf.ssr/response reads 10, 'rf.ssr/ssr-handler 7, 'rf.ssr/emit 6, 'rf.resource/route-entry 5,
    'rf.resource/invalidate-tags 5, against a live control of 231 quoted 'rf/ symbols.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A SWEEP: a module-naming where-sym may be exactly right. `:where` answers
"where did this fail", and for a failure inside the SSR emit pipeline the honest answer may well be
"rf.ssr/emit" — a place, not a door. That is a different contract from the rf/ family, where the string is
read as a name the author can type. If both are intended, they are two conventions and the difference
should be written down. If only one is, 57 sites are wrong.

THE QUESTION FOR MIKE, one of three:
  (a) MODULE NAMES ARE FINE. `:where` is a location, not an invitation to call something. Record the
      distinction in a tracked file so the next auditor does not re-file this, and leave the 57 alone.
  (b) MODULE NAMES ARE WRONG. `:where` must always name something resolvable; the 57 migrate to the
      owning namespace's real var, or to a namespace symbol that itself resolves.
  (c) SOMETHING NARROWER — e.g. module names are fine when no single var owns the failure, but a
      resolvable var is required when one does.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so this does not get re-derived: the rf2-z5lv gate BASELINES all 82 rather than
failing them, so nothing here is red today and no PR is blocked by this bead. The baseline is
scripts/where-sym-baseline.edn — 37 symbols, 82 sites, :min-where-syms 173, with an unlisted symbol taking
an implicit floor of 0 so NEW dead doors red immediately. Whichever way this rules, the mechanism to
enforce it already exists and the ratchet only has to be tightened.

ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH CARRYING INTO ANY IMPLEMENTATION: the rf2-z5lv oracle asserts about BOTH runtimes,
and it has to. `frame-provider` and `frame-root` are `#?(:cljs (def …))` facade exports, so a JVM-only
oracle reports both as dead doors — the union of JVM and CLJS publics is the only direction that cannot
manufacture a false red on a platform-specific name.

================================================================================
RULING -- 2026-09-09 13:21 AUSEST. Decided from the decision dossier plus an
independent Codex review, both re-measured on this tree. Dossier deleted.
================================================================================

DECISION -- option (c), the narrow one, with the spelling pinned:

  :where names A PLACE A READER CAN LAND ON. Three spellings satisfy it:
    1. a PUBLIC VAR in the alias dialect      -- 'rf/reg-flow, 'rf.ssr/emit-ui-tree
    2. a RESERVED PUBLIC EVENT ID as a symbol -- 'rf.resource/invalidate-tags
    3. a REAL NAMESPACE SPELLED IN FULL       -- 're-frame.ssr.emit
  A symbol that names none of those -- a var its namespace does not export, or a
  qualifier for a namespace that does not exist in the tree -- is a DEFECT.

  THE SPELLING FOR FORM 3 IS THE FULL NAMESPACE, 're-frame.ssr.emit, NOT the
  dotted require-alias 'rf.ssr.emit. Reason below; Codex won this point.

THE DELIVERABLE IS THE RULE, NOT A SWEEP. Three tracked files currently instruct
a reader that a where-sym must name a fn. They are made to agree, in ONE commit:
  * spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1789 -- "The :where slot names the user-facing
    surface fn symbol" -- the normative sentence; widen to the three forms.
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/error.cljc:108-110 -- the builder docstring,
    "the user-facing fn symbol that threw". A spec paragraph alone would leave
    this contradicting it. (Codex caught this; the dossier named only the spec.)
  * scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py:2196-2212 (_WHERE_SYM_FIX_HINT) --
    "it must NAME A REACHABLE VAR" plus the clause that pre-judges this bead:
    "nothing exports it (it is private, or it is a MODULE name rather than a
    fn): name the nearest PUBLIC entry point the author would actually call."
    THAT SENTENCE IS THE REASON "leave it, it costs nothing" LOSES. It is a
    live, committed instruction authorising exactly the 57-site sweep this
    ruling refuses, and a future fixer following it would do real damage.
    (Dossier cited it at :2263-2288; it is at :2210 on this tree.)

The 23 SSR sites are respelled IN THE SAME COMMIT -- see "the 23" below.

================================================================================
1. THE SIX-WAY RE-CLASSIFICATION -- THE BEAD'S OWN PREMISE WAS WRONG
================================================================================

THE OLD TITLE AND THE NOTES ABOVE SAY "57 where-syms name an internal MODULE".
THAT IS FALSE. THE TRUE COUNT IS 23. The 57 is an arithmetic residue (82
non-resolving minus the 25 bare-rf/ sites), never a measured shape. Classified
site by site it is SIX different things needing FOUR different answers. A worker
briefed on "57 modules" would normalise 34 sites that need a different answer or
none at all.

  B  NAMES THE ENCLOSING MODULE ......  6 symbols / 23 sites / 6 files
       ALL inside implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/. THIS is the bead.
       rf.ssr/response 9, rf.ssr/emit 6, rf.ssr/payload-policy 3,
       rf.ssr/html-helpers 2, rf.ssr.head/emit 2, rf.ssr/streaming 1.
  C  NAMES A RESERVED PUBLIC EVENT ID  2 symbols / 5 sites / 2 files
       rf.resource/invalidate-tags 4, rf.mutation/execute 1.
       A THIRD CONVENTION THE BEAD MISSES ENTIRELY, and the most defensible of
       the three. SANCTIONED -- leave every one of them exactly as written.
  D  REAL PUBLIC VAR, WRONG QUALIFIER  8 symbols / 21 sites / 7 files
       rf.ssr/ssr-handler 7, rf.ssr/cookie->set-cookie-header 5,
       rf.ssr/stream-handler 2, rf.http/decode-response-body 2,
       rf-machines/reg-machine* 2, rf.http/json-parse 1,
       rf-machines/reg-machine 1, rf-machines/make-machine-handler 1.
       *** ALREADY-RULED WORK IN DISGUISE. This is the SAME defect rf2-z67m and
       rf2-0v23 closed on, wearing a different qualifier. NOBODY FILES A
       CAMPAIGN FOR IT AND NOBODY DOES IT TWICE. Fix opportunistically as the
       files are touched; the baseline floors fall on their own. ***
  E  REAL PRIVATE VAR, RIGHT NAMESPACE 3 symbols / 4 sites / 3 files
       re-frame.router/build-envelope 2, rf.ssr.ring/import-fn 1,
       reagent2.impl.component/->react-element 1. LEAVE. An honest location.
  F  NAMES NOTHING AT ALL ...........  3 symbols / 4 sites / 3 files
       rf.ssr/manifest-script 2, rf.http/classify-response-body 1,
       rf.ssr/trusted-shell 1. Wrong under any reading; fix on sight, no bead.
                                     ------------------------------------------
       TOTAL                          22 symbols / 57 sites / 21 files

VERIFIED HERE, with a positive control. git grep over implementation/ssr/src for
quoted rf. where-syms, CRLF stripped, reads 28 total; the six B symbols sum to
exactly 23 (9+6+3+2+2+1) and the residue is 5 resolving facade names
(emit-ui-tree 2, read-server-payload, hydrate!, boundary). Per-file counts match
per-symbol counts exactly for all six B files -- i.e. EVERY module-family site is
written inside the very file whose namespace it names. That is not a typo
pattern, it is a deliberate "you are here", which is what makes form 3 worth
blessing rather than correcting.
  Control note: the first attempt at this census read a constant 0 because the
  files are CRLF and a dollar-anchor sat behind the carriage return. Caught by
  the positive control. Same family as the jq/CRLF trap in CLAUDE.md.
Also verified: re-frame.resource, re-frame.mutation and re-frame.http DO NOT
EXIST as namespaces in this tree (0 files each; re-frame.resources exists) -- so
the D and C qualifiers are genuinely unresolvable, not merely unfashionable.

================================================================================
2. THE SURFACING EVIDENCE -- WHY "LEAVE IT" LOSES ON FACTS, NOT TASTE
================================================================================

:where is one of four REQUIRED slots on every framework throw (Spec 009). It is
NOT in the exception message and NOT rendered by Xray -- but it does leave the
box. All four sites read verbatim on this tree:

  * tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1163
      (= 'rf.story/variant-plan (:where (ex-data e)))
    A REAL SEMANTIC CONSUMER -- Story BRANCHES on the value, and its own
    docstring calls matching on :where rather than on :rf.error/id
    "load-bearing". Pinned by a test at
    tools/story/test/re_frame/story/runtime_runpath_test.clj:303.
    *** THIS PRODUCER/CONSUMER PAIR IS FROZEN. Do not touch
    'rf.story/variant-plan. ***
  * tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:552
      "(ex-data err) now merges into the envelope ... the actionable slots
       beside it (:where, :recovery, and whatever the site carries) arrive at
       all"
    RELAYED VERBATIM OFF-BOX TO AN AI AGENT.
  * tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/result.cljc:142
      "Every other slot rides through as itself -- :reason, :where, :recovery,
       :kind, :id are all plain data and the walk returns them unchanged"
    SAME, second server.
  * spec/009-Instrumentation.md rosters specific :where values per catalogue row
    (:2257 'rf/replace-container!, :2408 rf.ssr/emit-ui-tree). Both are public
    vars, both conform to form 1 -- NO CATALOGUE ROW CHANGES.

So the field is not internal, and a label naming something that does not exist
is a real defect. Its severity is bounded and that bound is honest: nothing
renders :where by default, so a wrong value degrades an AI agent's diagnostic
rather than breaking a user's screen. Real, not urgent -- which is why the
answer is one rule change and not a campaign.

CODEX'S NARROWING ACCEPTED: relay proves a label CAN reach an agent, not that
any agent resolves or hyperlinks it. Only the Story branch is a proven semantic
consumer. That is still enough.

================================================================================
3. WHO WON THE CONFLICTS
================================================================================

CODEX WINS -- "OPTION 1b IS SELF-ENFORCING AT ZERO GATE COST" IS BACKWARDS.
Verified at scripts/check_thrown_error_messages.py, where_sym_findings
(~:1712-1724): if "/" not in site.symbol -> continue, with the comment
"Counted, never a finding." EVERY slash-free symbol is skipped BEFORE the
namespace index is consulted. So 'rf.ssr.emit and
'rf.ssr.this-module-does-not-exist are treated IDENTICALLY. The dotted spelling
does not make the convention enforce itself -- it makes it UNCHECKABLE. That was
Option 1b's headline mechanism and it is false. The dossier saw the skip and
read it as free enforcement; it is free silence.

CODEX WINS THE SPELLING -- full 're-frame.ssr.emit, not dotted 'rf.ssr.emit.
(namespace 'rf.ssr.emit) is nil and quoting does not expand an alias; the alias
rule in spec/Conventions.md:218 governs REQUIRE ALIASES and distinguishes them
from public namespace names. Decisively: the surfacing evidence above is an
OFF-BOX AI AGENT, which has no repo and cannot expand a dialect alias, but can
grep 're-frame.ssr.emit straight onto the ns form. The dossier's own best
evidence argues for Codex's spelling.

CODEX WINS A FACTUAL CORRECTION ON THE SCHEMAS. The dossier said :where is
"typed :symbol in normative wire schemas -- Spec-Schemas.md:1755, 1931, 2015,
2229, 2239". Read on this tree: :1931 and :2015 are [:or :symbol :string], and
:1755 is {:optional true} :symbol. Only :2229 and :2239 are bare :symbol. The
slot is less tightly typed than claimed. Does not change the ruling; recorded so
nobody re-derives it. Do NOT widen or unify those schemas as part of this work
-- and do NOT conflate them with the UNRELATED keyword-valued :where schema slot
(Xray projection, and
implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_projector.cljc:229, which controls SSR
HTTP classification). Two contracts, one key name.

THE DOSSIER WINS "DO THE 23 NOW", AND IT WINS ON CODEX'S OWN TERMS. Codex says
renaming must improve the diagnostic rather than reduce a finding count. Under
the spelling ruled here it demonstrably improves it -- 'rf.ssr/emit resolves to
NOTHING (re-frame.ssr exports no emit), 're-frame.ssr.emit names a real
namespace -- and the finding-count motive is provably absent, because Codex's
own finding is that the gate skips slash-free symbols either way, so the count
does not move. The objection dissolves. Leaving 23 sites that the freshly
written rule calls defects is the half-fixed state that got this bead re-filed
once already. 23 edits, 6 files, ONE isolated-surface artefact, no message text
changes (none of the 23 messages quote their own where-sym), no test changes.

BOTH AGREE, RECORDED ONCE: the true module count is 23 not 57; a 57-site
normalisation campaign is refused; bucket C stays as written and :where keeps
its symbol value type (no keyword-valued events); bucket D is already-ruled
work; the spec's single-shape sentence is narrower than the practice and the
practice is the better of the two.

================================================================================
4. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE -- NAMED REFUSALS
================================================================================

This decision naturally grows a lint rule, a CI gate and a backfill. ALL THREE
ARE REFUSED:

  * NO NEW LINT RULE, NO NEW CI JOB, NO NEW WORKFLOW.
    check_thrown_error_messages.py is and stays the only enforcement surface for
    this contract.
  * NO 57-SITE CAMPAIGN. Explicitly refused. It is four different jobs and two
    of them would make the diagnostics WORSE.
  * NO BUCKET D SWEEP (21 sites). Already ruled by rf2-z67m / rf2-0v23.
    Opportunistic only. Filing a campaign for it is litigating minutiae.
  * NO BUCKET E BACKFILL (4 private vars in the right namespace). Leave them.
  * NO BEAD FOR BUCKET F (4 sites naming nothing). Fix on sight.
  * NO EXTENSION OF THE GATE TO tools/. DEFAULT_SCAN_DIRS is implementation
    alone; tools/ carries 65 where-syms with 8 non-resolving across three
    further qualifier dialects. Genuinely separable and genuinely undecided --
    split out to its own bead, not folded in here.
  * NO LOCATION MAP, NO RESOLVER SERVICE, NO SOURCE-LINK REGISTRY, NO RUNTIME
    VALIDATION LAYER. (Codex named these; refused here too.)
  * NO CHANGE TO :where's VALUE TYPE. Reserved event ids stay SYMBOLS.
  * NO SPEC-SCHEMAS WIDENING, NO CATALOGUE-ROW EDITS, NO BASELINE HAND-EDIT.
  * NO TOUCHING 'rf.story/variant-plan (frozen producer/consumer pair).

================================================================================
5. NEXT STEPS -- one dispatch, then one regenerate
================================================================================

  1. ONE COMMIT, one worker: widen the rule at the three instruction sites named
     at the top (spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1789; error.cljc:108-110;
     _WHERE_SYM_FIX_HINT :2196-2212), AND respell the 23 SSR sites to the full
     namespace form ('rf.ssr/emit -> 're-frame.ssr.emit, etc. across the six
     files under implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/).
     *** spec/009-Instrumentation.md IS A CLAUDE.md HOT-ZONE FILE -- one
     toucher, sequence this against any other 009 bead, never parallel. ***
  2. THEN regenerate scripts/where-sym-baseline.edn through the checker's normal
     reviewed path (--write-where-sym-baseline; it only ever ratchets DOWN and
     reports suggested reductions rather than applying them silently). Six B
     symbols drop out of the findings. :min-where-syms does NOT move --
     slash-free symbols are still COUNTED, only never a finding.
  3. SMALL CHECKER ADDITION, same commit or immediately after, ~10 lines and NO
     new gate: form 3 is currently unchecked (the skip above). Reuse the
     existing PublicVarIndex.publics_of (:1431), which already distinguishes
     "namespace exists with no publics" from "namespace absent", to validate a
     slash-free dotted where-sym against the namespace index. This closes the
     hole the new rule opens and is the ONLY tooling change authorised.

title: [implementation/ssr-node] isolate-lost refusal from the worker exit arm carries an empty detail map
description:
Found by worker/ssr-b while delivering rf2-kirm (PR #9377); explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for that bead and left unfixed rather than folded in.

THE ASYMMETRY. In implementation/ssr-node/src/isolate.cjs the worker.on('error') arm builds its refusal with {isolate, threadId}, while the worker.on('exit') arm builds :rf.ssr-node/isolate-lost with the message 'the isolate exited mid-render' and an EMPTY detail map {}. Both arms reach the same refusal code.

WHY IT MATTERS. :rf.ssr-node/isolate-lost covers THREE distinct causes — a crashed worker, a worker that exited, and a replacement that will not boot — and they are distinguishable only by detail SHAPE. With an empty map the consumer cannot tell which isolate exited, nor which of the three causes it is looking at. rf2-kirm's repair now stamps afterChunks onto this arm, so the map is no longer empty in every case, but the identifying fields (isolate, threadId) are still absent where the sibling arm supplies them.

SMALLEST REPAIR: give the exit arm the same {isolate, threadId} the error arm already supplies. Keep the refusal code, the sanitised wording and the termination/replacement behaviour unchanged — this is a detail-map gap, not a policy change.

NOT A CORRECTNESS DEFECT: nothing serves wrong output, and no caller is documented to branch on these fields today. It is an observability asymmetry between two arms of one refusal, which is why it is P3 and not higher. Premise is worker-reported and re-verified at source before dispatching.

title: [implementation/epoch] Replay reports a child epoch when its own record was evicted
description:
Snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; current main 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795 has no implementation/epoch diff.

Expected / actual
`perform-replay!` (implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:632-666) promises the replayed event's own new epoch, or nil when the ring cannot retain it. It instead returns the first record currently in the history whose id was absent before dispatch. If a queued child evicts the replayed event's epoch before dispatch-sync returns, that first surviving record is the CHILD, but the response's :event-id still names the PARENT.

This is not a retention-policy complaint. Bounded eviction is correct; the returned causal evidence is wrong. Replay explicitly runs against current state/code (spec/Tool-Pair.md:158-170), so a replay may legitimately enqueue more work than the source run did.

Actual consumer impact
skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:2294-2300 feeds result :epoch-id into attach-cascade and consequence-from-summary. The child epoch therefore becomes the replay's reported cascade/consequence. Pair-MCP tools/replay_epoch.cljs:62-120 publishes that response as success. A developer/agent is shown the child's operation/state/effects as evidence for the replayed parent. Narrow P3 diagnostic/correlation bug; the event execution itself succeeds.

Actual-source isolated reproduction, bb core/src + epoch/src classpath:
```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.epoch]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as adapter]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(adapter/install-adapter! plain/adapter)
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 1}})
(rf/reg-event :review/child
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :child true)}))
(rf/reg-event :review/parent
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _]
    (cond-> {:db (update db :runs (fnil inc 0))}
      (:runs db) (assoc :fx [[:dispatch [:review/child]]]))))
(rf/make-frame {:id :review/eviction})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/parent] {:frame :review/eviction})
(def original (last (rf/epoch-history :review/eviction)))
(def result (rf/replay-epoch! :review/eviction (:epoch-id original)))
(println result)
(println (mapv #(select-keys % [:epoch-id :event-id])
               (rf/epoch-history :review/eviction)))
```
The first run enqueues no child, so its parent source is retained and replay preconditions genuinely pass. On replay, :runs is present, so the child settles after the parent and evicts it. Executed exit 0:
`:source {:epoch-id 1, :event-id :review/parent}`
`:result {:ok? true, :frame :review/eviction, :source-epoch-id 1, :event-id :review/parent, :epoch-id 3}`
`:returned-record {:epoch-id 3, :event-id :review/child}`
`:history [{:epoch-id 3, :event-id :review/child}]`
Expected :epoch-id nil under the implementation's documented retained-result convention, not child id 3.

Smallest repair / acceptance
Correlate the returned result with the replayed dispatch's actual epoch identity instead of any new retained record. If that epoch is no longer retained, return nil as documented; do not redesign retention/history or broaden the public API. Event-id alone is not reliable correlation when a child can use the same registration id.
- The real depth-1 scenario above reports nil, never the child id, while both parent and child state effects still happen.
- A sufficient-depth control reports the replay parent's own retained id, not the last child.
- Pair's attached cascade is absent/honest when the parent was evicted and refers to the parent when retained.
- Existing strict input/refusal semantics and depth policy remain unchanged.

Dedupe / limits
Searched active and closed epoch/replay records, plus description search for pre-replay-epoch-ids (none) and relevant dispatch identity memory. Closed rf2-ov144 introduced the one-call replay API; closed rf2-f8wu corrected depth transitions. Neither owns return correlation under ordinary bounded eviction. The independent redacted-input replay bug rf2-xlr0 is a pre-dispatch completeness issue, not this successful-dispatch response identity issue. No fixes/builds/full tests; isolated actual-source bb witness only. First probe attempt hit a scratch variable-name collision with bb's referred clojure.repl/source, before replay; renaming that local yielded the quoted exit-0 actual result. CLJS and tool integration tests were inspected but not executed.
acceptance_criteria: Depth-1 replay that queues a child returns nil for the evicted parent epoch, not the child id; sufficient-depth control returns the actual replay parent; Pair consequence attachment uses accurate causal evidence; no retention redesign.

THE FIX. `perform-replay!` previously took "the first record in the post-dispatch history whose
id was absent beforehand". That cannot answer the question: when a cascade commits exactly
`depth` records the retained window is IDENTICAL whether the parent survived or not, so no
count- or order-based reading of the ring distinguishes the two. Identity now comes from COMMIT
ORDER instead — `rf.epoch.state/arm-commit-observation!` arms a one-shot slot on the frame
across the dispatch, `commit-frame-owner-record!` fills it with the FIRST epoch committed for
that frame while the arming stands, and `take-observed-commit!` (in a `finally`, so the strict
`:rf.error/missing-required-cofx` still propagates unchanged) hands it back. The ring is then
asked SEPARATELY whether that epoch is retained; if not, the documented nil rides back.

Filled in `commit-frame-owner-record!` rather than `record!` deliberately: it answers "which
epoch did this dispatch commit?", which is true of a record the ring immediately evicted and
true at depth 0, where `record!` appends nothing at all. The arming token makes a concurrent
arming honest instead of silently clobbering (a caller whose arming was replaced gets nil — the
same "no retained epoch" the contract already means). Hot path cost when nothing is armed is one
map read. `reset-histories!` clears the slot alongside the other per-frame ledgers.

NOT A RETENTION CHANGE, per the bead's own fence. Bounded eviction is untouched: depth policy,
`append-record`, `enforce-depth!` and the `:trace-events-keep` rule are all unchanged. What was
wrong was the returned causal evidence.

CONSUMER. The Pair preload's `attach-cascade` already no-ops when the epoch-id does not resolve
to a record, so a `nil` produces an ABSENT `:cascade-summary` rather than a wrong one — the
bead's "absent/honest when the parent was evicted" criterion is met with no consumer change, and
`consequence-from-summary` is not reached. Verified by reading
`skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs`; not edited.

SPEC. `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s replay bullet said only `:epoch-id <the new epoch>`, which is what

when the ring did not keep it; `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` carries the same clarification.

title: examples(realworld-http): align host-page base with the /realworld URL/deployment contract
description:
`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html` carries a RELATIVE asset href (`href="_shared/css/style.css"`) beside a route with a path parameter. That is latently the rf2-g1gt defect in the repo's own routing example: on a one-segment route the relative path resolves to `/_shared/css/style.css` and works; on a deeper route it resolves against the route's directory (e.g. `/issues/_shared/css/style.css`) and the page silently loses its stylesheet.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (from rf2-g1gt, PR #9137, measured with `new URL()` over four cases): `_shared/css/style.css` on `/` -> `/_shared/…`; on `/issues/srv-1` -> `/issues/_shared/…`. Browser behaviour, not a Hicasso or re-frame2 behaviour.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN NOTING: an example is a teaching surface, and this one teaches routing specifically. A reader who copies its `index.html` inherits a bug that only appears once their routes get deeper than one segment — which is exactly when they stop reading the example and start writing their own routes.

BUT VERIFY BEFORE CHANGING: establish whether this example's routes actually GO deeper than one segment today. If every route it ships is one segment, the page is correct as it stands and the fix is a comment rather than an edit — a verified "correct today, fragile if extended" is a complete deliverable, and saying that plainly may serve a reader better than a silent correction.

THE TWO REMEDIES, both already verified in this repo and now documented in `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md`: absolute paths (which `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md`'s own `index.html` already uses), or `<base href="/">`, with `rf.routing/with-base-path` for a sub-path deploy (present at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc`). CHECK THE OTHER EXAMPLES TOO. A census of relative asset hrefs across every `examples/**/index.html` against the route depth each example ships is the real deliverable — one confirmed instance means the pattern is worth a sweep. Two independent instruments plus a control that fires; note that `git grep` with a pattern STARTING WITH `/` is MSYS path-mangled on this host and silently returns zero for everything, so use `grep -rn` as the second instrument rather than a second `git grep` pattern.

title: hic tooling: hm/shadow!'s own docstring example crosses :article-id, which reaches a reactified Reagent original as :articleId
notes:
FOUND while fixing chapter 20 §3 for rf2-z1cz (PR #9131). NOT RUN - derived by reading source on both sides, not by executing a shadow comparison.

implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs, shadow!'s docstring, opens with:

    :reference [:> (r/reactify-component old/article-row) {:article-id 7}]

The crossing renames the prop, silently, and the original's destructuring of :article-id gets nil:

- Hicasso side: impl.codec/host-entry - 'The caller (host-entry) camelCases the top-level KEY' - so {:article-id 7} is emitted as #js{articleId: 7}.
- Reagent side: reactify-component -> impl.component/as-class; a React parent's props carry no .argv, so props-argv falls to [(.-constructor c) (util/shallow-obj-to-map p)], and shallow-obj-to-map is (keyword k) on the RAW JS key name. "articleId" becomes :articleId, not :article-id.

The asymmetry is real rather than a bug in either half: codec/prop-key decodes "articleId" back to :article-id on the INWARD route (h/as-component), so names round-trip there. Nothing performs that decode on the OUTWARD route into a reactified Reagent component.

Two other infelicities in the same example, both minor:
- (r/reactify-component ...) is called INLINE, so a fresh component type is allocated per evaluation. as-component's own docstring states the law for the mirror-image case ('Call it ONCE, at top level ... a fresh one per render is a fresh element type that remounts the subtree, React.memo's own law').
- There is no in-repo witness for a FOREIGN :reference at all: test_kit/test/re_frame/hicasso/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs uses Hicasso views on both sides of every row. So the documented migration route is the one the door's own witness does not drive.

REMEDY, in preference order: cross a single-word prop (:id) in the example, hoist the reactify-component call to a top-level def, and consider a shadow_dom_cljs_test row with a genuinely foreign :reference so the route has a witness.

Chapter 20 §3 was corrected to :id and a hoisted def in PR #9131 and now states the renaming rule; this bead is the docstring and the missing witness, both under implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**, which was outside that dispatch's fence.

FENCE: implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**. A docstring-only edit does not change what check_guide_samples.py resolves; a test row is a CLJS browser-lane change (-dom-cljs-test).

The bead's mechanism was verified at source rather than assumed: OUT, raw-element reduces props through codec/host-entry whose slot comes from slot/prop-name, the camelCaser, so :article-id emits as articleId and raw-gate hands that object on untouched; IN, Reagent's reactify-component -> as-class, and a React parent's props carry no .argv so props-argv falls back to util/shallow-obj-to-map, which is (keyword k) on the raw JS key, giving :articleId; and nothing decodes it back on that route, codec/prop-key having only two call sites, both inward.
