title: Clarify private testbed editor process-stream lifecycle locals
description:
## Finding

The private process/stream lifecycle code in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj` uses short locals at the concurrency boundary. `drain-stream` binds `sb` for the retained diagnostic builder, `buf` for the character buffer, `cap` for the retained-character limit, `r` for the UTF-8 reader, and `n` for each read count. `launch!` binds `pb` for the process builder, `proc` for the child process, and `err-drain` for the stderr-drain future. These names sit at the timeout/pipe-concurrency boundary where each value has a distinct lifecycle role.

## Ambiguity cost

A maintainer must infer whether `cap` bounds the stream or only retained text, whether `n` is bytes or characters, and whether `err-drain` is a stream or future. The generic builder/process names also obscure which object owns stdout redirection versus stderr draining. This risks breaking deadlock prevention, UTF-8 accounting, or timeout lifecycle while ordinary tests stay green.

## Phase-1 exclusions and compatibility

This is private/local naming only. Preserve `launch!`, `drain-stream`, endpoint paths, `file`/`line`/`column`/`editor` flags, JSON keys, error tokens, exit codes, editor vocabulary, subprocess argv and ordering, stdout/stderr redirection, timeout/termination behavior, UTF-8 decoding, diagnostic cap, fixtures, and browser/JVM behavior. Exclude every vestigial, public, and test-file migration target.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rename those locals explicitly by role without changing behavior or output.
- Focused JVM and testbed-support CLJS/browser gates pass.
- No `sb`/`buf`/`cap`/`n`/`r`/`pb`/`proc`/`err-drain` binding remains for these roles.
- The diff is limited to private names and adjacent comments in this file.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit process/stream lifecycle locals; unchanged subprocess, timeout, diagnostics, and response contracts; focused JVM and testbed-support gates pass; diff limited to private names/comments.
close_reason: Renamed only private testbed editor stream/process lifecycle locals; focused JVM, CLJS, kondo, and lane-bijection self-test all pass with contracts unchanged.

title: Clarify test-quiet reporter namespace-banner state and callbacks
description:
## Naming finding

The shared CLJC reporter uses compressed `ns` terminology and names its state by incidental representation rather than domain role. In `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet.cljc:91-266`, `printed-banners` is actually a set of namespace symbols, `ns-stack` is the balanced stack of open test namespaces, and helpers such as `failing-ns`, `event-ns`, and `banner-ns` represent three distinct namespace sources. The current names force readers to repeatedly consult docstrings to distinguish stored namespace identity from rendered banner text and failure-var versus report-event versus fallback selection.

## Proposed names

Use explicit private roles: `printed-banner-namespaces`, `open-test-namespace-stack`, `open-test-namespace!`, `close-test-namespace!`, `current-test-namespace`, `namespace-banner-printed?`, `mark-namespace-banner-printed!`, `print-namespace-banner!`, `failing-test-namespace`, `report-event-namespace`, and `failure-banner-namespace`. Spell out private parameters/locals such as `namespace-symbol`, `test-var`, and `test-namespace`. Update both CLJ and CLJS branches and all comments/references together.

## Ambiguity cost

This reporter is intentionally stateful across nested `run-tests` calls. The abbreviated names obscure which namespace source is authoritative at each event and make future lifecycle fixes more likely to mutate the wrong state or mark the wrong banner as printed.

## Compatibility / risk

All proposed Vars are private and repository-wide searches find no out-of-namespace consumers or serialized use. Preserve the public namespace, reporter multimethod dispatch keys, output text/shape, nesting semantics, reload-safe default-method captures, and public runtime entry points. No Phase-1 bead targets these helpers; existing Phase-1 test-quiet beads concern copied selector coverage, exit-integrity coverage, and duplicate subprocess rows.

title: ssr-node render pipeline: distinguish frames, dispatch IDs, and module returns
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/service.cjs` bridges an isolate callback into the public async generator with `req`, `queue`, `wake`, `nudge`, `finished`, `failure`, `terminal`, and `run`. The names hide which side owns each value: the queue holds pending public frames, `wake` is the suspended generator continuation, `terminal` is the isolate's render result, and `run` is the completion/release promise. `src/worker.cjs` uses `mod`, `post`, `id`, `seq`, `snapshot`, `call`, and especially `out` for the application module's returned value at the fail-closed egress check. These names date to b2b35bf6e9; the body-only egress hardening in 67d4d9338a made the returned value security-significant without renaming it.

A reader currently has to infer whether `id` is the caller's `requestId` or the isolate-local render ID, and whether `out` is emitted HTML or the forbidden second-channel return. The callback/generator bridge similarly makes `run` and `terminal` easy to confuse with frames.

## Recommendation

Name service values by asynchronous role (`validatedRequest`, `pendingFrames`, `resumeConsumer`, `wakeConsumer`, `renderFinished`, `renderFailure`, `renderResult`, `renderCompletion`). Name worker-private values by boundary role (`renderModule`, `renderId`, `chunkSeq`, `stateSnapshot`, `runtimeSnapshot`, `renderCall`, `moduleReturnValue`, `postMessage`). Update comments and internal calls together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

Do not rename public `Service`, `renderFrames`, `renderToString`, `createService`, the render-module `render`/`emit` contract, message discriminators or keys (`t`, `id`, `seq`), request/frame fields, or serialized refusal details. Do not edit the worker `stack` payloads owned for removal by rf2-6r9j.77, and do not absorb the `chunkFrame` integration owned by rf2-6r9j.74.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Service bridge bindings identify pending frames, the suspended consumer, render completion, result, and failure without generic `queue`/`wake`/`run`/`terminal` names.
2. Worker bindings distinguish the isolate-local render ID, state/runtime snapshots, render call, and forbidden module return value.
3. Public APIs, render-module contract, worker message schema, frame schema, refusal behavior, and stack-removal target remain byte/shape compatible.
4. Exact old/new searches, lint, focused egress/streaming tests, and the full ssr-node gate pass.
close_reason: Implemented in bd05dceead: role-specific internal names across protocol, render pipeline, isolate/pool lifecycle, and HTTP launcher; public APIs and wire keys preserved. SSR-node gate, ESLint, syntax, exact legacy search, and diff check pass.

title: Routing URL ownership: distinguish installed, current, excluded, and conflicting frames

title: Remove unreachable legacy region scan from machines-viz raw-node-at
description:
Evidence
- chart/layout.cljc raw-node-at has a no-:region fallback: after a top-level lookup misses, it scans every parallel region for the same path.
- Its sole source call is attach-consumer-requires, which passes nodes produced by project-definition. project-parallel assigns :region to every region state and the synthetic region container; the layout regression suite explicitly asserts every parallel state knows its region.
- Flat and compound nodes lack :region but live under definition :states, so their first lookup resolves. Synthetic root nodes have empty paths and are rejected before lookup.
- Therefore the cross-region scan can run only for a hand-built obsolete node shape: non-empty region-relative path with its required :region identity removed. No source/test/Xray caller constructs that shape, and raw-node-at is absent from spec/API.md's enumerated public surface.
- The fallback was deliberately retained as legacy wording in commit 700767339d4 when region-aware identity fixed wrong-region lifecycle metadata; retaining it now preserves the ambiguous behavior that fix made unnecessary.

Impact
The dead branch encodes a dangerous first-region-wins lookup. If a malformed projected node loses :region, silently borrowing a sibling region's lifecycle requirements is worse than returning nil and exposes the old correctness bug as compatibility behavior.

Recommendation
For nodes without :region, resolve only under top-level :states. Remove the region scan and legacy wording; keep strict region-qualified lookup for parallel nodes.

Risks and contracts
Preserve flat/compound lookup, strict per-region resolution, empty/synthetic-node nil behavior, and lifecycle requirement projection. Do not change the machine grammar or region-scoped IDs. Reassess only if a supported external constructor of raw projected nodes is identified.
acceptance_criteria:
- raw-node-at never scans all regions for a node missing :region.
- Flat/compound nodes still resolve through top-level :states; valid parallel nodes resolve only through their own region.
- A regression proves a no-:region region-relative node returns nil rather than first-region data.
- Existing duplicate-path parallel-region lifecycle requirement tests pass on JVM and CLJS.
- raw-node-at remains absent from the documented public API, or any newly discovered compatibility obligation is documented before changing behavior.
close_reason: PR #9085: raw-node-at's no-:region cross-region fallback removed. Verified unreachable — project-parallel stamps :region on every region state and the region container, the parallel-root chip's path segment is the namespaced :rf.machines-viz.layout/parallel-root (cannot name a real state), the machine-root chip has an empty path, and a flat definition has no :regions to scan. New regression raw-node-at-no-region-node-never-borrows-a-sibling-region pins nil-not-first-region plus unchanged flat/nested/absent/empty-path lookup; gate liveness proved by restoring the scan (red at layout_cljs_test.cljc:1543, actual {:entry :enter-a}) then restoring to the identical blob. raw-node-at absent from spec/API.md and tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md — no compatibility obligation found.

title: Remove inert machine-timer rewrite from schemas fixture loader
description:
## Finding

The schemas conformance loader rewrites every bare auto-resolved keyword `::name` to `:rf.machine.timer/name`, even though no schema fixture contains such a token and the timer namespace belongs to the machines corpus. The code and its `clojure.string` dependency are an inert copy retained only "for symmetry"; if it ever activates on a future schemas fixture, it assigns an unrelated namespace rather than resolving that fixture's namespace.

## Evidence

- `load-fixture` in `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` (currently lines 146-156) slurps text, applies `str/replace` with `#"::([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)"` to `":rf.machine.timer/$1"`, then parses it.
- Its own docstring states that schemas fixtures do not use auto-resolved keywords, that the rewrite is for machines/SSR timer events, and that it is a no-op on this subset.
- The runner's exact selected corpus is five files: `error-schema-failure.edn` plus the four `schema-*.edn` fixtures. A controlled token census over those files returns zero `::name` matches, so `raw` and `fixed` are identical for every reachable input today.
- Applying the transform to a probe `::probe` yields `:rf.machine.timer/probe`, proving the claimed future robustness is not schema-generic; it silently invents a machines timer identity.
- The rewrite and commentary entered with the initial schemas runner in `54a3531931` and have never had a schemas-corpus consumer.
- All-status title/description searches for `auto-resolved`, `timer rewrite`, `rf.machine.timer`, and schemas conformance found no issue owning this residue. The one bead description mentioning `rf.machine.timer` concerns retired SSR skill guidance and is unrelated.

## Impact

Every current schemas fixture pays an unnecessary textual preprocessing step and the runner advertises support it does not implement correctly. A future schema fixture using `::foo` would not be rejected or resolved in its authoring namespace; it would be silently changed to a machine timer keyword, potentially making expectations pass or fail under a false identity.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the schemas-only auto-resolved-keyword rewrite, its now-unused `clojure.string` require if nothing else consumes it, and the copied timer-specific prose. Parse the original fixture text directly with `read-one-form`. If schema fixtures later need an alias/namespace facility, define it explicitly in the conformance format instead of borrowing a machines rewrite.

## Risks

Do not remove the analogous transform from machine/SSR/core runners without auditing their selected fixtures; this issue proves only that the schemas subset has zero consumers. Preserve exact-one-form throwing behavior and fixture filename diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
- `load-fixture` passes the original schemas fixture text directly to `read-one-form`; it contains no `:rf.machine.timer/$1` replacement or claim of auto-resolved-keyword support.
- `clojure.string` is removed from the schemas conformance namespace if the rewrite was its last use.
- The five selected schemas fixtures still parse and execute with unchanged IDs, capabilities, expectations, and results.
- A focused regression demonstrates that an injected bare `::probe` is not silently reclassified as `:rf.machine.timer/probe` (a parse failure is acceptable until the format defines such syntax).
- Schemas conformance and the full schemas JVM suite pass; machine, SSR, flows, and core fixture loaders are untouched by this slice-local cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). load-fixture now passes the fixture text to read-one-form verbatim; the ::name -> :rf.machine.timer/name rewrite and the copied timer prose are gone. A focused regression (loader-does-not-restamp-auto-resolved-keywords) pins that a bare ::probe never arrives as :rf.machine.timer/probe; it is live, verified by a negative control that restored the rewrite and turned both assertions red with actual :rf.machine.timer/probe, reproducing the exact silent restamping the bead describes. edn/read rejects ::probe outright (Invalid token), so the loader throws, which the bead permits. The five selected fixtures still load and execute unchanged (373 tests / 19223 assertions, exit 0). PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the conditional criterion 'remove clojure.string if the rewrite was its last use' does not fire — schema-fixture-file? still calls str/starts-with? and str/ends-with?, so clojure.string stays in the ns. Machine, SSR, flows and core fixture loaders untouched.

title: Remove three dead imports and bindings from the UIx test slice
description:
## Scope

Remove three mechanically dead bindings in the UIx adapter's test and smoke-testbed slice. No runtime API, event behavior, fixture shape, dependency recipe, or test intent changes.

## Vestigial finding

The UIx tree carries one unused namespace require and two event-handler destructures whose db values are never read:

1. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj:29 requires clojure.string as str, but the file never refers to str.
2. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:683 destructures db in the ::dollar-shape-seed handler, then replaces :db with a literal map without reading the old value.
3. implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:20 destructures db in :counter/init, then replaces :db with the literal initial counter without reading the old value.

## Evidence

A read-only clj-kondo pass over implementation/adapters/uix/{src,test,testbed} reports exactly these as unused-namespace/unused-binding findings:

- uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj:29, namespace clojure.string is required but never used;
- uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:683, unused binding db;
- adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:20, unused binding db.

Manual repository-wide/source inspection confirms no str-qualified call in the recipe test and no read of either destructured db before the literal replacement. The other linter warnings in this pass are unresolved cross-namespace CLJS vars caused by the standalone analysis classpath/macros and are deliberately excluded from this bead.

## Impact

These names imply dependencies on string helpers and prior database state that do not exist. That adds noise to a dependency-governance test and to the minimal adapter smoke whose source explicitly says not to grow it. It also prevents a focused unused-binding lint pass from being clean.

## Recommended disposition

Delete the clojure.string alias and name the unused event-handler parameters as intentionally ignored (or otherwise avoid destructuring them), keeping the event results byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Risks

Very low. The only risk is accidentally changing the literal seed maps or handler arity while cleaning the argument names; focused tests and smoke compile/runtime behavior cover that.
acceptance_criteria:
- Remove [clojure.string :as str] from uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj; no string helper is introduced as a substitute.
- The ::dollar-shape-seed and :counter/init handlers no longer bind db they do not read, while preserving their two-argument event-handler shape and exact returned :db maps.
- A focused clj-kondo pass reports no unused-namespace or unused-binding finding under implementation/adapters/uix/{src,test,testbed}. Do not broaden this task to unrelated unresolved-var diagnostics from standalone CLJS analysis.
- The UIx consumer dependency recipe JVM test, affected UIx browser test, and adapter-testbed smoke/compile remain green.
- No public API, dependency coordinate, initial counter value, frame behavior, or test assertion changes.

Removed [clojure.string :as str] from uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj (no str/-qualified call in the file; every bare str is clojure.core/str, which the alias never shadowed) and the unread db destructures in ::dollar-shape-seed and :counter/init, both keeping their two-arg shape and returning identical :db maps. title: docs(reagent-adapter): repair stale Reagent dependency pointer
description:
## Finding

`implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:11` says Reagent 2.0.1 is pinned in `implementation/core/deps.edn` and links to `../../core/deps.edn`. That manifest no longer contains the stock Reagent coordinate. The actual pin is `reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "2.0.1"}` at `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15`.

## Evidence

`implementation/core/deps.edn:18-25` explicitly says stock `reagent/reagent` is intentionally not a core dependency and that the Reagent adapter artifact is its sole owner. Commit `d44c4f7d20` (`fix(deps): move stock-reagent dep from core to the reagent adapter (rf2-enmvx6)`, 2026-07-11) removed the coordinate from core and added it to the adapter. `git blame` shows the README's current line was restyled later in commit `b22a0fef4c` on 2026-08-19 but retained the pre-move destination.

All-status bead searches for `reagent readme`, `dependency ownership`, `stock reagent`, `stale deps`, and description scans for `adapters/reagent/README`, `pinned.*core/deps`, and `implementation/core/deps.edn` found no current owner for this stale pointer. Historical dependency-move bead `rf2-enmvx6` is no longer present in the active bead store and its landed change did not repair this README.

## Impact

The adapter's own support-floor document directs maintainers and consumers to a manifest that proves the opposite dependency relationship. It obscures the deliberate artifact boundary, can lead audits to conclude that core still transitively installs Reagent, and leaves the stated version detached from its authoritative coordinate.

## Proposed disposition

Change the sentence to point at the adapter-owned `deps.edn` and make ownership explicit, for example: Reagent 2.x is currently pinned to 2.0.1 in this adapter's `deps.edn`. Keep the documented Reagent 2.x / React 19 floor unchanged.

## Risks

This is documentation-only, but the relative Markdown target must resolve from `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md`. Do not move the dependency or broaden compatibility as part of the repair.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` and follow the link attached to the stated Reagent 2.0.1 pin; it points to `implementation/core/deps.edn`.
2. Search that core manifest for `reagent/reagent`; the coordinate is absent and its comments state that stock Reagent is intentionally not core-owned.
3. Open `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn`; it contains `reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "2.0.1"}`, proving the README points at the wrong authority.
4. Use `git show d44c4f7d20` to verify that dependency ownership moved from core to the adapter while the README pointer was not repaired.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` links the 2.0.1 pin to `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn`, not `implementation/core/deps.edn`.
2. The wording accurately states that the adapter artifact owns the stock Reagent coordinate while core intentionally does not.
3. The documented Reagent 2.x / React 19 support floor and no-compat-shim policy are unchanged.
4. The repository documentation-link checker passes for the changed README, and a direct source check confirms the linked manifest contains the stated 2.0.1 coordinate.
close_reason: PR #9122: implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:11 now points the 2.0.1 pin at the adapter's own deps.edn and states the ownership split. Premise verified at source: core/deps.edn carries no reagent/reagent coordinate (only prose), 'clojure -Spath' from implementation/core resolves no reagent jar, and from implementation/adapters/reagent resolves reagent-2.0.1.jar whose META-INF pom reads <version>2.0.1</version> - the version was right, only the pointer was wrong. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0; a planted broken target at that same line returned exit 1 naming it.

title: xray(spec): finish retiring per-panel film-strip claims from Issues and summary prose
description:
## Finding

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/film_strip/header.cljc` is a 215-line shared panel component whose only current consumer is its dedicated unit test. Its namespace still claims every L4 panel mounts it, but spine navigation moved to the L2 Epoch list and the production callers were removed.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide exact namespace search for `day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.shared.film-strip.header` finds only the namespace definition and `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/film_strip/header_cljs_test.cljc`; no production namespace, testbed, example, build entry, public facade, or skill requires it.
- The namespace doc says it is "consumed by every L4 panel" and the dedicated test still asserts that premise. Current `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/panels-epoch.md` explicitly says "No film-strip header — the L2 events list owns spine navigation"; `trace_view_cljs_test.cljs` asserts the Trace panel has no film strip.
- Git history proves the lost-consumer path. Commit `4b4d1beb18` introduced the shared header. Commit `02aae4c239` removed Trace's require and `film-strip/header` render because the L2 list owns navigation. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel, removing another former caller. No current source caller remains.
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` and `skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md` still contain active-looking film-strip design/usage prose even though the current Epoch reference records the retirement.
- Bead title searches for `film strip header` and `film-strip`, plus description search for `film_strip/header`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The shipped bundle retains an unreachable component and a large self-test suite that proves only the orphan itself. Contradictory docs tell panel authors to reuse a component the current navigation architecture deliberately stopped mounting, increasing the chance of reviving a superseded L4 navigation model.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphaned namespace and its dedicated test. Reconcile active Xray specs/skill references so the L2 Epoch list is the single stated navigation owner; retain genuinely historical design notes only when clearly marked superseded. If a current panel is intentionally meant to restore the header, first identify and land that real consumer rather than preserving the component speculatively.

## Risks

Do not remove Epoch/L2 navigation, issue filtering, or the current panel focus events. Recheck concurrent panel work and out-of-repo published API policy before deletion, although the component is not facade-exported and no current in-repo caller exists.

- The orphan source file and dedicated self-test are removed if no consumer exists.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md is saturated at 3 bytes under the 16 KB leaf ceiling — the next addition forces a split
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md sits at 241 lines / 16,381 LF-normalised bytes against the family ceiling in skills/README.md (Leaf size discipline: each leaf SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB, i.e. 16,384 bytes). That is 3 bytes of headroom and 9 lines. Measured at tip after PR #9016.

HISTORY. PR #9006 left it at 241 lines / 16,336 bytes (48 B headroom) and its author predicted the next addition would force a split. rf2-wz1qa (PR #9016) was that next addition: its three corrections cost ~96 bytes gross, which did not fit, so two genuine restatements were trimmed to pay for them -- 'cross-reference the live catalogue rather than the skill's docs alone -- a live-catalogue check is' shortened to 'cross-reference the live catalogue -- that check is', and 'the pair-MCP conformance corpus' to 'the conformance corpus'. Both were honest de-duplications, and that seam is now spent: there is no comparable restatement left to trade.

IMPACT. The leaf is the skill's one on-demand reference and is still growing (rf2-vdqr9 is an open item against this same file, and would breach on its own). The next author either breaches the ceiling silently -- nothing gates it, wc -l -c is the only instrument -- or trims load-bearing content under time pressure.

DECISION NEEDED (not taken here, deliberately). Three options, and this is a judgement call rather than a mechanical fix:
(a) SPLIT the leaf by friction family. But SKILL.md routes to exactly one on-demand leaf and the family rule is one-level routing, so a split needs a routing decision, not just a file move.
(b) CLAIM the catalogue exemption. skills/README.md already carves one out: 'catalogue-shaped leaves (for example re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md) may exceed the ceiling if splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session.' known-frictions.md is a catalogue of friction classes and plausibly qualifies -- the stated test is 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?', and since the whole leaf loads on one trigger, a split arguably would not.
(c) TRIM content rather than structure, accepting the loss.

(b) looks strongest on the file's own shape and is much the cheapest, but it is a family-contract call the mayor/Mike should make, not a worker.

GATE. None -- the ceiling has no gate. wc -l -c before and after, plus check_doc_slugs.py if the routing changes.

Filed from PR #9016 (rf2-wz1qa + rf2-fpeig) rather than splitting on worker initiative, per the dispatch brief.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:1x AUSEST — OPTION (b), THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION, IS TAKEN. Recorded as MY call rather than Mike's so he can reverse it cheaply; the bead correctly refused to take it on worker initiative.

MEASURED AT bddc39f415 BEFORE RULING: 241 lines, 16,622 raw bytes, 16,381 LF-normalised. Ceiling at skills/README.md:239 is <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (16,384). So 3 bytes and 9 lines of headroom — the bead's figures reproduce exactly.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a) OR (c). The exemption at skills/README.md:245-248 states its own test: 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' known-frictions.md is loaded on ONE trigger — the retro's pattern-check step, SKILL.md:81 — and the whole leaf is consulted to answer 'is this a one-off or a product gap?', which is a question you answer by scanning the classes until one matches. A session cannot know in advance WHICH half holds its friction, so a split into two sibling leaves would load both on most sessions and add a file handle and a routing hop for nothing. The test therefore answers NO for this leaf, which is precisely the case the exemption exists for. (a) is refused on that reasoning, not on the routing objection the bead raises — a split into two siblings is still one level deep and would not be a SKILL->A->B chain. (c) is refused because the bead's own history shows the trim seam is spent: PR #9016 already paid for ~96 bytes by de-duplicating two genuine restatements, and there is no comparable restatement left to trade, so the next trim comes out of load-bearing content.

WHAT LANDS. skills/README.md's exemption bullet names known-frictions.md alongside re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md, with the one-trigger reasoning stated in a clause so the next reader does not re-derive it. The exemption is for THIS leaf on THIS shape; it is not a family-wide licence and no other leaf inherits it.

THE BOUND, because an exempt catalogue is not an unbounded one: each class stays at the density the existing nine already set. rf2-vdqr9's four new classes are written to that density, not longer. No second numeric ceiling is invented — per the stance, that would be litigating minutiae.

CONSEQUENCE: rf2-vdqr9 is unblocked and dispatches WITH this bead in one cluster, since its four classes are exactly the growth this ruling authorises.

That is wrong and I caught it by reading the file rather than the bead: the four classes ALREADY LANDED — known-frictions.md carries 'Dry-run versus a live write' (:119), 'Wire-boundary privacy elision and the raw-eval carve-out' (:132), 'Wire-size caps and pagination' (:145) and 'Hot-reload baseline misuse' (:156), and the 16,381-byte measurement INCLUDES them. rf2-vdqr9 was reopened by the PR #9006 audit and its live residual is much smaller: split the one Signals bullet at :124 by reason, so :rf.error/writes-disabled (the closed default-OFF gate, lifted at server launch) is separated from :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected (post-gate runtime refusals with their own epoch/drain/frame/schema remedies).

THE RULING IS UNCHANGED AND THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS IT. Splitting one bullet into two costs bytes against 3 bytes of headroom, so even this small correctness fix cannot land without the exemption — the leaf is saturated at a point where a genuine repair is blocked by structure. That is the situation the exemption is for, and it is a better argument for (b) than the one I wrote.

The density bound stands, now stated against the right work: the split bullet is written at the density the surrounding Signals bullets already set.

## CLAIM (three wrong statements + one gap, all in `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/capabilities.md`)

**(a) :76** — Time-travel table, "Restore failure surfaces":
> `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer {:op-type :error})` carries the structured tags

**(b) :38** — Core runtime visibility, "Inspect handler + interceptor chain + source coords":
> `handler-meta {kind: "event", id}` over `rf/handler-meta` (returns `:ns` / `:line` / `:file` / `:column` / `:handler-fn`)

**(c) :42** — "Show effects fired for one epoch":
> off-box each row's `:args` egresses as `:rf/redacted` by default (`:include-fx-args?` opt-in)

**(d) gap** — the Debugging-recipes table (:99-111) has "Watch all `:foo/*` events while I click around | *done*" with no route named, and no row at all for record / read-recording / watch-until, although the skill now has exactly five returned-result observation routes and this file is the capability scorecard.

## TRUTH AT TIP

**(a)** The form is the exact footgun `SKILL.md:78` and `references/ops.md:98,303` warn against: `trace-buffer` takes the **frame-id first** — an opts map as the sole arg "silently returns `[]`" — and `:op-type` is a **`:flat-only`** filter (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:523-531`: `:flat true` returns raw events; `:operation` / `:op-type` / `:since` / `:severity` are `(:flat-only)`). Correct form, already in ops.md:303: `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer :rf/default {:flat true :op-type :error})`. An agent copying capabilities.md's form gets `[]` and concludes there was no failure trace.

**(b)** `:handler-fn` is **stripped**, not returned: `preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:720-751` (`registrar-describe` — `(dissoc m :handler-fn)`, `strip-fns` over the map, augments `:handler-fn-hash`); `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs:46,250-262` repeats the dissoc server-side. `tests/runtime/registrar_describe_test.clj` pins the dissoc (`registrar-describe-dissocs-handler-fn`) and that `:handler-fn-hash` survives. The returned keys are `:ns` / `:line` / `:column` / `:file` / `:doc` / `:tags` / `:handler-fn-hash` / `:rf.mcp/source-uri` (ops.md:38).

**(c)** The arg is `include-fx-args` (no `?`): `descriptors_data.cljs:601` (`:include-fx-args {:type "boolean" …}`), `tools/args.cljs:75`, `dispatch_dry_run.cljs:66`. It is a `dispatch-dry-run` arg (and gated under `--allow-sensitive-reads`); the row reads as if it were a generic epoch-egress knob.

**(d)** `STATUS.md:17` names the five routes as the one supported live-observation workflow: dispatch consequence, `watch-epochs` / `trace-window`, `watch-until`, `record` + `read-recording`, `tail-build`. `references/ops.md:205-247` documents them. capabilities.md — whose stated purpose (:3) is "tell a prospective user honestly what the skill will and won't help with" — names none of them as a set, and the "Watch … while I click around" row (the one row a prospective user would look at after PR #8815 removed push streaming) says only *done*.

## IMPACT

(a) is a wrong command that fails silently (returns `[]`) — the class this review prioritises; it sits in a maintainer-facing scorecard rather than an agent-loaded leaf, which is why this is P3 not P2. (b)/(c) are wrong return/arg names an implementer would copy. (d) is the completeness gap the review was asked to check; it matters because the scorecard is where "what happened to streaming?" gets answered for a reader who does not open STATUS.md.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR, one file:
- :76 → `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer <frame-id> {:flat true :op-type :error})` (or simply "see ops.md §Time-travel for the read form").
- :38 → drop `:handler-fn`, add `:handler-fn-hash` (and `:doc` / `:tags` / `:rf.mcp/source-uri` if the list is meant to be complete).
- :42 → `` `include-fx-args` `` and say it is a `dispatch-dry-run` arg under `--allow-sensitive-reads`.

`bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` — `capabilities-uses-current-tool-names`, `render-key-recipe-uses-first-tuple-slot` (capabilities half) and `catalogue-count-matches-live-manifest` read this file and must stay green (do not reintroduce a retired op name or a stale count). Nothing validates the corrected forms — verify (a)–(c) by hand against the cited source lines and say so in the PR body.

title: test(ssr): multi_root_hydration fixture nests :config so its frames are never platform-tagged
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-jqvgp (PR #8915), reported by that worker as an incidental finding it deliberately did not fix.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): `rf/make-frame` opts are FLAT, but the fixture in `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc` passes `{:id fid :config {:platform :client}}`, which nests as `:config {:config {...}}`. The frames are therefore never platform-tagged at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is harmless TODAY only because CLJS defaults to `:client`, so the fixture gets the platform it meant by accident. The defect is that the assertion no longer discriminates — a JVM platform assertion added to this fixture would pass for the wrong reason, and so would a regression that broke platform tagging outright.

MINIMAL COMPLETION: flatten the opts to the shape `make-frame` actually reads, and add one assertion that the constructed frame's platform is what the fixture asked for, so the fixture cannot silently stop tagging again. Do not redesign the fixture or widen into the hydration contract.

SURFACE: test-only, `implementation/ssr/test/`. Gate: ssr JVM `clojure -M:test` plus the CLJS consolidated node-test.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-01 22:10 AUSEST — FIXED and landed in PR #8934 (draft at time of writing), commit 30055a3db5.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP. Verified at source rather than taken from the brief: make-frame's own docstring in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc is explicit that opts are FLAT — 'EVERY OTHER key is RECORD-CONFIG, honoured in the same call: :initial-events ..., :fx-overrides, :platform, :ssr, :doc, :preset, :tags ...'. The nested form was still present at tip on line 71.

WHAT CHANGED (test-only, hydration contract untouched):
  1. fresh-frame! now passes {:id fid :platform :client} instead of {:id fid :config {:platform :client}}, plus a docstring naming the trap.
  2. A new one-assertion deftest, the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged, reads the tag back through rf/frame-meta.

WHY frame-meta IS THE DISCRIMINATING ACCESSOR — this is the part worth keeping. frame-meta is (merge (:config f) (:lifecycle f) {:id (:id f)}): it flattens the frame's OWN config and performs NO platform defaulting. The RUNTIME path is different — fx/platform-for-frame-record is (or (-> rec :config :platform) (interop/active-platform)) — and that fallback to the host-wide marker is precisely why the defect was invisible: on CLJS the marker is already :client, so every hydration test passed either way. Asserting through frame-meta reads what the fixture ASKED FOR rather than what the runtime resolves, which is what makes the assertion bite.

CONTROL — THE PLANT DISCRIMINATED (this was the specified stop-and-report risk, and it did not materialise). Restoring the nested :config with the fix's assertion in place: captured exit 1, exactly ONE failure — the new test — reporting 'actual: (not (= :client nil))'. The platform read as nil, which is the 'never platform-tagged at all' claim demonstrated directly rather than argued. Test/assertion totals were identical to the clean run (608 tests / 2965 assertions at that point), so the plant crashed no namespace. Restored and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (line endings are translated in this checkout, so a byte digest of the working file is not sound); RESTORE: MATCH.

POSITIVE EVIDENCE THE CLJS RUNTIME SAW THE CHANGE, not just the source: out/node-test.js is only the 156K loader, so a zero count there means nothing. The compiled per-namespace file .shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/re_frame.ssr.multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.js contains the_fixture_frames_are_actually_platform_tagged (8 occurrences) and frame_meta (3). Confirmed independently by shadow-cljs.edn: 'ssr/test' is on the :node-test classpath and :ns-regexp is 'cljs-test$', which this namespace matches.

GATES, all on the final rebased base cdb9652c0f, exit codes captured on one command line and quoted from the captured file:
  ssr JVM clojure -M:test        exit 0   610 tests / 2991 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  CLJS node-test compile         exit 0   1874 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS node-test run             exit 0   11150 tests / 55135 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  (core exit 0 and machines exit 0 also re-run green on the same base)
The CLJS lane prints its config path and it named this worker's worktree — the worktree check for that gate.

PRECEDENT ALIGNED: machine_after_rearm_cljs_test.cljc had already been corrected the same way by rf2-jqvgp (the same PR that reported this finding) and carries the same docstring warning. This fixture now matches it.

INCIDENTAL, NOT SWEPT (a general audit was out of scope): the identical nesting is live at four more sites — failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc lines 89 and 298, failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs line 45, and multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs line 42 (the DOM sibling of this very fixture). Filed as rf2-33lfn with the fix recipe and the frame-meta rationale.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8934 (commit 30055a3db5). Premise held at tip: make-frame opts are flat and the nesting was still present. fresh-frame! now passes {:id fid :platform :client}, plus one assertion reading the tag back through rf/frame-meta, which does no platform defaulting and so discriminates where the hydration tests cannot. The control bit decisively: restoring the nesting turned that assertion red alone with 'actual: (not (= :client nil))'. ssr JVM 610/2991 exit 0; CLJS node-test 11150/55135 exit 0. Four more sites carrying the same nesting filed as rf2-33lfn.

title: core_machines.cljc emits :where (quote rf/reg-machine*) for a var that is :facade? false
description:
Surfaced by rf2-lzrza (PR #8912) while correcting source-file prose, and deliberately NOT changed there because it is an error-payload behaviour change rather than a prose fix.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc lines 137 and 139:

  (reg-machine-impl (quote rf/reg-machine*) machine-id machine)

The :where symbol names the re-frame.core facade spelling. But reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and is NOT a facade export - core.cljc line 391 says so explicitly (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl): reach it through re-frame.machines/reg-machine*. So an error raised from this path tells the programmer to look at a var that is not on the namespace the message names.

The docstring at line 146 describes this faithfully and was left intact by PR #8912 for exactly that reason - it is TRUE about what the code emits. Line 149, which was caller GUIDANCE rather than a description of behaviour, was corrected to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The sibling reg-machine (lines 157/159) emits (quote rf/reg-machine), which IS correct - that macro is a real facade export.

Decide whether the :where symbol should become rf.machines/reg-machine*. If it changes, the docstring at line 146 changes with it in the same commit.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-01 20:47 AUSEST — YES, CHANGE IT to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The :where symbol exists to tell a programmer where to look. reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and core.cljc states outright that it is not a facade export (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl), so an error raised from this path currently names a var that does not exist on the namespace the message implies. That is a worse failure than an unhelpful message: it sends the reader to a namespace, they find nothing, and the natural conclusion is that their build is broken rather than that the message is wrong. Naming the reachable spelling costs nothing and the pre-alpha posture has no back-compat claim on an error payload.

SCOPE: lines 137 and 139 of implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc, and the line 146 docstring in the SAME commit — that docstring is currently TRUE about what the code emits, which is exactly why PR #8912 left it alone, so it becomes false the moment the emission changes. Line 149 was already corrected by #8912 and needs nothing.

DO NOT TOUCH the sibling reg-machine at lines 157/159: it emits (quote rf/reg-machine) and that IS correct, because reg-machine is a real facade export. Changing it would introduce the defect this bead is closing.

CHECK FOR TEST PINS before editing: any test asserting the error payload's :where will pin the old symbol and must move in the same commit. Search for the literal both line-oriented and flattened.

NOT WANTED: a general audit of every :where symbol in the tree, a lint rule tying :where symbols to the facade manifest, or any change to the error's shape.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 22:11 AUSEST — RULING IMPLEMENTED as written. PR #8934 (draft at time of writing), commit 3c8541797b.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP, verified at source: spec/api-manifest.edn carries {:namespace "re-frame.machines", :var "reg-machine*", :tier :advanced, :kind :fn, :owner "005", :status "v1", :facade? false, ...}, and the sibling is {:namespace "re-frame.core", :var "reg-machine", :kind :macro, ..., :facade? true, ...}. So the ruling's two halves are both grounded: reg-machine* is not reachable as rf/reg-machine*, and reg-machine genuinely is rf/reg-machine.

LINE NUMBERS RE-DERIVED AT TIP rather than trusted (PR #8912 had moved lines in this file): emissions at 137 and 139, docstring at 144-146, sibling at 157/159 — all five matched the ruling exactly. After the edit the docstring block grows from 3 lines to 5, so the UNTOUCHED sibling now sits at 159/161. Line 149 was already rf.machines/reg-machine* from #8912 and needed nothing, as the ruling said.

WHAT CHANGED: lines 137/139 now emit 'rf.machines/reg-machine*, and the 144-146 docstring moved with them in the SAME commit — it had described the old emission truthfully, which is why #8912 left it alone, so it would have gone false the instant the emission changed. The sibling reg-machine at 159/161 still emits 'rf/reg-machine, untouched.

TEST PINS: NONE existed, so nothing had to move. Searched for the literal both ways as instructed. Line-oriented found 3 sites, whitespace-flattened found 4 — the discrepancy is line 146 carrying two occurrences, reconciled by counting occurrences per line rather than counting lines, not a line-broken pin. The control term 'rf/reg-machine' returned 1440 line hits / 1443 flattened, so the search was live rather than silently matching nothing. All hits were in core_machines.cljc itself; no test anywhere pins this symbol. The two :where pins that DO exist are on the sibling — machines/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:75-76 and machine_pure_error_contract_test.clj:389 — and late_bind_missing_test.clj:24 states in prose that it covers reg-machine only.

CONTROLS — TWO, because the specified one cannot bite, and the reason is itself the finding. Reverting the symbol on line 137 and re-running the machines suite came back GREEN (captured exit 0, 1220 tests / 4289 assertions, 0 failures). That is not a broken control: it is the measured explanation for how this defect survived, and it agrees exactly with the pin search above.

Because a green run proves nothing about WHICH TREE the gate read, a second and COVERED fault was planted at a line adjacent to the edit — the sibling's 'rf/reg-machine replaced with 'rf/BOGUS-SENTINEL-UUQEK. The machines gate went red naming it: captured exit 1, exactly 1 failure, 'actual: (not (= rf/reg-machine rf/BOGUS-SENTINEL-UUQEK))', totals otherwise unchanged. The sentinel existed only in this worktree, so a run that had strayed into another checkout would have come back green. That establishes the gate read the right tree AND that this file's :where mechanism is genuinely under test — which is the direct evidence for the ruling's DO-NOT-TOUCH constraint on the sibling.

Both plants restored and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (line endings are translated here, so a byte digest of the working file is not sound). Each plant's anchor match count was read as exactly 1 BEFORE the gate was spent.

GATES, all on the final rebased base cdb9652c0f, exit captured on one command line:
  core JVM clojure -M:test       exit 0   2174 tests / 11130 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  machines JVM clojure -M:test   exit 0   1220 tests / 4289 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  ssr JVM clojure -M:test        exit 0   610 tests / 2991 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  CLJS node-test compile / run   exit 0   1874 files, 0 warnings / 11150 tests / 55135 assertions

NOT WANTED, and not done: no general :where audit, no lint rule tying :where symbols to the facade manifest, no change to the error's shape, no edit to spec/api-manifest.edn, spec/API.md or spec/005-StateMachines.md (all read-only here, hot-zone).

OPERATIONAL NOTE for whoever times this locally: the core JVM suite takes ~8m50s, which sits just under a 10-minute harness ceiling. Three runs were killed at that ceiling while a peer shadow-cljs compile competed for the machine, each leaving a ZERO-BYTE log and no exit file. Those were treated as NO VERDICT rather than as passes, and the gate was re-run to completion.
close_reason: Mayor ruling implemented as written in PR #8934 (commit 3c8541797b). Lines 137/139 now emit 'rf.machines/reg-machine*, and the 144-146 docstring moved in the same commit; sibling reg-machine untouched (now at 159/161 after the docstring grew two lines). Line numbers re-derived at tip and all matched. No test pinned the old symbol — searched line-oriented and flattened, with a live control term. Two controls: reverting the symbol is GREEN, which is the measured reason the defect survived; a covered sentinel planted at the adjacent sibling line went red naming it, proving the gate read this worktree and that the sibling's :where is genuinely pinned. core 2174/11130, machines 1220/4289, ssr 610/2991, CLJS 11150/55135 — all exit 0.

title: spec(Conventions): roster :rf/settle-flows in the reserved :rf/* row
description:
rf2-kh73v added a second member to `re-frame.events/reserved-event-ids`: `:rf/settle-flows`, the framework-private flow-settle event the `:fx` walk enqueues after `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` (Spec 013 §Sequencing — settling on the dispatching frame).

spec/Conventions.md line ~46 is the normative reserved-namespace roster and its `:rf/*` row names the framework-wide pattern events individually, including `:rf/set-db` at length. `:rf/settle-flows` is not there.

Deliberately NOT taken by rf2-kh73v: spec/Conventions.md is a hot-zone one-toucher and is outside that item's enumerated scope (which named Spec 013, the API/core guides and the cart example). Filed rather than smuggled in.

Note the entry is not simply another `:rf/set-db`. `:rf/settle-flows` is reserved but NEVER REGISTERED — not in the registrar, not in the EP-0023 image standard registry. It resolves through the router's unresolved-handler seam (`router/framework-private-handler-metas`), which is what keeps it off `registrar/registrations :event` and therefore out of every app's event catalogue. It is listed in `reserved-event-ids` for a different reason than `:rf/set-db` is: the registrar is consulted BEFORE the seam, so an app `(reg-event :rf/settle-flows …)` would silently shadow the framework's settle and strand every flow-lifecycle effect. The roster entry should say that, not imply a second registered standard.

Applications must not depend on the id; the observable contract is the settle boundary, not the transport. Spec 013 §Sequencing states this already — Conventions just needs the roster row to agree.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-01 AUSEST (worker, PR #8902). PREMISE HELD, TAKEN.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not assumed. :rf/settle-flows exists at tip in
implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc (the reserved-event-ids value, the
settle-flows-event-id def, the handler and its handler-meta), fx.cljc:842 and
router.cljc:493. A fixed-string census of the id across ALL tracked markdown
returned ZERO hits, so Conventions did not merely omit it from one row - the id
appeared nowhere in the doc corpus. The census instrument was controlled: the
same flattened, whitespace-insensitive search returned 53 files for
rf/reg-machine, so the zero is a real zero and not a bad pattern.

THIS WAS A DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCE, not a cosmetic omission - which the item
did not know and which raises its value. spec/013-Flows.md:474 deliberately
does NOT name the private id, and instead says its "id is nonetheless reserved
(per Conventions Reserved namespaces) so an application registration cannot
shadow it". Spec 013 was delegating the reservation to a roster that was
silent, so at tip NO normative document recorded that the id is reserved.

THE ROSTER ENTRY DOES NOT IMPLY A SECOND REGISTERED STANDARD, per the item's
explicit instruction. It states the distinction: unlike :rf/set-db it is
reserved but NEVER registered - no registrar row, no EP-0023 image-standard row
- because it is materialised through the router's unresolved-handler seam, so
it never reaches an application's event catalogue, tooling projection or
generated code. It is reserved for a DIFFERENT reason: the registrar is
consulted BEFORE that seam, so an app reg-event on the id would silently shadow
the settle and strand every flow-lifecycle effect, and fails loud instead. The
row also carries Spec 013's own caution that applications must not depend on
the id, the observable contract being the settle boundary and not the
transport. Spec column gains 013.

The row already had vocabulary for this case - :rf/head and :rf/public-error
are described in it as "reserved-but-not-registered" - so the entry mirrors an
existing shape rather than inventing one.

ONE THING CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. Conventions rule 3 in the same
section reserves the bare :rf/* root for framework-wide pattern events that no
single AREA owns, and a reader could ask whether a flow-settle event should
have been :rf.flow/settle. It is defensible as-is: the event is defined,
enqueued and resolved entirely in core (events.cljc, fx.cljc, router.cljc), not
in the flows artefact, so it is core-owned like :rf/set-db rather than
area-owned. Recording the question rather than reopening a shipped id.

GATES. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, captured exit 0 on the final base after
rebasing onto b3c7a705db (redirect and echo on one command line; number quoted
from the .exit file). spec/ is inside that gate's DEFAULT_ROOTS, read at source
rather than taken on trust. check_readme_links.py --ci also 0, but it does NOT
cover this path - its DOCS_GATE_ROOTS excludes spec outright.

CONTROL, because the gate is silent on success and a green would otherwise be
unfalsifiable. A broken anchor planted at the line this change edits took the
gate to exit 1 naming spec\Conventions.md:46 and the planted token. The fault
existed only in this worktree, so a run that had read a sibling checkout would
have come back green - the red IS the discrimination. Restore verified by git
BLOB hash 1996b95f8b2a0b36ddafa6110c62804910ab70ed against the committed
object, not by reading a diff.

NOT COVERED BY ANY GATE, checked by hand and stated rather than implied. The
edit is a MARKDOWN TABLE ROW and nothing anywhere validates tables: column
count re-counted by hand at 3 across header, delimiter and the edited row,
unchanged, with no stray pipe introduced by the inserted prose. The new link
was not slug-derived - the anchor form matches the two links spec/013-Flows.md
already makes to the same heading. Prose and rendering are validated by
nothing.

FILED, not taken (both outside this item's fence):
  rf2-jgsl9 (P4) - events.cljc's comment block still says the reserved set is
    "today only :rf/set-db", five lines above the docstring that correctly
    lists two. rf2-kh73v updated the docstring and not the comment.
  rf2-wrzfb (P2) - discovered via the sibling item; unrelated to this one.
close_reason: Taken in PR #8902 (branch worker/docroster-z529y, based on b3c7a705db). Premise HELD, verified at source: :rf/settle-flows exists at tip in events.cljc / fx.cljc / router.cljc, and a controlled fixed-string census found the id in ZERO tracked markdown files, so no normative document recorded its reservation. That made it a dangling cross-reference rather than a cosmetic gap - spec/013-Flows.md:474 deliberately does not name the private id and delegates the reservation to Conventions Reserved namespaces, which was silent. The :rf/* roster row now names it and states the distinction the item required: reserved but NEVER registered (no registrar row, no EP-0023 image-standard row, materialised through the router unresolved-handler seam), reserved for a different reason than :rf/set-db (the registrar is consulted before the seam, so an app reg-event would silently shadow the settle and strand every flow-lifecycle effect), and applications must not depend on the id because the observable contract is the settle boundary rather than the transport. Spec column gains 013. Gate check_doc_slugs.py captured exit 0 on the final base; control was a planted broken anchor at the edited line taking it to exit 1 naming spec\Conventions.md:46, with restore verified by git blob hash. Table column count re-counted by hand (3, unchanged) since nothing validates tables. Residue filed: rf2-jgsl9 (stale events.cljc comment). Full verdict in the appended note.

title: spec/Pattern-WebSocket worked-example listing still teaches the :ws/fatal in-flight leak
description:
rf2-ni0ko composed fail-in-flight onto the :ws/fatal transition in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, so every door out of :active reachable from :connected now settles :in-flight exactly once.

spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md's worked-example listing was NOT updated (hot-zone, outside that bead's fence) and still shows the unrepaired shape:

  :ws/fatal    {:target :failed
                :action :record-error}

That is precisely the shape rf2-ni0ko's witness proves strands every in-flight slot and its waiting :reply-event, including across a later manual :ws/connect out of :failed. A consumer copying the spec's recommended listing inherits the leak.

Nothing in the spec is FALSE today — its stated invariant (§5 item 5, and the 'Leaking in-flight requests when the socket drops' pitfall) is scoped to the DROP door, not to every door out of :active — so this is teaching-drift, not a contradiction. Two other pre-existing divergences in the same listing are worth folding in while there: it carries no :ws/disconnect transition at all (rf2-b2jpr added one with :action :fail-in-flight), and it still shows :on-socket-lost with the fail-and-clear INLINED rather than routed through the fail-in-flight helper rf2-b2jpr factored out.

Also skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md line ~114 shows ':ws/fatal {:target :failed}' with no action at all, and its parent-level :on summary row omits :ws/disconnect.

Suggested shape: update the listing's :ws/fatal row to the composed action, add the :ws/disconnect row, and show :on-socket-lost delegating to the shared helper — plus a sentence generalising the invariant from 'when the socket drops' to 'every door out of :active that destroys the socket'. spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md is HOT-ZONE: sequence, don't parallel.
notes: FENCED 2026-09-01 15:32 AUSEST by the mayor: sequenced behind PR #8872 (rf2-ni0ko) MERGING. This item corrects a worked-example listing that teaches the :ws/fatal in-flight leak; #8872 is the change that FIXES that leak, so the doc must describe the repaired behaviour and cannot be written accurately before it lands. spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md is also hot-zone one-toucher. CAUTION for whoever picks this up: #8872 is currently a DRAFT whose author has been unresponsive for over two hours (see rf2-m7sto), so this fence may be held by a change that is not progressing — re-check #8872's state rather than assuming it is merely in flight.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8907 (worker/textfix-3). FENCE RELEASED, confirmed at source: PR #8872 (rf2-ni0ko) is MERGED, mergedAt 2026-09-01T08:01:11Z, and its commit is on origin/main -- so the caution note about an unresponsive draft author no longer applies. Treated as TEACHING-DRIFT, not a contradiction, exactly as the bead frames it: the page's stated invariant was drop-scoped (section 5 item 5 and the socket-drops pitfall) and the listing agreed with it, so nothing was false. The correction brings the listing level with the shipped example and generalises the teaching to every door out of :active -- which is what the example now implements and what the page's own :spawn bullet already implied (any transition that exits :active destroys the actor), so no normative claim was invented beyond what the pattern already asserts. LANDED in spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md: one fail-in-flight helper factored out as the example does, composed by :on-socket-lost (also bumps retries), :fail-in-flight (clean :ws/disconnect) and the new :on-fatal-error (also records the error); the :ws/disconnect row the listing never carried, at the :active parent level where the in-flight obligation lives, plus a line in the standard-transitions block; a note saying why :ws/auth-failed correctly keeps plain :record-error, since :register-request is bound only on :connected so :in-flight is provably empty by the time that door can be taken; and :origin :ws/local in the minted failure body, which section 5 and the two-producers paragraph already stated but the listing omitted. skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md got the same treatment at its own level of abbreviation -- it showed :ws/fatal with no action at all and omitted :ws/disconnect from the parent-level :on summary row -- plus one anti-pattern for the door-by-door version of the bug. DELIBERATELY OUT: the shipped example also carries :ws/disconnect on :reconnecting and :failed; those doors carry no in-flight obligation because :in-flight was settled on leaving :active, so neither listing gains them. MACHINE-SPELLING CARVE-OUT HONOURED: the file contains exactly one line matching rf/make-machine-handler and zero matching rf/machine-, and that line is untouched (rf2-wrzfb holds those). GATES: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, proven by plant to read this worktree -- four faults planted in PROSE across both pages returned exit 1 naming each by file and line, then restored and verified against the pre-plant git blob hashes 5830a4a864779e5e26f1ec25367b92b78cfa9a12 and d8cfa28c9293fb2e7798f7eee6ca94077b9c6955. check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: neither doc gate reads inside fenced code blocks and the ENTIRE listing correction lives inside one, so their green says nothing about the content of this change. Structure was hand-checked instead: paren/bracket/brace balance of every clojure fence in both pages, balanced before and after; table column counts uniform at 2; and no heading, anchor or link target added, moved or removed.

title: RULING: refusal contract shape - drop the :recovery keyword, :where, and the runtime meta-refusal
description:
impl/error.cljc is 356 lines (~60 code). Every refusal carries id + :where (emitting fn) + :reason + :recovery keyword + coords, and check-complete! mints :rf.error/hicasso-refusal-incomplete at RUNTIME (error.cljc:265) to police the package own call sites. :recovery is a keyword such as :declare-render-or-client-only-with-an-optional-fallback - spelled once, typed by nobody, tracking API renames (complaints.md:236-295 spend 60 lines ruling on when it moves; naming-ledger row 21 shows one option rename moved three recovery keywords across runtime + witnesses + Spec 009 rows). :where duplicates the stack trace. The valuable half - :view and :source from the macro-captured ledger - is ~30 lines.

RECOMMENDATION: (fail! id message extra) with the ambient :view/:source stamp; drop :recovery keyword and :where; delete the meta-refusal (a missing message is a code-review matter, not a runtime law). The message text still names the fix. Effort: ~2 hours + mechanical test edits (error_shape_cljs_test pins the shape). Counter-argument to weigh: a machine-readable recovery keyword could help an AI pair - but the reason string already carries the same words.
notes:

title: xray: render-panel! seats the DEFAULT frame but provides opts :frame — latent, no shipped caller overrides it
description:
LATENT, NOT LIVE — READ THE CONSEQUENCE SECTION BEFORE PRIORITISING THIS.

`render-panel!` seats one frame and provides a different one whenever a caller overrides `:frame`.

=== THE MECHANISM, MAYOR-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, trunk c35679191c ===

  panels.cljs:217   ([] (ensure-xray-handlers-installed! shell/default-frame-id))
  panels.cljs:~218  ([frame-id] ... (mount/ensure-xray-frame! frame-id))
  panels.cljs:256   (ensure-xray-handlers-installed!)          <- render-panel!, ZERO arity
  panels.cljs:~257  (let [frame (get opts :frame :rf/xray)
                          tree  [rf/frame-provider {:frame frame} ...
  panels.cljs:489   (ensure-xray-handlers-installed! frame-id)  <- mount-shell!, ONE arity

So `render-panel!` — the shared helper every `mount-<panel>!` delegates to — ALWAYS seats and
seeds `shell/default-frame-id`, then wraps the view in a frame-provider anchored at whatever
`opts :frame` says. On the default path those agree. On an override they do not, and descendants
anchor at a frame that was never seated or seeded — the same empty-frame class rf2-xhy9's step-2
repair warns about, reached through a different door. `mount-shell!` does not have this shape.

=== THE CONSEQUENCE DOES NOT CURRENTLY OBTAIN, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS P4 ===

The falsifying question is whether anything actually overrides `:frame` on a per-panel mount.
Measured across `tools`, `examples`, `testbeds`, `implementation`, `docs` and `spec`:

  EXACTLY ONE call site, and it is a TEST —
      tools/xray/test/.../panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs:355
          (panels/mount-epoch-panel! :mount-point {:frame :my-app/cart})

  ZERO shipped hosts, examples or testbeds. Control: the same pattern finds four `mount-shell!`
  callers that DO pass `:frame`, so the search is live and the zero is absence rather than a
  broken instrument.

And `tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md:113` documents `:frame` as a `mount-shell!` opt,
adding "in practice the default is what every shipped host uses."

**So no user is hitting this.** Do not raise the priority on the strength of the mechanism alone.

=== WHAT A FIX WOULD BE, AND THE PRIOR QUESTION ===

Mechanically trivial: pass the resolved frame into the installer — `(ensure-xray-handlers-installed!
(get opts :frame shell/default-frame-id))` — so the seated frame and the provided frame are the same
one by construction.

But the PRIOR question is whether the per-panel `:frame` override is a supported affordance at all.
`render-panel!`'s own docstring advertises it; the embedding contract describes it as a
`mount-shell!` opt. **If it is supported, the fix above is right. If it is not, the honest repair is
to stop advertising it in `render-panel!`'s docstring** — and that is a smaller change with less
surface. Decide that first; do not implement both readings.

There is also an undocumented ordering dependency either way: the plausible intended flow is a host
calling `mount-shell!` with `{:frame :my/x}` FIRST, seating that frame, then mounting panels with
the same `:frame`. If that is the design, it is written down on neither side.

=== PROVENANCE ===

Reported by the rf2-xhy9 worker (mountstep-a) while repairing the spec's step 2, explicitly
labelled LOW CONFIDENCE and correctly NOT acted on — it is code, and several workers were live in
`tools/xray/src`. The mechanism check and the consequence check above are the mayor's, run before
filing precisely because a sibling bead (rf2-wvch) was filed earlier today on a confirmed mechanism
whose consequence turned out not to obtain.
notes:
WORKER panelfix-a — PR #9638 (worker/panelfix-a). Bead left CLAIMED for the mayor to close on merge.

CENSUS RE-DERIVED, and it reproduces the bead exactly. Two axes over `tools`, `examples`,
`testbeds`, `implementation`, `docs`, `spec`: a single-line pattern, and a multiline
`mount-<panel>!(.|\n){0,200}?:frame` window so a `:frame` on a continuation line could not
hide. Per-panel callers passing `:frame` = 1, the test at panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs:355.
Shipped hosts / examples / testbeds = 0. Control: `mount-shell!` callers passing `:frame` = 4,
so the instrument is live. The multiline sweep surfaced one extra file the single-line one
did not — `panels/app_db_diff_mount_instance_id_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — and it passes
`:instance-id` only; its `:frame` hit is an `rf/dispatch` opts map, not a mount opt. Story's
`ui/xray_embed.cljs`, the only shipped consumer, calls `(mount-fn container)` at the 1-arity.

THE PRIOR QUESTION IS SETTLED BY THE SPEC, NOT THE DOCSTRING, so option A (seat the resolved
frame) is right and option B (stop advertising `:frame`) is wrong. `007-UX-IA.md` §Mountable
panel contract publishes the opts vocabulary as "`:frame` on every mount fn, defaulting to
`:rf/xray`, and `:instance-id` on `mount-app-db-diff!` alone". `008-Embedding-Contract.md`
§Frame-provider wraps the shell says every mount fn — the master AND every per-panel one —
opens an internal frame-provider whose frame carries the descendants' app-db, subs, dispatches
and machines; its `mount-shell!` paragraph adds that the requested own frame "is seated on the
way through — the host is not asked to pre-create it". So the spec was already right and NO
SPEC EDIT WAS MADE.

WHAT WAS WRONG BESIDES THE CALL: `render-panel!`'s docstring claimed "the panel facade always
opens with its own `frame-provider :rf/xray` when its body subscribes to `:rf.xray/*` data".
That is FALSE, and it is the reasoning that made seating a different frame look harmless. A
sweep of `frame-provider` across `tools/xray/src` finds exactly four constructed providers —
this one, `shell.cljs:2721` (`shell-view`), and `mount.cljs:397` / `:1697` — and none of them
is inside a panel view. Every panel's own docstring says its isolation comes from the
ENCLOSING provider. Docstring corrected in the same commit.

The default also now reads `shell/default-frame-id` rather than a second bare `:rf/xray`
literal — same value, and it keeps `defaults/default-frame-id` the single permitted bare
literal per 008 §Parameterized shell frame-id.

HOLLOW-GATE CHECK, and WHICH WAY IT WENT RED. The existing suite stubs
`rf.substrate.adapter/render`, so anything read off the captured tree observes the WRAPPER,
which was correct before the fix. The new deftest therefore reads the frame REGISTRY and a
`:rf.xray/*` subscribe inside the overridden frame instead — the rf2-lffg assertion shape.
Installer reverted to its zero arity with the test kept: line 389
`(some? (rf.frame/frame panel-cell-frame))` read `(not (some? nil))` — the override frame was
never seated — and line 395 `(some? (read-in-frame panel-cell-frame [:rf.xray/selected-tab]))`
read the same — the seed hooks never ran in it. Restored: 0 failures. The third row
(provided == seated) passed BOTH ways and is labelled in the file as a control, not a signal.

GATES, each runner's own exit status read directly: `npm run test:cljs` exit 0 (11620 tests /
58248 assertions / 0 failures); `tools/xray` `clojure -M:test` exit 0 (1276 / 6118 / 0);
`npm run test:xray-feature-gate:smoke` exit 0 (5 scenarios, 10 matrix rows, compiled
`:testbeds/panel-gallery`); `npm run test:examples-compile` exit 0 (all 58 builds, zero
warnings).

INSTRUMENT NOTE FOR THE NEXT READER OF THE SURFACE CLASSIFIER:
`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` takes paths as ARGUMENTS, not on stdin. Piping
them in is not an error — the script silently falls back to `HEAD^` and classifies the
PREVIOUS COMMIT's diff, returning a well-formed and entirely plausible surface list for the
wrong tree. Caught here because `story_xray_browser=false` contradicted
`is_story_xray_runtime_path`, which plainly returns 0 for `tools/xray/src/**.cljs`. Passed as
arguments the same three paths arm cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, examples_compile, tools_jvm,
mcp_conformance and story_xray_browser.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged as PR #9638, rebased onto main at 1f1125d99c.
