title: Incomplete: Static Sim timer-list claim omits action-only :after transitions
description:
Merged-PR audit #10130, d478fc34245f9275afaed0a51dc893081a4fa1c3, source rf2-pzuqw. The claim to list each active-path :after timer is incomplete: new after-rows-at in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc:203-217 filters candidates with :when (some? t), so legal targetless/action-only timers never become rows. A machine with only these timers presents an empty timer list and cannot fire them through the new rail control.

Measured against the exact merged core/machines/Xray helper sources in an isolated JVM probe, using public re-frame.machines/machine-transition, production build-initial-snapshot and step-sim. Flat fixture {:initial :loading :data {:n 0} :actions {:bump (fn [{:keys [data]}] {:data (update data :n inc)})} with :states {:loading {:after {5000 {:action :bump}}} :done {}}: available-after-transitions returns [], yet [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 0 [:loading]] keeps :loading, increments n to 1 and appends one audit row. Adding :target :done is the positive control: one listed row, state :done, n 1. Parallel-root :after {5000 {:action :bump}} likewise returns no rows while the event with decl-path [] increments n and leaves the region state unchanged. Probe exit 0; exact SHA and worker root recorded in ai/gate-audit-timer-audit-sep20-monitor-1.log. This establishes a listing omission, not an engine defect.

Spec 005 gives :after the normal transition shape and explicitly permits targetless/action-only parallel-root candidates. Preserve those candidates in timer discovery and render an understandable action-only row that invokes the existing sim-step/timer event path. Keep the fix in Xray; no new clock, registration, engine behavior or machines-viz change is needed. Existing open rf2-ky034 is specifically the older parallel :on picker defect and is not this correction.
acceptance_criteria: A flat action-only :after timer appears and can be fired through the Static Sim rail, updating data/effects and recording the real step while retaining state. Cover a targetless parallel-root timer with decl-path [] and retain an ordinary targeted-timer control. The row must not require or invent a target. Existing epoch/stale/guard behavior and hermetic simulation remain intact.
notes:
---

## MAYOR 2026-09-21 — THIS DEFECT HAS AN EXACT SIBLING ONE FUNCTION UP, AND THE `rf2-ky034` WORKER LEFT IT DELIBERATELY

The worker on `rf2-ky034` was fenced off this item and told so explicitly. It reported back that it
met the same filter on the OTHER side while designing its fix, and left it alone on purpose:

> My `on-rows-at` carries `:when (some? t)` **verbatim** from the pre-existing
> `available-transitions` body — I introduced no filtering and relaxed none; the only additions to
> each row are `:decl-path`. So **rf2-kmr2i has an exact sibling one function up**, and whoever
> fixes `after-rows-at` should decide consciously whether `on-rows-at` moves with it. A targetless
> action-only `:on` is equally legal and equally unlisted today. Flagging, not acting.

**So the question this item must answer is wider than its title.** `after-rows-at` drops targetless
action-only `:after` candidates; `on-rows-at` drops targetless action-only `:on` candidates, by the
same `:when (some? t)` clause, and that clause predates both — it came from the original
`available-transitions` body.

**Decide the pair together, or decide explicitly to split them and say why.** Fixing one and leaving
the other produces a rail where an action-only timer lists and an action-only transition does not,
which is harder to explain than either current state.

It also confirms the worker did not widen its fence: `after-rows-at` is **byte-identical** between
its merge base and its HEAD, 16 lines each, `diff` clean, and the only mention of that name in its
diff is a docstring cross-reference from the new `on-rows-at`.

**`rf2-ky034`'s change is OPEN, not merged, as this note is written** — PR #10133, ready for review
and still settling its checks. **So this item's SURFACE fence has not released**: it releases on
MERGE, not on the worker's report, and a second worker branched off today's trunk would not carry
#10133's diff, so the two would collide exactly where the fence exists to prevent it. **Do not
dispatch this item until #10133 merges.**

When it does, re-derive every line number here at tip before acting: `sim_helpers.cljc` has moved
twice today already (454 → 598 under `rf2-pzuqw`, and +105/−30 under `rf2-ky034`), and `on-rows-at`
is a function #10133 introduces.


---

## WORKER 2026-09-21 — FIXED, PAIR MOVED TOGETHER. PR #10138 (draft at time of writing).

**The pair moves together, and `rf2-4cm3k` is the same clause.** `after-rows-at` and
`on-rows-at` each carried `:when (some? t)`, both inherited verbatim from the original
`available-transitions` body. Both are relaxed; both row builders now emit every candidate the
normaliser yields.

**Before and after, BY RUN** — isolated JVM probe, real engine (`machine-transition`,
`build-initial-snapshot`) and real helpers, at merge base `a4e90ebaee` and again at branch HEAD.

- `:after`, the audit's own fixture `{:loading {:after {5000 {:action :bump}}}}`:
  `available-after-transitions` returned `[]` BEFORE, while
  `[:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 5000 0 [:loading]]` returned `:ok`, took `:n` 0 to 1, left
  the state `:loading`, and `step-sim` appended one audit row. AFTER: one row,
  `:target nil`, `:action :bump`, `:decl-path [:loading]`, same fire result.
- `:on`, rf2-4cm3k's parallel fixture (`:work` leaf declaring `{:ping {:action :bump}}`):
  `available-transitions` returned `[]` BEFORE, while `[:ping]` returned `:ok` with the
  configuration unchanged and `:n` 0 to 1. AFTER: one row at `:decl-path [:work :idle]`.
- Parallel ROOT targetless `:after` at `:decl-path []` reads the same way, both halves.
- Positive control on every case: the same fixture WITH a `:target` listed before the change and
  still does.

So this was a listing omission throughout and the engine was never at fault — nothing under
`implementation/machines/` is touched.

**THE THREE DESIGN CALLS.**

1. **Pair, not split.** Three independent findings reached the one clause: the `rf2-ky034`
   worker flagged it, the audit filed this item against the `:after` half, and `rf2-4cm3k`
   measured the `:on` half cold. Splitting would ship a rail where an action-only timer lists
   and an action-only transition does not. Spec 005 makes the `:on` half if anything MORE
   first-class: targetless is the only geometry the runtime flags `internal?`
   (§Self-transitions), and both the forbidden-transition idiom (§Parent fallthrough) and the
   region-override suppression are spelled exactly that way.

2. **An action-only row renders as `↻ internal :bump`** where a targeted row reads `→ :done`.
   No fabricated target. `internal` is Spec 005's own word for the geometry; the action is
   named because the action is the whole of what such a transition does. A candidate with
   neither target nor action is the forbidden-transition idiom and reads as the bare
   `↻ internal`. The formatter is a new pure `format-destination` in `sim_helpers.cljc`, shared
   by both row kinds so they cannot answer that question differently, and JVM-testable so what
   the rail says is pinned by unit test rather than only in a browser.

3. **The row stays fireable and needed NO change to become so.** An `:on` row fires by its
   event id; an `:after` row from its `:delay-key` and `:decl-path`. Neither firing path ever
   read `:target`. Firing a pure event-consumer comes back as the EXISTING amber "No change" —
   the same answer a guard-declined timer already gets, and the honest one.

**Gates**, captured exit codes, merge base then branch: node lane `npm run test:cljs`
12397/62219 then 12407/62289 at 0 warnings, exit 0; `clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`
1369/6692 then 1379/6762, exit 0. Delta +10 tests / +70 assertions on both lanes, matching the
prediction made from the diff before either run. clj-kondo plain form (NOT `--fail-level
error`) on `tools/xray`: errors 0, warnings 134 at base and 134 on the branch. Controls: a
broken assertion took the node lane to exit 1 naming the deftest at identical counts; a planted
unresolved symbol moved kondo 134 to 135, while `--fail-level error` exited 0 on that same
broken tree.

**Not closing, deliberately, though `docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md` permits it.** That
page allows a worker to close its own item after opening the change (line 50), and this item
says nothing to the contrary — but the same page also says to close only after merge or
verifiable completion (line 20), CI has not settled, and this is a bead filed BY the merged-PR
audit harness, which is exactly the class most likely to be reopened. A reopen ERASES
`close_reason` silently, so the reasoning is recorded HERE in notes, where a reopen cannot
reach it, rather than in a close reason that might not survive. Leaving the close to the mayor
on merge.

**One correction to the dispatch brief.** Its stated `tools/xray` JVM figure of 1362 / 6670 is
not the reading at merge base `a4e90ebaee`; measured there it is **1369 / 6692**. The brief's
number is 7 tests / 22 assertions low, most likely taken before `rf2-ky034` merged. Everything
else in the brief re-derived correctly except `on-rows-at`'s stated range.
Merged-PR audit #10138 (949e0245da76243a84b5dad4c0df6d82b406c829; merged 2026-09-21T01:45:17Z). Completeness: Both source defects are addressed together: targetless candidates now list in :on and :after discovery with nil targets and their actions retained. Merged regression cases cover flat and parallel leaf events, flat and parallel-root timers at [], targeted controls, an event consumer, mixed candidates, and understandable shared labels. Existing leaf-only :on and active-path :after policies remain intact. Correctness: Independently ran the exact merged Sim helper test namespace against extracted core/machines sources: 72 tests, 263 assertions, zero failures/errors, captured exit 0, verified worker root and merge SHA. Archive CRLF conversion was identified and the two reviewed namespaces restored byte-for-byte from Git before execution. Inspected both actual row renderers: event clicks set pending input, timer clicks build the existing elapsed event, and neither needs a target. The row-index addition distinguishes same-event candidate siblings. GitHub checks: 35 success, 53 skipped. Browser rendering and full CLJS suite were not independently rerun in this audit. Implementation quality: Small Xray-only correction: remove the two target-presence filters, retain action metadata, share one pure destination formatter, and add a row index to existing fragment keys. No engine change, new clock, registration, public API or duplicate stepping mechanism. No actionable finding after independent completeness, correctness and implementation-quality passes. ## Correctness review — slice fresco (rf2-3x7nj.7), 2026-09-23

### Tree
Frozen tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`, HEAD `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914` (verified with `git rev-parse HEAD`). No edits, no git writes, no shadow-cljs, no npm, no browser, no subagents.

### Scope read
- PRIMARY, in full: every file under `implementation/fresco/src/` — 27 files, 10,724 lines (`wc -l` total): `fresco.cljc` 831; `impl/codec.cljs` 2054, `impl/collector.cljs` 1333, `impl/intent.cljs` 626, `impl/mount.cljs` 621, `impl/overlay.cljs` 572, `impl/boundary.cljs` 387, `impl/controlled.cljs` 379, `impl/presence.cljs` 320, `impl/state.cljc` 255, `impl/route_link.cljs` 247, `impl/presence_react.cljs` 202, `impl/error.cljc` 173, `impl/frames.cljs` 169, `impl/roots.cljs` 130, `impl/frame_boundary.cljs` 111, `impl/generation.cljs` 81, `impl/slot.cljc` 74, `impl/portal.cljs` 62; `server.cljs` 546, `tool.cljs` 615, `overlay.cljs` 240, `forms.cljs` 232, `substrate.cljs` 181, `motion.cljs` 101, `evidence.cljs` 100, `native.cljc` 82.
- SUPPORTING, targeted: `docs/core/fresco/` 01-05, 13, 18 and `api-reference.md` (root/frame/controlled/forms/overlay sections); `docs/design/fresco/decisions.md` HD-027; tests `controlled_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (300-561), `revision_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (360-420), `overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (490-616, 1101-1115), `reincarnation_readset_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (1-50, 210-320), `foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (180-210), plus rg sweeps over the test tree; core `views/frame_boundary.cljs` (200-420), `adapter/context.cljs` (context classification), `registrar.cljc` (replacement and missing-doc paths), `subs.cljc` `subscribe`; routing `link.cljc` `activate-link!`; scripts `check_source_coord_elision.cjs` (full) and `check_optional_module_reachability.py` (header and roster).
- NOT read: `test_kit/src/**` (~4.4k lines) beyond names; `testbed/**`; most of the ~66k-line test tree (evidence, not scope).

### Method
Read src in full. For every head that lowers hiccup (body run, frame-root / frame-provider, error-boundary, presence, overlay, host, `[:>]`, portal) traced WHICH dynamic bindings (`intent/*frame*`, `intent/*dispatch*`, the refusal tier) are live when its children are lowered, and compared the answers. For the controlled-input path, checked the element-type choice against every axis along which the model can move (type, case, nil-ness). Walked the collector's cell/entry/reaper state machine, the root lifecycle, the hydration window and the SSR doors for leaks and mis-ordering. Confirmed or refuted each candidate against the tests with rg (each zero taken beside a search that finds the shape) and against the tracker (`bd list --status all --limit 0 --json`, Python over title/description/notes/close_reason, including the prior senior review rf2-pk4i6.6 and its follow-on rf2-dza90, both verified fixed at tip). All candidates are CLJS-only, so every finding is INSPECTED, none executed.

### Findings
| bead | P | title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.7.1 | 2 | a nil controlled `:value` counts as uncontrolled — `forms/buffered-field` throws `:rf.error/fresco-revision-not-controlled` on a nil committed value (the 05-forms guide's own example for a todo with no title), and a plain field remounts (focus lost) when its model moves between nil and text |
| rf2-3x7nj.7.2 | 3 | under a frame boundary nested in a body, inline intents fire into the enclosing view's frame while error-boundary / presence / overlay children and `:on-dismiss` / `:on-error` fire into the scoped frame (decision needed: which frame) |

### Considered and rejected (so nobody re-litigates)
- Modal `cancel` is not `preventDefault`ed, so an `:on-dismiss` that declines leaves the dialog closed while app-db says open — 13-overlays-and-focus says the handler MUST write the flag false; a programmer contract, not a defect.
- A route-link `:on-click` given as `h/event` has its returned vector ignored (`activate-link!` calls `(on-click e)`) — consistent with HD-027's one-intent-per-click law; dispatching it would be the second semantic event.
- A frame destroyed and recreated in a LATER task leaves a mounted boundary showing the predecessor until something re-renders — deliberate, pinned by `reincarnation_readset_dom_cljs_test` (rf2-3awu).
- `frame-root` opts compared with `=`, so fn-valued opts (an `:fx-overrides` fn re-def'd by a hot reload) raise `:rf.error/frame-root-reconfigured` — core's code, already considered and rejected on rf2-3x7nj.3 (loud; hoist the value).
- `reg-state`'s read-side bad-key refusal is recovered to nil by the sub layer rather than thrown — known and pinned in `state_cljs_test` (read once, recovered and cached).
- Presence's expiry timer does not re-arm when it finds nothing due — with one clock the floor arithmetic guarantees the deadline has passed; only a backwards wall-clock step reaches it. Not litigated.
- The composition carve-out skips `type=email` (not in `caret-types`), so an IME model correction there lands mid-composition — marginal (IME in an email field); the exclusion follows `setSelectionRange` applicability.
- Keyword props are camelCased on custom elements (`:some-attr` -> `someAttr`), as in Reagent; a string key is the verbatim escape.
- SSR per-request frames mint read-set entries in the Node process — reaped by the 4 ms entry reaper; frame-ops rows are forgotten on destroy. No growth.
- The boundary shell classifies raw `useContext` without `context-value->current-frame`, so a Reagent-stringified context value is not coerced — reachable only by a hand-written `[:> Provider {:value …}]`, not a supported authoring path.
- A second `h/render!` inside the hydration window would make React client-render the root — reachable only by an explicit second call before adoption; the boot line calls it once and `^:dev/after-load` runs later.
- `realize-deep` walks every collection in a boundary's props on each parent render — linear and priced in the-boundary-crossing-walk-priced.md.
- rf2-3x7nj.3.1 (Reagent render-owned reaction retention) — Fresco's collector subscribes at commit, inside React's `subscribe`, not during a render; no distinct Fresco instance found (not verified at the ratom level).
- Prior-review items rf2-pk4i6.6 #1 (missing-key at the crossing) and #2 (`h/event` in a key map): fixed at tip (rf2-dza90; `check-crossing-key!`, `key-map-handler`'s `callback?` arm).

### What could not be verified
- Nothing was executed: every Fresco form involved is `.cljs` (graded only by the CLJS lane) and shadow-cljs / a browser were out of bounds, so both findings rest on source tracing plus React's documented element-type and cancel-event semantics.
- `closedby` engine support: a modal with no `:on-dismiss` relies on `closedby="none"`; on an engine that ignores the attribute, Escape would close the dialog natively behind app-db. Not measured (the overlay tests assert only that the attribute is emitted).
- `test_kit/src/**` and `testbed/**` were not reviewed.

- `implementation/ssr-node/src/`: `envelope.cjs` 167, `http.cjs` 331, `isolate.cjs` 453, `pool.cjs` 284, `protocol.cjs` 729, `service.cjs` 254, `worker.cjs` 329

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj` lines 80-110 and 400-460: the JVM consumer of the sidecar's status contract, read only to establish the consequences of a sidecar status.

### Method

The slice is plain CommonJS on Node, not CLJS: there is no shadow-cljs anywhere in it, and its gate is `node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs`, run in CI by `node-ssr-node`. I read every source file for three things:

- per-request isolation, meaning shared mutable state across awaits in the parent;
- isolate/pool lifecycle through every terminal path: complete, worker error reply, deadline, crash, exit, close, and replacement failure;
- the HTTP framing and refusal paths, against the README contract and against Spec 011's description of the JVM adapter that consumes the status codes.

I confirmed suspected defects with BOUNDED, process-local Node probes that `require` the frozen tree's `src/` read-only. The probe files and the module they load live only in `scratchpad/review-wave/ssr-node/`. Each probe was one process under `timeout 60`, with stdout and stderr redirected to scratch. Nothing was written into the tree. I ran no shadow-cljs, no npm script, no test suite and no browser.

Every probe carried a control run through the same path with a value that should not fail. For duplicates I scanned a full `bd export`, taken to scratch on stdout. `bd search` matches titles only: a control search for `SERVICE_SATURATED`, a term known to be in a description, returned 0. The export scan covered title, description, notes and close_reason across 2158 issues, 71 of them mentioning ssr-node.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.15.1 | P3 | ssr-node: a render callback that throws null/undefined crashes the whole sidecar (isolate.cjs:200 reads err.message unguarded) |

Executed, with controls in both directions. `throw null` and `throw undefined` from a `setImmediate` callback exit the parent process with code 1, and the sibling isolate's concurrent render is lost. `throw 'a string'` and an unhandled `Promise.reject(null)` through the same path are both contained correctly: refused `isolate-lost` with service-owned detail, sibling served, pool replaced.

### Considered and rejected (one line each, so nobody re-litigates them)

- **An isolate that dies WHILE IDLE** stays in `idleIsolates`, logs nothing, reads `ready` in `/health`, and the next innocent request is refused `isolate-lost` ('this isolate is dead', detail `{}`). Pointers: `isolate.cjs:186`, `:266`, `:410-421`; `pool.cjs:169-170`. This was ALREADY FOUND as rf2-pk4i6.5 finding #3 and DISMISSED under Mike's 2026-09-16 ruling: "rare ... and self-healing after one 500; take the `onDeath` + `dead`-skip when ssr-node is next touched". I did not re-file it. Re-measured here, executed:
  - It is still present at `034d0c8fc8`. For the error arm and for the exit arm, stderr was 0 bytes, the next request was refused, and then replaced.
  - One fact for whoever next touches the file. With the SYNCHRONOUS `renderToString` module shape, the only shape the service supports today, even a zero-delay `setImmediate` throw lands on this idle path rather than on the mid-render path. So the README's "an exception that escapes the render call ... goes to the same stderr ... the pool replaces it" holds only for async modules.
  - rf2-3x7nj.15.1 touches the same handler.
- **Pool shrinks permanently after a failed replacement, and `/health` keeps `status: "ok"` even at `total: 0`.** Deliberate: `pool.cjs:204-206` says "A pool that cannot replace an isolate is a pool that shrinks". The stderr diagnostic is unconditional, and `/health` exposes `isolates.total`.
- **`worker.cjs` header overclaims.** It says per-request isolation "does not have to mean the render module was careful", while module state does persist across sequential renders on one isolate. README §1 correctly assigns the per-request frame to the render module, and the frame is the module's contract, so this is comment overreach that misleads nobody who reads the README.
- **A `buildId` with a character outside latin-1 makes every render 500 `render-threw` at `writeHead`** (`http.cjs:216-253`). It is loud on the first request, and the value is operator-chosen. Trust the programmer.
- **`--timeout-ms` is not clamped by `--max-timeout-ms`, and neither has an upper bound** (setTimeout overflow past 2^31-1; `protocol.cjs:670-681`, `bin/serve.cjs:121-122`). Operator misconfiguration.
- **A caller's tiny `timeoutMs` (e.g. 0.001) forces one isolate termination and boot per request.** The caller is the trusted JVM host on loopback.
- **`args` is not counted against `maxRequestBytes`** (`protocol.cjs:656-667`). The HTTP body ceiling bounds it over the wire, and an in-process host is trusted.
- **Over HTTP the state+runtime ceiling can never fire before the body ceiling.** Both use the same number, and body bytes are always at least the EDN bytes. Both refuse 413 `request-too-large`, and `--max-request-bytes` documents it as one knob.
- **`detail.returned` uses `Object.prototype.toString`** (`worker.cjs:234`), so a module-defined `Symbol.toStringTag` could place text in a refusal. That needs deliberate exfiltration by a module that could put the same text in its markup.
- **`STATE_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED`'s `detail.allowed` (`protocol.cjs:537`) and `service.entries` hand out live references to the allowlist arrays.** Only an in-process host could mutate them, and over HTTP they are serialised.
- **An `emit` made after the module's promise resolved is dropped silently** (`isolate.cjs:344`). The module contract says to await its work, so that is a module bug and not a service one.
- **Streaming mode omits `x-rf-ssr-chunks` and `x-rf-ssr-render-ms`, which the README lists.** Neither is knowable before the body, and the JVM adapter uses buffered `/render`.
- **The `envelope.judge` docstring says "never throws", but `percentile` throws on an empty sample.** The witness always supplies 200 samples.
- **SIGTERM's "graceful close" destroys in-flight connections** (`closeAllConnections`). The README says a restart loses in-flight renders.
- **The JVM's `:rf.error/ssr-node-build-skew` is effectively unreachable, because the sidecar refuses a mismatched request with 409 first.** `node.clj` documents that check as defensive on the answer, and it belongs to the ssr-ring slice (rf2-3x7nj.14).
- **Parent-side shared state across awaits:** checked and clean. `acquire`, `release` and `_offer` are synchronous. Every per-request structure (`pendingFrames`, the `onChunk` closure, `bufferedHtmlChunks`) is local to its call. Render ids stop late chunks from one render reaching the next. `_settlePendingRender` clears `pendingRender` before settling, so a deadline and a crash cannot both settle one render. I found no double release and no path that grows the pool past its size.

### What I could not verify

- **The test suite, not run.** Per the brief: no suites, no npm scripts. The tests were read as evidence only.
- **HTTP-level behaviour over real sockets, not probed.** That covers client disconnect mid-stream, keep-alive after a 413, and closing under load. Those conclusions are "inspected".
- **The idle-phase variant of the nullish crash is inspected, not executed.** Line 200 is unconditional, so it reaches the same crash.
- **The Fresco `render-body` entry and the CLJS side of the per-request frame** (`implementation/fresco`) are outside this slice.
- **My tracker writes.** I made no edits to tracked files and no git writes. The only tracker writes were creating rf2-3x7nj.15.1, this note, and the close.

Correctness review of slice ssr-node complete at frozen tree 034d0c8fc8. All of implementation/ssr-node/src (2547 lines), bin/serve.cjs, package.json and the README (985 lines) were read in full.

1 finding: rf2-3x7nj.15.1 (P3). A render callback that throws null or undefined crashes the whole sidecar process. The cause is isolate.cjs:200, which reads err.message unguarded in the worker 'error' handler. Executed: throw null and throw undefined each exit the parent with code 1 and lose the sibling isolate's concurrent render. Controls: throw 'a string' and an unhandled Promise.reject(null) are both contained correctly (isolate-lost, sibling served, pool replaced).

Not re-filed: idle-isolate death, which is already dismissed as rf2-pk4i6.5 #3 under Mike's 2026-09-16 ruling. I re-measured it as still present, with one extra data point for the next toucher; see the notes. Everything else considered and rejected is listed in the notes with a reason.

title: core-reactive: ratom render-owned claims retain every disposed sub reaction an owner ever read (unbounded, production)
description:
## Defect

On the ratom family (Reagent, reagent-slim) the render-owned reference that rf2-ty246 added keeps a strong reference to EVERY subscription reaction an owner has ever claimed, for the owner's whole lifetime, even after that reaction has been disposed and evicted from the sub-cache. `claim-render-owned-ref!` records each claim twice on the owning render Reaction — an entry in the owner's `rfSubRefs` map and a `release-render-owned-ref` closure pushed onto the owner's `on-dispose-arr` — and nothing ever removes either when the CLAIMED reaction dies. Each retained reaction still holds its compute thunk, which closes over the memo wrapper's volatiles: `last-db` (the whole app-db value from its last recompute) and `last-result`. So a long-lived component that re-reads a subscription after it has been evicted, or reads a parametric subscription with a changing argument, grows without bound in production, retaining historical app-db snapshots.

## Where

Frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`.

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1606-1623` — `claim-render-owned-ref!`: the owner cell is created at `:1611-1614`, a new holding is recorded with `vswap! cell assoc slot reaction` at `:1619`, and `rf.interop/add-on-dispose! owner (fn release-render-owned-ref …)` at `:1620-1622` captures `reaction`. A search for `rfSubRefs` over `implementation/` finds only `:1611` and `:1613`; no site ever dissocs from the cell, and no callback on the claimed reaction clears it.
- Called on every render read from `subscribe-in-frame`, at `subs.cljc:1813`.
- What a retained reaction keeps alive: `subs.cljc:1269` (`make-derived-value inputs memoised-body`) → `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:4117-4119` (ratom spine: `(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn source-containers compute-fn))`) → `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/memo.cljc:571-617` (`last-db` / `last-result` volatiles, written at `:615-616`), and likewise `:646-689` and `:710-743` for layer-2+.
- Stock Reagent 2.0.1 (`reagent/reagent` is pinned at 2.0.1 in `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15`), `reagent/ratom.cljs`: `f` is an immutable `deftype Reaction` field (`:362`). `dispose!` (`:481-494`) clears `watching`, `state` and `auto-run` but not `f`. `add-on-dispose!` (`:496-500`) only ever pushes.
- The owner is the in-flight `*ratom-context*`: `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:247` and `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:150`.
- Public entry point: `rf/subscribe` deref'd inside any `reg-view` render on the Reagent or reagent-slim adapter. Not debug-gated, so this happens in production too.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :ui/show-details? (fn [db _] (:show-details? db)))
(rf/reg-sub :ui/details       (fn [db _] (:details db)))
(rf/reg-view panel []
  [:div (when @(rf/subscribe [:ui/show-details?])
          [:pre (pr-str @(rf/subscribe [:ui/details]))])])
```

Toggle `:show-details?` N times while `panel` stays mounted.

1. Each "off" render stops deref'ing `[:ui/details]`.
2. Its Reaction loses its last watcher and auto-disposes (`ratom.cljs:371-376`), and re-frame's on-dispose evicts the slot.
3. Each "on" render rebuilds `[:ui/details]` as a new reaction R_i and claims it. That overwrites the cell entry and pushes one more closure onto `panel`'s render Reaction, capturing R_i.

After N cycles the render Reaction holds N closures. Each one retains a disposed R_i, its thunk, and its memo `last-db`, which is a full app-db snapshot. The same growth happens with no toggling at all when a component reads `[:search/results q]` while `q` changes on every keystroke: one retained reaction per distinct query, for as long as the page stays mounted.

The error paths grow too: a render reading an unregistered sub, or one hitting a parametric `input-fn` failure, gets a new never-cached reaction each render, so it pushes one more closure per render. So does each hot reload of a sub that a mounted owner reads.

## Evidence

Inspected, not executed. `claim-render-owned-ref!` is `#?(:cljs …)`-only and fires only under a ratom adapter, so no JVM probe can reach it, and shadow-cljs is out of bounds for this review.

- The retention chain was read end to end at the cites above, including the stock Reagent 2.0.1 `Reaction` source extracted from `~/.m2/repository/reagent/reagent/2.0.1/reagent-2.0.1.jar`.
- The zero-removal claim rests on a search for `rfSubRefs` across `implementation/`. The instrument can see: it returned exactly the two construction sites at `subs.cljc:1611` and `:1613`.
- The pinning test `implementation/core/test/re_frame/subs_render_owned_frame_slot_cljs_test.cljs` pins the count per (owner, slot) for re-renders over the SAME slot and the same reaction. It never evicts a claimed reaction and then re-reads it, and never changes the query, so it cannot see this.
- rf2-ty246 and rf2-kk986 (both closed) discuss the counting half only. Neither mentions retention.

## Smallest fix

Tie each holding's lifetime to the CLAIMED reaction as well as the owner:

- when claiming, also `add-on-dispose!` on the claimed reaction a callback that does `(vswap! cell dissoc slot)` when the entry is still that reaction;
- register ONE owner-level release per owner, walking the cell at owner dispose, instead of one closure per claim. Alternatively, have each per-claim closure reach its reaction through a box that the claimed reaction's dispose clears.

Either way the owner holds only live reactions. The fence is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc` (the CLJS branch). It touches no hot-zone file: Spec 006 §Which lifetime governs a ratom adapter already says the release is identity-guarded and needs no change.

## Gates

CLJS only — the code sits inside `#?(:cljs …)`.

- `npm run test:cljs` (node lane), for `implementation/core/test/re_frame/subs_render_owned_frame_slot_cljs_test.cljs`.
- The browser lane, for `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/sub_dispose_real_unmount_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and the reagent-slim twin.

A JVM green says nothing about this change. A regression test should toggle a conditional read, or change a parametric argument, N times, then assert that the owner's holdings and dispose callbacks stay bounded, and that no disposed reaction is reachable from the owner.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (2026-09-23, PR #10282): FIXED

Premise verified at tip bed2f4f65e (implementation unchanged since the frozen tree 034d0c8fc8). claim-render-owned-ref! recorded each claim on the owner (rfSubRefs map) AND pushed one release closure per new claim onto the owner's on-dispose-arr, and nothing removed either when the CLAIMED reaction was disposed.

Fix (subs.cljc, CLJS branch only). Each side of a holding now carries exactly ONE callback:
- owner-holdings! creates the owner's cell (slot -> [query-v reaction]) with one owner-level release. The release walks the cell, releases through unsubscribe-if-reaction, and nils the expando, so an owner re-run after disposal starts afresh.
- record-holder! keeps a JS Map (owner cell -> slot) on the claimed reaction, with one on-dispose callback. On dispose it dissocs the reaction from every owner cell still holding it (identity-guarded).
- The owner release deletes its cell from each held reaction's Map, and so does a slot overwrite, so the reaction-side registry names only live owners.

Dropping a holding early loses nothing: every eviction path dissocs the slot before disposing, so the release it replaces would have no-oped on its identity guard. The bead's suggestion of a callback on the claimed reaction PER CLAIM was deliberately not taken. It would have grown a long-lived reaction by one closure per owner that ever read it, which is the same leak in the other direction. That is not a design decision, just the bounded form of the suggested fix. No spec change: Spec 006's identity-guarded-release clause already covers it.

Regression: implementation/core/test/re_frame/subs_render_owned_retention_cljs_test.cljs (node lane), for both ratom adapters. Toggle rows and parametric rows (5 claims each) assert that the owner's on-dispose callbacks do not grow, that the holdings name only live slots, and that no disposed reaction is reachable. An owner-churn row pins the mirror property (green both ways on the old code).

Control shown RED in CI with the fix removed (control commit 674a0bd016, run 35861069313, CLJS :node-test job): 12429 tests / 62591 assertions, 12 failures, 0 errors, all in the new ns. Owner callbacks grew 2 -> 7 (toggle) and 1 -> 6 (parametric), stale slots were kept, and disposed reactions were reachable. Preconditions and the churn control stayed green. The restore was verified by a blob hash equal to the committed object, and the branch was reset and force-pushed. CLJS gates are relied on in CI (the shadow-cljs lane was not granted locally).
Green on PR #10282 head 210fd98698 (run 35862657704): CLJS :node-test 12432 tests / 62623 assertions, 0 failures; CLJS :browser-test 1103 / 6050, 0 failures; full rollup 88 checks, 76 success + 12 skipped. PR marked ready for review.
Merged-PR audit #10282 (9641387f0901696d21e0e5d997a25c6da5892a0b; merged 2026-09-23T13:18:11Z). Completeness: Both closed source claims are addressed: disposal removes holdings in both directions, owner callback count is bounded across query churn, and committed UIx subscriptions do not reacquire during adapter teardown. Inspected merged implementation and regressions at 9641387f0901696d21e0e5d997a25c6da5892a0b. Correctness: Traced owner release, claimed-reaction cleanup, identity guarding, slot replacement and current-adapter returning nil before cache disposal. Retrieved GitHub CI logs independently: Node 12432 tests/62623 assertions and browser 1103 tests/6050 assertions, zero failures/errors; rollup 76 success/12 skipped. CLJS-only behavior was not rerun locally. No material actionable defect found. Implementation quality: Internal lifecycle repair with one registry and callback per live endpoint, avoiding a reverse owner-churn leak. Adapter guard uses the existing lifecycle API; no public API growth or unrelated refactor. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.

DONE — merged as PR #10282 (head 210fd98698), with its sibling in the same PR. CI 88/88 at band (green run 35862657704: node lane 12432 tests 0 failures, browser lane 1103 tests 0 failures). Control by a do-not-merge commit removing both fixes (run 35861069313), then reset; both source blobs verified against the committed objects.

rf2-3x7nj.3.1 — FIXED (subs.cljc, CLJS branch). A render-owned holding now carries exactly one callback on each side: the owner's releases what it still holds and clears its record; the claimed reaction's removes itself from every owner still holding it, so disposal no longer leaves release closures and disposed reactions reachable. Deliberately NOT the bead's per-claim callback on the reaction, which would have leaked in the other direction on a long-lived sub (one closure per owner that ever read it). Test: subs_render_owned_retention_cljs_test.cljs, for Reagent and reagent-slim (conditional-read toggle, parametric arg change, owner-churn row for the reverse leak). title: core-frames: rf/destroy-adapter! throws :rf.error/adapter-disposed when a spine (UIx) use-sub is mounted - rf2-1frc reacquisition re-subscribes mid-disposal
description:
## Defect

With the React-hook spine (UIx; any adapter built by `spine/make-react-spine`), `rf/destroy-adapter!` throws `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` ("rf/make-derived-value was called after (rf/destroy-adapter!)") from an otherwise clean teardown whenever a component holding a committed `use-sub` is still mounted. The spine's adapter disposer walks and disposes every frame's sub-cache BEFORE it unmounts the active roots, so each mounted `use-sub`'s rf2-1frc reacquisition callback (`on-committed-disposed`) fires while its component is still mounted. Its guards (not released, same held reaction, frame still live) all pass — none asks whether the adapter is being torn down — so it calls `rf.subs/subscribe`, misses the just-cleared cache, rebuilds, and reaches `rf.substrate.adapter/make-derived-value`, whose `require-adapter!` throws because the generation is already claimed `:disposing?`. The walk records that throw as a teardown failure and the spine rethrows it as the primary failure at the end of `dispose-adapter!`. Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle has the adapter rethrow the first CLEANUP failure; here there was none, so a fixture or hot-reload cycle sees a failed teardown with an error that names the wrong cause. The throw also escapes the reaction's own `-dispose` callback loop, skipping any on-dispose callbacks registered after that hook on the same reaction.

## Where

All cites at `034d0c8fc8` (frozen tree `re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`).

- Entry: `rf/destroy-adapter!` = `rf.substrate.adapter/dispose-adapter!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:3019`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:208-225` — `claim-installed-for-dispose!` sets `:disposing? true` BEFORE the adapter's own cleanup runs (`adapter.cljc:270-276`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1924-1939` — `make-dispose-adapter!` calls `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!`, then `rethrow-teardown-failure!`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1845-1854` — `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` runs FIRST, the `(doseq [root @active-roots-cell] (unmount-op root))` second.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1776-1785` — cache snapshotted and reset to `{}`, then each reaction disposed; a throw is `record-teardown-failure!`d.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:976-1002` — the spine derived value's `-dispose` fires its on-dispose callbacks in a plain `doseq` (no per-callback try).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3501-3518` — `use-subscribe-2`'s `on-committed-disposed`: guards `released?`, held identity, `(some? (rf.frame/frame stable-frame-kw))`; then `(wire! (rf.subs/subscribe stable-query-v {:frame stable-frame-kw}))`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:1415-1460` (`compute-and-cache!` rethrows everything except `:rf.error/sub-cycle`) and `subs.cljc:1269` (`rf.substrate.adapter/make-derived-value`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:323-375` (`require-adapter!` throws `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` while `:disposing?`) and `adapter.cljc:632-633` (`make-derived-value` goes through it).

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/init! uix/adapter)`, `(rf/make-frame {:id :app})`, `(rf/reg-sub :n (fn [db _] (:n db)))`.
2. Mount a UIx component that calls `(use-sub [:n])` through the adapter's `render` / client-root (the root lands in the spine's active-roots set); let it commit.
3. Call `(rf/destroy-adapter!)` with the root still mounted — the case the active-roots drain exists to handle (test fixture `:after`, hot-reload teardown, adapter swap).
4. Expected: `nil`, sub-caches disposed, root unmounted. Actual: teardown completes, then `rf/destroy-adapter!` throws ex-info `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` with `:where rf/make-derived-value`. A native UIx root the app mounted itself (not in active-roots) reaches the same callback, since it is never unmounted before the walk.

## Evidence

INSPECTED, not executed: the path is CLJS/React-only (spine.cljs) and a probe needs the shadow-cljs lane, which this review may not use. Confidence comes from tracing every hop above at source: the claim precedes adapter cleanup; the cache walk precedes root unmount; the callback's three guards cannot see adapter state (frame liveness is untouched by adapter disposal); the rebuild's `make-derived-value` is unconditionally `require-adapter!`-gated; `compute-and-cache!` rethrows non-cycle errors; the walk records and the factory rethrows. The docstring at `spine.cljs:1776-1779` already anticipates "a re-entrant subscribe during a dispose callback" but only for its reachability, not its outcome.

Tests: `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs:119-149` destroys the adapter over a mounted root whose Probe tree has NO `use-sub`; `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs` has no case combining a mounted `use-sub` with `destroy-adapter!`. Nothing pins this path.

Tracker: rf2-1frc (closed) added this reacquisition; its guards were reasoned against `destroy-frame!` (frame liveness flips before the sub-cache disposal), not adapter disposal. A scan of all 2109 beads for `destroy-adapter!` + use-sub/reacquire/on-committed-disposed and for adapter-disposed during teardown found nothing on point (control: 9 hits for `rf2-1frc`; the one adapter-disposed hit, rf2-kuky.4, is the ruling that makes `current-adapter` return nil during disposal).

## Smallest fix

Add `(some? (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter))` to the `on-committed-disposed` guard (`current-adapter` already answers nil during terminal disposal, `adapter.cljc:180-205`), so the hook lets go exactly as it does for a destroyed frame. Alternative: unmount active roots before the sub-cache walk in `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!` (bigger, and still leaves natively-mounted roots exposed). Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs` only. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

CLJS lane only — the change is in a `.cljs` file: `npm run test:cljs` for the shared React suite, and the UIx DOM tests in the browser lane (`implementation/adapters/uix/test/*_dom_cljs_test.cljs`) for a regression test (mount a `use-sub` component via the adapter's client root, `rf/destroy-adapter!`, assert it returns nil). A JVM green says nothing about it.

## Decision needed

No.
notes:
## Worker verdict (2026-09-23, PR #10282): FIXED

Premise verified at tip bed2f4f65e (implementation unchanged since the frozen tree 034d0c8fc8), and reproduced in CI (below). on-committed-disposed in use-subscribe-2 (spine.cljs) had three guards: released?, held identity, and frame liveness. None of them sees adapter disposal, so the sub-cache walk inside rf/destroy-adapter! triggered a rebuild through make-derived-value, which threw :rf.error/adapter-disposed.

It mounts a use-sub through the UIx client root, with a precondition that a dispatch re-renders it (so the store subscription is committed). It then asserts that rf/destroy-adapter! returns nil, that the root is unmounted, and that the frame's sub-cache is {}.

Completeness: Both closed source claims are addressed: disposal removes holdings in both directions, owner callback count is bounded across query churn, and committed UIx subscriptions do not reacquire during adapter teardown. Inspected merged implementation and regressions at 9641387f0901696d21e0e5d997a25c6da5892a0b. Correctness: Traced owner release, claimed-reaction cleanup, identity guarding, slot replacement and current-adapter returning nil before cache disposal. Retrieved GitHub CI logs independently: Node 12432 tests/62623 assertions and browser 1103 tests/6050 assertions, zero failures/errors; rollup 76 success/12 skipped. CLJS-only behavior was not rerun locally. No material actionable defect found. - **Static Machines live count ignores spawned `<type>#<n>` actors.** Ruled "honest, no finding" in rf2-y8doi.1.

title: ssr-ring: explicit nil :script-src / :app-element-id (spec: 'use the default') drops the bootstrap script and renders <div id="">; :html-shell nil 500s every request
description:
## Defect

Spec 011 §Trusted shell hook contract says the four shell opts accept a string "or nil — meaning 'no override, use the default'", and the ssr-ring test that exercises nil states the same intent. The shell does the opposite for two of them: it destructures the defaults with `:or`, which applies only to an ABSENT key, so an explicit nil is used as the value. `:script-src nil` removes the bootstrap `<script src>` entirely (default `/main.js` never emitted) and `:app-element-id nil` renders `<div id="">` (the client hydrator looks the root up by id, default `app`). Both handlers answer 200, so the page silently never boots / cannot hydrate. The same explicit-nil trap hits `ssr-handler`'s `:html-shell` (documented "Defaults to `default-html-shell`"): `{:html-shell nil}` constructs cleanly and then every request is a projected 500, because `(merge handler-defaults raw-opts)` lets the nil win and the pipeline calls it. The idiom that produces these nils is ordinary Clojure — `{:script-src (:script-src cfg) :app-element-id (:app-id cfg)}` with the keys absent from `cfg`.

## Where

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:165-168` (`document-prefix`, `:or {app-element-id "app" lang "en"}`) and `:199-203` (`document-suffix`, `:or {script-src "/main.js"}`, then `(when script-src ...)`).
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:96-97,296` — `handler-defaults` merged under raw opts, so `:html-shell nil` overrides the default; called at `pipeline.clj:681`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/trust.clj:327-366` accepts nil at construction (correctly, per spec).
- Contract: `spec/011-SSR.md:1220`. The test that claims the contract but cannot fail for it: `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:1826-1833` ("explicit nil signals 'no override, use the default'") asserts only that construction returns a fn — it never renders.
- Public entries: `re-frame.ssr.ring/ssr-handler`, `re-frame.ssr.ring/stream-handler`.

## Failure scenario

`(ssr-ring/ssr-handler {... :script-src nil :app-element-id nil})` (or the same on `stream-handler`), GET `/` -> 200 whose document has no `<script src=...>` at all and whose app root is `<div id="">`; the client bundle never loads and a hand-loaded bootstrap cannot find `#app`. `(ssr-ring/ssr-handler {... :html-shell nil})` -> every request 500 "Something went wrong".

## Evidence

EXECUTED — bounded JVM probe (`probe2_nil_shell_opts.clj`, reviewer scratch dir), `-Dre-frame.debug=false`, frozen tree `034d0c8fc8`:

- CONTROL, keys absent: ssr and stream both `has-main.js-script= true`, `div-id-app= true`, `div-id-empty= false`.
- CASE, `:script-src nil :app-element-id nil`: ssr and stream both `has-main.js-script= false`, `any-script-src= false`, `div-id-app= false`, `div-id-empty= true`.
- `:html-shell nil` on ssr-handler: status 500, body begins `<!DOCTYPE html>...<title>Something went wrong`.

`shell.clj`'s own `document-suffix` docstring reads "(when a `:script-src` is in play)", i.e. the implementation half-intends nil = omit — the two sides disagree. Tracker search (all fields) for "script-src nil" / "app-element-id nil": 0 hits.

## Smallest fix

Resolve defaults with `or` rather than `:or` (`(or app-element-id "app")`, `(or script-src "/main.js")`, `(or lang "en")`) and resolve `:html-shell` the same way in `ssr-handler`; extend `ring_test.clj`'s nil case to render and assert the defaults. If an opt-out for the bootstrap script is wanted (a caller who boots via `:body-end` with `type="module"` or a nonce), give it an explicit spelling (e.g. `:script-src false`) and say so in Spec 011. Fence: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj`, `ring.clj`, `test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj`; `spec/011-SSR.md` only if the opt-out spelling is added. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

JVM: `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/ssr-ring`. No CLJS lane involved.

## Decision needed

Only the opt-out: keep nil = default everywhere (the spec's reading) and add `false` as the explicit "no bootstrap script" spelling, or ratify nil = omit for `:script-src` and change the spec line. `:app-element-id nil` -> `id=""` and `:html-shell nil` -> 500 are wrong under either reading.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-23 23:18:11 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==
Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.14.3.nil-shell-opt-means-default.md. ai/ is local-only and gitignored, so that path is a convenience that can rot; the decisive findings are restated below.
Trunk read at: e402782b8d. The cited paths are unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8.

RECOMMENDATION: A.
1. nil means "use the default" for every shell opt, as spec/011-SSR.md:1220 already says. Change the destructuring defaults to or at shell.clj:72-75 (:or {app-element-id "app" lang "en"}) and at :106-110 (:or {script-src "/main.js"}), and resolve :html-shell with or rather than letting (merge handler-defaults raw-opts) at ring.clj:296 pass the nil through.
2. Add :script-src false as the explicit "emit no bootstrap script" spelling. That needs a narrow carve-out in trust.clj:64-103 and a line in Spec 011 (:1220 and :1222) and Security.md:86.
Precedent: :scroll false in routing (spec/012-Routing.md:293).

DECISIVE FINDINGS (executed at trunk, ssr-handler and stream-handler):
1. :script-src nil with :app-element-id nil gives no <script src= at all and <div id="">. Control: absent keys give /main.js and id="app". :html-shell nil on ssr-handler gives a 500 on every request.
2. :head nil and :body-end nil already behave exactly as absent. :lang nil renders <html> with no lang attribute (the same trap). :script-src false is refused today with :rf.error/ssr-trusted-shell-opt-invalid.
3. stream-handler refuses :html-shell (lifecycle.clj:426), so without a false spelling its users would lose the only way to suppress the default bootstrap tag.

BEAD LINE CORRECTIONS: shell.clj:165-168 and :199-203 should read :72-75 and :106-110 (the file is 170 lines). trust.clj:327-366 should read :64-103 (the file is 103 lines).
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 00:19:58 AUSEST) ==

RULING: A. nil means "use the default" for every shell opt, and `:script-src false` is the one explicit spelling for "emit no bootstrap script". Three things are fixed under ANY reading and land with it: `:app-element-id nil` renders `id="app"`, `:lang nil` renders `lang="en"`, and `:html-shell nil` on ssr-handler uses `default-html-shell`. No hot-zone file.

Verified at trunk f6bb999d6e (= origin/main after `git fetch origin main`, exit 0). The cited paths are unchanged since the review tree 034d0c8fc8: the diff over them is empty, and the unfiltered control reads 31 files.

--- WHY ---

The dossier and Codex AGREE on A, independently. Codex ran its own JVM probe at 9641387f09 through both handlers, draining each streaming body. What decides it:
1. The contract already promises it. `spec/011-SSR.md:1220` says "The framework MUST accept all four as strings (or nil — meaning 'no override, use the default')". :1222 and `spec/Security.md` (the §Trusted shell hook contract paragraph around :83-86) restate it, and the handler docstrings promise `/main.js`, `app` and `default-html-shell`.
2. The code breaks it through `:or`, which fires only for an ABSENT key (Clojure's destructuring guide). Commit 8216a1d365 introduced the nil-as-default promise together with a test that only checks that construction returns a fn (ring_test.clj:1826-1833), so the test could never fail.
3. The trigger is ordinary composition. `{:script-src (:script-src cfg) :app-element-id (:app-id cfg)}` with the keys absent from `cfg` gives a 200 page that never boots and cannot hydrate, with nothing erroring on either side. The sibling renderer already guards against exactly this: fresco server.cljs:114-116 uses `or`, not `:or`, "a caller threading `nil` through … supplies the KEY".
4. WHY AN OPT-OUT IS NEEDED AT ALL. `stream-handler` refuses `:html-shell` (lifecycle.clj about :460-477, `(when (some? (:html-shell opts)) …)`), so the four hooks are its ONLY envelope controls.
   - An ES-module bootstrap needs `type="module"` (and possibly integrity or a nonce), which the default tag cannot express, so it goes in `:body-end`.

title: xray-domain-panels-a: Managed-Fx panel can never mark an overridden effect STUB/OVERRIDDEN, so a stubbed :rf.http/managed reads ISSUED exactly like a real request
description:
## Defect

The Managed-Fx panel can never mark an overridden managed effect as stubbed. The code has the machinery for it:

- an `:overridden` status, with its own colour, glyph and "OVERRIDDEN" label;
- a `:stubbed?` record field;
- a STUB pill whose tooltip reads "Stubbed — this effect is redirected by an :fx-overrides entry instead of running for real."

None of it is reachable from a real trace, for two reasons:

1. The walker keeps only effect rows whose `:rf.fx/id` classifies as a managed surface. The runtime's `:rf.fx/override-applied` carries `{:rf.fx/from X :rf.fx/to Y}` and never `:rf.fx/id`, so it is dropped.
2. `:stubbed?` is derived from the surviving `:rf.fx/handled` row's own op, which always maps to `:ok`/`:issued`.

What the panel shows instead depends on the override:

- **Fn-value override of `:rf.http/managed`.** This is the ordinary test or story stubbing idiom: the stub runs and no request is made. The panel shows a record IDENTICAL to a real request, `ISSUED` with no STUB pill. The helper's own docstring says `:rf.fx/handled` "means the request went out".
- **Other surfaces overridden the same way**, such as a `:rf.ws/*` fx. The panel shows `OK`.
- **Keyword redirect** (`{:rf.http/managed :app/fake-http}`). The record disappears entirely, because the handled row carries the target id, which classifies as no surface. The panel then gives no sign that a managed request was redirected.

This is related to rf2-3x7nj.22.3, the Epoch SIDE EFFECTS ledger, which shares the same producer-shape root cause. That bead lives in different code (`panels/epoch/projection.cljc` `fx-effect-rows`). This bead covers the managed-fx walker's own filter and derivation, which that fix will not touch. It is not a consequence of rf2-3x7nj.22.2 (`tag-of` false → nil): the tag here is absent, not false.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers.cljc`
  - `:163-164`: `fx-id-of` reads `:rf.fx/id`.
  - `:229-233`: `managed-fx-effect?`. Its docstring says "(or override / skipped)", but it classifies via `fx-id-of`, so an override row is never kept.
  - `:1082-1133`: `event-bundle->managed-fx-records` does `(filterv managed-fx-effect? effects)` at `:1111`. The docstring at `:1084-1086` promises one record per `:rf.fx/handled` "(or `:rf.fx/override-applied`, etc.)".
  - `:378-389`: `fx-event->status` maps `:rf.fx/override-applied` to `:overridden`. This arm is unreachable for real data.
  - `:622`: `:stubbed? (= status :overridden)`, which is therefore always false.
  - `:898-935`: `http-adapter`'s docstring already concedes "an overridden or skipped effect … stays an unattributed `:issued`".
- **View:** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:243-258` defines `stub-pill`, used at `:319`.
- **Producer:** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`
  - `:1198-1203`: the keyword redirect emits `{:rf.fx/from :rf.fx/to}`.
  - `:1587-1591`: the fn-value override emits `{:rf.fx/from … :rf.fx/to ::fn-value}`.
  - `:rf.http/managed` is overridable. It is not in `non-overridable-source-fx-ids` (`fx.cljc:507-511`).
- **Spec:** `tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:656-662` accepts a plain `ISSUED` for an overridden HTTP effect as the STATUS. It says nothing that retires the STUB marker the code carries for exactly this case.
- **Entry point:** the Xray Managed-Fx panel on any epoch whose event emitted a managed fx under `:fx-overrides` (`dispatch-sync` opts, `with-fx-overrides`, a frame's `:fx-overrides`, or story presets).

## Failure scenario

1. `(rf/dispatch-sync [:app/load] {:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed (fn [_ _] ...stub...)}})`, where `:app/load` returns `{:fx [[:rf.http/managed {:request {...} :reply-to [...]}]]}`.
2. The stub runs, and no request is issued: there is no `:rf.http/issued` row.
3. The Managed-Fx panel shows `:rf.http/managed · ISSUED` with no STUB pill, byte-for-byte the same record as an unstubbed dispatch that really did hit the network.
4. A programmer checking whether the stub took effect is told the real request went out.

## Evidence

**Executed.** A bounded JVM probe (`probe_override.clj`, reviewer scratch dir) ran the real runtime (plain-atom substrate, core and http from the frozen tree, a local `HttpServer`). It grouped the captured traces with `re-frame.trace.projection/group-by-event` and ran the frozen tree's `event-bundle->managed-fx-records` on the `[:app/load]` bundle.

| Case | Traces | Record |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline, no override (control) | `:rf.http/issued`, `:rf.fx/handled {:rf.fx/id :rf.http/managed}` | `{:surface :http :fx-id :rf.http/managed :status :issued :stubbed? false}`, label `ISSUED` |
| Fn-value override | `:rf.fx/override-applied {:rf.fx/from :rf.http/managed :rf.fx/to :re-frame.fx/fn-value}`, `:rf.fx/handled {:rf.fx/id :rf.http/managed}`; bundle `:effects` holds both | identical: `:status :issued :stubbed? false`, label `ISSUED` |
| Keyword redirect to `:app/fake-http` | `:rf.fx/override-applied {:from :rf.http/managed :to :app/fake-http}`, `:rf.fx/handled {:id :app/fake-http :from :rf.http/managed}` | none |

The stub was invoked twice, once per override case, so the overrides did apply.

**Test census.** `override-applied` appears in neither `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` nor `managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs`. As a control, `:rf.fx/handled` appears 3 times in the helper test. The only STUB-pill test (`managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs:882`) sets `:stubbed? true` on a hand-built record, so nothing drives a real override through the walker.

**Inspected only:** the other surfaces' `OK` path (`common-record` `:583-622`). Not run.

**Related:** rf2-3x7nj.22.3 (Epoch SIDE EFFECTS ledger, same root cause, different code). That reviewer flagged `managed_fx_helpers.cljc:385` as suspect and unprobed; this bead is that probe.

## Smallest fix

In `event-bundle->managed-fx-records`, read the bundle's `:rf.fx/override-applied` rows before filtering.

- **Fn-value case.** Collect their `:rf.fx/from` ids, and mark a handled row `:stubbed? true` when its fx-id is in that set.
- **Redirect case.** Key a handled row that carries `:rf.fx/from <managed id>` on that ORIGINAL id, with the target as detail and `:stubbed? true`.

For HTTP, keep the status `ISSUED` if Spec 019 §F.1's plain-ISSUED wording is to stand, and let the pill carry the fact. Or show `OVERRIDDEN` and amend `019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:659` to match.

A shared "override origin" reader in `common_helpers.cljc` would serve this and rf2-3x7nj.22.3 alike, but either fix can land alone.

**Fence:** `managed_fx_helpers.cljc` and `managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc`, plus the one Spec 019 sentence if the status changes. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

The tools/xray JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`) and `npm run test:cljs` (`managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc`). The template is `.cljs`, node lane only.

## Decision needed

A small one. Should an overridden HTTP effect's status stay `ISSUED`, with the STUB pill added (no spec edit), or become `OVERRIDDEN` (one sentence in Spec 019 §F.1)? The fixer can default to the first.
notes:
== DOSSIER WRITTEN 2026-09-24 00:35:06 AUSEST (analysis only — no status change, no dispatch, no edit) ==

Dossier: ai/decisions/rf2-3x7nj.23.5.overridden-http-status.md. The ai/ tree is local-only and gitignored, so this path is a convenience that can rot. The decisive findings are restated below.

Trunk read at 8f940c5d20, equal to origin/main. The probe ran at 8e65232c40. fx.cljc has changed since (a6b5ae77ce), but only its registration code: 0 of 108 changed lines touch overrides.

RECOMMENDATION: status OVERRIDDEN, not ISSUED plus a STUB pill. It is plainly right. The cost is one sentence in tools/xray/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md §F.1 (:660-666), which is not hot-zone: drop "an overridden effect" from the plain-ISSUED list, and add that a stubbed or redirected effect reads OVERRIDDEN with the STUB pill, listed under the emitted id with the target as detail.

DECISIVE FINDINGS
1. The code already encodes OVERRIDDEN.
   - fx-event->status maps :rf.fx/override-applied to :overridden (managed_fx_helpers.cljc:385).
   - The STUB pill is derived from that status: `:stubbed? (= status :overridden)` (:622).
   - http-adapter's relabel only rewrites :ok to :issued (:1003).
   So once the walker stops dropping the override row (the filterv at :1140, which keys on :rf.fx/id, and the producer never puts that tag on override-applied: fx.cljc:1230-1232, :1620-1621), OVERRIDDEN plus the STUB pill falls out with no special case. Keeping ISSUED needs extra code to decouple the pill, and it leaves an overridden WebSocket fx reading OVERRIDDEN while an overridden HTTP fx reads ISSUED in the same panel.
2. ISSUED asserts the request went out. The http-adapter docstring (:926-935) says ":rf.fx/handled ... means the request went out", and status->colour-token calls :issued "a statement about the request going out". For a stub no request went out, so ISSUED beside a STUB pill contradicts itself.
3. The Epoch SIDE EFFECTS ledger treats overridden as a status in place of ran: "✓ ran / ✗ threw / ↺ overridden / – skipped" (tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:3912). rf2-3x7nj.22.3's fix marks the row :overridden. OVERRIDDEN keeps both panels' vocabulary identical.

Executed probe (real runtime, walker WITH the live panel's join context):
- baseline: {:status :ok :completion :joined}
- fn-value stub: {:status :issued :stubbed? false :completion nil}
- keyword redirect: no record at all
- Epoch ledger: :ok for all three

Correction to this bead: "byte-for-byte identical to a real request" holds only without the join context. The live panel supplies it (managed_fx_subs.cljs:79-81, also present at the review tree), so a completed real request reads OK. The stub reads plain ISSUED, the same as a real request whose issued row aged out. The defect stands.

No earlier ruling. No trunk fix since 034d0c8fc8 (9b3e89f429 and a6b5ae77ce do not touch overrides).
== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:12:00 AUSEST) ==

RULING: `OVERRIDDEN`, not `ISSUED` plus a STUB pill — with one correction from the Codex review built in. An override never yields `ISSUED` on its own: an overridden managed effect whose capture holds NO evidence of what the replacement did reads `◑ OVERRIDDEN`, and one whose replacement genuinely issued a request (an `:rf.http/issued` row pairs to it) reads the ordinary observed status (`ISSUED`, `ISSUED · no completion in this capture`, `✓ OK`, `✗ ERROR`, `◌ CANCELLED`, `⊘ STALE`). Every overridden record carries one neutral override marker naming the replacement, and a redirected effect is listed under the id the handler emitted, with its target as detail. One sentence-pair in Xray spec 019 §F.1 changes; no hot-zone file.

WHY
- `ISSUED` is a claim that the request went out. The panel's own vocabulary says so: `http-adapter`'s docstring (managed_fx_helpers.cljc:926-935 at trunk a61f903c5c) — `:rf.fx/handled` "is emitted AFTER the handler returns true, so the row means the request went out" — and `status->colour-token` (:137) calls `:issued` "a statement about the request going out". For a no-op stub nothing went out, so `ISSUED` beside a STUB pill contradicts itself, and a reader scanning status colours sees the neutral `◦ ISSUED` grey and misses the small pill — the misreading this bead exists to fix.
- The code already encodes OVERRIDDEN: `fx-event->status` maps `:rf.fx/override-applied -> :overridden` (:385), the pill is derived from that status (`:stubbed? (= status :overridden)`, :622), and `http-adapter`'s relabel only rewrites `:ok -> :issued` (:1003), so `:overridden` passes through. Option 1 (ISSUED + STUB) needs extra code to decouple pill from status and leaves an overridden `:rf.ws/*` fx reading OVERRIDDEN while an overridden HTTP fx reads ISSUED in the same panel, and the Epoch SIDE EFFECTS ledger reading `↺` overridden (tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:3912, "`✓` ran / `✗` threw / `↺` overridden / `–` skipped-on-platform") once rf2-3x7nj.22.3 lands. Option 1 is rejected.
- WHERE THE TWO RECOMMENDATIONS DIFFERED, AND WHAT DECIDES IT. The dossier recommended OVERRIDDEN on the premise "no request went out" and proposed spec text saying so. Codex agreed on OVERRIDDEN but corrected the premise: an override replaces the fx HANDLER; it does not promise the replacement avoids I/O (spec/002-Frames.md:2363-2404 §`:fx-overrides` — "replace fx handlers"; a fn value "runs in place of the registered fx", fx.cljc:1200-1203), and a fn override that delegates to the real handler really issues a request. That is decided by measurement, not argument, and it was re-measured here (below): the delegating case issues exactly one real request and today reads `OK · joined`. So the blanket "no request went out" wording, a generic STUB label, and the pill's current tooltip ("...instead of running for real.") all overstate the evidence. The resolution keeps the dossier's headline for the case the bead is about (the no-op stub) and takes Codex's rule for the rest: the status reports what the capture EVIDENCES about the replacement, and the marker reports the override. Neither recommendation is split; the dossier's is refined.
- Converse trap, from Codex, carried as a hard rule: the ABSENCE of an issued row must never be read as an override. Plain `ISSUED` with no issued row still legitimately means "issued row aged out of the ring" or "a capture from before the row existed". Only override provenance (`:rf.fx/override-applied`, or `:rf.fx/from` on the handled row) marks an override.
- Correction to the bead's text (from the dossier, verified): "byte-for-byte the same record as an unstubbed dispatch" holds only when the walker is called WITHOUT the join context. The live panel supplies it (managed_fx_subs.cljs:79-81, `http-join-context`, present at the review tree too), so a completed real request reads `✓ OK · joined` and the stub reads plain `ISSUED` — the same as a real request whose issued row aged out. The defect stands: nothing says "stubbed", and a keyword redirect's record vanishes.

MEASUREMENT (Codex's probe, re-run by this ruling agent at trunk a61f903c5c, exit 0; real runtime on the plain-atom substrate, core + http from the mayor checkout, a local JVM HttpServer COUNTING requests with an assertion on the expected count per case, traces grouped by `group-by-event`, the walker called WITH the live panel's `http-join-context`; loaded-source lines confirmed the checkout):
    case                           network hits  bundle :effects                                  issued rows  record today
    no override (control)          1             [handled {:id :rf.http/managed}]                 1            {:status :ok :stubbed? false :completion :joined}
    fn-value no-op stub            0             [override-applied {:from :rf.http/managed         0            {:status :issued :stubbed? false :completion nil}
                                                   :to :re-frame.fx/fn-value}, handled {:id :rf.http/managed}]
    keyword redirect to a no-op    0             [override-applied {:from :rf.http/managed         0            NO RECORD
                                                   :to :review/noop}, handled {:id :review/noop :from :rf.http/managed}]
    fn override delegating to the  1             [override-applied fn-value, handled {:id :rf.http/managed}]   1   {:status :ok :stubbed? false :completion :joined}
      registered HTTP handler
  Producer shape, verified at a61f903c5c: keyword redirect emits `:rf.fx/override-applied {:rf.fx/from <orig> :rf.fx/to <target>}` (fx.cljc:1230-1232); fn-value emits `{:rf.fx/from <orig> :rf.fx/to :re-frame.fx/fn-value}` at the point the fn actually fires (:1620-1621); neither carries `:rf.fx/id`. `:rf.fx/handled` carries `:rf.fx/id` (the TARGET on a redirect) plus `:rf.fx/from <orig>` on a redirect (`emit-handled!`, :1298-1308). `:rf.http/managed` is overridable (not in `non-overridable-source-fx-ids`, :523). Both override rows carry the dispatch-id and land in the bundle's `:effects` (measured). No trunk change to any cited file since the review tree beyond 9b3e89f429 (reply-link bound) and a6b5ae77ce (fx registration); neither touches overrides; nothing cited moved between 8f940c5d20 and a61f903c5c.
  The defect's mechanism: the walker keeps only effect rows whose `:rf.fx/id` classifies as a managed surface (`managed-fx-effect?` :229-233 via `fx-id-of` :163, `filterv` at :1140), so the override row is dropped; `fx-event->status`'s `:overridden` arm (:385) is unreachable for real data; and a redirect's surviving handled row carries the target id, which classifies as no surface, so the record vanishes. Test census (from the reviewer, re-checked): `override-applied` appears in neither managed_fx_helpers_cljs_test.cljc nor managed_fx_template_cljs_test.cljs, against 3 hits for `:rf.fx/handled` in the helper test; the only STUB-pill test (template test :882) sets `:stubbed? true` on a hand-built record.

WHAT TO BUILD (all cites at trunk a61f903c5c)

No hot-zone file.
1. ONE RECORD PER `:rf.fx/handled` ROW, as today. The `:rf.fx/override-applied` row is PROVENANCE for a handled row, never a record of its own (Codex: merely admitting the provenance row is not the acceptance criterion; it must remain one useful record per invocation, keeping its request and redirect target).
2. KEYWORD REDIRECT: a handled row carrying `:rf.fx/from` is overridden. Classify and key the record on `:rf.fx/from` (so `:fx-id` is the id the handler emitted, e.g. `:rf.http/managed`), with the target (`:rf.fx/id`) as detail. Use ONE classification for the walker's filter (:1140), the `http-fx` set that feeds `pair-issued-rows` (:1143) and the adapter dispatch (:1151), or the three disagree. Edge: a redirect INTO a managed surface from a non-managed id (`{:app/fetch :rf.http/managed}`) — `:rf.fx/from` does not classify but `:rf.fx/id` does; keep today's record for it (do not let the fix make it vanish), marked overridden.
3. FN-VALUE: a handled row with no `:rf.fx/from` is overridden iff an `:rf.fx/override-applied` whose `:rf.fx/from` equals its `:rf.fx/id` sits in its window — after the previous effect row and before it, by trace `:id`, the same position discipline `pair-issued-rows` (:1085-1109) uses; never by `:time`. The producer emits override-applied immediately before invoking the fn and handled after it returns.
4. STATUS. In `common-record` (:583-622): an overridden record's handled-derived `:ok` becomes `:overridden`; cancel and failure evidence still win exactly as the existing `terminal-status` cond does (do not turn OVERRIDDEN into an unconditional replacement for a measured error — Codex). 5. MARKER. `:stubbed?` must stop being derived from status (:622): a joined delegating override reads `:ok` and must still be marked. Derive it from the override provenance, and carry the replacement on the record (e.g. `:override-to`, the `:rf.fx/to` value: a target fx-id or `:re-frame.fx/fn-value`). Naming is the worker's call; renaming `:stubbed?` to `:overridden?` is recommended because the pill no longer says STUB (the template's destructure at :262 and call at :319, and the template test's fixtures at :42 and :882, move with it).
6. TEMPLATE (`stub-pill`, managed_fx_template.cljs:243-258): label `STUB` -> `OVERRIDE`; tooltip neutral, e.g. "Overridden — an :fx-overrides entry replaced this effect's handler" plus ", redirected to <target>" for a keyword redirect or ", with a function" for fn-value. Today `OVERRIDDEN`, `◑` and `STUB` appear 0 times in tools/xray/spec (control: `ISSUED` 3 times in 019), so this is display vocabulary with no public contract. NOT hot-zone.

REGRESSION — fixtures in the PRODUCER's shape (fx.cljc:1230-1232 / :1620-1621 / :1298-1308), NEVER with `:rf.fx/id` on the override row: that exact drift is what lets rf2-3x7nj.22.3's existing test pass on a false fixture (epoch projection_cljs_test.cljc:2690).    - The template: a render test that a marked record shows `OVERRIDE` with the target in the tooltip (the existing :882 test re-seated).
10. LANES. managed_fx_helpers.cljc has no reader conditional (`#?` count 0), so the tools/xray JVM suite compiles and runs the helper and its `-cljs-test` `.cljc` namespace: `clojure -M:test` from tools/xray, or `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh`. `npm run test:cljs` (node lane) also runs it and is the ONLY lane for the `.cljs` template and its test — a machine-wide exclusive, so ask for the lane.
