title: xstate-parity: two XState-side records are stale at 6.0.0-alpha.59 — typed context is no longer compile-time-only (spec/005:638, skill xstate-translation.md:21) and an unhandled event does emit an inspection transition (spec/005:4670, spec/009:224)
description:
## Gap

Two XState-side sentences in re-frame2's own records are no longer true at xstate 6.0.0-alpha.59, and both sit on rows where re-frame2 is recorded as LEADING, so a reader "correcting" toward them would overstate the lead rather than fix re-frame2 backwards. Not a capability gap; a stale-record item (the brief's second bead class).

RECORD 1 — "XState typed context is compile-time only." spec/005-StateMachines.md:634-641 (the enforcement table) says "compile-time only — TypeScript types are erased at runtime; a value off the wire that violates the declared shape is not caught", and :641 "XState's typed context is a static contract a TypeScript compiler checks and then discards"; skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md:21 says "XState's typed context is compile-time-only and erased at runtime". Since 6.0.0-alpha.29 (changelog line 795, "Add opt-in runtime Standard Schema validation through `setup({ validator })`") XState validates `context` AT RUNTIME when a validator is installed: a transition that writes a context violating the zod schema errors the actor with `ActorValidationError { reason: 'invalid', boundary: 'context' }`, at the same macrostep-commit position re-frame2's `:where :machine-data` boundary uses; it also validates input, external and internal events (dead-lettered at the delivery boundary, alpha.50), emitted events, final output and child slots. What remains true: `types<T>()` is type-only and validates nothing; with no validator installed the poisoned context is accepted silently; the validator is opt-in from a separate `xstate/validation` entry, so production cost is zero unless installed. re-frame2 still leads on DEFAULT posture (validation is on in dev by default through the Malli adapter, DCE'd in production) — that is the lead to record, not "compile-time only". docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md:291 hedges correctly ("mostly compile-time") and needs no change.

RECORD 2 — "an unhandled event is a silent no-op ... which xstate emits nothing for." spec/005:4670 (§Parity re-validation item 4) and spec/009-Instrumentation.md:224 ("Unlike xstate (which emits nothing), re-frame2 keeps this benign observability trace"). At alpha.59 an unhandled event on a LIVE actor DOES emit an inspection event: `@xstate.transition` with `eventType` = the event, `microsteps: []`, `actions: []`, the same snapshot object — and a guard-blocked event emits the identical shape, so the two are indistinguishable in the wire protocol (`inspect.test.ts:543` "@xstate.transition inspection event should report no microsteps if an unknown event was sent" pins it). What remains true: xstate emits no DEDICATED signal and no classification, so re-frame2's `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` (which also separates "unhandled" from "guard-blocked": the latter emits `:rf.machine/guard-evaluated :outcome :fail`) remains a LEAD. The sentence should say "xstate emits no dedicated signal (its inspection stream carries a zero-microstep transition indistinguishable from a guard-blocked event)".

## XState evidence

Executed, `xs/E-11-runtime-validation.mjs` -> `E-11-runtime-validation.out`: A. `after poison: status = error | context = {"count":3,...}` (the violating write never landed), `error isActorValidationError: true | reason invalid | boundary context | issues ['count: Invalid input: expected number, received string']`; E. `NO validator installed: ... status active | context = {"count":"not-a-number",...}` (types erased, as the record says — but only WITHOUT the validator); F. `types<T>()` with a validator: accepted (type-only); B. invalid event payload -> `@xstate.deadletter invalidEvent`, context unchanged; C. invalid input -> `boundary input`; D. invalid output -> `boundary output`; G. pure `transition()`: the poisoned macrostep throws, an invalid external event returns the snapshot unchanged with a `@xstate.deadLetter` effect. Docs: `xs-docs/typescript.md:63-105` §Runtime validation; changelog alpha.29 (:795), alpha.39 (:646), alpha.50 (:302-320); test `runtimeValidation.test.ts` ("validates stable root context after the macrostep", :305).
Executed, `xs/E-5b-unhandled.mjs` -> `E-5b-unhandled.out`: rows 2-3 `{"t":"transition","eventType":"ZZZ",...,"microsteps":0,"actions":0}` and the same for the guard-blocked `GO`; `after ZZZ: same snapshot object? true`. `xs/E-5-inspect.out` field census confirms the three-event protocol carries no guard facts anywhere (`any key mentioning guard/cond in events or microsteps: []`).

## re-frame2 evidence

At trunk fe8de195bd: spec/005-StateMachines.md:634-641 (table + closing paragraph), :4670; spec/009-Instrumentation.md:224; skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md:21 (the "typed `context`" row); docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md:289-292 (already hedged). re-frame2's own side of both rows is measured and unchanged: `jvm/E/E2_trace.out` row 32 `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op {:actor-id :e2/parent, :state :busy, :event [:ZZZ]}` beside rows 7/10/21 `:rf.machine/guard-evaluated ... :outcome :fail` for the guard-blocked case; `[:schemas :data]` wiring is spec/005:501-591 and the machines suite's schema tests (dimension D notes the JVM probe classpath carries no validator adapter, by design — spec/005:556).

## Why it matters

Both sentences are load-bearing "where re-frame2 leads" records written so nobody fixes re-frame2 backwards (spec/005:4665's own rationale). Left as they are, the next re-validation reads them, finds XState now validating context at runtime and emitting a transition for unhandled events, and either concludes the spec is unreliable or "corrects" re-frame2's lead claims wholesale. Precision keeps the leads: default-on dev validation with zero production cost, and a dedicated, classified unhandled-event trace.

## Options

1. Reword the four sites: spec/005:634-641 (enforcement row -> "opt-in runtime validation since 6.0.0-alpha.29 via `setup({ validator })` + Standard Schema; nothing without it; `types<T>()` never validates") and :641; spec/005:4670 + spec/009:224 (-> "no dedicated signal; a zero-microstep `@xstate.transition` indistinguishable from a guard-blocked event"); skill row :21. Spec-only, ~6 sentences, no runtime change.
2. Fold RECORD 1 into the §Parity re-validation subsection as a fifth "checked" item with the alpha named (6.0.0-alpha.59), leaving the table as a historical statement. Weaker: the table is what a reader consults.
3. Leave as is. Not recommended for the reason above.

## Recommendation

Option 1, naming the alpha in each corrected sentence (the §Parity re-validation posture: periodic re-validation at a named alpha). One PR, spec + skill + spec/009, no code.

## Fence

- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` :634-641, :4670 — HOT ZONE
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` :224 — HOT ZONE
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md` :21
- (no change) `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md`

## Gates

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `python -m mkdocs build --strict` for the spec pages (link/anchor gates only — the prose itself is verified by hand; say so in the PR body); `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` does not reach the skill page's row (no links change). No JVM/CLJS gate applies to a prose-only change.

## Decision needed

no

title: xstate-parity: a child-declared transition to a proper ANCESTOR keeps the ancestor standing; XState 5.32.6 and 6.0.0-alpha.59 both exit and re-enter it (LCCA rule) — spec/005:342 and the pinning conformance test claim the opposite as v5 parity
description:
## Gap

XState (6.0.0-alpha.59, and xstate@5.32.6 measured as a control) runs the SCXML LCCA rule for a transition declared on a CHILD state whose target is one of its proper ANCESTORS: the ancestor is in the exit set, so its `exit` and `entry` run, its invoked children restart and its `after` timers restart, and it then re-descends to its `initial`. Concretely, at `p.c.leaf1`, a transition declared on `leaf1` with `target: '#p'` (no `reenter`) produces `exit:leaf1, exit:c, exit:p, enter:p, enter:c, enter:leaf1` and the invoked child of `p` is a new incarnation; declared on `leaf1` with `target: '#c'` it produces `exit:leaf1, exit:c, enter:c, enter:leaf1`. The transition declared ON the ancestor itself (`p: { on: { selfP: { target: '#p' } } }`) is the different, non-reentering case: `exit:leaf1, exit:c, enter:c, enter:leaf1`, `p` standing — and that one re-frame2 matches.

re-frame2 treats both as the same "self / proper-ancestor target on the active path" geometry: the targeted ancestor SURVIVES, only its active descendants exit and its `:initial` chain re-descends. Same chart: `up-p` produces `[:exit/leaf1 :exit/c :enter/c :enter/leaf1]` with the `:spawn` child of `:p` NOT restarted (`:b4kid#1` before and after), and `up-c` produces `[:exit/leaf1 :enter/leaf1]` with `:c` untouched. The final configuration is identical in both systems (`[:p :c :leaf1]`); what differs is every effect the ancestor owns — its `:exit`/`:entry` actions and their `:data` writes, its `:after` timers, its `:spawn` children. spec/005 §Self-transitions records the re-frame2 behaviour as XState parity ("Under the XState-v5 model re-frame2 tracks ... a self / proper-ancestor `:target` does not re-enter by default ... the declaring state itself ... or a proper ancestor"), and the pinning conformance test says "Verified against xstate@5.32.0" — both claims are wrong for the child-declared case at 5.32.6 and at alpha.59.

## XState evidence

Executed: `xs/B-4-geometry.mjs` -> `xs/B-4-geometry.out` (alpha.59). Rows `upP` = `{"value":{"p":{"c":"leaf1"}},"log":["exit:leaf1","exit:c","exit:p","enter:p","enter:c","enter:leaf1"],"kidRestarted":true}` and `upC` = `["exit:leaf1","exit:c","enter:c","enter:leaf1"]`; control rows on the same run: `selfP` (declared on p, target #p) = `["exit:leaf1","exit:c","enter:c","enter:leaf1"]`, `kidRestarted:false`; `toLeaf2`, `sib`, `sibre`, `selfLeaf`, `tgtless`, `rootToLeaf1` all match re-frame2 (16 of 18 rows match; only `upP`/`upC` differ).

Version control: `xs/B-4v5-geometry.mjs` -> `xs/B-4v5-geometry.out` against xstate@5.32.6 (installed as alias `xstate5` inside xs/): `v5 upP` = `["exit:leaf1","exit:c","exit:p","enter:p","enter:c","enter:leaf1"]`, `v5 upC` = `["exit:leaf1","exit:c","enter:c","enter:leaf1"]`, `v5 selfP` = `["exit:leaf1","exit:c","enter:c","enter:leaf1"]`. Identical to alpha.59 — this did not change between v5 and v6.

Mechanism, read at source (`B/xs-src/stateUtils.ts`, fetched from the `next` branch): `getTransitionDomain` returns the source only when every effective target is the source or a descendant of it (`targetStates.every(target => target === transition.source || isDescendant(target, transition.source))`); an ancestor target fails that test and falls to the LCA loop (`getProperAncestors(head)` ... `tail.every(sn => isDescendant(sn, ancestor))`), which for {p, leaf1} is the root and for {c, leaf1} is p — so `computeExitSet` puts the ancestor itself in the exit set. `transitions.md` documents only the source-relative rule ("A targetless transition can update context ... Set `reenter: true` when a self-transition should run exit and entry behavior again"); the ancestor case is the SCXML algorithm the code implements, documented in `how-xstate-runs-machines.md` only by reference. Changelog: v5 fixed exactly this family in 5.0 ("Fixed an issue with external transitions targeting ancestor states", CHANGELOG-next.md:7204-7208); no alpha changed it since.

## re-frame2 evidence

Executed: `jvm/B/B-4-geometry.clj` -> `jvm/B/B-4-geometry.out` at trunk `7d72690192` (identical files at `fe8de195bd`, the dispatch sha). Rows: `up-p` = `{:value [:p :c :leaf1], :log [:exit/leaf1 :exit/c :enter/c :enter/leaf1], :kid-restarted? false, :kid-before {[:p] :b4kid#1}, :kid-after {[:p] :b4kid#1}}`; `up-c` = `{:value [:p :c :leaf1], :log [:exit/leaf1 :enter/leaf1], :kid-restarted? false}`; `self-p` (declared on :p) = `[:exit/leaf1 :exit/c :enter/c :enter/leaf1]` — matches XState. `up-p-re` (`:reenter? true`) = full restart, matches XState.

Spec: `spec/005-StateMachines.md:342` ("Self / proper-ancestor target, without `:reenter?` (re-resolve descendants). Declare a `:target` that resolves onto the active path at or above the declaring state — the declaring state itself ... or a proper ancestor. The targeted state's own `:exit` / `:entry` do not fire, but XState v5 re-resolves its descendants"), the geometry table at :349-354 (row "self / proper ancestor T on the active path"), and §Computing the LCCA sub-case 1 at :1531 ("Self / proper-ancestor target B, without `:reenter?` ... B itself is not re-entered").

Engine: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` `compute-transition-geometry` — the `target-on-active-path?` predicate at :3118-3131 and the arm selection at :3251-3269 (`reenter-active-path?` / `target-on-active-path?`), where an ancestor target without `:reenter?` bounds the cascade at the target's own depth (`lca-len = (count target-base)`), so the ancestor is never in the exit set.

Pinned today by `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/scxml_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:1207` `scxml-default-ancestor-target-re-resolves-descendants` — a transition declared on `:two` targeting the ancestor `[:p :a]` expecting `[:exit-2 :ACTION :entry-1]` and stating "Verified against xstate@5.32.0" (the measured 5.32.6 answer is `exit-2, exit-A, ACTION, entry-A, entry-1`). `machine_active_path_geometry_test.clj:195` `ancestor-target-without-reenter-re-resolves-descendants-only` pins the ON-the-ancestor case, which is correct and unaffected. rf2-3x7nj.8.3 (closed, ruled) covered the ROOT-declared case only ("the rule's gate is now 'the source path is non-empty'"); the child-declared case was not in its scope.

## Why it matters

The final `:state` is the same in both systems, so nothing fails; the difference is silent and lands on exactly the things an author hangs on an ancestor: a `:spawn` child that XState would restart keeps running here (or vice versa when porting the other way), an `:after` timeout that XState restarts keeps its old deadline, and `:entry`/`:exit` `:data` writes run or do not run. An author or an AI translating an XState chart that uses "target the parent to restart it" (a common reset idiom written on a child state) gets a machine that looks right and never restarts. The spec's parity claim means a careful reader checking re-frame2 against XState concludes XState is the outlier — the record is wrong in the direction that prevents anyone noticing.

## Options

1. Align the runtime with the LCCA rule (runtime + spec + the one pinning test): when the declaring state is a proper DESCENDANT of the target, the target enters the exit set (domain = the target's parent), exactly as `:reenter? true` already does; the on-the-ancestor case (declaring state == target) stays non-reentering. Smallest aligned form: the arm at transition.cljc:3251-3269 gains a "declared below the target" discriminator that selects the existing `reenter-active-path?` geometry. Breaks any existing machine that relies on a child-declared ancestor target NOT restarting the ancestor's timers/children; the fix's own control is the pinning test flipping to `[:exit-2 :exit-A :ACTION :entry-A :entry-1]`.
2. Keep today's behaviour and correct the record (spec-only + test commentary): strike the XState-parity claim at spec/005:342/:1531, state that re-frame2 deliberately keeps the ancestor standing for a child-declared ancestor target, and re-label the conformance test's "Verified against xstate@5.32.0". No behaviour change, no breakage; the divergence becomes a recorded one under §Four non-substrate divergences.
3. Both: align the runtime AND add the SCXML IRP-style fixture pair (child-declared vs ancestor-declared) to `scxml_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` so the two geometries can never be conflated again.

## Recommendation

Option 1 (with the fixture pair from option 3): the ruling for the sibling case rf2-3x7nj.8.3 already chose "include the root" on the grounds that XState's `getTransitionDomain` re-enters a root-targeted child; the same reasoning applied to a child-declared ancestor target gives the LCCA answer, it is the SCXML rule, it is what both XState versions do, and `:reenter? true` already implements the geometry, so the change is a discriminator rather than new machinery. If Mike prefers stability over parity here, option 2 is cheap and must at least land, because the current record is wrong in the reassuring direction.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (`compute-transition-geometry`, :3118-3269)
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/scxml_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` (:1207 pin), `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_active_path_geometry_test.clj` (new sibling case)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` :342, :349-354, :1531 — HOT-ZONE (sequence, never parallel)
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` only if the `:reenter?` prose there restates the geometry — HOT-ZONE; `docs/machines/coming-from-xstate.md`, `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md` rows on self/ancestor targets.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines` (JVM); `npm run test:cljs` because `scxml_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` and `machines_hierarchical_cljs_test.cljs` are `-cljs-test` namespaces graded by the node lane alone; the conformance corpus if a fixture under `spec/conformance/fixtures/` encodes an ancestor target; `check_doc_slugs.py` + `python -m mkdocs build --strict` for the spec edit.

## Decision needed

Yes: align the runtime with the SCXML/XState LCCA rule for a child-declared ancestor target (breaks machines relying on the ancestor surviving; option 1) — or keep today's semantics and correct the false parity claim in spec/005 and the conformance test (option 2)?

QUESTION. A transition DECLARED BELOW an ancestor (declaring state D) whose vector :target T names a PROPER ANCESTOR of D, with no :reenter?: keep T standing and only reset its children (today), or exit and re-enter T per the SCXML / XState LCCA rule?

OPTIONS AND SIZES.
- Option 1: align the runtime. One discriminator in compute-transition-geometry (selects the existing :reenter? arm), two test pins flip, a pair of new regression tests, and prose narrowed across spec/005, Spec-Schemas, CP-5, the xstate-translation skill row, a fixture comment and machines-viz docstrings. Breaking for exactly one shape: a vector :target that is a proper prefix of the declaring path, without :reenter?. In-tree blast radius measured zero.
- Option 2: keep today's semantics and rewrite the record as a deliberate divergence (no engine change; same prose sites plus a fifth entry in spec/005's "Four non-substrate divergences" section, whose anchor is linked from several places; a documented new SCXML-emitter divergence).
- Option 3 (the bead's): option 1 plus the child-declared / ancestor-declared fixture pair.

RULING: OPTION 1 WITH THE FIXTURE PAIR (i.e. option 3). A transition declared below its targeted ancestor exits and re-enters that ancestor whether or not :reenter? is set; a transition declared ON T and targeting T itself (T == D) stays non-reentering by default, exactly as today. This lands AFTER the live workers on rf2-2n6uv.4.2 (history targets) and rf2-2n6uv.6 have MERGED, as its own PR, never combined with them.

WHY.
1. Measured, twice, independently: XState 5.32.6 and 6.0.0-alpha.59 both put the ancestor in the exit set for this shape, and both are the SCXML algorithm. SCXML has no form in which a targeted proper ancestor of the source stays standing. Today's behaviour is an accidental exception, not a design.
2. The fix is a predicate, not machinery: :reenter? true already implements the exact geometry, and every lifecycle effect (after-fx, after-cancel-fx, destroy-fx, the spawn phase) is derived downstream from the exit/entry pairs, so fixing the boundary fixes the lifecycle at its source.
3. Stance. Trust the programmer: an author who names an ancestor from below is asking for it; an author who wants only the children reset has idiomatic spellings that behave identically in re-frame2 and XState (below). Don't litigate the minutiae: no compatibility mode, no second restart flag, no :reenter? :descendants value. Option 2 is cheaper only in edit count; it is the more complex contract (a fifth geometry every reader and AI translator must carry, a permanent porting trap, and a new emitter divergence).
4. Standing rulings agree (supporting, not decisive): rf2-emz8l (Mike, 2026-06-04) ruled "ALIGN: a target to a proper ancestor must restart that ancestor" on exactly this shape (source [:p :a :x], target [:p :a] declared on :x). rf2-eicq0 (Mike, 2026-06-05) ruled the XState-v5 internal default for SELF transitions; its close reason extended the flip to "self/ancestor" with no XState measurement behind it. Option 1 honours both.

Vocabulary. D = declaring state (the node whose :on / :after / :always / :on-done carries the transition). T = resolved target base (before T's own :initial re-descent). Two shapes share the words "ancestor target":

- Child-declared ancestor: T a proper ancestor of D (:leaf1 or :c declares {:target [:p]}). THIS diverges. Only a VECTOR :target can produce it: a keyword resolves as a sibling of D (target-path's cond, transition.cljc ~:1625-1630) and :same-state names D itself.

What users feel. Final :state is identical in both systems, so no :state-only test can see it. What differs is everything the ancestor OWNS: its :entry/:exit :data writes, its :after deadlines (XState restarts them, re-frame2 does not), its :spawn children, its epoch. Worked example: a :checkout compound with :entry :stamp-started-at, :after {30000 :expired}, :spawn :price-quote, and {:start-over {:target [:checkout]}} written on the grandchild :review. At 25 s, today: exit :review -> enter :address; started-at stale; the 30 s timer fires 5 s later mid-"fresh" checkout; the old quote child keeps running. Under option 1: exit :review -> exit :checkout -> enter :checkout -> enter :address; timer restarted; child respawned.
Consequence to expect, and correct: when the ancestor now exits, it RECORDS history if it owns a history pseudo-state (the recording is driven by the exit cascade), matching SCXML.

Migration spellings for an author who wants the children reset and the ancestor kept (both identical in re-frame2 and XState):
- target the child you want from D, e.g. from :review {:target [:checkout :address]} (child-declared sibling; T's parent is the domain and survives). Preserves event availability.
- write the transition ON the ancestor ({:target :checkout} on :checkout, the T == D case). Changes event availability: it then fires from every child.

title: FALSE: machines-viz prose says descendant targets survive without reentry
description:
Audit of merged PR #10372 (46250fb5808a727d6cc19707695f5e128d3b8791), source rf2-2n6uv.4.1. The machines-viz prose edits replace self/ancestor with self/compound-declared-descendant but retain the claim that the TARGET does not re-run its own exit/entry without :reenter?. That claim is FALSE for a proper descendant target, the very distinction the updated Spec 005 now carefully explains.

At tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/layout.cljc:346-351, the new text explicitly says a self / compound-declared-descendant target does NOT re-run the target's exit/entry unless :reenter? is true. Related descriptions at layout.cljc:246-252 and grammar.cljc:429-436 similarly attach the restart axis to the target's timers/spawns rather than distinguishing the declaring state from its descendant target.

Concrete counterexample, already covered by existing tests: D=:parent, target T=[:parent :leaf], active at T. Without :reenter?, compute-transition-geometry selects target-descendant-of-decl? and boundary=count(D) (transition.cljc:3295-3298), so T exits and re-enters while D survives. With :reenter?, the boundary is parent(D), so D ALSO restarts. The existing parent-declared-compound-descendant-re-enters-the-descendant test at machine_active_path_geometry_test.clj:325 and Spec 005 Self-transitions describe this correctly. The new ancestor fix is sound; this finding concerns the newly edited explanation, not a request to alter runtime behavior.

Required correction: explain grammar/reenter? as reading the explicit flag, whose effect for self/descendant targets is to restart the DECLARING state. State that a proper descendant target already re-enters without the flag, and that ancestor targets restart independently of it. Keep the helper and renderer/emitter behavior unchanged; no new geometry abstraction, public API, or test framework. Accurate state ownership matters here because this text is used to explain timer/child lifecycle while reading or modifying diagram/export code.
acceptance_criteria: The changed layout and grammar docstrings agree with the existing descendant geometry: self without the flag preserves the declaring state, a compound-declared descendant re-enters that descendant by default, and :reenter? additionally restarts the declaring compound. Ancestor targets remain independent of the flag. Source review against the existing tests/spec is sufficient; no new runtime machinery or broad gate rerun solely for this prose fix.

description:
## What

Three loose ends of the reserved-key refusal that rf2-a5ara landed (PRs #10398 and #10400, merged at trunk edcf243218). Worker ssrsec2-a5ara reported them and correctly left them, being outside its ruling or its fence. Re-verify each at your trunk.

## Items and ruling (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

1. KEBAB ALIAS NOT REFUSED. re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree now refuses key, ref, children and dangerouslySetInnerHTML in an element's :attrs, in bare, :x/, string and symbol spellings. But the KEBAB spelling :dangerously-set-inner-html is still written out as an ordinary escaped attribute, while Fresco's slot rule maps that very spelling into React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
   - RULING: refuse it too. It is an alias of a refused name, and 004B refuses aliases so each reserved slot keeps exactly one spelling.
   - Implement it as "refuse any key whose React prop name canonicalises to a reserved slot", reusing the emitter's existing name canonicalisation (react-prop-name / dom-attr-name), not as a longer literal list. Then any other canonicalising spelling is covered too.
   - Keep :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed, red-first. The hiccup tier is unchanged; it drops.
2. FRESCO REACT EMITTER PARITY. spec/004B says BOTH emitters refuse :children and dangerouslySetInnerHTML in an attribute map. A grep finds no such refusal in Fresco's React emitter (implementation/fresco).
   - Verify by running it, not by grep.
   - If Fresco passes them through, RULING: make Fresco refuse them as 004B says, with a structured error, red-first. The spec is the artefact.
   - STOP and report instead if refusing would break a legitimate Fresco use the spec does not know about, for example a documented React-space escape hatch.
   - Do not change Fresco's React-space :x/ref and :x/key routing: that is the slot mapping, not an attribute map.
3. implementation/ssr-node/src/pool.cjs: the rejection comment in release() still says "err.stack in the detail". That is true only for an UNCAUGHT fault reaching isolate.cjs's error handler. A caught boot exception's stack goes to stderr and its detail is only {modulePath}. Make the comment say so. Prose only.

title: FALSE: route-sub tracing is free of reactive container dependencies
description:
Audit of merged PR #10371 (bf45a99443848894055d37eeae44b92428c4697a), source rf2-tv5ac.3. The revised subs/memo.cljc:194-217 and 278-281 describe trace classification as reaction-safe, without a reactive container read. That claim is FALSE for the built-in route read subs, an exception the PR explicitly left unverified.

Concrete call path: validate-and-trace emits synchronously inside the subscription compute (subs/memo.cljc:683-685); trace.cljc:879-887 projects before delivery with no tracking suppression. classification.cljc:636-649,663-672,707-712 calls :routing/project-route-sub-egress for :rf/route, :rf.route/query and :rf.route/params. routing/sub_egress.cljc:123-126 calls elide-wire-value; elision.cljc:1339-1343 -> elide-against-frame:1147-1150 -> registry-of:122-125 reads the frame runtime-db projection through substrate/read-container. frame.cljc:1739-1754 explicitly identifies this as a reactive projection, and the ratom adapter read is a deref.

In a Reagent/slim reaction with tracing enabled, this adds the entire runtime-db projection as an undeclared dependency of the layer-2 query/params subs, whose declared sole input is [:rf/route] (routing.cljc:412-417). An unrelated runtime change can therefore wake a route leaf even though its route input did not change. The memo wrapper may suppress its body, so this finding does NOT assert a wrong returned route value or prove a user-visible glitch. It concerns real extra dependency capture, invalidation and trace activity, and the corresponding false isolation claim; ordinary non-route sub classification does not take this path.

Required correction: keep route egress classification/redaction while making its policy read non-capturing within a subscription computation using the smallest suitable existing mechanism. Correct the prose to cover the route-specific path. Do not remove redaction, broaden sub-output propagation, or introduce a new public API merely for this fix. Author-reported tests are accepted; this finding follows the concrete source path, not a failing full-suite claim.
acceptance_criteria: A focused Reagent or slim regression keeps :rf.route/query and :rf.route/params observed, enables normal trace projection, and shows the route leaves do not acquire an extra runtime-db dependency or wake solely for unrelated runtime updates. Genuine route changes still update the leaves; sensitive route query/params remain redacted in value and prev-value trace slots. Updated memo prose accurately covers registration classification plus the narrow route projection. Keep the fix bounded; no broad reactive API redesign.

== WORKER VERDICT 2026-09-25 (audit001-core): REPRODUCED RED; STOPPED — the fix needs a new substrate op, which is an operator design call ==

Trunk: 46250fb580. The mayor ruled this a correct stop and declined to widen the fence (a new substrate op extends the adapter contract). Nothing was changed for this bead: memo.cljc prose stays as it is until the mechanism is decided, because correcting it now would record the defect as the contract.

## Reproduction (red, measured)

A new CLJS namespace re-frame.routing-sub-egress-reaction-cljs-test, placed at implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_sub_egress_reaction_cljs_test.cljs, runs on the Reagent adapter with tracing on (dev). Its full source is below. It is NOT in any PR, because a red test cannot land.

Command, from implementation/: node scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test out/node-test.js (exit 0), then node out/node-test.js --test=re-frame.routing-sub-egress-reaction-cljs-test

Result: exit 1, "Ran 1 tests containing 17 assertions. 3 failures, 0 errors."
- Both leaf Reactions, [:rf.route/query] and [:rf.route/params], list the frame's runtime-db projection (rf.frame/runtime-db-container) in their Reagent .-watching array. Their one declared input is [:rf/route], which they also watch.
- One unrelated (rf.frame/swap-runtime-db! f assoc ::unrelated 1) followed by (ratom/flush!) woke both leaves. The leaf traces read [:rf.sub/skip :rf.sub/skip]; the memo wrapper suppressed the body, so the returned values were right.
- The redaction assertions PASSED. The :token and :secret slots are :rf/redacted in both :rf.sub/value and :rf.sub/prev-value of the leaves' :rf.sub/run after a genuine route change, and the leaves update on that change. A fix must keep those green.

A detail for whoever writes the fix: the test's last block (unrelated write AFTER a genuine route change) passes even pre-fix. Its recompute ran through a NON-reactive deref, and Reagent's Reaction -deref with *ratom-context* nil calls f raw, capturing nothing. The first three blocks are the discriminating ones. A probe confirmed the container object was identical and simply not in .-watching after that recompute.

## The capturing read path (verified at source)

subs/memo.cljc validate-and-trace emits :rf.sub/run inside the reaction compute
-> trace.cljc emit! -> maybe-project-marks (synchronous, before delivery)
-> classification.cljc project-trace-event -> project-sub-tags -> project-route-sub-slot
-> late-bound :routing/project-route-sub-egress = routing/sub_egress.cljc project-route-sub-egress (a seed path exists only for :rf/route, :rf.route/query and :rf.route/params)
-> elision.cljc elide-wire-value -> elide-against-frame -> registry-of
-> rf.substrate.adapter/read-container on (rf.frame/runtime-db-container frame-id), a make-derived-value Reaction on the ratom spines. spine.cljs read-container is @container, and Reagent 2.0.1's Reaction -deref calls notify-deref-watcher! whenever *ratom-context* is bound, so it is captured by the leaf being computed.

Non-route subs do not take this path (route-sub-seed-path answers nil, so no registry read). For :rf/route itself the capture duplicates its declared runtime-db input, which is harmless. The damage is to the two layer-2 leaves.

## No existing untracked-read mechanism (the search)

- core/src, the Reagent and reagent-slim adapter sources, and tools/: no code binds *ratom-context* to nil, and nothing calls _peek-at. The only occurrences are inside the substrate implementations themselves: reagent2/ratom.cljs, and Reagent's own Reaction _peek-at.
- re-frame.interop offers ratom, make-reaction, activate-derived-value!, reactive? and dispose!. It has no untracked read.
- The late-bind directory's :adapter/* hooks, and make-ratom-adapter's op list, include :reactive? and :reactive-owner, which READ the capture context. Neither suppresses it.
- Spec 006 defines no untracked or peek read.
- No non-reactive mirror of the per-frame elision registry exists. frame.cljc keeps only the commit-epoch counter beside the containers.

## Sketch of the smallest new op (not implemented; operator's call)

A routed substrate op, e.g. :adapter/read-container-untracked, taking a container and returning its value without registering a reactive dependency:
- core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs: make-ratom-adapter accepts an injected op and routes it with route-hook!. Its chain-bottom is plain read-container, which is correct for the push-based substrates (the React-hook spine, UIx, plain-atom and test-react capture nothing).
- adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs and adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs each supply (fn [c] (binding [ratom/*ratom-context* nil] @c)).
- core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc gets a new :adapter/* entry. The directory pins must move with it: core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj, and the adapters' publication cross-checks such as reagent-slim-adapter-hooks-cross-checked-against-directory.
- A core-side reader, for example in re-frame.interop or re-frame.substrate.adapter. elision.cljc registry-of then reads through it.
- The memo.cljc prose (the §Privacy section and the inline comment at the emit) is corrected to say that the route read-sub projection reads the frame's elision registry NON-capturingly.
- Whether Spec 006 (a hot-zone file) must document the op is part of the same call.

The regression below turns green once registry-of stops capturing.

## A second instance of the same class (code reading only, NOT reproduced)

views.cljs emits :rf.view/rendered INSIDE the view's render. When the view took render args, classification.cljc project-view-rendered-tags -> frame-has-declarations? -> rf.elision/sensitive-declarations -> registry-of makes the same capturing read of the runtime-db projection. On a ratom substrate with tracing on, that would make the view's render reaction depend on runtime-db, so any runtime-db write would re-render it. The fix sketched above covers it too, because it lands in registry-of.

## Reproduction test source (not committed anywhere)

```clojure
(ns re-frame.routing-sub-egress-reaction-cljs-test
  "The route-sub egress projection stays OUT of the reactive graph.

  With tracing on, every `:rf.sub/run` of `:rf.route/query` and
  `:rf.route/params` passes through the routing egress projector, which reads
  the frame's elision registry out of runtime-db to redact the route's
  `:sensitive` query / params. That read happens INSIDE the leaf's reaction
  compute. On a ratom substrate a capturing read there would register the whole
  runtime-db projection as an undeclared input of a leaf whose one declared
  input is `[:rf/route]`, so an unrelated runtime-db write would wake the leaf.

  The suite stands an eager consumer over both leaves (an auto-running
  `ratom/run!` reaction, the stand-in for a mounted view) under the Reagent
  adapter and pins:

    * the leaf reactions watch `[:rf/route]` and NOT the runtime-db
      projection;
    * an unrelated runtime-db write wakes neither leaf (no `:rf.sub/run`, no
      `:rf.sub/skip`);
    * a genuine route change still updates both leaves, and their
      `:rf.sub/run` traces redact the `:sensitive` slots in BOTH `:rf.sub/value`
      and `:rf.sub/prev-value`.

  The ns ends in -cljs-test so the always-on :node-test build runs it."
  (:require [cljs.test :refer-macros [deftest is testing use-fixtures]]
            [reagent.ratom :as ratom]
            [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [re-frame.frame :as rf.frame]
            [re-frame.privacy :as rf.privacy]
            [re-frame.routing :as rf.routing]
            [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as rf.adapter.reagent]
            [re-frame.test-support :as rf.test-support]))

(use-fixtures :each
  (rf.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture
    {:adapter rf.adapter.reagent/adapter
     :init-fn rf.routing/reset-counters!}))

(def ^:private leaf-ids #{:rf.route/query :rf.route/params})

(defn- leaf-sub-traces
  "The `:rf.sub/run` / `:rf.sub/skip` traces the two route leaves emitted —
  one per reaction wake."
  [events]
  (filterv (fn [ev]
             (and (#{:rf.sub/run :rf.sub/skip} (:operation ev))
                  (contains? leaf-ids (get-in ev [:tags :rf.sub/id]))))
           events))

(defn- watches?
  "True when Reagent reaction `rx` currently lists `source` among the reactive
  sources it captured on its last run."
  [rx source]
  (boolean (some #(identical? % source) (array-seq (.-watching ^clj rx)))))

(deftest route-leaves-do-not-capture-the-runtime-db-projection
  (let [f       (rf.frame/make-anon-frame-record! {:doc "route-sub egress reaction frame"})
        traces  (atom [])
        rxs     (atom {})
        visit!  (fn [url]
                  (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.route/handle-url-change url {:rf.route/cause :link}]
                                    {:frame f}))]
    (rf/reg-route :route.sub-egress/vault
                  {:sensitive [[:query :token] [:params :secret]]
                   :query     [:map [:token :string]]}
                  "/vault/:secret")
    (visit! "/vault/first-secret?token=first-token")
    (rf/register-listener! :trace ::leaf-traces (fn [ev] (swap! traces conj ev)))
    (let [driver (ratom/run!
                   (let [q (rf/subscribe [:rf.route/query] {:frame f})
                         p (rf/subscribe [:rf.route/params] {:frame f})]
                     (reset! rxs {:query  q
                                  :params p
                                  :route  (rf/subscribe [:rf/route] {:frame f})})
                     [@q @p]))]
      (try
        (ratom/flush!)
        (let [{:keys [query params route]} @rxs
              runtime-db                   (rf.frame/runtime-db-container f)]
          (testing "the leaves read the route in-process RAW"
            (is (= {:token "first-token"} @query))
            (is (= {:secret "first-secret"} @params)))

          (testing "each leaf watches its declared input and not the runtime-db projection"
            (is (watches? query route) ":rf.route/query watches [:rf/route]")
            (is (watches? params route) ":rf.route/params watches [:rf/route]")
            (is (not (watches? query runtime-db))
                ":rf.route/query carries no runtime-db dependency")
            (is (not (watches? params runtime-db))
                ":rf.route/params carries no runtime-db dependency"))

          (testing "an unrelated runtime-db write wakes neither leaf"
            (reset! traces [])
            (rf.frame/swap-runtime-db! f assoc ::unrelated 1)
            (ratom/flush!)
            (is (= [] (mapv :operation (leaf-sub-traces @traces)))
                "no :rf.sub/run or :rf.sub/skip from either route leaf"))

          (testing "a genuine route change updates both leaves and redacts their traces"
            (reset! traces [])
            (visit! "/vault/second-secret?token=second-token")
            (ratom/flush!)
            (is (= {:token "second-token"} @query))
            (is (= {:secret "second-secret"} @params))
            (let [runs (into {}
                             (keep (fn [ev]
                                     (when (= :rf.sub/run (:operation ev))
                                       [(get-in ev [:tags :rf.sub/id]) (:tags ev)])))
                             (leaf-sub-traces @traces))]
              (is (= #{:rf.route/query :rf.route/params} (set (keys runs)))
                  "both leaves recompute on the route change")
              (is (= rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel
                     (get-in runs [:rf.route/query :rf.sub/value :token])))
              (is (= rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel
                     (get-in runs [:rf.route/query :rf.sub/prev-value :token])))
              (is (= rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel
                     (get-in runs [:rf.route/params :rf.sub/value :secret])))
              (is (= rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel
                     (get-in runs [:rf.route/params :rf.sub/prev-value :secret])))))

          (testing "after a genuine route change the leaves still ignore unrelated runtime-db writes"
            (reset! traces [])
            (rf.frame/swap-runtime-db! f assoc ::unrelated 2)
            (ratom/flush!)
            (is (= [] (mapv :operation (leaf-sub-traces @traces))))
            (is (not (watches? query runtime-db)))
            (is (not (watches? params runtime-db)))))
        (finally
          (rf/unregister-listener! :trace ::leaf-traces)
          (ratom/dispose! driver))))))
```
DECISION NEEDED (mayor, 2026-09-25): OPERATOR HOLD. Do NOT dispatch this bead until Mike picks an option; then record his choice here.

Worker audit001-core reproduced the defect on the node lane with Reagent. Both route leaf reactions list the frame's runtime-db projection in .-watching, and an unrelated runtime-db swap makes both leaves re-run. The worker's note on this bead has the details and the test source.

The required correction ("the smallest suitable EXISTING mechanism") cannot be met: no untracked-read mechanism exists anywhere in core/src, the adapters or tools. The capturing read is elision.cljc `registry-of` -> `substrate.adapter/read-container`, which derefs a Reagent Reaction under a bound *ratom-context*.

The class recurs. views.cljs `:rf.view/rendered` goes through the same `registry-of` read inside a render (found by code reading, not reproduced).

Options:
- A. Add ONE optional substrate op, an untracked read (e.g. :adapter/read-container-untracked).
  - Reagent and reagent-slim implement it as (binding [ratom/*ratom-context* nil] @c).
  - Push-based substrates fall back to plain read-container.
  - Route egress and view-render classification use it.
  - It touches spine.cljs, both ratom adapters, late_bind/directory.cljc and its drift and publication pins, plus spec/006's adapter contract (HOT).
  - It is a small, standard reactive primitive that fixes the whole class.
- B. Keep the behaviour and correct the prose. Tracing is dev-only and production erases it, and the finding shows no wrong returned value. So say plainly that route and view trace classification adds a runtime-db dependency while tracing is on. Cost: extra dev-time invalidations, and trace noise such as :rf.sub/skip rows that could mislead someone reading Xray.
- C. Move the classification out of the reactive compute: defer the projection until after the compute returns. That is likely a larger change to trace delivery than A.

Mayor's recommendation: A. It is one optional op with a safe fallback, it fixes both known instances, and "untracked read" is a primitive every reactive library carries. B is acceptable under the stance if Mike would rather not grow the adapter contract for a dev-only effect.
DOSSIER (mayor, 2026-09-25): at Mike's request, the decision is written up as ai/decisions/rf2-24bwn-untracked-read.md. It sets out options A / B / C with their cost and touch lists; the mayor recommends A. The operator hold stands until Mike rules.
== RULING (mayor-delegated ruling agent, 2026-09-25, under the stance) ==

Written 2026-09-25 14:36:36 AUSEST at trunk 8b807b89ac. Source: the decision dossier ai/decisions/rf2-24bwn-untracked-read.md (the mayor's options A, B and C, with the mayor recommending A) and the independent "Codex Recommendation" review inside it (which also chose A, with refinements). That dossier is deleted once this note is verified, so everything decisive from it is carried below.

## Ruling

Option A, refined. Tracing must not add dependencies to the computation it describes. Add ONE internal, optional substrate op, an untracked container read. The two ratom adapters publish it, and elision.cljc `registry-of` reads through it. That fixes the route-sub instance (reproduced) and the view-render instance (found by reading, then confirmed at reaction level by the Codex probe) in one place.

B is rejected. It would document a debugging tool that perturbs what it observes: with tracing on, views re-render and route leaves wake on unrelated runtime-db writes, and Xray shows :rf.sub/skip rows that read like route activity. memo.cljc's own §Privacy prose already names a capture inside a compute as breaking the glitch-free db -> layer-1 -> layer-2 layering.

C is rejected. It moves trace delivery timing, which spec/009's two-tier timing rule and several tests pin, to reach the same outcome.

OPERATOR HOLD LIFTED. This bead is now DISPATCHABLE as one bounded worker item. The mayor dispatches it, and this note does not change its status.

SUPERSEDED CLAUSE. The description's "Required correction ... using the smallest suitable EXISTING mechanism" is superseded by this ruling. No such mechanism exists (the worker's search recorded above stands), and the new internal op is the ruled mechanism, so an implementer must not stop on that clause again. The description's other limits still stand, and this ruling satisfies them: redaction stays, there is no sub-output propagation, and the op is NOT a public or app-facing API. The acceptance criteria are extended by the regressions listed below.

## The refined contract (exact)

1. WHAT. `read-container-untracked`: given a container, it returns exactly the value `read-container` would return at that point, and it records NO dependency on the enclosing reactive computation. Otherwise it evaluates exactly as `read-container` would there. In particular, it must NOT switch the substrate into its non-reactive read path (see Correction 2).
2. SHAPE. It is an optional routed late-bind hook, `:adapter/read-container-untracked` (the name is the implementer's call). `make-ratom-adapter` publishes it through `route-hook!`. It is NOT an adapter-map key, so the ten-fn adapter contract (6 required + 3 optional + 1 lifecycle) is unchanged. Spec 006 §make-derived-value already sets this precedent for `:adapter/derived-container?` and `:adapter/activate-derived-value!`. Where the Codex review says "optional in the adapter map", read it as optional in the late-bind table.
3. FALLBACK. Plain `read-container` is a correct fallback ONLY for substrates whose reads capture nothing: the React-hook spine/UIx, plain-atom, test-react and SSR. A substrate whose reads capture dependencies MUST publish the hook to be conformant. Say this ONCE in Spec 006, beside the two sibling hooks. Add no capability negotiation and no runtime warning. An adapter that omits the hook gets today's behaviour, which is extra dev-time invalidation and never a wrong value: trust the programmer.
4. CORE READER. One internal (^:no-doc) fn in `re-frame.substrate.adapter`, beside `read-container`. `registry-of` is the one call site that matters today.

## Correction 1: the chain-bottom cannot BE read-container

The dossier says make-ratom-adapter's "chain-bottom is plain read-container". But `route-hook!` (substrate/adapter.cljc) calls its fallback as a ZERO-argument thunk, `(if previous (previous a) (fallback-fn))`, so a chain-bottom never sees the container and cannot read it. Mirror the `container-class-unknown` precedent instead: the routed hook's fallback returns a no-opinion sentinel, and the core reader falls back to `read-container` when the hook is unpublished OR answers the sentinel. Use a sentinel rather than nil, because nil is a legitimate container value.

## Correction 2: suppress capture WITHOUT the non-reactive read path (measured)

Both the dossier and the Codex review spell the op as `(fn [c] (binding [ratom/*ratom-context* nil] @c))`. The runtime-db projection is a Reaction: on the ratom spine, `make-derived-value` is `(make-reaction (build-recompute-fn ...))` (spine.cljs). For a Reaction, that spelling takes the NON-REACTIVE branch, whose first act is `(when non-reactive (flush!))`. That drains the substrate's whole reaction queue synchronously, inside the enclosing compute.

The source for this is stock Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent/ratom.cljs` Reaction `-deref` (lines 465-467 in the 2.0.1 jar) and reagent-slim `reagent2/ratom.cljs` `-deref` (lines 415-417 at 8b807b89ac). reagent-slim's own `pr-atom` comment already records it: reading a Reaction "under a nil context would additionally force a `flush!` and an on-demand recompute — a behaviour change well beyond suppressing capture."

Measured 2026-09-25 by this ruling agent, under node, on the mayor checkout's compiled node-test bundle. Stock reagent.ratom is 2.0.1, whose compiled source Codex matched to the installed JAR. reagent2.ratom was compiled 2026-08-07, and its -deref flush branch is unchanged in current source. The probe did the read inside an auto-run reaction T, whose container was a non-auto-run Reaction kept live by a watcher. It compared three spellings of the read:
- tracked: plain `@c` (today's behaviour);
- nil: `*ratom-context*` bound to nil;
- sink: `*ratom-context*` bound to a throwaway `(js-obj)`.

Case 1 left an unrelated reaction dirty in the queue, then fired T:
- how often the neighbour ran INSIDE T's compute: tracked 0, nil 1, sink 0;
- whether T watches the container: tracked true, nil false, sink false;
- the value was the same in all three.

Case 2 left a reaction D dirty in the queue, then had its auto-run parent pull D before the queue reached it. D's own compute did the read:
- D's runs for one change: tracked 1, nil 2, sink 1;
- the maximum re-entry depth: tracked 1, nil 2, sink 1.

The results were identical on both kernels (12 of 12 rows).

So the nil spelling suppresses the edge, but it can also run unrelated reactions mid-compute and RE-ENTER a reaction whose own compute is still on the stack. The next step is from source reading and was NOT measured: `deref-capture` resets `.-captured` at entry, so the inner run clobbers the outer run's capture list. That risks a missed dependency, and so a wrong value, which is strictly worse than the extra invalidation this bead fixes. The sink spelling suppresses the edge and changes nothing else: it is exactly today's evaluation minus the dependency.

The ratom implementation is therefore:
- Inside a reactive context, read with the capture context bound to a fresh throwaway object. Stock Reagent ships this as public API: `reagent.ratom/check-derefs` runs f under `(js-obj)` (line 561 in the 2.0.1 jar). So the Reagent adapter can inject `#(first (ratom/check-derefs (fn [] @%)))` or the equivalent `binding`. reagent-slim can bind `reagent2.ratom/*ratom-context*` to `(js-obj)`, or add a kernel twin of check-derefs; either is fine.
- Outside a reactive context, do a plain read. There is no edge to suppress, and the sink would push a non-reactive read onto the reactive branch.

Both kernels declare `*ratom-context*` with `(declare ^:dynamic ...)` and already bind it (reagent2 in `call-with-ratom-context`), so no kernel change is needed.

## Implementation brief (for the eventual worker)

Fence. These files change:

title: INCOMPLETE: root lifecycle tracing misaddresses Xray source links
description:
PR #10407 (abc2be08ce6f7f72e4259ba135bd783cf2c6b8fe), source rf2-2n6uv.5.1, correctly runs root entry/exit but does not carry their root declaration location into Xray action rows. transition.cljc run-root-action:3045 passes state [] only to the structured cascade; collect-actions:2217 calls run-action without a root discriminator, and run-action:2063 emits action-id/phase/input but no declaring state. projection.cljc action-cascade-row:904 therefore cannot distinguish root from child boundary actions. enrich-cascade-rows:1290 borrows surrounding transition states; format.cljc:498-501 derives inline entry/exit source keys from those borrowed child states.

Concrete case: a machine with inline root entry/exit and a leaf :a later transitioning to :b/final emits root lifecycle rows whose source keys can resolve to [:states :a :entry] or a leaf :exit instead of root [:entry]/[:exit]. With no nearby transition the link is absent. Named action definition links already use [:actions id] and are not affected. The source implementation handoff acknowledges this limitation, but no separate open correction was found. This is actionable because click-to-source can send a programmer debugging a root hook to unrelated child code, beyond a cosmetic label.

Required correction: carry the actual root action declaration through the trace/projection and use it for root action source resolution and the state label, preserving existing child and named-action behavior. Account for root source coordinates instead of relying on the current state-spec-path-prefix, which deliberately elides []. Keep this an internal tooling correction, with no new public API or broader trace redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Focused projection/source-resolution coverage for inline root entry and exit, with distinct child hooks and surrounding transitions, proves root rows resolve the root declaration or safely omit an unavailable link, never a child declaration. Named action and ordinary child lifecycle source links remain correct. Document any added trace field in the existing trace contract.
notes:
RULING (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance): ACCEPTED as a real defect. It is not minutiae, and this corrects the mayor's own earlier disposition on rf2-2n6uv.5.1's close reason. A click-to-source link that sends a programmer debugging a root hook into unrelated child code is wrong information from a debugging tool, not a cosmetic label.
Direction: carry the declaring node through the trace the smallest way that works. The root step already passes state [] to the structured cascade, so thread that same state (or a root discriminator) into run-action's emitted trace, and have Xray's action-cascade-row and format use it for the source key and the state label. Keep child and named-action behaviour unchanged. Add no new trace event and no new public API. Red first: a machine with inline root entry/exit and a leaf transition must produce root action rows whose source keys resolve to [:entry] / [:exit].
Audit PR #10427 follow-up: rf2-j3qdj — INCOMPLETE: root lifecycle source keys have no macro-stamped source coordinates. Separate open finding; existing status and content preserved.

title: xstate-parity: pure Level-1 machine-transition result cannot say whether the event was HANDLED (no snapshot.can / getNextTransitions analogue; engine computes handled? and the facade drops it)
description:
## Gap

XState v6's pure surface answers "can this event be taken from here?" two ways: `snapshot.can(event)` evaluates guards against the current snapshot and returns a boolean, and `getNextTransitions(snapshot)` enumerates the candidate transitions from the active configuration (exact, wildcard, `always`, `after`) with their targets, sources and whether a guard is attached.

re-frame2's pure Level-1 result `machine-transition def snapshot event -> {:status :snapshot :fx}` cannot say whether the event was handled: an UNHANDLED event and a MATCHED targetless no-op transition (an action returning `nil`) produce `=` results — `{:status :ok :snapshot <unchanged> :fx []}` both times. The engine computes the fact (`re-frame.machines.result/handled?`, stamped on every `:ok` Result and used to gate the `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` trace) and the facade's `public-result` drops it. Xray's Sim mode has already paid for this: its spec says a step that moved nothing "surfaces as one inline diagnostic naming all three possible causes (no transition matched · a guard declined · the matched transition was a no-op), because the engine's public result cannot tell them apart". There is no enabled-events query at all; the closest is the static, whole-machine `declared-event-inputs` in `re-frame.machines.tooling`.

## XState evidence

- Executed: `xs/C-8.mjs` → `xs/C-8.out`: `getNextTransitions from idle: [{"eventType":"go","target":["working"],"guard":true,…},{"eventType":"reset",…},{"eventType":"*",…},{"eventType":"","target":["never"],"guard":true,…}]`; `snapshot.can(stop): true can(go): false can(kick): true`.
- `xs/node_modules/xstate/dist/declarations/src/transition.d.ts` (`getNextTransitions` and its ordering), `xs-docs/snapshots.md` (`can(...)` in the cheatsheet), `xs-docs/states.md`.

## re-frame2 evidence

- Executed: `jvm/C/c1.clj` → `jvm/C/c1.out` (fe8de195bd): `pure unhandled [:nope]: {:status :ok, :snapshot {:state :idle, :data {:n 0}}, :fx []}` / `pure matched no-op [:noop]: {:status :ok, :snapshot {:state :idle, :data {:n 0}}, :fx []}` / `identical public result for no-match vs matched-no-op? true` / `public result keys: (:status :snapshot :fx)`. Control: `pure handled [:go]` moves to `:working`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/result.cljc:134-151` — `with-handled` / `handled?` ("Stamp the optional `::handled?` flag onto an `:ok` Result … `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` trace exactly once when EVERY region declines").
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:123-137` — `public-result` projects `{:status :snapshot :fx}` only; its comment: "None of that is the app's business."
- spec/005 §Testing Level 1 (4257-4287): "An event no transition matched is `:status :ok` with the snapshot unchanged and `:fx []` — a benign no-op, not a failure."
- `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1462` — the Sim rail "lists the current state's outgoing `:on` transitions with their targets … tagging a guarded one `[guard]` without predicting a verdict, and a step that moved nothing surfaces as one inline diagnostic naming all three possible causes … because the engine's public result cannot tell them apart".

## Why it matters

Table-driven and property tests at Level 1 (the level the spec recommends as "fastest") cannot assert "this event is NOT accepted in this state" — the forbidden-event test the XState testing page calls out as part of a machine's behaviour — without registering a machine and reading traces. Tooling and AI agents asking "what can this machine do next?" (Xray Sim, the pair skill's dry-run) get a static list with no verdict. Both are one field away from the engine.

## Options

1. **Expose `:handled?` on the Level-1 result (runtime, tiny).** `public-result` adds `:handled? true|false` to the `:ok` map (the engine's flag; `true` when absent today). Spec: one line under §Testing Level 1 and Spec-Schemas' result shape. Additive; breaks nothing (callers destructure).
2. **Add a pure `enabled-events` / `can-handle?` query (runtime, small).** `re-frame.machines/can-handle? def snapshot event` → boolean by running the pure transition and reading the flag; and a tooling-side `next-transitions def snapshot` in `re-frame.machines.tooling` enumerating the candidates along the active path (exact, `:ns/*`, `:*`, `:always`, `:after`) with `:guard?` and targets — the `getNextTransitions` analogue, unevaluated, which Xray Sim already half-builds.
3. Leave it; read the `:rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op` trace at Level 3. That is where today's tests are, and it makes the cheapest test level the wrong level for the question.

## Recommendation

Option 1 now (it is the fact the engine already has, and it turns Xray's three-cause diagnostic into two), with option 2's `next-transitions` enumerator left to a consumer that needs it beyond Sim.

## Fence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc` (`public-result`), `machines/result.cljc` (no change)
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (HOT ZONE — §Testing Level 1, 4262-4275) and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (HOT ZONE) if the result shape is schema'd there
- `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1462` (the diagnostic can drop one cause) and `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim.cljs` if Sim adopts it
- test: `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_transition_public_result_test.clj` (new) or beside the existing Level-1 tests

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/machines`; `npm run test:cljs` if Xray consumes it; conformance corpus untouched unless a fixture pins the result keys.

## Decision needed

No.

title: Xray machine rows: root lifecycle source links, region transition-action keys, root :spawn child in cascade
description:
## What

Two merged PRs added engine metadata that Xray's machine rows do not yet read. Re-verify each item at your trunk.

1. **Root lifecycle source links.** PR #10442 (rf2-j3qdj, trunk 993afa1f90) now stamps `:source-coords` / `:source-code` on the machine root at `[]` and on each region body at `[:regions r]`. Region links already work with today's Xray code. A ROOT `:entry` / `:exit` row still shows no link, because two functions skip the root path:
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`, `state-node-source-coords`
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`, `cascade-row-source-form`
2. **Region transition-action keys.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/format.cljc` builds a transition action's source key without the row's `:region`. So it never reaches the new `[:regions r :states … :on …]` metadata, and a region transition's inline action shows no link.
3. **Root `:spawn` child.** PR #10436 (rf2-rkkse, trunk 1f56b77b6e) added a machine-lifetime child spawned at the root (invoke-id `[]`). The worker reported that the Xray cascade view does not draw it yet.

## Ruling (mayor, 2026-09-25, under the stance)

- **Item 1.** Root lifecycle rows resolve against the root's `[]` metadata directly.
  - Do NOT add a fallback that sends an unresolvable `[:states …]` key to the root's coordinate. A missing link is honest; a link to the root form for a state row would point at the wrong place.
- **Item 2.** Include the row's `:region` when building the key, so a region transition's inline action resolves against `[:regions r :states … :on …]`.
- **Item 3.**
  - If the cascade already draws a STATE's spawned child, draw the root child the same way, reusing that vocabulary.
  - If it has no place to hang it, report that rather than inventing one.
  - If the premise does not hold (the root child already shows), say so with the evidence.
- No new API. Put new tests in NEW files, not in an existing test file.
- Each item needs a regression that is red with its fix removed. Item 1's test registers a literal machine and checks that the root row's link resolves.

## Surface

tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/ (projection.cljc, view.cljs, format.cljc, and the cascade code if item 3 applies), plus new test files under tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/.

## Gates

- CLJS lanes: rely on CI.

title: machines-viz chart: a machine root's :entry/:exit/:tags are dropped from the chart projection (the engine honours them)
description:
## What

Worker mviz4-6p7jr reported this while mirroring the machine-root refusal into the viz grammar (rf2-6p7jr, PR #10414). PR #10407 made the engine honour a root's `:entry`, `:exit` and `:tags`. The machines-viz CHART drops all three silently. The worker checked a flat root and a parallel root that each declared all three: the chart output carried every state's own actions and tags, and none of the root's.

Mermaid and SCXML show entry/exit/tags for NO state, so the root is not a special case there; leave them alone.

## Required correction
Make the chart project a root's `:entry`, `:exit` and `:tags` the same way it projects a state's, wherever the chart already shows a state's actions and tags. Reuse the existing state-level projection; add no new visual vocabulary unless the root has no node to hang them on, and in that case report it rather than inventing one. title: machines: a function-valued :spawn-all :children throws a host IllegalArgumentException instead of :rf.error/machine-spawn-all-bad-shape
description:
A :spawn-all whose :children is a FUNCTION (rather than the literal vector the grammar requires) throws a host java.lang.IllegalArgumentException on the JVM instead of being refused with :rf.error/machine-spawn-all-bad-shape. Measured by the completeness pass of rf2-ahrss at c456e717e9; not independently reproduced by the mayor.

The grammar check that :children is a literal vector is at implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:306-311 (the refusal exists); the host exception suggests something touches the value before that check runs, or the check is not reached on this path. A user who writes a function there, the natural spelling for a runtime-sized fan-out, gets a stack trace instead of the error the guide tells them to read.

Low priority; verify first, then either route the function through the existing refusal or refuse it earlier.
notes:

REPRODUCED on the JVM at trunk 016e3cc7dd plus the rf2-hefqg commit.
- Registering {:initial :s :states {:s {:spawn-all {:children (fn [_] [...]) :on-all-complete [:done]}}}} raised java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Don't know how to create ISeq from: <fn>.
- It was thrown at validation.cljc:2191, in validate-spawn-spec-keys!, called from validate-machine! (validation.cljc:2495).

CAUSE: the premise holds, as "something touches the value before that check runs".
- validate-spawn-spec-keys! walks (get-in node [:spawn-all :children]) with doseq, to scan each child's keys.
- It runs in validate-machine! BEFORE validate-spawn-all!, whose check that :children is a non-empty vector (validation.cljc ~306-311) would have refused the fn.

FIX (route the fn through the existing refusal). In implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc, validate-spawn-spec-keys! now scans :children only when it is seqable?. Anything else reaches validate-spawn-all! and is refused with :rf.error/machine-spawn-all-bad-shape, ":children must be a non-empty vector of child specs". The file is .cljc, so the CLJS path is covered by the same guard; there a seq of a fn throws a JS Error. No CLJS test pins it.

title: docs/api review in four serial steps: completeness, correctness, quality, holistic structure
description:
Mike asked (2026-09-26) for a review of docs/api/ (24 pages), in FOUR SERIAL steps. Each step reviews the tree the previous step left. It produces a read-only report, which is triaged, and then its accepted findings are applied as one commit. Step N+1 starts only on the tree step N produced.

1. COMPLETENESS: compare what is taught with the full API.
   - Are the happy path AND the unhappy paths discussed?
   - Are errors explained: which error ids a reader can meet, what each means, and how to recover?
   - Are values fully enumerated, each with the explanation it needs (option keys, states, statuses, enum values)?
   - Are the likely use cases covered?
   The source of truth for "the full API" is the implementation and spec/api-manifest.edn; the spec comes second.
2. CORRECTNESS: check every factual claim and every code sample against the implementation (then the spec). Evaluate samples where the code is portable. A spec or implementation defect found along the way is filed as its own bead, not fixed here.
3. QUALITY: review for a human senior developer, against docs/AUTHORING.md.
   - Do the docs make a good tutorial, with progressive disclosure?
   - Are they cohesive and consistent?
   - Are they human-friendly?
   - Do they use good, simple examples that build progressively?
4. HOLISTIC QUALITY: repeat step 3, taking a view of the folder as a whole.
   - Is the current set of pages the right way to teach this?
   - Do they have the right structure? Should the tutorial structure be improved?
   - Should new pages be created, content be moved between pages, or pages be removed?
   Step 4's report states each structural proposal with its reasons. The mayor rules on them under the stance before any page is created, moved, split or removed. Keep or update every inbound anchor, and grep the repo for links into a page before moving or removing it.

How it runs: one worktree and one worker per step (or one worker running the steps in order), with one PR per step, or one PR for the whole bead if the steps are small. Every step names the gates that actually cover what it changed. Per CLAUDE.md § Build & Test, check_doc_slugs.py, mkdocs build --strict and the fenced-block and zero-link caveats all apply. The worker verifies anchors and table column counts by hand and says so. Prose follows AUTHORING.md and the present-tense rule.

Scope: Reference pages, one per artefact namespace. For an API reference, step 1 means every public var and option in spec/api-manifest.edn has an entry, and step 3/4 judge the pages as REFERENCE rather than tutorial: scannable, consistent entry shape across pages, links out to the guides for teaching.

SEQUENCING: several live changes touch docs/api now. re-frame.machines.md (rf2-yocd0, PR #10509), re-frame.ssr.md (rf2-kz6ki), re-frame.http.md (possibly, rf2-k3v1o/n1w8n), re-frame.core.md (rf2-82qih), re-frame.resources.md (rf2-n8hbe, rf2-rzsv5, queued). Start once those have merged. The manifest-tier decisions in rf2-pd54a (held with rf2-kusgs) decide which vars count as public, so step 1 reads that bead's ruling.

title: skills: family descriptions still use ~108% of Claude Code's listing budget; lower the ratchet after the review PRs merge
description:
From GitHub issue #10543 (closed into this bead). Original text:

**Type:** task · **Priority:** P3 · **Do after:** the nine skill-review PRs merge (#10529–#10531, #10533–#10537, #10539)

## Gap
`scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py` measures the nine skill descriptions against Claude Code's whole-listing budget:
- **Before the review PRs:** 8,853 characters, about 110% of that budget.
- **With all nine review PRs combined:** 8,618 characters. Measured by applying every branch's `SKILL.md` on top of main.
- **Budget:** the script reports the family at **107.7%** of the whole-listing budget, meaning about 8,000 characters. Past that point, whole descriptions are dropped from the listing, lowest priority first. The family is still over.
- **Ratchet:** the pinned ceiling `FAMILY_FOOTPRINT_CEILING = 8_864` allows the family to grow back by ~250 characters unnoticed.

## What to do
1. After the review PRs merge, re-run `python3 scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py --verbose` on main and lower `FAMILY_FOOTPRINT_CEILING` to the measured footprint, keeping the ratchet tight.
2. Decide whether to get the family under 100%: trim descriptions family-wide, or accept that low-priority skills may drop out of the listing. Each skill's trigger evals (`skills/*/evals/`) should be re-checked after any trim.
3. In the same pass, refresh the dated size records in `skills/README.md` (~L312-315), which several reviews made stale, for example `known-frictions.md`, `phase-2-impl-order.md` and the reagent-migration catalogues.

## Acceptance
- The ceiling equals the measured footprint on main.
- The listing-budget decision is recorded.
- The `skills/README.md` size records are current.

MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): all nine review PRs have merged (#10529-#10531, #10533-#10537, #10539).
(1) Lower FAMILY_FOOTPRINT_CEILING to the footprint measured on main.
(2) Get the family UNDER 100% of the listing budget by trimming descriptions family-wide. A skill silently dropped from the listing fails to trigger with no signal, which is worse than a shorter description. Keep each skill's trigger words, and trim the lowest-value clauses first. After the trim, lower the ceiling again to the new footprint.
(3) Refresh the dated size records in skills/README.md.
Trigger evals need a live-model harness a worker may not have: run them if it is available, and otherwise say plainly that they were not run.

title: Story Tests pane: render the variant's framed canvas inside the pane and run through the one run owner with :runner :auto (DOM-step variants read falsely failed; the pane destroys the canvas frame)
description:
Split from rf2-5oj7o item 15 by the Story fixes worker (worker/storyfix-5oj7o, PR #10558), measured 2026-09-26.
The Tests pane runs DOM-step variants headless: its run opts carry no :runner. Raising the runner alone does not fix it. The :test tab renders test-view INSTEAD of framed-canvas (shell.cljs main-pane `case mode-tab`), so no variant view is mounted while the pane runs; DOM steps resolve under [data-test="story-canvas-frame"] or the document, and would FAIL instead of refusing. A second symptom: the pane's reset-variant destroys the canvas's own frame and re-runs its play headless, which leaves the canvas reading PLAY FAIL.
MAYOR RULING (2026-09-26): option (a). The Tests pane renders the variant's framed canvas inside itself (for example a "view" section at the top of the pane), and re-runs go through the one run owner (rerun!/listen-runs!) with :runner :auto. The canvas's own runs also carry :runner :auto, so a DOM variant's unified result stops carrying false :cannot-run rows. The pane must not destroy the canvas's frame. Regressions for both symptoms. Regenerate the docs/story Test-mode screenshot afterwards; that needs the shadow-cljs lane through the mayor.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor, 2026-09-26)
HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/storyfix-5oj7o (PR #10558, rf2-5oj7o / rf2-bdj6r; it edits tools/story/src). Dispatch once that PR MERGES.
HELD — SEQUENCED BEHIND worker/storyfix-5oj7o: DISCHARGED — PR #10558 merged at trunk 34a833ac37 on 2026-09-27.
== IMPLEMENTED (worker storyfix2-o9jja, 2026-09-27 04:49 AUSEST) — PR #10573, commit "fix(story): the Tests pane renders the canvas and re-runs through its run owner (rf2-o9jja)", built to the mayor ruling option (a).

What changed:
- The Tests pane renders the shell's framed canvas at its top (test-view takes the canvas as a second arg; data-test story-test-canvas). The canvas owns the variant's run.
- Both preparers of the canvas's run, the canvas itself and the shell's selection edge (ensure-variant-frame!), now pass one public ui.canvas/run-opts, which carries :runner :auto. A DOM variant therefore selects :dom and runs against the mounted view.
- The pane runs nothing itself. test-mode.state/follow-run! is a runtime/listen-runs! listener that stores every settled run of the variant the pane shows, whoever started it, and drops superseded generations.
- Re-run (run-variant-pane!) calls prepare-run! with the canvas's run-opts and then resume-run!. It no longer calls reset-variant, so it never destroys the frame.
- The pane records the variant it shows (show-variant!) on every change and never clears it on unmount. Reagent disposed the mounted pane's with-let state between renders, and the with-let finally cleared the slot while a run was settling. That was traced by stack in the browser lane (reagent.impl.component cleanup -> ratom dispose -> with-let-destroy -> show-variant! nil), and it made both promotion-row DOM tests red.
- Spec 003, spec 009 (new View section 0, Run semantics) and docs/story chapters 04 and 05 describe the new run semantics.

Regressions, each shown red with its fix removed:
- Node lane, one_run_owner_cljs_test (4 deftests). With :runner :auto removed from run-opts, Re-run reverted to reset-variant and the follow-run! registration disabled, the targeted run read 61 tests / 176 assertions with 11 failures. Those included: the canvas's run and the selection-edge run :headless instead of :dom with a :runner-lacks-capability refusal; the Re-run destroying the frame once (expected 0), with the generation not advancing; and the pane not storing the shown variant's run. Restored and verified by blob hash (git hash-object == git rev-parse HEAD:path for canvas.cljs and test_mode/state.cljs); the same targeted run then read 0 failures.
- Browser lane, pane_canvas_dom_cljs_test: a [:click]-then-[:assert-dom] variant passes through the pane with :runner :dom before and after Re-run, and the canvas stamps data-run-status "pass". The promotion_row and view_variant_switch DOM tests mount the pane with its canvas.
- The with-let finding: at the commit before that fix the browser lane read 1158 tests / 6356 assertions with 6 failures, all in promotion_row_dom_cljs_test ("the canvas's run reached the pane" nil). With the fix it read 1158 / 6356 / 0.

- npm run test:browser on the rebased tree read 1158 / 6357, 0 failures.
- JVM tools/story read 2118 / 8082, 0 failures.

Screenshot: story-tutorial-04-test-mode.png was regenerated with docs/scripts/generate-story-tutorial-screenshots.cjs. It shows the canvas at the top of the Tests pane.

For the mayor, not fixed here, pre-existing: after the step-debugger's Start (prepare-variant calls reset-run-owner!, which drops the owner's stored :opts), the play chip's rerun! runs with nil opts, which means headless and no run-key. The pane's own Re-run is immune because it passes explicit opts.
