title: Read continuation reply :value leaks an enveloped infinite feed's declared item fields
description:
Sibling of rf2-cudar, found while fixing it (PR #10624). Same defect, different carrier: the READ continuation reply.

An infinite feed's `:reply-to` `:value` is the MERGED item list (re-frame.resources.events/infinite-reply-value, Spec 016 §Read completion continuations). At off-box egress, re-frame.resources.trace-egress/redact-reply-declarations runs re-frame.resources.classification/redact-continuation-reply, whose carrier-decl-paths re-roots a page-relative `:data` declaration under `:value`. For an enveloped feed (`:page->items :items`, declaration `[[:data :items :ssn]]`) that yields `[:value :items :ssn]`, which names nothing in a list of bare items. Index-free walking skips sequence positions, not map keys.

Measured on the JVM at trunk 1c338d310c, calling the public fn directly:
- `(redact-continuation-reply {:value [{:ssn SECRET :name "public"}]} {:sensitive [[:data :items :ssn]] :page->items :items})` returns the value UNREDACTED;
- control: with `{:sensitive [[:data :ssn]]}` (a vector-page feed) the same value comes back with `:ssn :rf/redacted`.

rf2-cudar fixed the READ SUBS by projecting the merged list through the same accessor over the raw pages (trace_egress/project-merged-items). The reply carrier holds only the merged value, not the pages, so that fix does not transfer directly. Either the reply must be classified where it is built (events/infinite-reply-value has the entry's pages) or the egress projector needs the pages. Choosing that is part of this item. Keep raw in-process delivery (the app's own `:reply-to` handler is entitled to the decoded body).
notes:
== FENCE: routed to worker/resegress-lafas (PR #10624), 2026-09-29 17:12 AUSEST. Do not dispatch separately. Cleared when that worker either reports this bead done in #10624 or declines it; if it declines, dispatch fresh after #10624 merges (its surface: implementation/resources/src, spec/016-Resources.md). ==
== WHERE THE CLASSIFICATION CAN HAPPEN (from the rf2-cudar worker, PR #10624; source-verified at trunk 2daba64dd7)

- SOURCE-SIDE IS NOT AVAILABLE AS-IS. The reply map built at events/infinite-reply-value IS what the app's own `:reply-to` handler receives in-process, so redacting its `:value` there breaks raw in-process delivery. trace_egress/redact-reply-declarations documents this: reads redact at egress deliberately, because the handler and the trusted-local `:rf.egress/include-sensitive?` opt-in are entitled to the decoded body.
- EGRESS-SIDE (trace_egress/redact-reply-declarations) has the merged `:value`, the `:resource/key` and the current owner spec, but NOT the pages. The read-sub fix (trace_egress/project-merged-items: redact the raw pages, then merge them through the same accessor) needs the pages. Three candidate routes:
  (a) read the live entry's pages for the reply's key at egress, merge-check them against `:value`, and fail closed on mismatch; this can go stale when egress runs after a load-more;
  (b) translate paths for a keyword accessor (a path through the accessor key loses that key; keep the as-is path for vector pages) and fail closed, redacting the whole `:value`, for a callable accessor;
  (c) add a pages or classification carrier to the reply, which changes the reply shape (a Spec 016 contract question).
== FENCE CLEARED: worker/resegress-lafas (PR #10624) DECLINED this bead, 2026-09-29 17:19 AUSEST. Dispatch fresh after #10624 merges (its surface: implementation/resources/src, spec/016-Resources.md). ==
== MAYOR RULING 2026-09-29 17:19 AUSEST: route (b) ==
Of the three routes above, take (b): at egress, translate the declared page-relative paths through a KEYWORD accessor (a path through the accessor key loses that key; a vector page keeps the as-is path), and for a CALLABLE accessor fail closed by redacting the whole `:value` off-box whenever the feed declares sensitive paths.
Why under the stance: it is the smallest change, it covers the spec's own shape (`:page->items :items`), it adds no reply-shape contract, and it cannot go stale the way (a) can. Failing closed off-box costs nothing in-process: the app's `:reply-to` handler and the trusted-local include-sensitive opt-in still receive the raw body.
Not (a): a staleness race needs its own mismatch handling. Not (c): it would change the reply shape for one carrier.
Record the callable fail-closed behaviour in one Spec 016 sentence beside the continuation-reply egress text. Regression: the enveloped keyword feed redacted, a callable-accessor feed redacted wholesale, and a vector-page feed unchanged as the control. Show each red with the fix removed.

title: Incomplete async-effect example lets a late clipboard reply mutate a recreated frame
description:
PR #10670 audit, merge 6046a26e5ee29165b9532225467a34db6bfc685a: docs/async/custom-effects.md introduces a clipboard effect that closes over ctx :frame, then uses rf/dispatch with {:frame frame} in both Promise completions. That ctx value is a frame-id keyword (implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1691), so the callback addresses whichever incarnation currently owns the id. The copy-token guard only distinguishes requests within the same app-db lifetime. Destroying and recreating the article frame restarts its token at 1; a late token-1 completion from the old frame can mark the new frame's pending copy complete or failed. The lifecycle guidance that a destroyed frame's callback is dropped is incomplete when that id is reused.

Measured with a focused JVM probe of the example's unchanged issuing/reply handlers and a deferred custom fx callback: create frame :audit/article, issue copy 1, retain callback, destroy the frame, recreate :audit/article, issue its copy 1, then run the old callback. Successor state became #:article{:copy-token 1, :copy-status :copied}, even though its own callback was not run. Control: the dispatch-sync operation obtained from rf/capture-frame before destruction left the successor at :copying. Probe attempt 2 exited 0, using only implementation/core's JVM classpath; no shadow-cljs build. Evidence log is ai/gate-clipboard-lifecycle-audit-sep23-monitor-2.log; the decisive measurement is inline here so it survives cleanup.

Small correction: use the existing (rf/capture-frame frame) inside the effect before registering Promise callbacks, and its captured dispatch in both success and failure callbacks. Keep the request-token guard for overlapping copies. Match the async-lifetime guidance and sample test to this behavior; docs/api/re-frame.core.md#capture-frame already documents and demonstrates this exact pattern. No new runtime API or cancellation infrastructure is needed.
acceptance_criteria: The example captures its issuing frame instance before the Promise callbacks. Old success and failure callbacks leave a same-id replacement frame unchanged; a current callback still updates it, and the existing per-request token guard remains. Explain the lifecycle boundary using capture-frame and verify the changed example with a focused probe.

title: epoch: restore-rewinds-route-slice-and-route-sub never subscribes a route sub
description:
Owner: rf2-98kzs.14 (found while pruning implementation/epoch/test; not fixed there).

`re-frame.epoch-test/restore-rewinds-route-slice-and-route-sub` never subscribes to a route sub.

It registers two routes, writes the route slice through framework-authority handlers, restores the earlier epoch, and then reads the slice through `rf/frame-state-value` (`[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/routing :current :route-id]`). No subscription is created, so the "route-sub" half of the name is unpinned: nothing shows that a route subscription observes the rewound slice. A rewind that updated the container but left route-sub caches stale would pass.

Fix shape: subscribe to the current-route sub before the restore, and assert its value after the restore.

title: Live HTTP, Fresco and epoch examples in the core guide (docs/core/, outside fresco/)
description:
## This section

`docs/core/` outside `fresco/` is the core guide. It already has ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells on 10 pages, but only for core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. Look for the places where it teaches something that can now run:
- `views.md`: the closing "another way to write views" passage introduces Fresco. A Fresco cell beside the `reg-view` one can show the same counter both ways.
- `effects.md`: the HTTP section (`:rf.http/managed`) can run against a stub, showing loading, success and failure.
- `app-db.md` and anything else that mentions epoch history: a counter cell with a "rewind" button using `rf/epoch-history` and `rf/restore-epoch!`. The engine runs with `goog.DEBUG` on, so epochs are recorded.
- `frames.md`: `:fx-overrides` on `frame-root` is now demonstrable with the HTTP stub.
- `how-to/add-auth.md`, `how-to/build-a-form.md`, `where-state-lives.md`, `errors.md`: only where a request, a form or an error is the point and a cell makes it clearer.
- `testing/*`: leave static. Those pages teach test code, not running UI.

The core guide teaches `reg-view` as its normal path. Add Fresco cells only where the page itself compares the two or introduces Fresco; don't change the guide's default.

## Start after

PR #10791 (Playground: Fresco and every optional artefact in cljs-rf2 cells) must be merged first. Check with `gh pr view 10791 --json state`. Until it merges, the engine on `main` cannot run the cells this bead asks for.

## The new capability

The docs' live ` ```cljs-rf2 ` cells run on `docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js`, built from `docs/tools/playground/sci`. That engine now bundles:

- re-frame2 core and reagent2 (reagent-slim), as before;
- **Fresco**: `re-frame.fresco` and its `forms`, `overlay` and `motion` modules;
- **every optional artefact**:
  - machines, flows and schemas (as before);
  - **HTTP**: `re-frame.http.managed`, plus `re-frame.http.test-support` for stubs;
  - **resources**, **routing**, **epoch** and **SSR**.

Before PR #10791, a cell could use only core, reagent2, machines, flows and schemas. So pages teaching Fresco, HTTP, resources, routing, epoch history or SSR could only show static code. Now a reader can run those examples, edit them, and see the result.

## How to write a live cell

The fence is ` ```cljs-rf2 `; there is no separate Fresco fence. A cell runs when the page loads, and again on Mod-Enter after an edit. Its last form is rendered.

- **Which renderer.** The last form renders through **Fresco** when it contains:
  - a Fresco view (`h/defview`), or `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider`; or
  - a handler written as data, such as `:on-click [:inc]`.

  Otherwise it renders through **reagent2**. Plain hiccup looks the same either way. One page can mix reagent2 and Fresco cells, but one tree cannot. A plain fn or `reg-view` head inside a Fresco tree raises `:rf.error/fresco-bad-head`.
- **What a cell can require.**
  - `re-frame.core`, which includes `reg-view`, `reg-machine`, `reg-flow`, `reg-app-schema`, `reg-resource`, `reg-route`, `epoch-history` and `restore-epoch!`
  - `re-frame.fresco`, `.forms`, `.overlay` and `.motion`
  - `reagent2.*`
  - `re-frame.schemas`
  - `re-frame.http.managed` and `re-frame.http.test-support`
  - `re-frame.resources`, `re-frame.routing`, `re-frame.epoch` and `re-frame.ssr`
- **Not available:**
  - `h/defhost`, since a cell has no foreign React component to wrap
  - `re-frame.fresco.native`, `re-frame.fresco.server` and the Fresco test kit
  - Story, Xray, and the Ring/Node SSR hosts
- **Frames.** A cell that creates no frame uses `:rf/default`. A cell that wraps its tree in `frame-root` uses that frame, as a real app does.
- **Shared page state.** All cells on a page share the registrar and the frames, so a later cell can render a view an earlier cell registered. Leaving the page unmounts everything, destroys frames and removes the page's registrations.
- **HTTP without a network.** Stub `:rf.http/managed` and route the frame to the stub:

  ```clojure
  (require '[re-frame.core :as rf]
           '[re-frame.http.managed]
           '[re-frame.http.test-support :as http-test-support])

  (http-test-support/install-managed-request-stubs!
    {[:get "https://api.example.com/articles/intro"] {:reply {:ok {:title "Welcome"}}}})

  ;; ... events, subs and a view ...

  [rf/frame-root {:id :demo :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-test-stub}}
   [article-view]]
  ```

  - Key each stub on the exact `[method url]` the request sends. A miss reaches `:on-failure` with `no stub matched`.
  - Use `{:reply {:failure {...}}}` to demo errors.
  - Install stubs and never uninstall them: the stub stack is global.
  - Real requests also work, but only to `https` endpoints that allow CORS, and they depend on the network. Prefer stubs.
- **Never create a `:url-bound? true` frame.** It would take over the docs site's address bar. Routing works on in-memory frames.
- **Working examples to copy:**
  - The cells in `docs/tools/playground/test/smoke.test.mjs` cover a Fresco view, a data-handler cell, a stubbed HTTP request, a `reg-resource` load, `reg-route` and `render-to-string`; all of them pass in CI.
  - `docs/tools/playground/README.md` has the full rules and a troubleshooting table.

## What to do

1. Read `docs/AUTHORING.md` and follow it. Examples must be real, use the actual API, and be self-contained; keep the page's continuing example domain.
2. Go through each page in this section and find the examples where **running** the code would teach something reading it cannot. Good candidates are behaviour that changes on a click, a request moving through loading, success and failure, data flowing into a view, and a rendered result. Introduce running examples there: convert a static block to ` ```cljs-rf2 `, or add a cell next to it.
3. Do not convert every block. Keep code static when it is:
   - a fragment, an `ns` form or configuration;
   - server-side, or needs the unavailable pieces listed above;
   - or the live version would need setup that buries the point.

   A page with one well-chosen live example beats a page where every block runs. If a page gains nothing, leave it.
4. Within one page, give each cell's registrations distinct ids unless a later cell is meant to reuse an earlier one's. Cells share the registrar.
5. Fix stale prose you touch, but keep the diff to this section.

## How to verify

Nothing in CI runs the docs' cells, so clicking them yourself is the only check. Say what you clicked in the PR body.

- Build the engine: `cd docs/tools/playground && npm install && npm run build`. `npm run build:rf2` enters shadow-cljs, so it uses the machine-wide build lane; ask the coordinator for it first (`AGENTS.md`).
- Run `mkdocs serve` from the repo root. Open every page you changed and use every cell: it renders, its buttons and inputs work, and no cell shows `ERROR`. Then navigate to another page and back.
- Run `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`.
close_reason:
Done in PR #10798 (marked ready, CI green on head 7cf2e9c3ed). Five core-guide pages gained one live cljs-rf2 cell each.

- views.md (2 cells): the todo list rewritten with h/defview. It reuses the first cell's events and subs, in its own frame.
- effects.md (2): the HTTP section's handlers now run against install-managed-request-stubs! through frame-root :fx-overrides. One route succeeds and one is a 404.
- frames.md (2): two frames run the same handlers with different :fx-overrides, one routed to the route-map stub and one to :rf.http/managed-canned-failure.
- observability.md (1): epoch-history entries render as buttons that call restore-epoch!.
- errors.md (1): "A handler throws" runs, and nothing commits.

Finding: the old errors.md example never threw in ClojureScript. max is variadic there, so (apply max ()) returns nil and (inc nil) is 1; reduce max behaves the same way. The example now runs str/trim on a missing :new-title, which throws on both hosts, and the error record at the top of the page matches it. SCI refuses interop method calls on String, so the cell uses str/trim rather than .trim. The docs engine prints no console record for the error, so the page no longer points readers at the console.

Left static:
- app-db.md: epoch history is taught on observability.md, so the cell went there.
- how-to/build-a-form.md: it uses Malli, which the engine does not expose, and spans a dozen blocks.
- how-to/add-auth.md and where-state-lives.md: their blocks are fragments.

title: re-frame-migration: give each rule fact one owner (corpus owns WHAT, skill owns HOW) and cut the duplicate recipes for M-0, M-8, M-27, M-40/M-11, M-42, M-51, M-70, M-71
description:
## Problem

A re-frame-migration rule's facts live in several places, nothing keeps them in step, and the field feedback loop spends most of its effort reconciling them.

- **Detection surface** (what to search for): up to four places. They are the corpus's "What to look for" in `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`, the trigger-index cell in `references/breaking-changes.md`, the Step 3 table in `references/inventory-and-plan.md`, and step 1 of the recipe leaf.
- **Type A/B label:** up to five places. They are the corpus Type-tag summary, `breaking-changes.md` "at a glance", the trigger-index Type column, the `SKILL.md` reference map, and the leaf preambles.
- **The procedure itself:** sometimes twice. The five-step M-8 procedure sits in both corpus `README.md:313-405` and `references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:483-562`.

## Evidence (one week, 2026-10-02..09, 45 non-test commits)

- **22 of 45 commits** were reconciliation between copies, or rework because the first fix missed a copy.
- **Two statements of one fact disagreeing:** #10811, #10816 (reopened twice; follow-up 3d1b1ef0e4), #10819, #10831, #10848, #10855, #10893, #10908, #10909, #10924, #10927.
- **Missed-copy rework:** 7b41549edf, fb39c2427f, e66ad7c5f5, e0a9745598, a2b03cf434 (#10811 reopen), 411baa81ec; corpus-only follow-ups 3d1b1ef0e4, c2d0dc1e07, 92b54aeefe.
- **Rules patched in both corpus and skill:**
  - M-8: a94ec5a408 #10869, 29a8e0d775 #10872
  - M-27: 8e8df7e356 #10885
  - M-42: 84f0fd83d6 #10924, 19a8f552fb
  - M-70: 4b84ec2c60 #10888
  - M-71: 945d87a1c7 #10811
  - M-40 vs M-11: e0bff2d891 #10927
  - M-0: a4a889b6ee #10819, 5a1e3dba5c #10816
- **A copy drifting right now (verified at 9e84689562):**
  - The M-51 search at corpus `README.md` ~L2106 is `rg -U 'reg-fx[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\(fn \[[a-zA-Z_-]+\]'`. It requires a newline and a bare-symbol parameter.
  - The skill's copy at `references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md` ~L580 is `rg -U 'reg-fx[^\n]*\n?[^\n]*\(fn \[[^]\s_][^]]*\]'`. Its optional newline admits same-line handlers, and its parameter class admits the destructured `(fn [{:keys [url]}]`, which that leaf calls the canonical http-fx shape.
  - The skill copy was fixed on 2026-09-13 (7735100e16); the corpus copy never was.

## Why it is structural

- **The copies are required by design.** `skills/re-frame-migration/spec/inputs.md` §6 ("Update procedure") says a new Type A rule gets a shape added to `auto-*.md` and a Type B rule gets a walkthrough in `guided-*.md`. Every new rule therefore creates more copies.

title: Schema :decode without Malli silently returns unvalidated data (nothing emitted in production); refuse at dispatch
description:
## Bug

When a request names a Malli schema as `:decode` and `malli.core` is not loaded, the response gets no validation. The parsed JSON flows to `:accept` and the success reply unchecked, so a body the schema would reject arrives as a success. A production build emits nothing about it, and a dev build emits one warning per process.

The gap is only discovered after the request has gone out, so a write has already reached the server. It is easy to reach on CLJS: a schema is plain data, so nothing in the build has to require Malli for the request to compile.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:206-233` (`malli-decode`) — when the late-resolved `malli.core/decode` and `malli.core/validate` are both nil, `decoded` is the input value (`:222`) and validation is skipped.
- The warning, `warn-malli-absent!` (`:190-204`), is gated on `rf.interop/debug-enabled?` and on a one-shot latch (`:182-188`).
- Malli is resolved lazily (`:164-180`): `requiring-resolve` on the JVM, compile-time `resolve` on CLJS. Its absence makes no noise when the namespace loads.
- A test pins this as intended: `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_decode_test.clj:72-96` (`malli-absent-decode-passes-through-and-warns-once`) asserts `(= "notanumber" (malli-decode :int "notanumber"))`.
- *Probed* at trunk on the JVM, from `implementation/http`:

  ```clojure
  (def args {:body-text "{\"id\":\"not-an-int\"}"
             :headers   {"content-type" "application/json"}
             :decode    [:map [:id :int]]})
  (d/decode-response-body args)
  ;; Malli present → throws :rf.error/http-schema-validation-failed
  (with-redefs [d/malli-decode-fn      (delay nil)
                d/malli-transformer-fn (delay nil)
                d/malli-validate-fn    (delay nil)]
    (d/decode-response-body args))
  ;; → {:id "not-an-int"}
  ```

Contrast with the contract and with its sibling check:
- Spec 014 §JSON decoder hardening (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:309`) specifies the skip. It accepts that "a body the schema would reject still succeeds" and that "a production build skips validation with nothing emitted".
- The same artefact already refuses a *marked* schema at dispatch when the schemas walker is missing (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:253-280`, `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing`). So one missing dependency fails loud for its privacy half and silently for its validation half.

## Expected

An explicitly authored schema `:decode` either validates the response, or is refused at dispatch before any network request.

## Fix direction

- In `handlers/normalise-args`, beside the existing `decode-schema-marks` call (`handlers.cljc:280`), throw when `(privacy-body/schema-decode? decode)` holds and Malli's decode and validate fns are unresolvable. The request is then never issued.
- The error can reuse `:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing`, whose remedy (add `day8/re-frame2-schemas` and require `re-frame.schemas`) is the documented fix, or it can be a dedicated id.
- Delete `warn-malli-absent!`, its latch, and the `:rf.warning/http-malli-absent` row.
- `:auto`, the keyword modes and custom decode fns keep working without Malli.
- Update spec 014:309 and the spec 009 catalogue to match.

## Acceptance

- A test replaces `malli-absent-decode-passes-through-and-warns-once`. With the three Malli delays rebound to `(delay nil)`, it dispatches `:rf.http/managed` with `:decode [:map [:id :int]]`, then asserts the dispatch-time error and that no request reached the transport. It is red before the fix and green after.
- Under the same rebinding, `:decode :auto`, `:json`, `:text` and a custom fn still decode.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (14 §5); the Opus review (http Insight 5, Action 4(a)) adopted Sol's dispatch-time form.
- Related: closed rf2-v1cxy and rf2-zkew7 documented the current skip in spec 014 and on the API page. Neither one ruled on whether the skip is right.
- Hot-zone files: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, where the `:rf.warning/http-malli-absent` row at `:2289` is retired, plus a new error row if the fix uses a dedicated id.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/14-http.md` §5; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/http.md` Insight 5 and Action 4.

title: Cross-origin network drops classify as :rf.http/cors on CLJS, so the spec's retry policies never retry them
description:
## Bug

On CLJS, every fetch `TypeError` against a cross-origin URL is classified `:rf.http/cors`. That includes an ordinary network drop (offline, DNS failure, connection refused or reset), because the browser raises the same `TypeError` for both. An app whose API lives on another origin therefore never retries a network blip under the spec's own retry policies, and tells its user to check the server's CORS configuration.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_cljs.cljc:448-452` at 475bdcaacf:

  ```clojure
  (and (= "TypeError" err-name)
       (cross-origin? url))
  {:kind    :rf.http/cors
   :message (or (.-message err) (str err))
   :url     url}
  ```

  The comment above it (`:443-447`) concedes that "network drops surface as TypeErrors too". The only discriminator is the URL's origin (`cross-origin?`, `:353-403`), which says nothing about why the fetch failed.
- The classifier test pins the conflation (`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs:39-46`). The same `(js/TypeError. "Failed to fetch")` is `:rf.http/cors` against `https://other.invalid/x?a=1` and `:rf.http/transport` against `https://app.example/api/items`. "Failed to fetch" is also what Chrome reports for an offline or refused connection.
- The retry gate (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1441-1445`) retries only when `(contains? on-set kind)`. Spec 014's policies leave `:rf.http/cors` out:
  - its canonical example retries `#{:rf.http/transport :rf.http/http-5xx}` (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:56`);
  - its "Common defaults" are `#{:rf.http/transport :rf.http/http-5xx :rf.http/timeout}` (`:372`);
  - `:396` makes `:rf.http/cors` opt-in, because it is "frequently a permanent configuration error".

  So a cross-origin network drop is never retried under the spec's own policies.
- Spec 014:509 admits that the category also catches "a plain network drop to a cross-origin host, which the browser reports the same way". The same row justifies the category by saying "a CORS rejection is a configuration error, not a network error".
- The shipped example shows the effect *(read)*:
  - realworld_http talks to `https://api.realworld.show/api` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/http.cljs:48`), which is cross-origin from any dev or deploy origin;
  - its reads retry under `data-fetch-retry` `{:on #{:rf.http/transport :rf.http/http-5xx :rf.http/timeout} :max-attempts 3 ...}` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/http.cljs:89-103`; used at e.g. `realworld_http/articles.cljs:285`);
  - it renders `:rf.http/cors` as "Blocked by the browser's cross-origin policy — check the API's CORS configuration." (`realworld_shared/http.cljs:138`).

  A Wi-Fi blip during any read is not retried, and the user sees that message.
- *read*: this is the CLJS-only path. No browser probe was run.

## Expected

A fetch rejection that the transport cannot attribute to CORS classifies as `:rf.http/transport`. A policy that names `:rf.http/transport` then retries it.

## Fix direction

- Classify a cross-origin `TypeError` as `:rf.http/transport` with a diagnostic hint such as `:cross-origin? true`, keeping timeout and abort precedence unchanged.
- Retire `:rf.http/cors` from the closed category set and from `retryable-categories` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc:42-49`).
- Update every page that describes the category:
  - spec 014: §Failure categories, the §Retry tables, §CORS classification, and §`:rf.http/cors` is CLJS-only;
  - the rows in spec 009, Security.md, API.md (`:453`) and Conventions.md;
  - realworld's `failure->message` arm, which can branch on the hint instead.
- This is breaking: the closed set drops from eight categories to seven.

## Acceptance

- In `http_cljs_test.cljs` `cross-origin-classification-under-injected-origin`, the two cross-origin `TypeError` rows expect `{:kind :rf.http/transport … :cross-origin? true}`. They are red before the fix and green after.

- `:retry {:on #{:rf.http/cors}}` is refused with `:rf.error/http-bad-retry-on`. Update `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_retry_on_validation_test.clj:19`.
- A grep for `rf.http/cors` across `spec/`, `docs/`, `skills/`, `examples/`, `migration/`, `testbeds/` and `tools/` leaves no live description of the old category.

title: TESTING.md: stale routing prod-gate roster, and its spec-only-PR classifier claim contradicts the spec/* catch-all
description:
## Bug

`TESTING.md` makes two claims that contradict the scripts:
- It says the routing production-gate lane runs 18 of 37 namespaces with "19 rostered known-red". The script's known-red roster is empty and the lane runs the whole suite.
- Its spec-impl-pair section says top-level `spec/*.md` "has **no classifier rule**", so a spec-only PR runs only the always-on jobs. The same file's classifier table, and the classifier itself, say `spec/*` arms the JVM tier through a catch-all.

Contributors and AI pairs who rely on this prose will mis-predict which jobs run and what a green prod-gate lane covers.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- **Routing counts.**
  - `TESTING.md:112` says: "18 of 37 namespaces, 98 tests, 613 assertions, green; 19 rostered known-red under rf2-o5dbf."
  - `scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh:94-95` reads `known_red=(` followed by `# EMPTY.`
  - The floor is `RF2_MIN_TESTS` default 256 (`:256`) (*read*).
- **Classifier contradiction.**
  - `TESTING.md:327`: "Top-level `spec/*.md` has **no classifier rule**: a spec-only PR runs only the always-on jobs … First regression through this gap triggers a surgical per-spec-file rule, not a blanket one."
  - `TESTING.md:191` (the `implementation_jvm` row): "nearly all of `spec/*` via a catch-all".
- Repro (*probed*):
  - `bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh spec/002-Frames.md` prints `implementation_jvm=true`.
  - The control, `… docs/index.md`, prints no `=true` line.
  - So a spec-only PR does queue the JVM tier, and `:327` is false.
- `TESTING.md:113` has the same staleness for the SSR lane. **rf2-6c25z (open) already owns that line**, so it is not repeated here.

## Expected

`TESTING.md` says the routing production-gate lane runs its whole suite, and it says `spec/*.md` arms `implementation_jvm`, with the escapes `:191` already lists.

## Fix direction

- Replace the routing row's counts with "runs the whole suite; the floor lives in the script". Leave counts out of the prose, so it cannot go stale again.
- Rewrite the opening of §Spec-impl-pair convention to match the catch-all. Keep the pairing advice if it is still wanted.
- Land this together with rf2-6c25z's `TESTING.md:113` fix, or sequence it after; both edit the same table.

## Acceptance

- By hand: the routing row matches `scripts/test-routing-prod-gate.sh`.
- The classifier statements at `:191` and in §Spec-impl-pair agree with `report-changed-surfaces.sh spec/<file>.md`.
- `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` stays green (`TESTING.md` is repo-root markdown).

## Notes

- **Origin:** Opus tooling review (Insight 1).
- **Related:** rf2-6c25z (open; owns `TESTING.md:113`, the SSR lane counts). Fold this into it, or sequence after it.
- **Hot-zone files:** none. `TESTING.md` is not on the list, but it is shared with rf2-6c25z.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/tooling.md` Insight 1.

title: Reagent and reagent-slim hydrate with no root options: no mismatch trace, :on-recoverable-error and prefix ignored
description:
## Bug

Reagent and reagent-slim hydrate with a bare two-argument `hydrateRoot`, which installs no root options at all. Three things follow:
- a mismatch React recovers from emits no `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`;
- a host-supplied `:on-recoverable-error` is silently ignored;
- `:identifier-prefix` cannot be set.

The hiccup tier's render hash, the only other channel on these adapters, never expands a component head. So in an ordinary root → layout → page app, a mismatch anywhere below the root view reaches neither re-frame channel, only React's default console report. Users, and dev tools that read the trace, see a clean hydration that is not clean.

## Evidence

Trunk 475bdcaacf. Paths are under `implementation/`.

- `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:129` and `adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:40`: both inject `:hydrate-root (fn [mount-point tree] (rdc/hydrate-root mount-point tree))`.
- `core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:4085-4094`: the ratom `mount-root!` calls `(hydrate-root mount-point render-tree)` and ignores every opt except `:hydrate?`.
- `core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1176-1217` and `:1346`, `:1373`: the React-hook spine (UIx) builds the composed `native-hydration-reporter` with an adoption window, composes over the host's `:on-recoverable-error`, and passes these as root options. The ratom spine has no equivalent.
- `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:256-257`: "The Reagent adapters' `render!` hydrates without root options, so `:on-recoverable-error` takes effect on this adapter only."
- Stock Reagent 2.0.1, `reagent/dom/client.cljs:69-78`: `hydrate-root` destructures `on-recoverable-error` and `identifier-prefix` but calls `hydrateRoot` without them. Forwarding opts through `rdc/hydrate-root` would therefore still do nothing. slim's `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` does accept JS options (`adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:298-313`).
- `ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc:271-288`: every fn head in the render tree hashes to the same `#fn[]` token, so `[layout [page x]]` never contributes the page's markup.
- `ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_root_view_hash_test.clj:55-76`: the repo pins that a delegating root verifies `:verified` under `:on-mismatch :hard-error` against a payload with a planted divergence.

Repro (*read*; traced in source, not run):
1. A Reagent app whose root view delegates, `(defn root [] [layout [page]])`, is server-rendered on the JVM.
2. The client hydrates through the adapter's `render!` with `{:hydrate? true :on-recoverable-error f}`, but `page` renders different text on the client.

Expected: `f` is called and `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` is emitted in dev. Traced result:
- the render hash verifies, because it compares only `[#fn[] …]`;
- React recovers through its default `reportError`;
- `f` is never called, and no framework trace is emitted.

Contract contrast:
- Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection (`spec/011-SSR.md:885-886`) assigns Reagent and reagent-slim to the hash tier and gives only native UIx roots the adoption reporter, so these adapters are left with a check that cannot see past the root view.
- Spec 004C §3 (`spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md:117-119`) requires a hydrating root's `identifierPrefix` to be the server's. The ratom path has no way to set one.

## Expected

A ratom-family hydrating root gets the same composed reporter, adoption window, `:on-recoverable-error` composition and `:identifier-prefix` handling as the hook spine.

## Fix direction

Give the ratom spine's `mount-root!` the hook spine's hydrate options. Build `hydrate-root-options` (reporter plus adoption window) and the prefix, mount the adoption-window closer, and hand the options to the injected `:hydrate-root`, which becomes a 3-arity.

For stock Reagent, the adapter must call `react-dom/client`'s `hydrateRoot` with options itself, because `rdc/hydrate-root` drops them, while still building the element the way Reagent's root does. Show that equivalent rather than assume it. slim can pass the options straight through. The reviews' follow-on step, deleting the shallow hash channel once adoption covers all substrates, is Mike's call (Opus ssr open question 3) and is not part of this bead.

## Acceptance

On Reagent and on reagent-slim, a hydrating mount reports through the composed reporter in each of these cases:
- a nested text mismatch;
- a nested structural mismatch (missing or extra element);
- a host `:on-recoverable-error` callback, which is called;
- a recoverable error after the hydration commit, which delegates without the framework emit.

Also: `:identifier-prefix` is passed to React's root options (a client `useId` carries it), a later update still goes through Reagent's own scheduling, and these tests fail on today's code.

## Notes

- Origin: Opus ssr review (decision 5, action 2 step 1) and adapters review (decision 4, action 8). Sol reports 17 §6 and 28 §2 confirmed it by source check (an Opus-derived claim).
- Related: none open.
- Hot zones: none in code. If the tier text changes, that touches `spec/011-SSR.md` (not listed as hot) and possibly `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §The client root (hot).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr.md` decision 5; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/adapters.md` decision 4; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/28-ssr-hydration-egress.md` §2.
notes:
== WORKER VERDICT (adapters-hydrate, PR #11072) — 2026-10-10 AUSEST

FIXED. A hydrating Reagent or reagent-slim root now hydrates with root options.

What changed:
- The ratom spine's mount (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, make-ratom-spine) builds the same hydrate options the React-hook spine does: hydrate-root-options, the composed reporter plus its adoption window. It adds :identifier-prefix as identifierPrefix and hands the options to a 3-arity :hydrate-root.
- The adoption-window closer WRAPS the tree as a single child rather than sitting beside it, because a sibling moves every useId tree position. Probed on React 19.3 renderToString: the bare tree and the tree under one or two wrappers all give _pfx-R_2_; behind one or two siblings it gives _pfx-R_a_ / _pfx-R_b_. Later updates render through the same wrap.
- reagent-slim passes the options to reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root.
- Stock reagent.dom.client/hydrate-root drops its options. The Reagent adapter therefore calls react-dom/client hydrateRoot itself, over the element rdc/render builds against a root that only records what it is handed, which is the element hydrate-root builds. Equivalence is pinned by DOM row hydrated-root-element-is-reagents-own: the committed top component is identical to stock's reagent-root, and both roots commit the same DOM. Node row render-hydrate-uses-hydrate-root pins the element type.
- Spec: 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection (the representation decides whether a root also gets the hash; every React-family root verifies by adoption), 004C §3 (where a root takes :identifier-prefix), one sentence in 006 §render naming the stock hydrate path, and Spec 009's :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch row, whose adoption tier now names every React-family root.

Evidence (the CLJS lanes ran on CI; the shadow-cljs lane was not granted locally):
- red-before: scratch PR #11070, run 38041348012, browser job 114183037678. 16 failures, all in the two new namespaces (both adapters: nested mismatch / host rows, prefix rows, post-commit host row, closer position).
- green-after: run 38043095900, browser job 114188125429 (966 tests / 5045 assertions, 0 failures) and node job 114188125023 (7400 / 22898, 0 failures).
- red-again: run 38043170972 (src fix alone reversed): browser job 114188178766, the same 16 failures; node job 114188178654, the 5 updated hydrate pins.
- final base: PR #11072 run 38047913681 on head 8f442ddb41, browser job 114202151871 (968 / 5051, 0 failures), node job 114202151765 (7412 / 22952, 0 failures). The rollup had 88 checks, none failing.

Not done here, and not part of this bead: deleting the shallow hash channel.

title: machines-viz standalone viewer renders unusably: xyflow's stylesheet is never loaded and the chart collapses to 23px
description:
Found by the rf2-kyi1j worker (PR #11094), by rendering it: the standalone machines-viz viewer page is unusable on its own. These are CLAIMS to re-check at tip:
- Nothing loads xyflow's layout stylesheet; only Xray injects it. Nodes are unpositioned, and the zoom controls cannot be clicked.
- The chart area collapses to 23px tall, because the chart's default height of 100% has no definite parent height to resolve against.
The worker had to inject both the stylesheet and a height to get a usable render.

Fix direction: give the standalone viewer page what Xray already gives the chart, with the smallest change. Load xyflow's stylesheet the way Xray does (share the injection if it is a function, rather than copying it), and give the viewer's container a definite height. Do not change the chart's own default sizing, because Xray relies on it.

Gate: render the viewer and describe what you see. This needs a browser and the shadow-cljs build lane, granted by the coordinator. Also clojure -M:test from tools/machines-viz, and CI's machines-viz lanes and viewer release build.
notes:
== WORKER SUMMARY (2026-10-11 AUSEST): PR #11110, commit 81477ed62b, branch worker/mviz-viewer
Both claims in the description held at tip c3b4f67c2f. Nothing loaded xyflow's stylesheet outside Xray. The viewer's :page column had min-height 100vh, so the flexed :chart area had no definite height and MachineChart's default 100% height collapsed.

FIX, one commit in two files under tools/machines-viz:
- public/viewer.html carries @xyflow/react/dist/style.css verbatim in its own <style>. It is byte-identical (LF-normalised, 17639 bytes) to the 12.4.2 file implementation/package.json pins, which is the same file Xray injects.

WHY A COPY: Xray's CSS is the ^:private react-flow-base-css def in tools/xray theme/global_styles.cljs. Its only public entry point, install-into!, injects all of Xray's styles, and tools/xray/deps.edn depends on day8/re-frame2-machines-viz, so machines-viz requiring Xray would be circular. The copy lives in the HTML rather than in CLJS because the page has its own head. That keeps hosting at two files and needs no injection code. The copy has to be replaced when the @xyflow/react pin moves, and the HTML comment says so.

RENDER: shadow-cljs release build plus stage, before (base files) and after (this commit), both exit 0. Headless Chromium at 1280x800 on file:// with a four-state share fragment.
- Before: the chart root is 23px tall. There are 0 .react-flow rules. All 10 nodes are position static and 5-13px tall. The Controls are static, and the point at the zoom-in button's centre hit-tests a canvas SVG rect, so the click times out at 3000ms and the zoom stays at scale(0.2).
- After: the chart root is 736px tall. There are 100 .react-flow rules. All nodes are position absolute; the state nodes are 240x93 and inside the chart. The Controls are absolute at the bottom-left. The zoom-in click lands and scale goes from 1.556 to 1.867. The whole topology is fitted and readable.

title: Retire the :rf.cascade/captured aggregator (re-frame.trace.cascade): delete the ns, settle call, late-bind hooks, bundle-isolation entry and shadow module; drop it from Spec 009; :rf.cascade/* becomes reserved-and-never-recycled
description:
DECISION FOR MIKE. Retire the :rf.cascade/captured aggregator (re-frame.trace.cascade's focus hook, set-focus-predicate! / clear-focus-predicate!), or keep it and correct Spec 009?

WHAT IS TRUE NOW (rf2-bv3yu, PR #11012, merged 2026-10-08 at 844fb47dfd): Spec 009 says a consumer installs the focus predicate; nothing in core is meant to. The intended consumer, the Xray Reactive panel, stopped reading :rf.cascade/captured (rf2-p1qas, commit 47051e731e) and now reads the epoch record's :sub-runs and :renders, which carry the same data; tools/xray spec 021 §3 says "nothing reads a :rf.cascade/captured aggregate". No tool has ever called set-focus-predicate!. In the browser builds where Xray runs the namespace never loads, because re-frame.core requires it on the JVM only, so the documented use cannot work there. No memory or closed bead rules on it either way.

THE WORKER'S RECOMMENDATION: retire the aggregator in its own bead. The deletion crosses several fences: the epoch call site, the bundle-isolation gate entry, the module in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (hot zone), Spec 009 (hot zone), the Conventions and Ownership rows (hot zone), and tools/xray spec 021. If you would rather keep it, the fix is Spec 009 text saying no shipped tool installs the predicate and the event never fires in browser builds.

MAYOR'S READ: a documented trace event with no consumer that cannot fire where its consumer runs is dead weight; under the stance, retire it. But it is a Spec 009 contract removal, so the call is yours. If you say retire, this becomes a P2 implementation bead touching several hot-zone files, dispatched alone.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:46:13 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==
DECISION: Retire the `:rf.cascade/captured` aggregator. Delete `re-frame.trace.cascade` and everything that exists only to carry it: the JVM-only require in `re-frame.core`, the settle call site in `re-frame.epoch`, the three `:trace.cascade/*` late-bind hooks, the bundle-isolation entry, its positive-control module and the `:trace-cascade` shadow module. Spec 009 stops documenting the `:rf.cascade` family and the `:rf.cascade/captured` operation. Conventions keeps `:rf.cascade/*` as a "Reserved and never recycled; nothing emits it." row. The epoch record (`:sub-runs`, `:renders`, `:trace-events`) is the one supported source of per-event reactive detail.

WHY: Under the stance (elegance, a minimal API, no gold plating, trust the programmer), a documented trace contract has to earn its place. This one earns nothing:
  - Nobody consumes it. No tool, example or testbed has ever called `set-focus-predicate!`, and Xray's Reactive panel reads the epoch record instead.
  - Its only consumer runs in the browser, and the namespace does not load there.
  - Where it does fire (the JVM), it reports less than the epoch record for the same event, because it runs once at settle and misses the post-settle back-fill.
  - Its output is kept nowhere: not in any epoch record and not in the trace ring.
Keeping it means maintaining a 260-line namespace, three hooks, a gate entry, a shadow module and three tests, all to support a feature whose honest description is "do not use this". Every need it was built for is already met by the epoch record and the event-bundle projection, and both are documented. Removing it costs no capability, changes no behaviour in any browser build, and simplifies the instrumentation model an AI pair has to learn.

REJECTED:
  - B (keep it, correct Spec 009): the spec would become accurate, but it would then describe a feature nobody should use. The maintenance cost stays, and an AI pair still has to work out that the epoch record is the real route. That is hot-zone effort spent documenting dead weight.
  - C (make it work: load it in CLJS dev builds, have Xray install a predicate, fix the post-settle gap): the gap has no clean fix. Back-filled renders and sub-runs arrive on later ticks with no natural "end", so the aggregate would have to re-emit or be computed on read, and computing it on read is just reading the epoch record. No consumer has asked for it.
  - Deleting the Conventions `:rf.cascade/*` row outright (the dossier author's first preference, with "retired; never recycled" offered as belt and braces): rejected. Conventions says the reserved set is fixed-and-additive ("names already in the table cannot be repurposed"), and the table already has a house form for exactly this case: `:rf.ssr.head/*`, `:rf.ui.compile/*`, `:rf.ui.tree/*`, `:rf.ui.evidence/*`, `:rf.ui.tool/*` and `:rf.pp/*` each open with "**Reserved and never recycled; nothing emits it.**" Rewriting the row into that form costs the same as deleting it, and it keeps the table true to its own rule.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED: Every opinion recommends retirement: the rf2-bv3yu worker, the mayor's read on this bead, the dossier author (Option A) and Codex. I agree with both reviewers. Three refinements were settled:
  (1) "Cannot fire in a browser": Codex said this overstates it, because an app could require `re-frame.trace.cascade` explicitly in a CLJS dev build. The dossier records the same caveat. Both are right. The accurate statement is that it is not wired anywhere in the browser and nothing in the repo requires it there. The fact does not change the decision. Codex also notes that a repository search cannot rule out an outside application requiring the namespace. Accepted: the risk is pre-alpha, the name is in no released artefact, it is not in `spec/API.md` or either api-manifest file, and Spec 009 says "tools ignore operations they don't understand".
  (2) Xray 021 §11.3: the dossier proposed restating the two capture rows as "met by the epoch record's `:sub-runs` / `:renders`". Codex objected that the 50-sub / 100-view caps are not a storage guarantee of the epoch record. Codex is right. The rows are rewritten so they make no bounded-capture claim for the epoch record (see guidance).
  (3) Not raised by either review, found at HEAD 200a67df2d: three more stale references to the aggregator. Spec 009:262 (`:rf.sub/skip`: "The cascade-DAG consumer reads this…"), Spec 009:621 (`:rf.flow/skip`: "consumed by the cascade-DAG aggregator") and Conventions:101 (`:rf.trace/event-id`: "…epoch records, and the cascade aggregator"). They are in the guidance.
Status of the coupled bead: rf2-w2sz4 is CLOSED. PR #11090 merged at 5eef8e1e2c (mergedAt 2026-10-10T12:19:25Z), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 5eef8e1e2c HEAD` exits 0. The dossier's "wait for PR #11090" constraint is therefore discharged. Its item-4 Xray test comment was "ALREADY GONE" per its close reason, so nothing folds into this work.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 200a67df2d; `git diff --stat 2fdf565945 200a67df2d` over every cited code, test, gate and spec file is empty except Spec 009, whose cascade lines 162/208/262/304/448/621/1052 are unchanged):
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:54-60` requires the namespace under `#?@(:clj [[re-frame.trace.cascade]])`, so it loads on the JVM only. The comment there claims "Xray's Reactive panel loads the ns explicitly from its tools-side build", and that is false: a repo-wide search finds no require of `re-frame.trace.cascade` in `tools/`, `examples/` or `testbeds/`. The only CLJS require is the bundle-isolation positive control (`implementation/scripts/bundle-isolation-positive-control/src/re_frame/bundle_isolation_positive_control/trace_cascade.cljs`).
  - `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/cascade.cljc`: the default focus predicate always answers false (`:61-62`); the namespace holds `set-focus-predicate!` / `clear-focus-predicate!` (`:64-79`) and `aggregate-cascade`, which caps at 50 subs and 100 views and has NO db-paths slot; `capture-for-epoch!` emits `:rf.cascade/captured` (`:216-237`); the three late-bind keys are published at `:247-249`. The comment at `:57-58` ("A consumer (Xray's Reactive panel) calls `set-focus-predicate!` once at mount") is false.
  - `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:302-309`: after the owner-record commit, `settle!` looks up `:trace.cascade/capture-for-epoch!` via `get-fn-cached` and calls it once with the harvested `events`, then emits snapshotted/outcome and notifies listeners. The `events` binding is also used for record assembly (`:288`), so removing the block leaves no unused local.
  - Back-fill: `re-frame.epoch.capture` routes post-settle renders and sub-runs through `:epoch/record-render!` / `:epoch/record-sub-run!`. The directory's own descriptions say these fire "at React commit time, after the causing cascade settled" and "at React deref time … because reactions recompute lazily". Nothing calls the aggregator again for them.
  - Spec 009:304 promises "the full per-cascade DAG — db-paths, subs recomputed and skipped, flows computed and skipped, views rendered" and calls itself "the substrate side of the Xray Reactive panel's … budget". Neither claim holds: there is no db-paths slot, and the panel reads the epoch record (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs:590-635`, `project-record`: `:sub-runs`, `:renders`, flow counts from `:trace-events`). Xray 021 §3 (`:905`) itself says "nothing reads a `:rf.cascade/captured` aggregate".
  - History: the aggregator landed in `3d9439e618` (2026-05-20, #1729), and `47051e731e` (2026-05-21) switched the Reactive panel off it. Even that reader never matched: it expected a counts-only `{:subs-ran N …}` under `:payload`, while the emitter produces DAG vectors under `:tags`.

title: SSR: cut the Root Manifest; hydrate! drops :container/:manifest, hydrate-page! and the install ledger stay, and its docstring example hydrates through render!
description:
## Bug

`hydrate-page!`'s docstring example cannot work on any page a shipped server renders. Each root in the example passes a `:container`, so `hydrate!` looks for the Root Manifest that must sit immediately after the container. No server path in the repo emits a manifest, so preflight throws `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid {:missing :manifest}` for every root. The isolation boundary catches each throw, so every root comes back `{:status :failed}`, its `:mount-fn` never runs, and nothing mounts. A developer copying the example gets a blank page plus one always-on `:rf.error/root-boot-failed` per root.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:548-614` (trunk 475bdcaacf) — `hydrate-page!` docstring example: `(ssr/hydrate-page! (for [[rid container] page-roots] {:frame :app/main :root-id rid :container container :mount-fn #(rdc/render ...)}))`. `:516-546` `boot-one-root!` runs `(hydrate! (dissoc opts :mount-fn))` first and calls `mount-fn` only if that returns, catching any throw into `{:status :failed}`.
- `boot.cljc:383-388` — `hydrate!` calls `rf.ssr.install/preflight!` with the root's `:manifest` and `:container`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/install.cljc:253-292` `resolve-manifest!` — with a `:container` and no `:manifest`, it discovers the manifest from the container's next sibling or throws `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid` with `:extra {:missing :manifest}` ("Either server-render this root so its manifest rides the response, or mount it client-only").
- No producer: outside `re-frame.ssr.manifest` itself, server code uses only its wire predicates (`edn-carryable?` in `ssr-ring/.../node.clj:248` and `render_state.cljc:282-283`, `portable-number?` in `payload_policy.cljc:862`). Nothing in `implementation/*/src`, `examples/` or `tools/` calls `manifest/manifest` or `script-html`, or emits `data-rf-root`.
- The spec admits it: `spec/011-SSR.md:681` calls the producer obligation "UNMET", and `:519` says the manifest suite runs over "hand-built" manifests. `hydrate-page!` is `:tier :implementation` (`spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1814`).
- *Read*, not run (`discover-manifest` is browser-side).

## Expected

A documented multi-root boot example either works against a page a shipped host renders, or is not offered.

## Fix direction

Mike's call:

- **Delete multi-root** (the Opus review's recommendation): remove the Root Manifest, the install ledger and `hydrate-page!` (about 1,100 lines and five test namespaces; 011 §Root Manifest v1, §Hydration preflight, §Failed-root isolation; 004C §2-§10). Keep `edn-carryable?`, `portable-number?` and `numeric-collision` in a small `re-frame.ssr.wire` namespace, and document "hydrate once, mount N roots, each in a try/catch".
- **Finish it**: ship a server-side manifest producer in the hosts and prove two real roots through emission, discovery, one seed and native adoption. Sol's review also requires that a schema-rejected seed claims nothing (today the claim is inferred from frame liveness, `boot.cljc:436-440`) and that no raw exception reaches the always-on `:rf.error/root-boot-failed` record (`report-root-boot-failed!`, `boot.cljc:469-513`).
- Stopgap if neither is chosen soon: rewrite the docstring example so it does not pass `:container` (the manifest-less path), or mark it as requiring a hand-emitted manifest.

## Acceptance

- Delete: no `data-rf-root`, `:container`, `:manifest` or `:root-id` opt on `hydrate!`; `ssr-ring` `node.clj` and `render_state.cljc` import the wire namespace; the ssr lanes are green.
- Finish: a browser test renders a two-root page through a shipped host and boots it with the docstring example verbatim; both roots report `:hydrated` and mount (fails today: both `:failed`).

## Notes

- Origin: Opus review (ssr decision 9) and Sol review (SSR hydration §3); wording on containment corrected in the cross-review.
- Related: rf2-gwye.19 / rf2-fzbj.10 (closed) fixed an install claim retained after a refused payload.
- Hot zones: deletion touches `spec/API.md` + `spec/api-manifest*.edn`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (three error rows), core's late-bind directory row for manifest discovery, and `spec/004C-Roots-and-Mount.md` (not hot).
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/ssr.md` decision 9, Action 4, open question 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/28-ssr-hydration-egress.md` §1, §3, §5.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:49:58 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==
DECISION: Option B. Cut the Root Manifest and keep manifest-less multi-root boot. `re-frame.ssr.manifest` is deleted, except for its EDN wire-crossing predicates, which move to a small `re-frame.ssr.wire` namespace. `hydrate!` loses its `:container` and `:manifest` opts, and preflight becomes the frame-id check plus the install ledger. The `:ssr/discover-root-manifest` hook goes, and so does `:rf.error/root-manifest-invalid`. `hydrate-page!`, the idempotent install ledger, the content-digest conflict, release-on-failed-seed and the always-on `:rf.error/root-boot-failed` record all stay exactly as they behave today. The `hydrate-page!` docstring example becomes the manifest-less form `docs/api` already teaches, and it mounts through the adapter's `render!` with `{:hydrate? true}` rather than `rdc/create-root` plus `rdc/render`.

WHY:
- The defect is not really the docstring. It is a mechanism whose only runtime effects are to make `:container` throw and to supply a default `:root-id` for ledger attribution when the caller passes none.
  - No server, example, tool or testbed emits a manifest. Its producer namespace is internal, and spec 011 calls its own consumer obligation "UNMET".
  - Its consumer reads one defaultable field. `:identifier-prefix`, `:props`, `:frame-payload-ids` and `:render-fingerprint` are read by nothing.
- Everything of value works today without it: multi-root boot, idempotent install, conflict refusal and per-root isolation (probe below).
- Under "elegance ... not over-engineering ... trust the programmer", that is dead weight to cut, not a feature to finish. B cuts exactly the dead half and keeps the working half that rf2-kuky.44 ruled in.
- The Root Descriptor / Root Manifest family is residue of the compiled-view substrate programme (EP-0030 stages S1/S5). Its only descriptor producer went with `re-frame.ui`, which is removed permanently.
- This bug is the third report on the same mechanism in two weeks (rf2-ysb2m item 5, rf2-z4syu item 2, this one). A text-only fix would leave it to be filed a fourth time.

REJECTED:
- A (fix the text only): honest and cheap, and its text changes are a strict subset of B's. But it keeps about 730 source lines and about 680 test lines for a contract nothing delivers, and the spec keeps contradicting itself (004C §3 says a hydrating root takes identity from its manifest; 011 §Step 1 exempts the manifest-less path every shipped page uses).
- C (delete multi-root wholesale, the Opus review's recommendation): it deletes the working half to fix the broken half.
  - It reverses rf2-kuky.44.
  - A second `hydrate!` into a live frame becomes a silent reset again, because `:replace-frame-state` is the locked merge policy. That is the harm 011 §Step 2 describes.
  - A failed root stops emitting its always-on record unless every host writes its own.
- D (finish it: shell emission, client doors reading the hook, 004C §7 Layer 2, a server multi-root render concept): it reverses rf2-ysb2m's ruling (5), "DECLINED: no demonstrated need; trust the programmer". It builds a feature with no caller across hot shells, specs and 009. Revisit only if a concrete host needs automatic discovery of independently rendered roots.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- The dossier author and Codex both recommend B, and both reject C and D. They agree on every fact.

title: Spec 011 says ssr/render-to-string delegates through the installed adapter; it is a plain alias of the SSR emitter
description:

## Problem

`spec/011-SSR.md:201`, in the paragraph beginning "The SSR adapter is plain-atom-shaped", says:

> callers using `ssr/render-to-string` (which delegates through the installed adapter) get the SSR emitter without any late-bind wiring

It doesn't delegate. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:39` is

    (def render-to-string rf.ssr.emit/render-to-string)

title: Error source-coord can name a replacement registered while the throwing implementation is still running
description:
PR #11057 / rf2-mn2ht.17 follow-up. OPEN, separately trackable finding; do not reopen or rewrite the source bead.

The descriptor coordinate is correct, but error-emit/executed-coord calls live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution again instead of reading the descriptor/generation that supplied the failing handler. That seam first flushes pending reprojection. If the handler has been re-registered while the old implementation is running, error emission flushes the new generation and reports the replacement's coordinate for the old exception. This also forces a new resolution inside error handling.

Verified with a small JVM probe against the exact merged core source at 102b51824969e0277b3fd800f10792a815e0e110 (extracted into an ignored probe directory, without editing source). Also reproduced against origin/main 4ba25ea69e15fa911376ea03623b7d9756764bf6. Both commands exited 0. The control registers a throwing :audit/throws at audit.coord line 10, constructs :audit/frame and dispatches it: the handler-exception record reports line 10. The second run registers the same old throwing implementation at line 10, whose body first registers its replacement at line 20 under the same namespace/id and then throws. The exception is still the old implementation's, but the record reports line 20. Both registrations bind source-coords/*pending-coords* exactly as the public reg-* macro does; all dispatch, image refresh and error fan-out are real. No shadow-cljs run was needed or started.

The deterministic in-handler registration models the same generation change a REPL/hot-reload or JVM thread can cause during a long-running handler. Accurate attribution during hot replacement is the purpose of the source fix. Current live ledger has no open owner for this remaining case (full export searched for source/error coordinate and re-register/throw references).

Proposed action: carry/read the coordinate from the descriptor or resolution generation that actually supplied the operation. Avoid re-flushing the frame solely to attribute its already-thrown exception; retain correct attribution when a different frame's image is deliberately targeted. Keep the public API unchanged and preserve the existing programmatic-registration/no-coordinate and production elision rules.

Acceptance: a focused regression with the line-10 old handler registering a line-20 replacement before throwing reports line 10, then a subsequent dispatch resolves the replacement. Keep the existing two-image, frozen-move, no-macro and production-coordinate witnesses green. No new metadata registry or general tracing mechanism is needed.

B1 — implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:526 carries :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}. That is a REPO-WIDE DEFAULT ON EVERY BUILD. P0 WORKER STALLED MID-REVERT, RESUMED — AND IT FOUND SOMETHING THE MAP DID NOT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

WHAT HAPPENED. The bench re-home worker hit the harness watchdog after 600 seconds with no progress. Its last words: the JSON rewrites hit BLOB-PINNED PROVENANCE RECORDS inside the recorded measurements, and it was reverting them because they must move verbatim.

THAT FINDING IS IMPORTANT AND SHOULD SURVIVE ANY RESTART. The 36 .json and 4 .edn recorded-measurement files are not inert data — they carry blob-pinned provenance. So the mechanical path rewrite that the .cjs runners need is exactly WRONG for the .json and .edn records: rewriting a path inside one breaks the pin that ties the record to the run that produced it. My brief said move them verbatim; the worker discovered WHY, which is stronger.

STATE WHEN IT STOPPED: 219 modified files, ZERO commits. Roughly two hours of work entirely in the working tree. I did not commit on its behalf — a half-reverted state committed by someone else is worse than no commit, and only that worker knows how far its revert reached. Resumed via message instead.

THE LIKELY CAUSE IS MACHINE LOAD, NOT THE CHANGE. Processor queue read 81 with five workers plus CI contending. That is the same condition behind the par-compile abort another worker saw today.

ALSO FLAGGED TO IT: its dirty list includes implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, .gitattributes, implementation/README.md and two docs/design/hicasso/studio pages — NONE of them in its fence. Most likely a path-rewrite sweep that widened. core/src especially needs a specific reason, because the phase-1 map established core has ZERO requires on Freehand.

LESSON FOR THE NEXT P0 BRIEF, whoever writes it: require commits at milestones rather than at the end. A branch with commits survives a stall; a working tree does not. This move is large enough that the natural rhythm — move files, fix requires, fix paths, run gates — is four commits, and any of them would have been worth keeping.

*** THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM. *** The epic sequences the atomic deletes (R2b, R3b) FIRST and the sweeps (R4, R5, R6) AFTER. But CI evaluates the whole tree, so between the delete landing and the sweeps landing there is no green state. The deletes cannot merge, and the sweeps are dependency-blocked behind them. (c) INVERT THE ORDER - unpoint FIRST, delete LAST. Do R6's prose sweep and R5's corpus-and-workflow removal while the trees still EXIST, each landing green on its own because nothing is missing yet. Then R2b/R3b become near-trivial deletes of trees nothing references, and go green immediately.

It also splits naturally into parallel dispatches by surface - skills/, docs/, .github/, catalogues - where (a) cannot be split at all.

Under (c) the branch is not repaired, it is REBASED onto a trunk where the unpointing has already landed, and most of the nine failures disappear without anyone editing the branch. title: api(views): (rf/view id) answers every substrate's mountable head — Hicasso publishes its alias under :handler-fn; correct the view / reg-view spec lines
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.5); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`(rf/view id)` is the framework's late-bind view lookup (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:788` → `re-frame.views/view-head`, `views.cljs:771-805`) and the spec's answer to "find a view by its registered id" (`spec/API.md:215`, `spec/Conventions.md` §Render-tree shape vs runtime lookup). It is true on Reagent and UIx and `nil` on Hicasso by design: `h/defview` registers through `registrar/register!` with the minted head under a PRIVATE key `:hicasso/component` and `:executable-key :hicasso/component`, and no `:handler-fn` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:1203-1230`; docstring at `hicasso.cljc:200-209`). A registrar answer that is true on two substrates and nil on the third is the "private-API spelunking" Principles forbid: Story's `:reagent` substrate reads `rf/view` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:227-236`) while Hicasso needs a second substrate hook; a tool enumerating `:view` must know a second descriptor shape. The stated reason for the bypass — `reg-view*` "consults the `:adapter/wrap-view` hook at registration time, which at namespace load precedes `rf/init!`" (`collector.cljs:1218-1221`) — is stale: `view-head` re-derives lazily against the installed adapter (`views.cljs:777-783`, rf2-oz7wr / rf2-8mkmb). The SHAPE reason is still load-bearing: a Hicasso boundary is a React component, not a hiccup render fn, and `reg-view*` would wrap and componentise it (`views.cljs:433-501`, `spine.cljs:2378-2418`). title: Overrides apply after interceptor factories run, so a removed factory still executes and a throwing one fails the dispatch
description:
## Bug

At dispatch the router resolves the whole interceptor chain first, which invokes every `[id arg]` factory, and only then applies `:interceptor-overrides`. So an override that removes a factory reference (`{[:my/factory arg] nil}`) still runs that factory on every dispatch. If the factory throws, for example after a hot reload, the dispatch fails even though the override was meant to take the interceptor out.

Registration also validates references by invoking the factory. Stories and tests that override interceptors are the ones affected.

## Evidence

**Where (trunk 475bdcaacf):**
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2458-2463` (`prepare-handler-ctx`): `resolve-chain` runs over the whole prepended chain, then `apply-icpt-overrides` runs over the resolved chain.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor_registry.cljc:428` (`resolve-ref`) and `:371` (`resolve-factory`): resolving an `[id arg]` ref calls the factory.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:169-187` (`validate-refs-registered!`): registration calls `resolve-ref` on each ref, so the factory runs at `reg-event` time too.

**Repro (*probed*):** JVM, `clojure -M` from `implementation/core`, plain-atom adapter. Run at HEAD 9b20bf0093, whose `implementation/core` is byte-identical to 475bdcaacf.

```clojure
(def factory-calls (atom 0))
(rf/reg-interceptor :probe/fact {:factory (fn [arg] (swap! factory-calls inc) {:before identity})})
(rf/reg-event :probe/guarded {:interceptors [[:probe/fact 1]]}
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (assoc db :guarded-ran true)}))
;; 4a. factory-calls after reg-event => 1
(reset! factory-calls 0)
(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/guarded] {:frame :probe/f :interceptor-overrides {[:probe/fact 1] nil}})
;; 4b. factory-calls => 1, handler ran => true   (the removed factory still ran)

;; hot reload the factory into one that throws; keep the same nil override
(rf/reg-interceptor :probe/fact {:factory (fn [arg] (throw (ex-info "factory boom" {})))})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:probe/guarded] {:frame :probe/k :interceptor-overrides {[:probe/fact 1] nil}})
;; 4c. dispatch-sync throws :rf.error/interceptor-factory-arity; handler ran => false
```

**Contract:** the code follows the spec here. `spec/002-Frames.md:2570` says: "After refs resolve, the runtime applies the merged override map". The defect is that order, which means a removal cannot remove the factory's execution. The same spec stores chains as references precisely so they can be edited before execution (§Validation and resolution timing, `:2574-2583`).

## Expected

A reference that an override removes or replaces is never built, so its factory is not called.

## Fix direction

- Apply `:interceptor-overrides` to the raw authored references (keys already match authored refs exactly), then resolve only the surviving references, once.
- At registration, check id existence and reference shape (a bare keyword for a static descriptor, `[id arg]` for a factory) without calling the factory.
- Bad factory arguments then surface when a surviving stage is built at dispatch, not at registration.
- Reword `spec/002-Frames.md:2570` and the registration-time bullet of §Validation and resolution timing to match.

## Acceptance

- New test: with `{[:probe/fact 1] nil}`, the factory's call counter stays 0 at dispatch, and a replaced factory ref is never invoked. Probe 4c's dispatch runs the handler. All three fail at trunk.
- Unknown ids and wrong reference shapes still fail at registration with their current error ids.
- Re-registering an interceptor still takes effect on the next dispatch.
- Exact `[id arg]` matching is unchanged: `{[:rf.interceptor/path [:cart]] nil}` removes only that instance.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (sol/04 §5, read); reproduced by JVM probe at trunk.
- Related: rf2-vfp6f (closed) fixed bare-keyword override matching against an entry's `:id`. A throwing factory surfaces as `:rf.error/interceptor-factory-arity`, which is an odd id for a factory exception. It is not part of this bead.
- Hot zones: `spec/002-Frames.md`.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/core-event-pipeline.md` D5 attack 3 and action 7; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/04-core-events-effects.md` §5.

The resolved chain no longer carries an authored-ref stamp (:rf/interceptor-ref, authored-ref-key deleted; its only reader was the override matcher); override-key-matches? now compares a key against the authored ref directly. override-summary walks the authored chain.
REGISTRATION: new interceptor-registry/check-ref! and check-chain! check id existence and reference shape (bare keyword names a static descriptor, [id arg] names a :factory) without calling the factory. reg-event (events.cljc validate-refs-registered!) and make-frame (live_frame.cljc validate-frame-interceptors!) use them.
